  - **BUILT: the floor, in `weekBounds` (`src/lib/sync/ingest-week.ts`), the column's only writer.** `last_game_ends_at = allFinal ? (prior ?? max(observation, floor)) : null`, where `floor` is the first Tuesday 00:00 `America/Los_Angeles` STRICTLY AFTER the week's `nfl_weeks.starts_at`. New pure helper `src/lib/leagues/time/release-floor.ts` — a Pacific twin of `stats/nflverse/eastern-time.ts`, offsets read from IANA zone data via `Intl`, no clock read anywhere, and under `src/lib/leagues/**` so the D3 fence covers it with no `.eslintrc.json` edit. `readWeeks` now selects `starts_at` and carries it BESIDE `WeekBounds` (a `StoredWeek` wrapper) rather than inside it — `WeekBounds` is the write payload and drives `sameBounds`, so a read-only calendar column added to it would be written back into `nfl_weeks`. **No migration**: no SQL anywhere computes a Pacific boundary, and every SQL reader already compares the column to `p_at`.
  - **THE ANCHOR IS THE WEEK, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE TRAP.** Deriving the floor from the last kickoff (or `first_kickoff_at`, or `now`) would send Chris's Tuesday weather-delay case to the FOLLOWING Tuesday and hold every player an extra week. From `starts_at` the floor is a constant of the week, so a game finishing Tuesday 14:00 PT stamps 14:00 PT. Pinned by name in `ingest-week.test.ts` ("CASE 2 — past the floor (THE TRAP)").
  - **A HELD WEEK STAMPS THE FUTURE FLOOR, IT DOES NOT HOLD NULL** — decided rather than improvised, because existing code already assigns all-final-and-NULL a meaning: `calendarFindings`' `all_final_unstamped` ALERT (`scoring/reconcile.ts:388`, F238 — "the release was never OBSERVED by a sync-live poll"). Holding NULL for the ~3.3 h hold would fire that for every league every week and destroy the alert's meaning. A future stamp keeps players locked (`p_at < window_ends_at`, 115:270), keeps the week `live` (`<= p_now`, 118:1846), and lets `lineup_lock_tick` write a real instant instead of `'infinity'` (116:59-66). Pinned in `reconcile.test.ts` ("an all-final week holding a FUTURE release stamp is NOT unstamped").
  - **THE SIM GAINS A `release` BEAT.** `season-runner.ts`'s `close` beat sits at `lastEnd + 1 min` — ~27 h before the floor — so `league_week_advance` can no longer flip the week there; the close beat now asserts the ruling's NEGATIVE half (games over, week still `live`) and a new `release` beat at `floor + 1 min` runs the advance. Without it the flip would depend on the NEXT week's `open` beat, which the last driven week never gets.
  - **NOT BUILT, DELIBERATELY: the Wednesday 00:00 Pacific CEILING.** (c) routes its four consequences to M5 (waivers) and M8 (the operator's notice), and says the timing rule is *"recorded here for M5 to build to, not built now"*. **F333** carries it. The finalize half still waits on (e).
  - **KNOWN COSMETIC DRIFT, filed not fixed:** 039:47 (`updated as games finish (MNF)`), 115:535/:606 (`week % clears at % (when its last game ends…)`) and 116:307 still describe the column as the last game ending, which is imprecise for a held week. They are SQL literals; correcting them needs a migration this TypeScript change does not justify. Fold the correction into the next migration that replaces those bodies.

**Q49 — HOW LONG MAY A LIVE DRAFT ROOM RENDER A STATE IT HAS ALREADY MOVED PAST, WHEN BROADCAST DELIVERY STOPS ENTIRELY? THE BUILT ANSWER IS 45 SECONDS — AND ON A SURFACE WITH 30 s PICK CLOCKS THAT MEANS A MANAGER CAN WATCH A FULL PICK CLOCK ELAPSE ON A ROOM STATE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS, WITH NO BANNER AND NO INDICATION ANYTHING IS WRONG. OPEN, filed 2026-09-09 by the F308 Builder; **HEADLINE AND FRAMING CORRECTED at the #280 fix round (R952-round ruling, taken 2026-09-09).** The original headline said the constant was "derived from a heartbeat cadence the engine no longer uses". That CONFLATED TWO DIFFERENT BEATS and had to be fixed before this reached Chris: the arithmetic was right, the framing was not, and half of what Chris would be changing had been dropped from the quotation. See **(3)**. Ledger F312.**

**(1) THE MEASUREMENT, BY CONSTRUCTION (D334(4), three probes on the shipped tree, md5 restored).** With the manager's realtime socket dropping ONLY the `drafts` frame that carries a nomination, the room healed in **4,125 ms** — `heartbeatSignalsGap` sees the next 5 s beat carrying the new bid deadline, mismatches the nomination deadline it holds, and refetches. With EVERY server frame dropped — a subscribed-but-deaf channel, F74/D325's documented shape — the room rendered the pre-nomination state for **49,000 ms** before the beat-silence watchdog fired. The exposure is therefore precisely the total-silence case, and it is `HEARTBEAT_SILENCE_MS` (45 s) plus one `ROOM_WATCHDOG_MS` beat.

**(2) IT IS REACHABLE WITHOUT ANY BUG IN OUR CODE.** `realtime.send()` traps its own errors (068 ARM 3), so the database records success; the Realtime service can then refuse the broadcast — measured here as `UnableToBroadcastChanges: :too_many_requests` at up to 28,316/minute against a 100 events/s tenant ceiling (F311) — and the client receives no error, no close and no signal of any kind. Presence keeps working throughout, because it is channel-level rather than `realtime.send()`, so the room looks healthy: live seats, a running clock, and state that stopped 45 seconds ago.

**(3) WHICH BEAT THE NUMBER ACTUALLY MEASURES — THERE ARE TWO, AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS QUESTION RAN THEM TOGETHER (corrected at the #280 fix round).** `HEARTBEAT_SILENCE_MS` measures ONE thing: the **INBOUND `tick` BROADCAST**. `lastBeatAtRef` is written in exactly one place, the `tick` handler (`use-draft.ts:396-397`); §9.1 **prints** that cadence as 15 s and 068 ARM 3 **ships** it at 5 s (`068:1265` `cron.schedule('draft-tick', '5 seconds')`). The OTHER 15 s in this room — `use-draft.ts:527`'s `setInterval(touch, 15_000)` — is the **OUTBOUND `draft_touch` liveness beat**, which `068:309` states is **NEVER broadcast** (D102) and which therefore never reaches `lastBeatAtRef` at all. The original headline's "a cadence the engine no longer uses" pointed at that outbound beat; **the engine uses it, unchanged, at 15 s.** **So the accurate statement is:** the docblock justifies 45 s against the cadence §9.1 PRINTS (15 s tick, ≤ 2 missed beats); the cadence that actually SHIPS is 5 s; and measured against the shipped one, 45 s is nine missed beats rather than two. **AND THE DOCBLOCK'S SECOND JUSTIFICATION, WHICH THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS QUESTION DROPPED WHEN IT QUOTED THE COMMENT — restored here, because it is the half that is NOT out of date and Chris must be told both.** The full clause is "≤ 2 missed printed-cadence beats, **the `draft_liveness_freshness` symmetry**". That server-side function is `interval '45 seconds'` and 068:18-20 derives it as **3 × the ~15 s `draft_touch` cadence** — the OUTBOUND beat, which ships at exactly 15 s — with pgTAP 022 pinning the literal, and 068's "ONE constant" instruction binding 069's commissioner-outage arm to the same function. **The consequence, stated plainly: the client's 45 s currently MIRRORS the server's 45 s liveness grace.** Lowering the client number to 15 s fixes the stale half of the justification and BREAKS the live half — the client would start doubting a room the server still calls fresh for another 30 s. That is a legitimate choice (the client's arm only refetches; see (3b)), but it is a choice, not a correction. **And why this is a question and not a fix:** the spec does not define the room's staleness bound at all — it prints a cadence, never a tolerance; no sentence in §9 or §16.5 bounds how long a room may render a state it has moved past; and §16.5.4's reconnecting banner arms off JOIN FAILURE (`connectionAfterJoinFailure`), which a subscribed-but-deaf channel never trips. The exposure is **undefined by the spec, not defined-and-violated**. Lowering the constant to clear a red would also be the exact move F308's task forbade: it repairs no drop and shortens no cause.

**(3b) WHAT IT COSTS A MANAGER — the part that deserves an answer regardless of F308.** The constant has exactly **one** consumer: `roomWatchdogWantsRefetch`'s live arm, which returns a boolean that triggers a REST **refetch of server truth**. It writes nothing, gates no autopick, decides no grace and renders no UI — so a shorter tolerance cannot diverge client from server, and there is no wrong output to point at. That is precisely why this is a product question rather than a defect wearing a question's clothes. **The cost is entirely on the human.** On a surface whose pick clock can be **30 s**, 45 s + one 5 s beat means a manager can watch a **full pick clock elapse** — a lot nominated, bid up and awarded — against a board that stopped being true 45 seconds ago, with no banner, no spinner and no indication anything is wrong; presence keeps rendering live seats and the clock keeps counting down (see (2)). That is user-visible, and it is currently nobody's decision.

**(4) OPTIONS.** **(a) Leave 45 s** and treat total broadcast silence as an infrastructure concern only (F311). Cheapest; keeps a 45 s blind window on a surface with 30 s pick clocks. **(b) Re-derive the tolerance from the SHIPPED cadence** — 3 missed 5 s beats = 15 s — and fold §9.1's printed 15 s → 5 s as an erratum in the same change. A live room then re-asks after 15 s of silence; a healthy room never reaches it, so the added cost is one REST read per 15 s only for rooms that are already broken. **Its price, named at the #280 fix round:** it ends the `draft_liveness_freshness` symmetry (3), so the client would doubt at 15 s while the server still calls the seat fresh for 45 s. Defensible — the two numbers answer different questions ("is my render stale?" vs "is this manager still here?") and the client arm only refetches — but it should be chosen, and the docblock should then say so instead of claiming a symmetry it no longer has. **(c) Make silence VISIBLE as well as recoverable**: at the same threshold, surface the existing degraded banner (R263's) so a manager knows the room is re-syncing rather than seeing a confidently wrong board. **(d) Escalate the ASK rather than the threshold** — keep 45 s for the banner but refetch at 15 s.

**RECOMMENDATION: (b) + (c) — restated at the #280 fix round now that BOTH halves of the docblock are on the record.** (b) makes the constant's FIRST justification true against the cadence that actually ships, and the fold-back erratum removes a spec/build divergence that has already misled one reader — but it deliberately ENDS the SECOND, the `draft_liveness_freshness` symmetry (3), so it must be taken with eyes open and the docblock rewritten to claim only what remains true. That trade is worth making, because the two numbers answer different questions — "is my render stale?" is the client's, "is this manager still here?" is the server's — and only the client's arm is a pure refetch. **If the symmetry is judged worth keeping, (d) is the cheaper answer:** refetch at 15 s, leave the 45 s grace and the banner where they are. (c) costs nothing new — the banner exists — and it is this repo's own doctrine that a wrong render must not be silent ("never let 'nothing happened' mean 'it worked'"). **WHAT THE ANSWER DOES NOT DECIDE — stated plainly, at the #280 fix round's direction, so nobody reads this question as F308's fix: NEITHER ANSWER CLEARS F308.** Even at 15 s the room needs 15 s **plus a beat** against `auction-live.spec.ts:213`'s 20 s assertion, so a total-silence event inside that window still reds the spec — correctly. F308 stays open on its own terms, B11 stands, and the drop itself stays **F311**'s question. This ruling changes what a manager sees; it changes nothing about the red.

**Q47 — IS "POST-WINDOW" THE INSTANT THE CORRECTION WINDOW CLOSES, OR THE STATE OF THE WEEK BEING FINAL? A WEEK HELD SHORT OF `final` PAST ITS OWN WINDOW STILL ACCEPTS DELTAS. OPEN, filed 2026-09-08 by the L.D6.3 Builder; **CAUSE ESTABLISHED 2026-09-09 at the fix round — this is no longer a 1-in-9 mystery but a mechanism reproducible on demand, and the question is narrowed to the RULING alone.** Ledger F302. BLOCKS NOTHING — the gate now CLASSIFIES the state with the finalize job's own reason and NAMES the wider one**

**Q47 — WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED AT THE FIX ROUND (2026-09-09), and why it is a §3 question rather than a migration.**

**(1) THE MECHANISM, from the source.** `finalize_matchups` (HEAD at 118:1945) claims a week only when `lw.status = 'correction_window' AND w.correction_window_ends_at <= p_now` (118:2049), and then holds it on either of two guards, each of which `CONTINUE`s and leaves the row UNTOUCHED: guard 1 at **118:2054** — `week_games_state_internal(...).all_final` false ⇒ `games_not_final` (§23.2, no league state advances on partial data); guard 2 at **118:2074** — `week_results_pending_internal(...)` non-NULL ⇒ `pending_scores` / `pending_results` (E61 — absence is not a score, never coerced to 0.00). 118:2073 states the consequence verbatim: *"The week is SKIPPED BY NAME and stays `correction_window`."* And `correction_window` is precisely the status the write door ADMITS — 119:566 refuses only `final`, 119:570 says the door "writes only a live or correction_window week". `score_write_week_batch` never reads `correction_window_ends_at` at all: `grep -c correction 119` is **1**, and that one hit is the error string. The door has no access to the window instant.

**(2) DEMONSTRATED, ROLLED BACK, on the 122 chain (2026-09-09).** A minimal in_season league, week 1 in `correction_window`, `nfl_weeks.correction_window_ends_at = 2099-09-11T10:00Z`, one matchup with a NULL home score, every in-week game `final`. At `2099-09-12T00:00:00Z` — past the window: `week_results_pending_internal` returned `{"reason":"pending_scores","pending":1}`; `finalize_matchups` SKIPPED it with its own reason `{"week":1,"reason":"pending_scores","pending":1}` and reported `nothing_finalized`; `league_weeks.status` stayed `correction_window`; and `score_write_week_batch` then **ACCEPTED** the post-window batch (`"written":1`), moving `matchups.home_score` from **NULL to 123.45** — a league cell changed after the window closed. **CONTROL:** the same week flipped to `final`, same door, same batch ⇒ refused by name, `week_final — ... a post-window delta changes no league cell (D295, §23.4)`. The whole probe ran inside one transaction and ended `ROLLBACK`.

**(3) WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY A CHAIN BUG (the reason it stays a question and no migration was written).** (i) **"A post-window delta changes NO league cell" IS NOT SPEC TEXT.** It exists only in D295(b) — a PROGRESS decision — and is quoted FROM there into 119:567's error string and the worker docblock. The spec's own normative sentence is §23.4 (spec:2187): a post-window correction *"is not auto-applied — it surfaces as a flagged event the commissioner may apply via override."* (ii) **SOFTENED AT THE SECOND FIX ROUND (#278 review's Q47 ruling) — this pillar overreached and is NOT load-bearing; the ruling should rest on (i), (iii) and (iv).** It used to read *"the spec never contemplates the divergent state … there is no spec vocabulary for a week past its window that is not final."* That is too strong: §11.4's finalization bullet DOES name the state — `pending_results` for a `total_points` week missing a seated team's row, and F238's *"past its window both jobs NAME it"* — but every one of those names sits inside the `*(v2.16.22 — … measured …)*` **as-built annotation**, not in the normative bullet, whose own sentence is only *"after the week's games + the stat-correction window … the matchup is marked `final`."* Under this repo's own rule — **R888**'s precedent, applied by name in the L.D5.5 review's "verified against the LAW" line (*"read as AS-BUILT annotations, not rules (R888's precedent)"*) — the annotation DESCRIBES the divergent state without RULING it. So the accurate, narrower claim is: **no normative sentence governs a week that is past its window and not final** — which is exactly what makes this a §3 question. Nothing else in the argument depends on it. (iii) **Refusing would strand the week, and the law supplies no lever to unstick it.** The delta being refused is often exactly the datum that would COMPLETE the pending cell finalization is waiting on; §10 (spec:680) gives the commissioner `reopen_week` (`final → correction_window`, 110:287) and no inverse — there is no force-finalize, and 112:1192's audited vocabulary is `reopen_week`, not `close_week`. (iv) **The neighbourhood is already an open question: Q37**, which shows the hold can be PERMANENT (a cancelled NFL week-18 game holds every league week forever, and nothing can release it). Q37's hold is guard 1; this question's is guard 2; neither had cross-referenced the other until now. So the law is genuinely ambiguous HERE, and improvising a migration would harden one reading of it — the exact thing the standing rules forbid.

**(4) A SECOND, DISTINCT "past its window but not final" STATE, found in the same pass and worth the ruling's attention.** 118:2031-2041 detects a **`live`** week past its `correction_window_ends_at` whose `nfl_weeks.last_game_ends_at` is unrecorded, and only REPORTS it (`live_past_window`, F238) — the claim loop at 118:2049 requires `correction_window`, so such a week can never be finalized until ingestion writes the game end. That state is writable at the door too (119:570 admits `live`). Whichever way Q47 is ruled, it should be ruled for BOTH states or the ruling will be half-applied.

**(5) WHAT THE GATE DOES NOW (changed at the fix round; it does not rule, and it no longer merely names).** The `correction_post_window` arm CLASSIFIES every post-window write to a still-open week using the FINALIZE JOB'S OWN two oracles, read at the same instant and never mirrored in TS (D289/D33): `week_games_state_internal` (guard 1) and `week_results_pending_internal` (guard 2). A write explained by a lawful hold is reported WITH that reason; a write to a week that is neither `final` nor held is **UNEXPLAINED and FAILS the gate** — that would be a week the job should have finalized and did not, a different bug that must not hide behind this gap; a write to a `final` week still fails as the D295(b) breach it is. This is the same posture the reconciliation takes for a lawfully held week.

**RECOMMENDATION UNCHANGED: (a), finality governs** — with D295(b)'s sentence qualified to "of a week that has finalized" in the same erratum, and §23.4 gaining one sentence for the held-week case. (b) is now clearly worse than it looked: it needs a commissioner path that does not exist, and Q37 proves the hold it would make permanent is not hypothetical. **ORIGINAL FILING FOLLOWS.**

**Q47 (as filed 2026-09-08) — the narrower guarantee and the wider one** — D295(b) says a post-window delta "changes NO league cell", and the chain implements that through the DOOR: `score_write_week_batch` raises `week_final` for a week whose `league_weeks.status` is `final` (119:566) and writes a week that is `live` or `correction_window` (119:570). Those two are not the same test. A week is `final` only once `finalize_matchups` has claimed it, and finalization lawfully HOLDS while a cell is pending — so a league whose week is held past its own `correction_window_ends_at` is still open at the door, and a post-window delta writes it. **MEASURED at the gate's own scale:** across nine 100-league runs, one produced `1 write / 198 week_final skips` where the other eight (and five later re-runs) produced `0 / 200`; the writing league's week 1 was not `final` at that instant and finalized at the next finalize pass. **The gap:** §23.4 talks about the WINDOW (an instant — "in-window deltas auto-recompute; post-window deltas are flagged for commissioner apply"), while §23.2's worker and 119's door talk about FINALITY (a state). Nothing says which governs when the two disagree, and they disagree exactly when finalization is held. **Options:** **(a) finality governs** (as built): the door's test is the law, a held week is genuinely still open, and a delta that completes the very cell holding finalization is the RIGHT thing to apply — D295(b)'s sentence gains the qualifier "of a week that has finalized"; **(b) the window instant governs**: `score_write_week_batch` gains a `correction_window_ends_at` check beside its `week_final` check, so a held week refuses post-window deltas too — cost: a CREATE OR REPLACE against 119's file text (D137), and a week held for a pending cell can then never be completed by the correction that would have completed it, so it needs a commissioner path (M6's, which does not exist yet); **(c) leave the disagreement and require finalization never to be held past the window** — rejected: holds are lawful and §23.2 is incremental. **Recommendation: (a)**, with the D295(b) sentence qualified in the same erratum. **What the gate does meanwhile:** the `correction_post_window` arm asserts the two things that ARE unambiguous — the door refused by name at least once, and NO post-window write landed on a week whose `league_weeks.status` read back as `final` (a direct read at the instant, because the door's report says it WROTE and not what the status was) — and NAMES every write to a still-open week in full, with its door report. "No FINAL week's cell changed" stays enforced run-wide by invariant 6 (`final-cell-immutable`), which is part of `report.green`. *(Filed rather than folded: making the gate assert zero writes would make it FLAKE at 1-in-9, and making it ignore them would fold an unruled definition into a green — R801.)*

**Q46 — WHAT DISCHARGES THE L.D6.3 ROW'S ITEM 2, "RECONCILIATION (L.D2.3) RUNS CLEAN OVER THE WHOLE SEEDED POPULATION"? OPEN, filed 2026-09-08 by the L.D6.3 Builder. Ledger none. BLOCKS NOTHING — the gate is green on the recommendation** — `scripts/reconcile.ts`'s own docblock (`:1-6`) claims *"the gates (L.D6.3 / L.D6.4) invoke it by name"*, which reads as a requirement for an `npm run reconcile` STAGE. The gate does not have one, and three measured facts say it must not: **(a) the population is GONE by then** — `season-runner.ts:493-518` calls `cleanupSweep` in a `finally` on every path and the season command has no keep-leagues flag (`scripts/sim.ts:111-122`), so after any season run zero seeded leagues remain; **(b) it would exit 0 on nothing** — `scripts/reconcile.ts:72-75` exits 1 only when `report.alerts > 0`, and `reason: 'no_leagues_in_scope'` exits 0, so a post-sweep stage is a textbook "nothing happened means it worked"; **(c) it defaults to PRODUCTION** — `:25` loads `.env.local` and `:46-47` reads the URL/service key with NO local-only guard, unlike `scripts/sim.ts:141-145` and `scripts/sim-census.ts:55-58` which refuse any non-127.0.0.1 URL; its header documents an override recipe, which is a docblock, not a guard. **Options:** **(a) the in-run `reconcileSeason`** (built): the run calls the LIBRARY by name over `leagueStates.map(s => s.leagueId)` — the whole seeded population, at the only moment it exists — and surfaces `reconcileSummary` + `reconcileClassified`, which the gate's evidence stage transcribes and asserts covered every seeded league with a non-zero cell count; **(b) a `--keep-leagues` flag + a standalone `npm run reconcile` stage + an explicit sweep stage** — doubles the reconcile cost, lets a mid-gate failure strand 900 leagues, and needs a local-only guard added to `reconcile.ts` first; **(c) leave the docblock's claim and satisfy it literally** — rejected: it would be (b) without the guard. **Recommendation: (a)**, and amend `scripts/reconcile.ts`'s docblock to say the gates invoke the LIBRARY through the run rather than the script. *(Filed rather than quietly diverging from a claim a shipped file makes about this task — the divergence itself is the thing worth a ruling.)*

**Q45 — DOES AN EMPTY STARTING SLOT FAIL THE SYNTHETIC GATE? OPEN, filed 2026-09-08 by the L.D6.3 Builder. Ledger F288. BLOCKS NOTHING — the gate is green on the recommendation** — an empty starting slot is LAWFUL: `114:585-588` flags one and never blocks on it, and a manager may legally field ten men. But before L.D6.3 the sim's `lineupSlotsLeftEmpty` was PRINTED and entered `report.green` nowhere (`season-runner.ts` — the count sat beside the seating line and in no predicate), so a league with **71 of 96** starting slots filled read as fully seated, and the K and D/ST scoring rules went unexercised across a whole gate run. **Root cause, measured on the restored local pool 2026-09-08:** the first kicker sits at ADP rank ~138 and the first defense at ~95, while `SEASON_ROSTER` starts six positions off `SEASON_ROUNDS = 7` — 112 picks in a 16-team league and 56 in an 8-team one — so a pure-ADP board reaches NO kicker at ANY league size. **The gap:** nothing in the spec says what "a seated lineup" means for CERTIFICATION purposes. §11.1's legality rules say what a lineup MAY be; they do not say what a gate must have exercised before it certifies scoring. **Options:** **(a) FAIL the run** (built): every starting slot must be filled, named by slot key when it is not, because the honest failure mode of a gate whose job is certifying scoring is a position it never scored; **(b) print and do not fail** (the status quo ante) — lawful, and it is exactly the "nothing happened means it worked" shape CLAUDE.md opens with; **(c) fail only when a whole POSITION is empty run-wide** — a middle reading that tolerates one odd board but catches an unreachable position. **Recommendation: (a), with the fix that makes it achievable** — season-mode personas now mirror the server's own need-aware autopick (`086:552-748`: capacities from `roster_settings`, force when `remaining <= unfilled`), gated to season mode so draft-mode personas and the M2/M3 gates' stored-literal seed-42 runs are untouched. MEASURED after the fix: 96/96, 72/72, 48/48, 96/96, 84/84, 96/96 slots filled at 6 leagues over three consecutive runs, and 0 empty across all nine 100-league gate stages. **The residual to know about:** (a) makes the gate depend on the restored pool holding a kicker inside `POOL_WINDOW` (400 rows by ADP). If a future restore does not, the gate reds — which is the CORRECT red (the K rules would be unexercised), but it is a red caused by DATA, and the message says so. *(Filed because the ASSERTION, not the fix, is the unruled part — R801.)*

**Q44 — CAN THE GATE ASSERT E61 PENDING-NOT-ZERO ON THE D15 CHARTED KEY AT LEAGUE LEVEL, WHEN THE SPEC FORBIDS ANY DOCUMENT THAT WOULD PAY IT? OPEN, filed 2026-09-08 by the L.D6.3 Builder. Ledger F283 (whose prescribed discharge is the thing that cannot be executed), F301 (the forward half). BLOCKS NOTHING — the gate is green on the recommendation** — the tasks-M4 §6 L.D6.3 row requires `charted_late` to "render pending-not-zero on D15 placeholder keys (E61)" and `charted_revision` to "recompute in-window". Both need a scoring snapshot that PAYS `example_charted_yards`. **The chain and the spec both refuse one, and it is MEASURED, not inferred:** the key is the registry's ONLY `tier: 'charted'` entry and carries `scoring_surface: 'reserved'` (`stat-keys.ts:204`); §23.5 (`spec:2200`) defines `reserved` as *"deferred bonuses, placeholders, IDP — never scorable in a format-2 doc, validation-rejected"*; §7.3.3.1 (`spec:341`) makes placeholder advanced keys non-editable; 103's `c_reserved` list refuses the key by name behind 104's `ENABLE ALWAYS` wall on `leagues.scoring_rules_snapshot` — `scoring_rules_validate({...ESPN Standard, example_charted_yards: 0.1})` answers, verbatim, *`Scorable allowlist (§7.3.3.1 guardrail 1): "example_charted_yards" cannot be scored — it is a reserved key (§23.5) — deferred bonuses, placeholders and IDP are not exposed by the cohort editor.`* And there is no legal substitute: the charted tier's intended consumer is **FieldScout Ultra**, one of the DEFERRED templates (`spec:2195-2199`), and none of the eight shipped templates pays any charted or tracking key (`templates.ts:289-361`; grep for `charted|tracking|air_yards|yac` returns nothing). **F283's cited precedent is not a forked DOCUMENT at all:** `score-week-worker-db.test.ts:282-295` is `withSnapshotOverlay`, a test-only client interceptor that rewrites what the worker READS while the DB row stays valid — its own comment (`:668-673`) says so. **Options:** **(a) a sim-level snapshot overlay** — install the same interceptor at the seam where the season runner hands the service client to the production worker: the gate would then certify a configuration that cannot exist in production and the spec forbids, and it would buy a SECOND copy of a proof that already exists at unit (`score-week-worker.test.ts:185-243`) and stack (`score-week-worker-db.test.ts:564,728`) level; **(b) assert what is LEGALLY observable at league level** — §23.5's own promise for a charted arrival: the value is INGESTED into `player_stats.advanced`, ENQUEUES a `score_fanout` delta, DRAINS and is RECOMPUTED by the real worker (to `no_change`, since no rules key pays it), changes NO league cell, and *"finalization timing does not move"* (§23.5's two-phase bullet, verbatim) — under two NEW assertion names, with `pending_not_zero`/`recomputed_in_window` kept in the union and deliberately UNEMITTED as the target state, and a printed, non-failing `coverageGaps` line on every run naming exactly what is not covered and what closes it; **(c) ship an Ultra-class template, or promote a charted key to `scorable`** — a §23.5 data task plus a template migration, outside L.D6.3's scope. **Recommendation: (b) now, (c) eventually — BUILT AS (b).** It is the only option that leaves the gate both green and honest; (a) is precisely the thing a gate exists to prevent. If Chris rules (a) or (c), the two new names retire and the two reserved names start being emitted — the union already carries them, and `gate-m4-evidence.ts`'s REQUIRED map is the one place that changes. *(Filed rather than folded per R801: the task text and the ledger cannot both be satisfied, and choosing between them is a ruling, not a build note.)*

**Q42 — A STARTER WITH NO STAT LINE FOR THE WEEK SCORES 0, NOT PENDING — THE WORKER'S READING OF THE LAW, BUILT AND PINNED. OPEN, filed 2026-09-07 by the L.D2.2 Builder (the Q41/Q39(B) shape: the recommendation shipped and pinned so it reds if ruled otherwise). Ledger F263(c). BLOCKS NOTHING** — `computeTeamWeek` scores a starter without a `player_stats` row as 0 and NAMES him (`no_stat_row`, per team on the report); a starter WITH a row whose applicable rules key is undelivered is PENDING (the door's NULL). **The gap:** §11.4 says a team's score is "Σ fantasy points of that team's locked starters" and E61/§23.5 say a rules key with no delivered stat is pending, never 0 — but no sentence says which of the two a starter with NO line at all is. The calculator's letter (`scorePlayerWeek(rules, {})`: every key pending) would make him pending; the provider contract's letter says the opposite in three places — the synthetic provider emits no line for an inactive ("scratched — never plays, never scores"), for a postponed-out game ("scores 0 this week (§23.3/E43)") and before kickoff; §23.3 prints "players in a game postponed out of the window score 0"; D293 prints "byes/OUT start and score 0, flagged". **Why 0 was built:** under "pending", every team is NULL until its LAST starter's line exists, a healthy scratch (no line, ever) holds the week at `pending_scores` FOREVER (finalize never claims it), and the live "week so far" number §16.5.3 renders would not exist until Monday night — the pending reading is unfinalizable, not merely different. Under "0 by name", the number is a running total (the industry's), a DNP/bye/scratch is the §23.3 zero, and E61's badge stays where the spec puts it — on a KEY the provider does not deliver for a player who played. **Options:** **(a) 0 by name** (built; the report lists every `no_stat_row` starter so a UI can render "yet to play" from the count — L.D5.2's); **(b) pending until the player's game is FINAL in `nfl_games`, then 0** (a kickoff-time read the worker deliberately does not make — §23.3 reads are the jobs'; a team would be NULL all Sunday; a scratch in a final game resolves to 0 correctly; the cost is the live number and a `nfl_games` read per starter per drain); **(c) pending, period** (rejected above — unfinalizable). **Recommendation: (a).** If (b) is ruled: one arm in `scoreStarter` reading the starter's game status through the week's `nfl_games` rows (the `lineup_kickoff_internal` datum, D291), the two pure pins (`no_stat_row` → 0) flip to null-until-final, and the stack's first-drain cell gains a final-game twin. **Residual the options above omit (R871, the #267 review):** at FINALIZATION "0 by name" cannot distinguish a DNP from a PROVIDER GAP — a starter of a `final` `nfl_games` row with NO `player_stats` line finalizes at 0.00 silently under (a) (and under (b) too, once the game is final). The check is §23.2's reconciliation's, not the worker's: "starter in a final game, no line" → alert, never a silent fix — routed to L.D2.3 as **F263(g)**. *(Recorded because R801 says a definition the LAW lacks is a question even when the reading is derivable — the derivation is above; nothing is folded as LAW: v2.16.30's §22.2 annotation states the reading and names this question.)*

**Q41 — A FRANCHISE RETIRED DURING THE PLAYOFFS: DOES THE SUCCESSOR PLAY ITS BRACKET LINE, OR IS THE LINE FORFEITED? OPEN, filed 2026-09-07 by the L.D1.10 Builder (migration 120). Ledger F262(b) (the application); F256(e) routed here. DOES NOT BLOCK MERGE** — 120's retire arm REFUSES BY NAME while `leagues.status = 'playoffs'` (068 H1: nothing written; the message names this question and points at takeover / vacate now or retirement after the season); the `in_season` and `complete` arms are complete and pinned. **The gap:** §7.2.1(b) (`spec:183`) says the successor "takes over the schedule position" and inherits the W-L record "for seeding math only", and that retirement is "primarily an offseason action; mid-season it's allowed as an audited override"; E49 (`spec:2012`) says "roster/FAAB/schedule slot". Neither sentence, nor §11.5's five ruled playoff sentences (Q39), says what happens to a retired franchise's LINE IN A LIVE BRACKET — and the bracket is not a schedule row like any other: 118's `playoff_bracket_state_internal` reads each round's survivors from the stored rows' team ids (`118:1181-1189`, `:1208`), and `playoff_bracket_sync_internal` builds round r+1 from those survivors and compares the STORED pairing text to the DESIRED one by team id (`118:1505-1522`) — so a re-pointed unplayed bracket row (the successor's id) would read as a MOVED verdict on the next pass and be rewritten back to the retired id (or refused as history by R839 if played). Rows the retired franchise already PLAYED are history (R839) and must keep its id. **Options:** **(a) the seat continues** — the successor plays the line: unplayed bracket rows re-point like the regular season's; `playoff_bracket_state_internal` hands survivors through the successor chain (`team_id` → the live franchise), and the sync compares stored-vs-desired on LIVE ids (both sides through the lineage), so a played round with the predecessor's id and a re-pointed later round read as the same bracket; the seeds frozen on the rows stay; the champion, if the successor wins, is the successor's id. Cost: a `playoff_bracket_sync_internal` + `playoff_bracket_state_internal` CREATE OR REPLACE against 118's file text (D137) — which attaches F258(a)/(b) to the same PR — plus a 066-style mid-playoff fixture. **(b) refuse during the playoffs, permanently** — the v1 posture as built minus the word "yet": vacate (autopilot) covers an abandoned seat for the ≤ 4 remaining weeks, takeover seats a friend, and the franchise is retired after `complete` — the LAW's own "primarily an offseason action"; the bracket never sees a re-point; History Mode still partitions correctly (the whole season is the retired franchise's). Cost: one message edit. **(c) forfeit** — the opponent advances by the (A) higher-seed rule: nowhere in the LAW; rejected as an invention. **Recommendation: (b) for v1** — zero bracket risk on a surface that just landed five rulings, the two existing modes already cover the human situation, and retirement is a History-Mode attribution device rather than a competitive one; (a) is recorded above as the return path with its exact cost if Chris wants the successor to play. *(Numbering note: Q39's (E) parenthetical informally reserved "Q41" for the current-week-boundary question — never filed; it takes the next free number if it ever is.)*

**Q39 — THE PLAYOFF BRACKET NEEDS FIVE DEFINITIONS THE LAW DOES NOT SUPPLY — AND ONE OF THEM (`total_points` brackets) THE CHAIN CANNOT FINALIZE OR SCORE AS BUILT. ~~OPEN~~ ~~RULED~~ **APPLIED 2026-09-07 — RULED (A)–(E) by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, one sub-question at a time (the Q30/Q31 shape), and applied by L.D1.8 / migration 118 on `feat/M4-L.D1.8-playoffs` (spec v2.16.25 §11.5 / §11.7 / §7.3.1 / §16.2 + changelog; D318; pgTAP 066); blocker B9 CLEARED. The two offered readings were handled as the header says: (B)'s equal-sum arm is BUILT as the higher seed and PINNED (066 J1 — reds if Chris rules otherwise); (E)'s "move the current-week boundary to the rollover" is NOT built and NOT filed as a question — 110/116's `starts_at` boundary stands and nothing in 118 needed it (the sync reads the rollover from `league_weeks.status`, which 116 flips ON `last_game_ends_at`). A `leagues` CHECK on the (C) pair was authored and WITHDRAWN (D318(4)).** Filed 2026-09-05 by the halted L.D1.8 Builder (`halt/M4-L.D1.8-playoffs-Q39`). ~~BLOCKS~~ Blocked L.D1.8 and, through it, the rest of the M4 schema lane (L.D1.9 → L.D1.10) — blocker B9. L.D2.1 / L.D3.1 (the data lane) depend only on L.D1.1 and stay takeable; the L.D4.x / L.D5.x surfaces that read the bracket wait.** No migration was written — 118 / 066 stay reserved (heads confirmed 117 / 065 with `ls`). Every silence below was found by reading §11.5 / §7.3.1 / §11.7 / §7.3.7 / E38 against 109 / 110 / 116 / 117 before a line of 118 was authored; the house rule (tasks-M4 §11; the R801 / Q38 precedent — "a definition the spec lacks is a QUESTION, not an annotation") routes them here. Each is one sentence for Chris and one golden for the Builder.
- **(A) A playoff matchup that ends in a two-decimal tie — who advances?** **RULED (a) by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, verbatim: "A."** — the HIGHER SEED advances; the row's `result` stays `'tie'` (E38's letter holds — no hidden precision consulted, no score rewritten; only the ADVANCEMENT reads the seed). Scoped to this sub-question; (B)–(E) remain OPEN. Application: one sentence in §11.5 + one 066 cell with two scores tied at two decimals. ** The spec's only tie rule is E38 (`spec:1996` — "`result = 'tie'`; standings W-L-T and tiebreakers handle ties") plus §11.4's finalization sentence ("a two-decimal tie is a tie"); both are regular-season statements. §11.5's Playoffs bullet (`spec:744`) and §7.3.7 (seeding, "at end of regular season") say nothing about advancement, and a bracket cannot carry a tie forward. As built, 117's `matchup_result_internal` writes `'tie'` on a playoff row exactly as on a regular one (D313(7)(g): playoff rows finalize generically). Options: **(a) the higher seed advances** — ESPN/Yahoo/Sleeper's default; the seed is the regular season's own verdict, so no hidden precision is consulted and E38's letter holds (the row's `result` stays `'tie'`; only the ADVANCEMENT reads the seed); (b) bench points / a stat tiebreak — consults data E38 forbids ("no hidden extra precision"), rejected; (c) the commissioner decides — M6's override; the bracket sits stuck until a human acts, for every league on the same night. **Recommendation: (a)**, one sentence in §11.5; pinned by a bracket cell whose two scores tie at two decimals.
- **(B) `playoff_weeks_per_round = 2` — what decides a two-week matchup?** §7.3.1 (`spec:210`) says only "2 = two-week rounds". A pairing spans two `league_weeks` rows (110:757 writes a row for EVERY plan week, `first .. first + rsw + rounds × wpr − 1`) and 109's uniqueness is per (league, season, week, round_type, side), so the representation is two `matchups` rows of the same pairing, one per week, each finalized on its own with its own E38 `result`. Options: **(a) aggregate** — the higher SUM of the two weeks' scores advances (every incumbent's reading; a week-1 loss can be overturned); (b) best-of-two with (A) breaking 1–1 (no platform does it); (c) the second week alone (absurd). **Recommendation: (a)**, with (A) applied to a tied aggregate; the per-week rows keep their own `result` for the record and `team_week_results` is untouched. Golden: the week-1 loser wins the aggregate and advances. **RULED by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, verbatim: "in a 2 week playoff round the scores are added together and the winner is the team with the most points over both weeks."** Each week's row keeps its own W/L/T; the round's verdict is the two-week SUM. *Orchestrator's reading, offered for confirmation, not assumed: an exactly equal two-week total has no "most" and falls to (A) — the higher seed.* (C)–(E) remain OPEN.
- **(C) `total_points` leagues with `playoff_teams > 0` — §11.7's "H2H brackets from points-seeding" (`spec:778`; task item 3) cannot be FINALIZED or SCORED by the chain as built, and the fix is a per-WEEK mode across three lanes.** The mode is branched per LEAGUE everywhere: 110 writes no `matchups` for the mode (`110:772`); 117's `finalize_matchups` flips `matchups` only under `IF v_mode = 'h2h'` (`117:610`); `week_results_pending_internal` asks `pending_scores` only on the h2h side (`117:250`); `week_results_write_internal`'s `total_points` arm reads no `matchups` at all (`117:425-434` — it flips the worker's rows `is_final`); F241(a)'s door contract and F241(b)'s worker contract (rows in `team_week_results` only for a `total_points` league; R800: nothing writes them today) know no playoff arm. A bracket 118 writes for such a league would stay `live` forever. Options: **(a) per-week mode** — a playoff week of a `total_points` league IS an h2h week: 118 replaces 117's three helpers + `finalize_matchups` (against 117's file text, D137) to branch on "`playoff` rows exist for this week" rather than on `schedule_mode`, and the ruling's application files two F-rows — L.D1.9's door scores those rows, L.D2.2's worker writes matchup scores for them; `league_standings` is unchanged (E64's skip is the regular season's). **(b) narrow v1** — `total_points` + `playoff_teams > 0` refuses at creation/edit (`validateLeagueSettings` + the 060/105 SQL checks) and the shrink chain writes 0; a `total_points` league's only playoff is §11.7's "final-week points race" (the v1.x shape the paragraph says it replaced — but the three lanes stay untouched and the bracket for the mode returns as one task when a cohort league asks). (c) write the bracket and leave finalization to a later task — a bracket nobody can finish, rejected. **Recommendation: (b) for the 2026 cohort with (a) recorded as the return path** — the cohort's feedback focus is auction + custom scoring (CLAUDE.md Active Builds), the local dev restore holds 0 leagues of any mode (measured 2026-09-05 — hosted not queried), and (a) is three lanes of contract for the mode §11.7 itself calls the alternative. If Chris rules (a), L.D1.8 grows by the 117 replacement and the two F-rows. **RULED (a) by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, verbatim: "a"** — NO playoff bracket for a `total_points` league; the season-long points race IS its playoff (the champion is the points leader when the regular season ends — the `complete` instant is (D)'s); `playoff_teams > 0` combined with `schedule_mode = total_points` is REFUSED at settings time with a plain message (`create_league` / `update_league_settings` + the Zod schema + the settings panel). The per-week mode (a total-points regular season with an H2H December bracket) is the RECORDED RETURN PATH, not built — an F-row at application. (D)–(E) remain OPEN.
- **(D) `playoff_teams = 0` — who is the champion, and when does the league `complete`?** §7.3.1 (`spec:208`): "0 = no playoffs (points-only champion)"; §11.7: a `total_points` league's playoffs "reduce to a final-week points race". Nothing says WHEN `complete` happens, or — for an h2h league at 0 — whether "points-only" means the PF leader or `league_standings` rank 1 (Win % first). Options: **(a) rank 1 of `league_standings` at the last regular-season week's finalization, both modes** (§7.3.7: "exactly one ranking rule in the product"; in `total_points` the chain is PF-first so the readings coincide); (b) the PF leader regardless of mode (the literal "points-only" — an h2h league's champion may then disagree with its own standings table). **Recommendation: (a)**; `complete` + the champion land in the transaction that finds the last regular-season week `final`. **RULED (a) by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, verbatim: "a"** — with `playoff_teams = 0` (and, by (C), every `total_points` league) the champion is **standings rank 1 through the FULL tiebreaker chain** (`league_standings`, 117 — record, PF, H2H, PA, coin flip; for `total_points` the chain's own E64 skip makes this the points leader), and the league flips `in_season → complete` **at the instant the last regular-season week goes `final`** (`finalize_matchups`, ~~via 110's F4 guard~~ *corrected 2026-09-07 at R843(iii): F4 guards `league_weeks`; the LEAGUES flip is the sync's `UPDATE leagues SET status = 'complete' … WHERE status = 'in_season'` with ROW_COUNT asserted — rider (vi), as 118 does*). Application: one sentence in §11.5, `leagues.champion_team_id` written at that flip, one 066 golden where rank 1 and the points leader DIFFER (an H2H league with playoffs off). (E) remains OPEN.
- **(E) The trigger instant — the task text (tasks-M4 L.D1.8 item 1: "when `league_week_advance` OPENS `playoff_start_week`: seed the bracket from `league_standings`") is unsatisfiable on the calendar as seeded.** `league_standings` reads `is_final` regular-season rows only (`117:1061`; §11.5 "never reads a provisional row"); a week opens at `nfl_weeks.starts_at` (Wed 00:00 ET) and the previous week finalizes at its `correction_window_ends_at` (Thu 06:00 ET — §23.4) — measured on the stack's 2026 rows: week 15 opens `2026-12-16 05:00Z`, week 14's window closes `2026-12-17 11:00Z`, **30 hours later**. At the open instant the standings are one week short (`weeks_final = rsw − 1`) and a bracket seeded then is wrong by construction. Options: **(a) seed when the LAST regular-season week goes `final`** — the hourly advance job (`:00`, after finalize's `:05`) writes round 1 and flips `in_season → playoffs` in ONE transaction the first run it finds the last regular week `final` and no `playoff` rows; round r+1 the same way once round r's weeks are all `final`; the champion + `complete` once the final round's weeks are `final`. The playoff week's `league_weeks` row still opens on its own boundary (auto-carry, the tick's locks and the door's `live` rows unaffected — the round's rows are inserted `live` when the week already is), and a late finalization (F238 / Q37) is a bracket NOT YET written, named hourly (`bracket_waiting` + the reason) — never one seeded from a provisional table. (b) seed at open from projected standings — §11.5 forbids it, rejected. (c) seed inside `finalize_matchups` — immediate, but 117's text for a consequence D313(7)(g) / D314(6) assigned to L.D1.8's advance replacement. **Recommendation: (a)** — a mechanics ruling filed here only because it contradicts the task text's letter; tasks-M4 L.D1.8 item 1 is amended at application. **RULED by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, verbatim: "i would build the playoff bracket immediately and then rebuild it after the final stat correction is made."** — a PROVISIONAL bracket the moment the playoff week opens, built from standings that INCLUDE the just-played regular-season week (its games are over and scored; its rows are `correction_window`, not yet `final`), then a REBUILD from the final standings when that week's correction window closes (Thursday 06:00 ET — before any playoff kickoff). *Orchestrator's reading, offered for confirmation, not assumed:* (i) if a correction moves a seed the pairings change and the playoff `matchups` rows are rewritten; saved lineups survive (keyed by team-week, not opponent); (ii) each later round is provisional when the prior round's games end and final when its corrections close; (iii) this REQUIRES standings that count a not-yet-final week — the projected/provisional arm L.D5.3 deferred as F253(a) — which now rides L.D1.8 (a 117 replacement or a `p_include_correction_window` argument) rather than waiting. None of the Builder's three options was this; option (a) "seed at final" is the rebuild half of it. **Chris's elaboration, 2026-09-07, verbatim: "the way most platforms work is they have a tab called 'playoffs' with a bracket all season that shows what the bracket would be if the playoffs started today."** — so the bracket is a SEASON-LONG PROJECTED VIEW ("if the playoffs started today", from projected standings over every week incl. live/correction-window ones), not an event at the playoff week's open; (E)'s "build immediately" is the moment that projection becomes the real bracket, and the rebuild after corrections is its final form. *Orchestrator's reading:* the projected-standings arm (F253(a)) is therefore a season-long feature on L.D1.8's/117's critical path, and the bracket VIEW **is specced** — §16 lists `src/components/leagues/playoff-bracket.tsx` (spec:1792 — seeds, byes, reseed; commish edit affordances via `commish-action-modal`) hosted on the standings page (spec:1721 "Standings + playoff bracket") — but **no M4 task row builds it** (L.D5.3 built `standings-table`; L.D5.4 is heroes/FA/activity), and **§11.5:744 says the bracket is generated "when `playoff_start_week` arrives"** — the season-long "if the playoffs started today" projection is Chris's new direction and needs a spec fold at application (§11.5 + the §16.2 row's copy). So: (i) L.D1.8's engine exposes the projected bracket as a read (the same `league_standings`-with-projection arm feeds both), and (ii) a task row for `playoff-bracket.tsx` on the standings page — sequenced after L.D1.8; the loop will file it as a breakdown addition (the L.D1.5b/L.D1.5c precedent) rather than wait for a separate Architect pass. **Chris's correction, 2026-09-07, verbatim: "no, the bracket should be built at Midnight PST when players go on waivers. which should be the same for all other weeks, no?"** — so "immediately" = the WEEK'S ROLLOVER: the instant the last game ends and players go on waivers — **`nfl_weeks.last_game_ends_at` — TUESDAY ≈ 00:00 PT, i.e. midnight at the end of Monday night's game (Chris, 2026-09-07: "it should technically be Tuesday morning not Monday night") — the SAME instant Q34(B) ruled for the game-day lock's release.** Recorded as the EVENT (the last game finishing, per Q34(B)'s "after the last game has finished… usually midnight"), not a fixed clock — a Monday-night game that runs past midnight PT (overtime, a late doubleheader) must not unlock players mid-game; a hard Tuesday 00:00 PT clock is available if Chris prefers it, not assumed. **One ABSOLUTE instant per league, not a local-midnight-per-user** (Chris, 2026-09-07: "for central and eastern timezones it's already hours into Tuesday") — stored `timestamptz`, rendered in each viewer's zone by the UI ("Tue 2:00 AM CT" / "Tue 3:00 AM ET"); copy must never say "midnight" as if it were everyone's midnight (an L.D5.x/L.D6.2 pin: the rollover rendered through the viewer's timezone, never a literal) — NOT Wednesday's calendar `starts_at` (the previous reading, struck) and not Thursday's correction-window close. The bracket (the season-long projection AND the real one at playoff time) is (re)built at each week's `last_game_ends_at` from that week's provisional scores, then rebuilt at `correction_window_ends_at` if a correction moved a seed. "The same for all other weeks" — YES: every week's standings/bracket update at its rollover; every week's results go official Thursday 06:00 ET. *NOT read into it, filed for Chris only if he means it:* whether the app's "current week" (`league_weeks` flips on `nfl_weeks.starts_at`, Wednesday 00:00 ET — 110/116) should ALSO move to the Monday-night rollover — that touches the lock tick and week-advance jobs and gets its own question (number at filing — R861: `Q41` was later taken by the mid-playoff retirement question, L.D1.10) rather than a reading. **All five sub-questions are now RULED — B9 CLEARS at application.** *[L.D5.5, 2026-09-08 — the (E) UI pin LANDED (D326(6)): `playoff-bracket-ops.test.ts`'s timezone-render fixture renders ONE `timestamptz` (`2099-12-15T08:00Z`, midnight Pacific) as 12:00 AM in Los Angeles · 2:00 AM in Chicago · 3:00 AM in New York with the league zone on hover, and refuses the word "midnight" on every copy constant and rendered state; a NULL `rollover_at` renders the EVENT. Shown red through a fixed zone (5 of 49), reverted.]*

**Riders the Builder will PIN AS MECHANICS unless Chris objects (not questions — stated so one ruling can confirm them):** (i) **bye arithmetic per size** — bracket `B = 2^rounds` (110's `schedule_playoff_rounds` / `derivePlayoffRounds`); byes = `B − playoff_teams`, to seeds `1..byes`; round 1 pairs the rest outside-in: 2 → 1v2 · 4 → 1v4, 2v3 · 6 → 1–2 bye, 3v6, 4v5 · 8 → 1v8, 2v7, 3v6, 4v5 · 10 → 1–6 bye, 7v10, 8v9 · 12 → 1–4 bye, 5v12, 6v11, 7v10, 8v9 — each a stored-literal golden. (ii) **`playoff_reseed = false`** = a fixed bracket (round-2 slots pre-assigned by position — 6 teams: the 3v6 winner meets seed 2, the 4v5 winner meets seed 1); `true` = survivors re-ranked by seed, best v worst each round; the on/off divergence pinned on the 6-team fixture where the two conventions place the 4v5 winner differently. (iii) **seeds FROZEN at generation** — `matchups.home_seed` / `away_seed` SMALLINT (109 has no seed column; §16's `playoff-bracket.tsx` "seeds, byes, reseed" and §10's "edit playoff seeds/bracket" need a stored seed; a later regular-season reopen never reseeds a written round) — a D-row, not a rule. (iv) **the champion** — `leagues.champion_team_id UUID REFERENCES teams(id)` (§12.1 has no column; "Champion recorded on `complete`", §11.5), written in the `complete` transaction — a D-row. (v) **a retired team is never seeded** (117's `seated` CTE already excludes it; L.D1.10's lineage seam untouched — D314(6) / R806). (vi) **status flips forward only** — the job flips `in_season → playoffs → complete` and never claims a `complete` league; `playoffs → in_season` is §7.1's audited commissioner override (M6), not a job path — pinned by the claim WHERE + one cell. (vii) **the home side** of a bracket game is the higher seed (a convention the UI reads; §11.7's home/away alternation is the regular season's).

Fold-back homes: §11.5's Playoffs bullet (A/B/D/E), §11.7's scoring-format paragraph (C), §7.3.1's `playoff_weeks_per_round` note (B). Answerable from this file alone.

**Q40 — WHAT DOES THE "LOCK COUNTDOWN" COUNT DOWN TO UNDER THE ONE PER-PLAYER LINEUP LOCK? OPEN, filed 2026-09-05 by the L.D5.1 Builder. Ledger F251. BLOCKS NOTHING** — the team page ships with the R779-mandated record ("Locks from <the earliest starter kickoff on record>") and a named placeholder where the countdown goes (`data-lock-countdown="placeholder-q40"`); the surface is honest and the number is one function away. **The gap:** §16.5.1's `in_season` row prints the primary CTA as *"Set lineup (lock countdown)"*, tasks-M4 L.D5.1 says the team page "hosts it with the lock countdown", and §16.2's `lineup-editor` row lists "per-player 🔒 at kickoff" — but no sentence in the spec says what instant the countdown targets. Under `first_game_of_week` the referent was obvious (the whole lineup locked at one instant); Q34(A) retired that mode (v2.16.20), and under `per_player_kickoff` a lineup has as many lock instants as starters with games. `team_lineups.locked_at` is the RECORD of the EARLIEST starter kickoff (R779: "locks at", never the lock) — after the first kickoff it is in the past while other slots are still open, so counting down to it is wrong for most of a Sunday. Folding a definition into the spec would be R801's shape (a rule dressed as a build note), so it is a question. **[L.D5.4, 2026-09-08 — the league-home Set-lineup CTA (§16.5.1's "Set lineup (lock countdown)") shipped WITHOUT a countdown: it renders the same R779 record ("Locks from <the earliest starter kickoff>", the stored `locked_at` viewer-local) and links the team page, where the named placeholder stands. Building the CTA needed no referent the spec lacks, so no option was added and nothing was folded; the recommendation (a) stands, and its application is still one pure function over `starters[].kickoff_at` + one spec sentence, now at TWO sites (the team page's placeholder and the hero's record line).]**
- **(a) The next slot to lock** — count down to the earliest kickoff STILL AHEAD among the team's current starters (from the tick-refreshed `starters[].kickoff_at`, E42), relabelling as each passes ("Next lock: RB Open · Sun 1:00 PM"); "All starters locked" once none is ahead; no countdown for a bye-only lineup. **Recommendation** — it is the one number a manager acts on (which seat can I still change, and for how long).
- **(b) The first kickoff** — count down to `locked_at` (the earliest starter kickoff) and stop there ("Lineup began locking at …"). Simplest; matches the CTA's pre-Q34 reading; says nothing useful after the first game.
- **(c) The week's last kickoff** — count down to the latest starter kickoff (the moment the whole lineup is final). Least actionable.
Answerable from this file alone; each answer is one pure function over `starters[].kickoff_at` + a TimeProvider read in the component, and one spec sentence in §16.5.1/§16.2.

**Q35 — DOES `player_game_lock` SURVIVE AT ALL FOR THE ADD HALF, OR IS IT RETIRED ENTIRELY? RULED (a) — RETIRED ENTIRELY. Chris, 2026-09-05, in-session, verbatim: *"we don't need this toggle from what i can tell"* and, on the add half specifically: *"picking up a player mid-game makes no sense."* Filed OPEN by the L.D1.5b Builder from the Q34(B) ruling (below); ruled by Chris while that PR was in build and recorded on its branch by the orchestrator before review (the Q32/Q33 shape). Ledger F236. **APPLIED 2026-09-05 by L.D1.5c — migration 115 + pgTAP 063, spec v2.16.21 (D312; F236 ✅).** Consumed by L.D1.5c: both halves unconditional, the setting leaves the schema/Zod/panel (the `settings-panel.tsx:958-960` row goes, not only its hint), `p_enforced` goes with it.** *(The Builder's recommendation below was (b); Chris ruled (a) — the OFF position, like `first_game_of_week`, never described anything a real league does.)* Q34(B) makes the DROP lock unconditional — "once a player has kicked off … they are locked" — so `player_game_lock`'s §7.3.4 row (*"a rostered player locks for drops at their kickoff, until the week clears … off reproduces lax incumbent behavior"*) loses its drop half. The setting's §7.3.4 text governs BOTH halves (§13.1: *"with `player_game_lock` on, a player cannot be added or dropped from their kickoff until the week's correction window closes"*), so the add half needs its own answer.
- **(a) RETIRE the setting entirely** — adds lock at the player's kickoff unconditionally too (no in-game stat-sniping pickups for anyone); `p_enforced` goes, the `settings-panel.tsx:958-960` toggle goes, 061's lax-add controls (§H1's add half, §H4) are re-cut. - **(b) KEEP the setting for the ADD half only** — the toggle governs whether a kicked-off free agent may be picked up mid-game (the incumbent-lax add); the drop half is unconditional per Q34(B). `p_enforced` stays for the add caller only; the panel hint ("Unowned players lock for adds when their game starts") becomes exactly true. Smallest behaviour change beyond Q34(B) itself.
- **Recommendation: (b)** — it applies Q34(B) as given without extending it, and the toggle's remaining meaning is one a commissioner can understand from the panel line. Either way L.D1.5c owns the application; the spec rows (§7.3.4 `player_game_lock`, §13.1's game-day-locks paragraph, E32) fold with it.

**Q38 — POINTS AGAINST WAS DEFINED BY THE BUILDER WHERE THE SPEC WAS SILENT (v2.16.23, migration 117) — THREE SUB-QUESTIONS, ONE FOLD STANDING PROVISIONALLY. - **(B) In a `total_points` league PA is identically 0 (measured on the production shape: every team `PA 0`), so E64's "falls to Points Against" hop is VACUOUS and the effective chain is PF → coin flip.** Is that intended, or should E64 read "falls to the coin flip"? **Recommendation: erratum E64 to say so** — a printed tiebreaker that can never break a tie is a trap for the next reader.

**Q37 — A GAME THAT IS CANCELLED (never `final`, never moved to a later week) HOLDS EVERY LEAGUE WEEK FOREVER — AND FOR NFL WEEK 18 NOTHING CAN EVER RELEASE IT. OPEN, filed 2026-09-05 by the orchestrator from the #258 final re-review (R797). Ledger F243. BLOCKS NOTHING in M4** — the code posture is §23.2's (never advance on partial data) and it is named hourly, not silent; the escape today is an operator edit of `nfl_games` (M6's override reopens WEEKS, not games). The gap is vocabulary: the spec has no `cancelled` game state (its only `cancelled` is on claims/trades), `nfl_games.status` is an unconstrained `TEXT DEFAULT 'scheduled'` (001:92), and E43 defines "out of the week" only as a kickoff moving past a later `nfl_weeks.starts_at` — which week 18 has no row after. Demonstrated rolled-back by the reviewer: week 18 with one `final` + one `postponed` game reads `open 1, all_final false` whether the kickoff is in-week or moved to March. A league CAN reach NFL week 18 (`playoff_start_week` ≤ 16 + three rounds).
- **(a) E43-with-zero:** ingestion writes `status = 'cancelled'`; the gate treats a cancelled game as "left the week" and finalizes without it, its players scoring 0 (their locks release, E43's lock half). The NFL's own 2022 Bills–Bengals precedent (the game was cancelled, not made up, and every platform scored it as a no-play). **Recommendation.**
- **(b) Commissioner act only:** no new state; a cancelled game stays `open` and the commissioner reopens/force-finalizes the week through M6's audited override. Honest but manual for every league in the app on the same night.
- **(c) Both:** (a) as the automatic rule, (b) as the escape when ingestion is late. Cheapest to build on top of (a).
The owner is L.D2.1's ingestion for the status vocabulary + a one-line E43 erratum; the code in 116 needs one more arm. Answerable from this file alone.

**Q34(A) — RULED (a), ERRATUM.** *`lineup_lock = first_game_of_week` is retired; `per_player_kickoff` becomes the only lineup lock. What a dropped player becomes (waivers vs FA) stays the existing `free_agency` / `fa_hold_hours` machinery. **Task filed, NOT built in this PR: L.D1.5c** (§2; tasks-M4 §6 — sequenced before L.D1.6). **APPLIED 2026-09-05 — L.D1.5c, migration 115 + pgTAP 063, spec v2.16.21 (D312): both gates unconditional, the release `nfl_weeks.last_game_ends_at`, NULL = locked without a raise — the orchestrator's reading above was verified against 039 / 113 / `ingest-week.ts:288` and built as read; its one stated consequence (a past week whose stamp is never written keeps binding) is F238.** ~~**Open sub-question: Q35** (above) — whether `player_game_lock` survives for the ADD half.~~ **[Q35 RULED (a) 2026-09-05 — the setting retires entirely, applied by L.D1.5c — recorded at `5b6b55f`, R780 struck the leftovers.]**

**Q34 — THE `first_game_of_week` LOCK MODE DOES NOT FIT THE PLAYER-LEVEL MODEL CHRIS RULED IN Q32, AND THE SAME RULING'S "OFF" CASE GIVES A MANAGER A DO-OVER ON A PLAYED SLOT — TWO PRODUCT CALLS, ONE ROW. ~~OPEN~~ RULED above (2026-09-05: (A)(a) applied by L.D1.5b; (B) → L.D1.5c + Q35), filed 2026-09-03 by the L.D1.5 fix-round Builder on PR #254 (`feat/M4-L.D1.5-pool-add-drop`) from the re-reviewer's R762 (the missing F-row) and R759 (the missing consequence). BLOCKS NOTHING TODAY** — 113 ships the settings' letter unchanged and both behaviours are pinned; the ledger row is **F230**, discharged by Chris or by an Architect docs task **before L.D1.6 renders the mode**.

**(A) `first_game_of_week` — erratum or Q30-shape cut?** Q32's amendment is verbatim: *"there really isn't a such thing as a 'lineup locking' players lock and once a player has locked because their game has started they can't be moved."* §7.3.6's `first_game_of_week` says the opposite — the WHOLE lineup freezes at the week's first kickoff, so a Monday-night bench player cannot be moved on Sunday morning, which is exactly the case the ruling's own example says must work. 112 ships the mode (060 pins it), 113 does not read it for droppability, and 061 §H1 carries its one composition cell. **Nothing was cut or altered in this PR** — the mode is untouched pending this answer.
- **(a) ERRATUM — retire the mode, `per_player_kickoff` becomes the only `lineup_lock`.** Matches the ruling exactly. Cost: a settings-column migration + the §7.3.6/§11.2 rewrite + 060/061's mode-specific cells re-cut; any league already created with it is migrated (none exist — the cohort has no league on it). **The reviewer's and this Builder's recommendation** if Chris confirms the amendment is meant to be the whole model.
- **(b) Q30-SHAPE CUT — keep the column, pin the select to one option.** The divisions precedent (Q30(d)): the mode stays in the catalog, the UI shows one choice, §7.3.6 is marked inert for v1, and 112's code path survives untouched for a later revisit. Cheapest, reversible, and it needs no migration.
- **(c) KEEP BOTH MODES and treat Q32's amendment as scoped to `per_player_kickoff`.** Honest only if Chris actually wants a whole-week freeze available; it leaves the spec self-contradictory for anyone reading §7.3.6 beside §13.1.

**(B) Should the player-level drop lock bind REGARDLESS of `player_game_lock`?** With the toggle OFF (a commissioner setting, `settings-panel.tsx:961`) and the DEFAULT `per_player_kickoff`, the shipped verb does this — measured, pinned in 061 §H3: a manager drops a starter whose game has already been PLAYED, the slot clears, and the very next `set_lineup` re-seats it with a player who has not kicked off. So the team loses the played player's points *and* chooses again for that slot after seeing his result. §7.3.4 calls this config "lax incumbent behavior" — but incumbents keep the played player's points in the locked slot (that is E34); here the points are lost and the slot is re-opened, which no incumbent does.
- **(a) MAKE THE DROP LOCK UNCONDITIONAL** — one clause in 113 (`IF v_game_lock AND (v_drop_lock ->> 'locked')` → drop the `v_game_lock AND`), plus the §7.3.4 row's "off" sentence and one 061 pair. `player_game_lock` then governs ADDS only. Never-weaken direction; kills the do-over. **This Builder's recommendation** — the amendment ("once a player has locked … they can't be moved") reads as a statement about players, not about a setting.
- **(b) LEAVE IT AS THE SETTING'S LETTER (what ships today)** — "off reproduces lax incumbent behavior" is §7.3.4's own sentence, the default is ON, and the cohort's leagues use the default. Now disclosed in spec §13.1 (v2.16.19) and pinned, so nobody is surprised by it.
- **(c) MAKE THE OFF CASE MATCH E34 INSTEAD** — keep the drop legal but freeze the emptied slot for the week (a 112 reservation). Restores the incumbent shape, but it re-introduces exactly the phantom-slot machinery Q32 removed, so it is the most expensive of the three and the reviewer's R753 argument applies to it again.

**Recommendation: (A)(a) or (A)(b) — whichever matches Chris's intent, both are cheap — and (B)(a).** Nothing is built on this answer until it exists; the fix round took R759's fixable half (the missing 061 cell + the record correction) and left the clause alone, per the standing rule that a product semantic is never Builder-decided.

**Q32 — RULED (Chris, 2026-09-03, in-session via the orchestrator — the C34/C41 precedent). Verbatim: *"a user can drop a player as long as that player hasn't locked. for example, if its mid day sunday and all the users starters are locked due to games starting but they have a player on their Bench that doesn't play until Monday night, that player can be dropped."* AMENDMENT, verbatim: *"there really isn't a such thing as a 'lineup locking' players lock and once a player has locked because their game has started they can't be moved. so if they are on the bench they are stuck on the bench, if they are in the lineup they are stuck in the lineup."*** **Applied on PR #254 (the Q10-application shape): the lock model is PLAYER-LEVEL — a player locks at his own kickoff (until the week clears, E32's window) and then cannot move in ANY direction (not bench→lineup, not lineup→bench, not into another slot, not dropped); a player whose game has not started moves and drops freely regardless of what else is locked. For 113: a drop is refused iff the player's OWN game has kicked off (E32, both settings' letter); the `kept_in_locked_lineup` phantom branch is REMOVED (a droppable player has not played — nothing to keep); a dropped player's `slot_map` entry is ALWAYS cleared; E34 stays M5's `bench_lock`-off claim-processing path. For 112's merged `set_lineup`: `per_player_kickoff` already IS the player-level model (a locked slot's player never moves — 060 E5; a kicked-off BENCH player cannot enter a slot — 060 E4, re-pinned in 061 F6 as the composition after a drop), so NO 112 change was needed. The `first_game_of_week` mode (§7.3.6) does not fit the model — NOT cut or altered here (112's semantics untouched, no new mode-specific pins beyond those already passing); its fate is pending Chris — **now a filed question, Q34, with its own ledger row F230** (R762: a hand-off with a named actor and no F-row is itself a finding, §6's rule). Residual RECORDED, not asked (D309(3), the D220 shape), **and corrected 2026-09-03 (R759)**: with `player_game_lock = OFF` §7.3.4/§13.1's letter is lax incumbent behaviour — a played player may be dropped and his slot clears, **and the slot then stays empty only under `first_game_of_week` (061 §H1). Under `per_player_kickoff` (the DEFAULT) the next `set_lineup` RE-SEATS the emptied slot with a player whose own kickoff is ahead — 061 §H3 pins the refuse-then-accept pair on a new lax × per_player_kickoff league.** The ruling was given for the on-by-default case; whether the lock should bind drops regardless of the toggle is **Q34/F230**, Chris's call. Pins: 061 F6 (the ruling's own example — Sunday midday, every starter kicked off, the bench player with a Monday game drops, refuses once his game kicks off, a kicked-off starter refuses by name; the per-player composition — an emptied slot whose own kickoff is ahead re-seats, a kicked-off bench player cannot enter it; NO PHANTOM — no `slot_map` value names an unrostered player), F1/F2/H1 (the slot always cleared). **Q32 — DOES THE LINEUP LOCK (§11.2) BLOCK DROPPING A PLAYER WHO SITS IN A LOCKED SLOT OF THE CURRENT WEEK? — ~~OPEN~~ RULED above, filed 2026-09-02 by the L.D1.5 Builder on PR #254 (`feat/M4-L.D1.5-pool-add-drop`) from the reviewer's BLOCKER R753. ~~BLOCKS L.D1.5's merge and, through it, the M4 schema lane (L.D1.6 → L.D1.10) — blocker B8.~~**

**The premise, quoted so it can be checked.** §7.3.4 `player_game_lock`: *"a rostered player locks for drops at their kickoff, until the week clears … off reproduces lax incumbent behavior."* §13.1: *"with `player_game_lock` on, a player cannot be added or dropped from their kickoff until the week's correction window closes … Both settings off reproduce incumbent-lax behavior."* §11.2: *"Locked slots are read-only to managers."* E34: *"Player dropped mid-week after starting (bench_lock off, incumbent-lax config) → The locked starter's stats still count for the dropping team's matchup that week; the player enters waivers; edge documented in UI copy."* §7.3.4 `bench_lock`: *"A waiver claim whose drop player has already played this week fails at processing."* tasks-M4 §4 rule 9: *"Dropping a player who is a locked STARTER (§11.2) — decide from the spec text whether the lineup lock also blocks the drop, cite it, pin it; if the spec is silent, STOP and file."*

**What 113 built (D309(3)) and what the reviewer measured (R753).** The Builder read E34 as the general consequence of dropping a locked starter and built: the lineup lock does NOT block a drop — only E32 does — and a dropped player whose slot is LOCKED at the instant is KEPT in `team_lineups.slot_map` (`kept_in_locked_lineup`) so his stats count for the dropping team. The reviewer measured a §11.2 bypass BY COMPOSITION: under `lineup_lock = per_player_kickoff` + `player_game_lock = false`, a manager drops a locked starter (kept), and the very next `set_lineup` re-seats that locked slot with an unstarted bench player, because 112 skips a stored player who is no longer rostered (112:894 *"dropped since (113) — nothing to lock"*) — evidence: `set_lineup` moving QB2 into qb:0 while QB1 rostered → refused "slot qb:0 is locked"; drop QB1 → `kept_in_locked_lineup: true`; `set_lineup` re-seating qb:0 with QB2 → ACCEPTED. That destroys the very E34 guarantee the keep exists for (the stored starters no longer carry him; F227(b)'s fan-out would score the replacement). And E34's own scenario names **`bench_lock` off** — a WAIVER-CLAIM processing setting (M5's path) — not the manager's direct drop, so the text the reading leaned on is narrower than the reading. The spec is therefore SILENT on the direct-drop × lineup-lock interplay — rule 9's STOP condition, applied late.

**Options.**
- **(i) The lineup lock blocks the drop** — `roster_add_drop` refuses dropping a player who sits in a LOCKED slot of the current week (per_player_kickoff: his stored slot's kickoff has passed; first_game_of_week: the week's first kickoff has passed), naming the slot and the instant; E34 stays exactly what its trigger says — M5's `bench_lock`-off claim-processing path — and the `kept_in_locked_lineup` branch is removed. Never-weaken direction (refuse more); no phantom, no double-count edge in M4; one refusal + its one-unit twin in 061; no 112 change. **The reviewer's recommendation and this Builder's.**
- **(ii) 112 treats a kept phantom's slot as read-only** — the keep stays; `set_lineup` reserves a locked slot whose stored occupant is no longer rostered (a submit may omit the key, the canonical map re-inserts it, the fit reserves the slot); a 060 phantom cell + a 061 composition cell; F227(b)'s fan-out duty stands. Preserves the lax-league "his stats still count" reading at the cost of a phantom that every later surface (L.D2.2 scoring, L.D5.1 editor, L.D1.6 auto-carry) must understand.
- **(iii) Lineup lock blocks the drop only when `player_game_lock` is ON** — rejected by both parties: under lax + per_player the same bypass remains, and it invents a coupling neither table prints.

**Recommendation: (i).** It matches §11.2's letter ("locked slots are read-only"), keeps E34 in the scope its trigger names, and removes the composition hole without touching 112. If Chris prefers (ii), the resume builds the 112 reservation and both cells. Either way: a 061 composition cell, a 060 phantom (or refusal) cell, and the rewording of spec §13.1 (v2.16.17's "lineup interplay" sentence — marked PENDING now), D309(3), F224(i), F227(b).

**Q33 — `free_agency = continuous`: IS A LAPSED `waivers_until` FCFS-ADDABLE, OR CLAIM-ONLY FOR A PROCESSOR THAT DOES NOT EXIST UNTIL M5? — ~~OPEN~~ RULED above, filed 2026-09-02 by the L.D1.5 Builder on PR #254 from the reviewer's should-fix R756. ~~Held with Q32 under blocker B8.~~**

**The premise, quoted.** §7.3.4 row: *"`free_agency` | `immediate_after_waivers` | immediate / continuous | Unclaimed players become FCFS."* — the row's ONLY note. §13.1: *"Managers add an unowned player (FCFS after waivers clear)."* D294: *"a lapsed `waivers_until` is FCFS-addable per `free_agency` — state evaluated at read, no sweeper needed in M4."* tasks-M4 §1: waivers/FAAB claim PROCESSING is M5's.

**What 113 built (D309(4)) and why the reviewer objects (R756).** The Builder read `continuous` in its incumbent (Yahoo) sense — unclaimed players stay on waivers for the processor to clear — and built: under `continuous` a LAPSED `on_waivers` player is NOT FCFS-addable (refused by name naming M5), while a player with no pool row stays addable under both values (pinned, 061 §H2). The reviewer's objection: that is a Builder-decided PRODUCT semantic written into the spec — §7.3.4's only note says unclaimed players become FCFS, and no claim processor exists until M5, so in a `continuous` league every dropped player is unaddable by everyone for the rest of M4 (a stranding, not a lock). The STOP rule was not applied.

**Options.**
- **(a) FCFS at the lapse under BOTH values until M5 lands claim processing** — `continuous` behaves as `immediate_after_waivers` in M4 (the row's own note, literally), the `continuous` refusal is removed, and M5's processor — which owns the "stay on waivers" semantic if Chris wants it — reintroduces the distinction with its claims. The never-strand direction. **The reviewer's recommendation and this Builder's.**
- **(b) Keep the reading with a DATED M5 flag** — `continuous` leagues strand lapsed players until M5; recorded in F227(a) with the date; the cohort's default (`immediate_after_waivers`) is unaffected.
- **(c) Cut `continuous` from v1** — pin the select to one option (the Q30 shape) until M5 defines it.

Fold-back: the §7.3.4 note gains "(M4: FCFS at the lapse under both values; M5 defines `continuous`)" and v2.16.17's `free_agency` sentence (marked PENDING now) is rewritten; D309(4) and F227(a) follow.
