and on the **proof**, because its outer `NOT EXISTS` makes any idempotence guard unreachable. **A separate worker** loses on contention and duplication: it would write `team_lineups` rows the tick is also updating (`119:876-886`) on an independent schedule, would have to take the same `leagues FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, and so serializes behind the tick anyway while duplicating the batching, `v_seen`, failure-containment and injected-instant scaffold — a fourth cron row for coordination you already had. **`commish_edit_lineup`'s own path** loses on the standing rule itself: it requires a commissioner to act, which is precisely what autopilot exists to spare him (twelve lineups a week by hand), and it would write a commissioner receipt for something no commissioner did. **What falls out is SIMPLER than the superseded design:** the carry keeps doing "last valid" at week open, unchanged; autopilot does "fill and substitute" every minute thereafter. **`lineup_carry_internal`, `league_week_advance` and `118:1825` are all UNTOUCHED** — three `CREATE OR REPLACE`s and three superseded-head citation traps deleted in one move. ***NUMBER WARNING, and it must be discharged at merge:*** **F326's row in PROGRESS §6 (`PROGRESS-leagues.md:2847` at the time of writing — **that file is live; find the row by `grep -n "Consistent with" docs/specs/PROGRESS-leagues.md`, never by line**) ALREADY REFERENCES A `D337`** — *"Consistent with **D337**'s no-fold decision for `schedule_actions`/`lineup_actions`"* — and no D337 exists in PROGRESS §4 today (head D334). It is a dangling forward reference, and the moment this PR transcribes the band it silently starts pointing at the autopilot hook, which says nothing about folding ledgers. **F342's merge-time actor fixes F326's sentence in the same pass** (name the decision it meant, or footnote it as unresolved); this bullet is not it.
- **D338 — AUTOPILOT IS A SYSTEM ACT: IT WRITES NO `commissioner_actions` ROW, AND IT DOES NOT INHERIT THE COMMISSIONER'S LOCK EXEMPTION.** It **cannot** write one as built: `actor_id` is `UUID REFERENCES profiles(id) NOT NULL` (`123:278`) and every writer in the verb uses `auth.uid()` (`123:1145`, `:1185`, `:1266`), which is NULL for pg_cron. Inventing a synthetic actor to satisfy the audit table weakens the column that makes the audit meaningful, and `spec:733` already calls the analogous act *"logged as a system — not commissioner — action"*. **And it must respect the per-player kickoff lock exactly as a manager does** — standing rule (g) exempts `commish_edit_lineup` because a *human* takes responsibility with a reason and a receipt; autopilot has neither. Every candidate whose `kickoff_at <= p_at` (the predicate `114:455-456`, refusal `:457-461`; and `114:469-470`, refusal `:471-475`) is excluded and **named** in `skipped_locked`, never silently dropped. **Chris's one condition still applies to the tick's REPORT even with no audit row:** a pass that fills nothing says WHY — *no unmanaged seats* / *nothing fillable* / *every candidate locked* — never a quiet zero.
- **D339 — AUTOPILOT'S "NO MANAGER" PREDICATE READS `league_members`, NEVER `teams.status`, AND A TEAM WITH NO MEMBER ROW IS REPORTED, NEVER AUTOPILOTED.** The predicate is the exact complement of `set_lineup_internal`'s auth (`114:240-243`, under the comment that states the doctrine at `114:237`: *"AUTH, in-body (F35: league_members' cache column, never a stint)"*): `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.league_members m WHERE m.team_id = t.id AND m.user_id IS NOT NULL)`. It covers **both** unmanaged shapes with no `OR`, because they converge in that table — `add_placeholder_seat` mints `(user_id NULL, is_placeholder TRUE, team_id SET)` on a `teams` row that takes the DEFAULT status `'active'` and gets **no stint** (`063:455-464`; `team_managers.user_id` is NOT NULL by design, `053:82`), while `remove_manager`'s vacate arm sets `user_id = NULL, is_placeholder = TRUE` keeping `team_id` and only THEN sets `teams.status = 'orphaned'` (`120:645-650`, `:656-659`). **A predicate keyed on `teams.status = 'orphaned'` misses all eleven of Chris's seats.** It must also not key on `is_placeholder`, which is `BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE` with no NOT NULL (`052:69`; `052:66` is `user_id`) and so can be NULL. **The failure direction is unsafe and must be ASSERTED, not inferred:** `NOT EXISTS` is also TRUE for "this team has no `league_members` row at all", and in that case autopilot would seize a human's team. The invariant that makes it safe is stated in code, not schema (*"ONE league_members row per seat, always (§12.2)"*, `120:558`; `120:561-564` is the D301 FAAB note) while `league_members.team_id` is `ON DELETE SET NULL` (`052:67`). This is CLAUDE.md's "never let 'nothing happened' mean 'it worked'" in its exact shape — a zero-row read meaning two different things — so a team with no member row is a **named, reported state**.
- **D354 — AN UNMANAGED SEAT WITH NO LINEUP ROW IS MATERIALIZED, NEVER SKIPPED; AND ARM (c) DOES NOT RIDE (b)'s LOOP.** D337's hook is right and the (b) loop really does re-visit Chris's twelve `slot_map = '{}'` rows every minute (`119:840-849` — `'{}'` IS NOT NULL). But (b) reads **FROM `team_lineups`** (`119:839-850`), so it can only ever see a seat that ALREADY HAS a row, and `add_placeholder_seat` mints a seat with **no** `team_lineups` row until the next week opens (`063:455-465`). The carry that would have written one is one-shot and already spent for this week (`118:1794`, `:1816-1824`). Such a seat would be invisible to an UPDATE-only arm, produce no line in `autopiloted[]`, `autopilot_unfillable[]` or `autopilot_reason`, and leave exit criterion 4 false while every cell passed — **"nothing happened" read as "it worked", in the one task written to abolish it.** So: **arm (c) gets its OWN driving query** over `teams` LEFT JOIN `team_lineups` (the shape is in §5), **(b)'s SELECT list is not touched at all** (one fewer hunk in a `CREATE OR REPLACE`), and a matching seat with `tl.id IS NULL` is **materialized by calling `lineup_carry_internal` unchanged** (`116:369`) and then filled, reported in `seats_materialized[]`. **The rejected alternative is "report `no_lineup_row` and move on":** it is honest but it leaves the seat empty for the whole week, which is the zero the slice exists to remove. A MANAGED seat with no row is still only reported — autopilot never materializes for a human.
- **D355 — 064/067's NEW `league_members` COVERAGE SEATS EVERY TEAM NEITHER SUITE DEPENDS ON BEING UNMANAGED, AND LEAVES THE REST ALONE (L.E1.3).** 064 gained 18 rows (L1's 10 teams + L2's 8, reusing the same 10 widened `auth.users` ids — `96…0001`–`96…0010` — across the two leagues since `league_members`' uniqueness is per-`(league_id, user_id)`); 067 gained 7 (L1's T2–T8, widening its `unnest(array[1, 99])` to include 2–8). **Seat 1 of each of 064's two `in_season` leagues is the `commissioner`** (`case when i = 1 …`), matching both leagues' `owner_id` `96…0001` and 067's existing shape: `create_league` ALWAYS seats its creator `commissioner` (`118:2418`) and `063:327`'s partial unique `one_commissioner_per_league` caps it at one PER LEAGUE, so a fixture with 18 managers and zero commissioners is a state §7.2 forbids and no sanctioned path can produce — and it would make `is_league_commish` (`052:96`) FALSE for every user in the file, so every later commissioner-refusal cell would pass because NOBODY is commissioner (R989, §4 rule 14's exact species). **EACH SUITE CARRIES ONE PREMISE CELL, because a seating with no assertion is unfalsifiable** (R987, reversing this decision's first cut): `064` **B1** and `067` **C1**, each one stored-literal golden string over `teams` LEFT JOIN `league_members` — D339's `NOT EXISTS` predicate read from the other side, which additionally pins §12.2's ONE-row-per-seat invariant (`120:558`) that D339 says must be asserted and never inferred. `plan(140)→141`, `plan(148)→149`; the task's "byte-identical" requirement is over the tick REPORTS, not the plan count. **The proof is the 14 tick-report JSONs plus every pre-existing `ok` line, NOT the NOTICE/WARNING text** (R991): 064 emits 23 such lines and 067 emits **zero**, so for 067 a NOTICE diff compares two empty sets and cannot fail — "nothing happened" read as "it worked", in the ledger row of the task written to abolish it. **L3 in 064 and L2–L4 in 067 are untouched on purpose** — no cell in either suite reads `league_members` or depends on any of those leagues' teams being managed (064's L3 is 'scheduled' and C2j/C2k already assert it is untouched by every worker in the file), so seating them would assert nothing and is scope the task never asked for (tasks-M6A §4 rule 14(d) names only 064's full suite and "067 seats 8 teams in league b7…0001").
- **D356 — AUTOPILOT'S BUILD MECHANICS: A PURE CHOOSER + A WRITING ARM, TWO FIT PASSES, AND A PRECISELY-WORDED SILENCE (L.E1.4, migration 125 / pgTAP 073).** Six decisions a Builder had to make that D337-D340/D354 leave open, recorded so the next schema task inherits them rather than re-deriving them. **(1) THE SPLIT.** `lineup_autopilot_internal` READS and RETURNS; it never writes. The `team_lineups` UPDATE and its loud `ROW_COUNT <> 1` live in `lineup_lock_tick` arm (c), which is where §5 puts them — so there is exactly ONE writer, the `119:882-886` pattern is reused verbatim, and pgTAP can call the chooser directly for the posture cells. The chooser RAISES `P0002` when the row is absent: D354 puts materialization in the caller, under the league lock, through the unchanged carry, and an invented lineup would be the silent second row 116's banner refuses. **(2) TWO FIT PASSES, which is what makes Q63 EXACT.** One pass cannot express *"substitute only when a healthy replacement actually takes the key"*: the matcher's augmenting path will not evict an unhealthy incumbent (it re-routes him instead, and if he has nowhere to go the healthy candidate goes unplaced — the OPPOSITE of a substitution). So pass 1 offers every empty slot AND every vacated unhealthy-unlocked slot to the HEALTHY candidates only; a vacated man whose key nobody took is then RESTORED `fixed` at that key; pass 2 re-seeds pass 1's whole assignment `fixed` (`112:501-505` seeds a fixed player unconditionally, so pass 1 is reproduced exactly) and offers what is left to the unhealthy tail. Consequence, stated because it is a product-visible line: **an occupied slot is never turned into an empty one**, under either value of `allow_illegal_lineups` — item 4c's hard filter governs SEATING SOMEONE NEW, and leaving an incumbent where he already sits is the status quo, which is also the shape of `114:605-610`'s own exemption. **(3) THE NO-OP IS `slot_map` EQUALITY**, `set_lineup`'s own test (`114:633`); `starters`/`bench`/`locked_at` are projections of it and arm (b) owns the kickoff refresh of an unchanged row — which is what makes the idempotence cell honest rather than accidental. **(4) THE SHORT-CIRCUIT LIVES IN THE CHOOSER**, immediately before the first fit call, because it is the one place holding both halves of the predicate (no empty slot AND no unhealthy unlocked starter); half-duplicating it in the tick, where designations and kickoffs are not in scope, is how the two halves drift apart. **(5) FOUR COLUMNS, NOT FIVE.** `set_at` and `edited_by_commish` are deliberately NOT written: item 3 enumerates four, autopilot is a SYSTEM act (D338), and `edited_by_commish` is a user-visible badge (`team-page.tsx`) whose meaning D346 is already widening for a different reason. **(6) `no_unmanaged_seats_in_a_live_current_week`, in those words.** Arm (c)'s driving query is bounded to `lw.status = 'live'`, so "the arm saw nothing" also covers an unmanaged seat whose current week has closed into `correction_window`. A bare `no_unmanaged_seats` there is precisely the plausible-looking silence §4 rule 15 forbids, so the string says what was actually measured. Pinned by pgTAP 073 §I with a positive control at the SAME instant (ordered control-first, because the `league_weeks` transition guard permits only `upcoming → live → correction_window → final`, §12.17/F4). **(7) ADDED BY THE FIX ROUND (PR #295, R998–R1002 — amended in place, the D355 precedent: D356 does not exist on `main`, so there is no landed history to rewrite). (7a) THE KILL SWITCH'S TABLE IS HARDENED IN THE MIGRATION THAT MAKES IT A SAFETY CONTROL.** `REVOKE TRUNCATE ON TABLE system_flags FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated` is migration 125 section 0 — a grant narrowing, not DDL — because RLS does not cover TRUNCATE and the Supabase default granted it to `anon`/`authenticated` (D350's own lesson, `123:410`/`:491`), so the banner's *"a `service_role` write and nothing else"* was false as measured until this PR. No BEFORE TRUNCATE trigger: that belongs to `commissioner_actions`, where §12.12 makes immutability a LAW claim; this is operational state whose owner must stay able to truncate it in a recovery (`123:484-491`'s shape). The assertion is PER ROLE with `has_table_privilege` (073 §F1e/§F1f) — a `pg_policies` cell structurally cannot see a TRUNCATE grant, which is how the hole survived 070. Origin recorded as **F348** (122 omitted it), app-wide sweep as **F349** (64 of 67 `public` tables still grant it, 65 before this PR). **(7b) `autopilot_reason`'s ARMS ARE ORDERED AND EACH NAMES SOMETHING MEASURED.** The D339 decline gets its own value, `every_unmanaged_looking_seat_declined_no_league_members_row`; `no_row_and_no_materialize` is restricted to a seat that REACHED the materialize step and still had no row, detected by re-reading `team_lineups` after the carry returns, and its arm sits AHEAD of the `v_ap_seats = 0` arms because such a seat is `CONTINUE`d before `v_ap_seats` is incremented. Before this, the same pass that correctly REFUSED to seize a team reported either a materialization failure that never happened or *"nothing_fillable"* about seats it never evaluated — §4 rule 15's own shape in the field built to abolish it. Every emittable value now has a cell (073 §J/§K/§L), and the one that is unreachable while the carry's INSERT-or-RAISE contract holds is proven by FAULT INJECTION inside the test transaction rather than asserted as a guard that cannot fire (§4 rule 14(b)). **(7c) A DEFECT THE NEW CELL CAUGHT, AND IT WAS IN (2).** `lineup_designation_internal` returns NULL for a healthy player, `NULL IN (…)` is NULL, and the classification loop's `IF v_locked OR NOT v_unhealthy` therefore fell to its ELSE for EVERY healthy seated starter: a manager-set or carried placement was displaced and re-contested on value (a D340 violation), and because such a man also re-entered the candidate pool, the restore clause could seat him at his old key while pass 1 had placed him elsewhere — **one player written into two slots**. Both classification sites now wrap the `IN` in `COALESCE(…, FALSE)`. It was invisible to every original cell because **no fixture ran the pass over a map containing a healthy seated starter**; §J is that fixture. The general lesson for the rest of M6A: in this codebase a designation read is three-valued, so any boolean built from one and then NEGATED needs `COALESCE` — the `IF (x) IN (…) THEN` form used at `112:1051` / `114:596` / `116:520` / `123:979` is safe only because a NULL `IF` does not fire.
- **D357 — THE MATCHUP OVERRIDE'S BUILD MECHANICS: ONE INTERNAL UNDER TWO ROUTES, THE RECEIPT BEFORE THE WRITE, AND A BACKSTOP THAT BINDS THE OWNER (L.E1.5, migration 126 / pgTAP 074).** **(1) NUMBERS.** Migration head measured `125_lineup_autopilot.sql`, pgTAP head `073_lineup_autopilot.sql` (`ls … | tail -1`, D161/D166) ⇒ **126 / 074**, confirmed again at write time. **THE SPLIT SEAM WAS NOT TAKEN** — items 1–5 all fit one migration, so **131 / pgTAP 079 stay unspent** and §6's graph is unamended; **127 was never at risk**, it is L.E1.6's. **(2) ONE INTERNAL, TWO ROUTES, ONE REPLAY NAMESPACE.** `commish_matchup_override_internal(league, matchup, home, away, winner, action_id, at, reason, verb)` is PLAIN + `search_path=''` + triple-REVOKEd; `commish_edit_score` and `commish_set_result` are thin DEFINER wrappers passing `now()` and their own name. `p_verb` does three jobs — it names every refusal after the route the client actually called, it selects the `action_type` (`edit_score` / `set_result`, both already in §12.12's printed vocabulary, so **no new column**, D336), and it is itself validated so the internal cannot be driven from an unexpected caller. **The two routes SHARE `commish_matchup_actions`** (D350) because they are one verb family over one row: a retry carrying the same `action_id` must return the same document whichever route sent it, not two. **(3) THE ORDER OF THE RECEIPT AND THE WRITE IS §12.12'S, NOT 123'S, AND IT IS FORCED TWICE OVER.** D336 part (2) says the log call goes AFTER the state write. Here it cannot: the backstop refuses an `is_overridden` write with no GUC and **the GUC is a side effect of the logging helper** (`123:447`), so a verb that wrote first would be refused by its own guard; and `matchups.override_action_id` is an FK to the row the helper mints (`123:459-460`), which D341's single statement needs in hand. §12.12 prints exactly this order (`PERFORM set_config(...)` then the trigger sketch). **The load-bearing half of D336(2) is untouched:** both the log call and the write sit INSIDE `IF NOT v_no_changes THEN`, so Chris's one condition holds, and a failed UPDATE aborts the transaction and takes the audit row with it — a receipt can never outlive its change. **(4) `before`/`after` MIRROR FOUR VALUE DIMENSIONS AND `override_action_id` LIVES IN `metadata`** — because its *after* value IS the audit row's own `id`, which cannot exist before the call that consumes the document, and printing a row's primary key inside its own `after` is noise. `metadata.override_action_id_before` carries the id being replaced (NULL the first time) and 074 **E6** asserts `matchups.override_action_id = commissioner_actions.id` directly. `metadata.affected_team_ids[]` per D353, home-then-away, away omitted on a bye. **(5) THE NO-OP INCLUDES THE FLAG, AND IT MUST.** `v_no_changes` compares `home_score`, `away_score`, `result` **and `is_overridden`** by `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` — the scalar analogue of `123:1013-1018`'s jsonb equality, scale-blind on NUMERIC exactly as the write door's own comparison is (`119:653-654`), which 074 **G5** pins with `77.00` over a stored `77`. Dropping the flag from the comparison would report *the first* override of an untouched row as `no_changes` and write no receipt for a change that freezes live scoring. `override_action_id` is deliberately NOT a dimension — it is the receipt of a change, so it moves only when something else does. **(6) THE BACKSTOP'S HOT-PATH COST IS PAID IN THE `WHEN` CLAUSE.** 123 deferred this trigger because `matchups` is UPDATEd in loops by 111/116/117/119. The predicate D343 mandates sits in the trigger's `WHEN (NEW.is_overridden IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.is_overridden)`, so those loops never enter the function at all; it is **re-stated in the body** so a `prosrc` pin can see it (074 **B15**) and so the guard survives a trigger recreated without its `WHEN`. `BEFORE UPDATE` only, never INSERT: every INSERTer of `matchups` takes the column default and no client holds an INSERT policy (`109:193-194`), so guarding INSERT would buy nothing and cost every schedule generation a trigger call. **(7) D137 — `rebuild_team_week_results` HAS EXACTLY ONE BODY HUNK**, authored against `117_standings_rebuild.sql:758-891`'s FILE TEXT and never against `pg_get_functiondef`. The hunk is the first guard (`117:779-782`). The contract DOCBLOCK above it is re-stated rather than copied, because its authority bullet is the sentence this migration makes true; that is a comment, and the banner says so, so the diff is not read as a second hunk. 074 **B18** asserts every one of 117's named refusals (`week_not_final`, `matchup_not_final`, `result_drift`, `already_consistent`) survived, and **B17** that it is still one overload. **(8) THE TIE GAP IS ROUTED, NOT LEFT.** `spec:1693`'s `winner` UUID cannot express a tie. A tie IS reachable — through the score arm with equal scores, where `matchup_result_internal` derives `'tie'` — so the refusal for a winner who is not a side NAMES that route rather than leaving the commissioner to discover it. **F351** carries it to L.E1.12's copy. **(9) THREE EXISTING pgTAP SUITES AND TWO STACK SUITES CHANGED, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS THE NEW LAW ARRIVING, NOT A TEST BENT TO FIT.** 045's census is a stored literal whose own text says a migration that adds a table must move it and re-derive §C/§E's mid-state allowlists — done, and the allowlists came back UNCHANGED (`commish_matchup_actions` is unreachable from a mock: zero policies, DEFINER-only writer). 057's `is_overridden = NULL` cell reded because `NULL IS DISTINCT FROM FALSE`, so the backstop now pre-empts the NOT NULL constraint; the cell keeps D302's claim (the write is refused) ~~and **gains a `col_not_null` sibling so the constraint itself stays provable** — without it, dropping the trigger later would leave a three-valued flag with nothing red~~ **[CORRECTED in the fix round, R1009 — the sibling was a byte-equivalent duplicate of `057:76`, which has pinned `col_not_null('public','matchups','is_overridden', …)` since before this PR and already reds in exactly that case. The stated rationale was therefore factually wrong. The sibling is DROPPED and `plan(213)` reverts to `plan(212)`; the comment now points at `:76` instead of restating it. The SUBSTANCE of the 057 change stands and is stronger than it claimed: the rewritten cell pins D343's predicate as well as D302's refusal, because §12.12's printed form would let the NULL fall through to the NOT NULL constraint and restore 23502 — **measured under break probe 1, where 057 cell 103 reds alongside 074's B15/H3/H4/H10–H14**]**. 059's fixture arms the GUC around its one direct flag flip and clears it immediately so no later cell inherits it. `reconcile-db` and `score-week-worker-db` reached the overridden state through a **service-role** `UPDATE`, which the backstop now refuses — correctly: exit criterion 1 is about the OWNER and `service_role` is no different, and §12.12's own caveat is that RLS does not restrain it. A `set_config` cannot ride a PostgREST request, so both now RE-CREATE the row (the trigger is BEFORE UPDATE; INSERT is unguarded by design and 126's banner says why), with the reason in a comment naming F325/D343. **(10) Q61 SHIPPED TO ITS RECOMMENDATION WITH THE DEFAULT ON ONE LABELLED LINE** — grep `Q61 SWAP LINE`. See §3's Q61 for the exact swap and what it does not move. **(11) ADDED BY THE FIX ROUND (R1007 — amended in place, the D355/D356 precedent: D357 does not exist on `main`): AN OPEN QUESTION'S OTHER BRANCH IS CODE, SO IT GETS A TEST, WHICH MEANS THE DECISION MUST BE AN ARGUMENT AND NOT A LITERAL.** "The swap is one line" was true in PLUMBING and false in CORRECTNESS. The freeze copy was an inline `CASE` written around the shipped `v_set_over := TRUE`, and its `ELSE` silently assumed *"not frozen AND the matchup is not final ⇒ the week is final"* — true only while that literal stands. Trace the documented swap on a LIVE week with a LIVE matchup, which is the exact case Q61's other ruling exists to serve, and the verb reported **`week_final — live scoring for this week is over`** while the week was live, and the chat post (a bare `CASE WHEN v_frozen … ELSE '' END`) said **nothing at all** about the drain about to overwrite the commissioner's number — §4 rule 15's discovered consequence, hiding on the one branch no cell walked, because 074's E11/E12/J5 only ever exercised the `TRUE` arms. The remedy is **`commish_override_freeze_internal`**, a PURE `IMMUTABLE` chooser (PLAIN, `search_path=''`, triple-REVOKEd) taking `p_set_over` / `p_week_final` / `p_matchup_final` / `p_was_overridden` and returning `{frozen, why, chat_clause}` — the `lineup_autopilot_internal` pure-chooser shape (D356(1)) applied to a decision that is still Chris's. It adds a `not_frozen` arm naming the overwrite, single-sources the three texts so the receipt and the chat post cannot drift, and makes **both rulings testable today without editing the swap line** (074 §L, eleven cells, all five states plus a delegation pin so the `CASE` cannot be re-inlined). **The general rule for the rest of M6A: when a spec question's other answer is documented as a one-line swap, the branch that line does not take is unproven code — put the decision behind an argument and walk both arms, or the swap is a promise rather than a fact.** **(12) THE GUC IS NOT THE SECURITY BOUNDARY, AND BOTH THE BANNER AND THE REFUSAL NOW SAY SO (R1010).** 126's banner claimed *"the rebuild still refuses every caller who cannot also reach a `commissioner_actions` INSERT"* and the backstop raised *"…with no audit entry"*. **Neither is true as built, and it was measured:** with the 074 fixture and the owner role, `set_config('app.commish_action_id','forged-not-a-uuid',true)` then a direct `UPDATE matchups SET is_overridden = true` **moved the flag** with `override_action_id` NULL and **zero** `commissioner_actions` rows — because both guards read a string and join it to nothing. (The PR's own modified 059 fixture is the living demonstration: it sets a UUID naming no audit row and gets through.) **This is NOT a hole** — the only reachable actor is the table owner, who is already omnipotent; `authenticated` has no UPDATE policy on `matchups` at all (`109:193-194`) and no EXECUTE on the rebuild (`117:892-893`, pinned by 074 A2), and §12.12 prints the GUC-only check. But a banner that credits the wrong mechanism is how somebody later GRANTs EXECUTE on the rebuild believing the GUC would hold the door. Both texts now name the REVOKE and the missing policy as the boundary and the GUC as an **intent marker, not a credential**. **(13) A `lives_ok` OVER A ZERO-CHANGE WRITE PROVES ITS CLAIM AND EXERCISES NOTHING (R1011).** 074's H5 asserted *"a status-only UPDATE passes untouched"* against a row the fixture already inserts as `'final'`, setting it to `'final'`. The `WHEN` clause is correctly false either way, so the cell was true and hollow. H5 now aims at `d5…42` (`live` → `final`, on a week this suite never finalizes) and is bracketed by **H5a**, asserting the starting status so the transition is real, and **H5b**, asserting it landed.
- **D358 — THE ROSTER OVERRIDES' BUILD MECHANICS: ONE INTERNAL UNDER TWO VERBS, A NO-OP DEFINED BY THE REQUESTED END STATE, AND A LINE BETWEEN TIMING AND LEGALITY DRAWN GATE BY GATE (L.E1.6, migration 127 / pgTAP 075).** **(1) NUMBERS.** Migration head measured `126_commish_matchup_override.sql`, pgTAP head `074_commish_matchup_override.sql` (`ls … | tail -1`, D161/D166) ⇒ **127 / 075**, confirmed again at write time. No split seam was needed or taken. **(2) ONE INTERNAL, TWO VERBS, ONE REPLAY NAMESPACE, TWO INTERNALS TOTAL.** `commish_roster_override_internal(league, team, add, drop, player, from, to, action_id, at, reason, verb)` is PLAIN + `search_path=''` + triple-REVOKEd, and `commish_move_player` / `commish_force_add_drop` are thin DEFINER wrappers passing `now()` and their own name (126's `p_verb` shape, validated in-body so the internal cannot be driven from an unexpected caller). A SECOND internal, `commish_roster_lineup_sync_internal`, carries the lineup consequence because a MOVE runs it TWICE — once per side — and duplicating 115's interplay loop inline is how the two copies drift. **Both verbs share `commish_roster_actions`** (D350): they are one family over one league's rosters, so a retry carrying the same `action_id` must return the same document whichever route sent it. **(3) THE TWO VERBS NORMALIZE TO ONE PLAN — "this team loses a player, that team gains one" — which is what lets ONE body carry the receipt, the no-op, the chat post, the transactions row and the scoring clause.** A MOVE is an `UPDATE` of the ONE `league_rosters` row (which is why exclusivity is preserved *by construction* rather than by a check); a force add/drop is a DELETE and/or an INSERT. Everything downstream reads `v_lose_team` / `v_gain_team` / `v_lose_player` / `v_gain_player`. **(4) THE NO-OP IS "THE REQUESTED END STATE ALREADY HOLDS", AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT REACHABLE AT ALL.** D336(3) mandates a no-op detected by value, and §4 rule 14(b) forbids a cell asserting a guard that cannot execute — so the no-op had to be a state this family can actually reach. Empty arguments are NOT it: a submit that names no player is a MALFORMED call and is refused by name (126's rule). The reachable no-op is `commish_move_player` naming a player who is **already on the destination**, and `commish_force_add_drop` whose add is already on this roster and whose drop is already on none. The rejected alternative — 115's refusal, *"he is on X's roster, not Y's"* — makes a fallback verb non-idempotent in the one direction it most needs not to be: a retry under a fresh `action_id` after a network loss. A player on a THIRD team (neither source nor destination) is still refused, because there the commissioner's view is wrong in a way that matters. **(5) THE TIMING / LEGALITY LINE IS DRAWN GATE BY GATE, IN THE BANNER, UNDER STANDING RULE (i).** LIFTED, each NAMED in `bypassed[]` and each **evaluated** rather than assumed (the lock helper really runs, so the receipt names a lock that was measured closed): E32's drop and add arms, the waiver period, the acquisition caps, the manager-only auth. KEPT, each refused BY NAME with the lawful route in the message: player exclusivity, `roster_size`, a `retired` franchise (**F352**), D294's broken mirror, and the season gate (rosters do not exist before draft completion, so that one is the absence of a subject and not a timing rule). **F324's second site is this list**, recorded and not decided. **(6) A CONSEQUENCE OF D353's OWN SHAPE, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED (§4 rule 15): a commissioner force-add does not CONSUME the team's acquisition budget.** `115:497-506` counts a team's acquisitions by `initiator_team_id`, and `transactions.initiator_team_id` is NULL for a commissioner move by design (`109:243`). So the verb neither obeys the cap nor spends it, and the result says so in `caps.commissioner_move_not_counted`. **(7) THE ORDER IS D336(2)'s PLAIN ONE, not 126's inversion.** The receipt goes INSIDE the no-op guard and AFTER the state write. 126 had to invert it because the `matchups` backstop refuses a flag write with no GUC and because `override_action_id` is an FK; neither applies here — no trigger guards `league_rosters`, `league_player_pool` or `team_lineups`, and the one FK to `commissioner_actions` is the `transactions` row, which is therefore written LAST. **This verb is `transactions.related_action_id`'s FIRST writer** (the FK landed at `123:461-462` with zero rows behind it). **(8) `before`/`after` DESCRIBE THE ROW OF `target_id`, AND THE DROP SIDE OF A COMBINED CALL LIVES IN `metadata`.** §5's printed shape has room for ONE roster row; an add+drop moves two. `target_id` is the added or moved player when there is one, else the dropped one, and `metadata.drop_before` / `drop_player_id` / `drop_to_state` carry the other half. pgTAP 075 **D14** asserts `before || after` equals `after` exactly, which is what proves the two documents' KEY SETS are identical rather than merely overlapping. **(9) THE SCORING CLAUSE IS 123's, AND THE SYMMETRIC DIFFERENCE IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED.** The sync helper RETURNS the current-week slot it vacated, and the enqueue set is built from that — so "an added player lands on the bench and is therefore never in the difference" is a fact the code reads back, not a comment. Stamp, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, `score_enqueued` / `score_not_enqueued` / `score_stale` / `score_stale_reason` are 123's verbatim, and all three arms are walked (075 §C, §D, §H). **`edited_by_commish` is written on EVERY lineup row the verb changes and `set_at` on none** — the D356(5) four-not-five posture: nobody SET this lineup, a roster move changed it underneath. **(10) F350 IS RE-ROUTED, MEASURED OUT OF ITS OWN ROUTING.** It was routed here because `commish_move_player` was expected to seed fixed placements into `lineup_fit_internal`. It does not call the matcher at all (075 **I3** asserts zero `prosrc` hits), because a roster move is not a re-fit — it copies 115's interplay loop, which removes a key by name and appends to the bench behind a `NOT (bench ? p_add)` guard, so the map it writes is always the stored map MINUS one key. The verb carries its own site-local duplicate assertion anyway (the added player in NO `slot_map` value and EXACTLY ONCE on the bench, on every row it touched), because a duplicate written HERE would double-count in `startersOf`. The matcher still has no guard; its three callers still rely on their own COALESCE discipline (D356(7c)); no remaining M6A task adds or replaces a caller, so the owner is the next migration that does (M5's trade verbs). **(11) A THIRD SCORING HALF D346 DID NOT HAVE, FOUND BY THE STACK TEST AND NOT BY READING (F353).** The worker maps a queued player to LEAGUES through `league_rosters`; `commish_edit_lineup` never meets that because its benched player stays rostered, but a force-DROP deletes the row, so the queue row the verb writes for the dropped man maps to nothing and the drain never arrives. Measured: the first cut reded with `report.leagues: []` on the drain after the drop while the identical drain before it reported the league `written`. So 127 queues a changed starter only if the league still rosters him (naming the rest `unrostered`), ALSO queues a REACH SET of players the league still rosters so the drain ARRIVES, and then MEASURES reachability with the worker's own predicate — `score_reach_enqueued[]` / `score_reachable` on the receipt, `score_stale_reason = 'unreachable'` when the answer is no. **The general rule for the rest of this family: an enqueue is only a signal if the queued player is still reachable from the thing you want recomputed. Any future verb that REMOVES a player and expects a re-score inherits this.** **(12) ADDED BY THE FIX ROUND (R1016–R1023), because four of the eight findings are mechanics the next verb in this family repeats. (a) **TWO ENQUEUE SITES NEED TWO CELLS.** 127 writes `score_fanout` twice (the symmetric difference and the reach set) and the first cut pinned only the second, so a probe on either one reded the same cell and attributed nothing. A verb with N insert sites owes N independent pins and at least one cell that SHOWS the other site was empty at that call. (b) **A VERB'S `action_type` DESCRIBES THE PLAN THAT EXECUTED, NEVER THE PARAMETERS THAT ARRIVED** — the normalized plan is the only honest source once any arm can be a no-op; the sole exception is a TOTAL no-op, where nothing executed and the document's job is to report the request. (c) **`action_id` IS A SHARED NAMESPACE**: `uniq_transactions_league_action` spans every verb that writes a `transactions` row, so any new writer owes the R732 check in its own direction or it ships a 500. (d) **AN IR SPOT IS NOT A STARTING SLOT**, and the predicate to use is the scoring worker's (`startersOf`/`irKeysOf`, prefix-split on `':'`), not 123's whole-instance-key form, whenever the field exists to predict what the worker will do.
- **D359 — THE TEAM-RENAME VERBS' BUILD MECHANICS: TWO DOORS OVER ONE NAME GATE, AN AUTHORITY GAP SAID OUT LOUD, AND A GUARD DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN (L.E1.7, migration 128 / pgTAP 076).** **(1) NUMBERS.** Migration head measured `127_commish_roster_moves.sql`, pgTAP head `075_commish_roster_moves.sql` (`ls … | tail -1`, D161/D166) ⇒ **128 / 076**, confirmed at write time. No seam needed or taken; **129 / 077** is next free. **(2) 128 REPLACES NOTHING — ZERO D137 HUNKS, and the banner states that rather than leaving it to be inferred.** Six new objects, no `CREATE OR REPLACE` against another migration's file text, so there is no decoy head to get wrong. This is the first M6A schema task with no provenance risk at all, and saying so is cheaper than a reviewer re-deriving it. **(3) TWO DOORS, ONE SHARED NAME GATE.** `team_rename_normalize_internal(name, verb)` is the single place the bound (`z.string().trim().min(1).max(100)`, the league-rename bound) and the EXPLICIT `E' \t\r\n'` trim class live, so the commissioner's verb and the manager's cannot drift on what counts as a name. Plain `btrim` strips SPACES ONLY (R745, fixed twice already at `112:756` / `114:315`) — a naive `NULLIF(btrim(x), '')` ships a franchise called `E'\t'`. **(4) THE COMMISSIONER'S HALF IS 123's TEMPLATE UNCHANGED** (D336's seven parts, mapped line by line in the banner): its own zero-policy `commish_team_actions` ledger with `REVOKE TRUNCATE`; ONE audit row through the shared helper, inside the no-op guard and after the state write, with `IF v_audit_id IS NULL RAISE`; the no-op detected by value over the ONE dimension the verb can change; the in-txn non-disableable chat post; PLAIN internal + DEFINER wrapper; the three-layer reason gate; and a result that names what did and did not follow. **(5) THE MANAGER'S HALF CARRIES NONE OF IT, AND REPORTS EACH ABSENCE AS A FIELD** — `audited: false` + `audited_why`, `system_post: null` + `system_post_why`. No reason (he is not exercising a §10.1 power), no audit row, no chat post (§10.3's post is for OVERRIDE messages; auto-posting an ordinary manager action would be new product), and **no `action_id` and no ledger**, because setting a name to a value is idempotent by construction and the verb has no second effect to dedupe. **A STANDALONE TEAM IS ROUTED, NOT HANDLED TWICE**: `league_id IS NULL` already has a working door (`095:636-639`'s UPDATE policy, proven live by 076 **C3**), so the verb refuses by name and says which one rather than becoming a second writer for a surface that is not broken. **(6) ~~A GUARD DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN, AND THE MECHANISM ASSERTED IN ITS PLACE (§4 rule 14(b) / D267).~~ RETRACTED 2026-09-14 (R1029) — THE GUARD IS WRITTEN, AND THE LESSON IS THE OPPOSITE ONE.** ~~`rename_own_team` has no `retired` refusal: `120:540` is the only writer of `status='retired'` in the whole chain and the same arm re-points the seat's `league_members` row at the SUCCESSOR with `user_id = NULL` (`120:565-570`), so the auth predicate structurally excludes a sealed franchise and a guard placed after it could never execute — nor be proven without a fixture the product cannot produce. 076 B1 asserts the premise and F7 asserts the mechanism, so a future migration that leaves a seated row on a sealed franchise turns that cell red. The general rule: when a guard is unreachable, assert the thing that makes it unreachable — never ship a guard no cell can fire.~~ **THE CORRECTION:** the exclusion was an INVARIANT maintained by three other verbs' guards (`create_league_invite` `062:378`, `claim_league_invite` `062:865`, `assign_manager` `063:688`), not a structure — `seat_league_member_internal`'s fallback at `077:428-437` INSERTs a `league_members` row for whatever team id it is handed, and none of the three guards was pinned by 076. F7's fixture omitted the seated row BY HAND, so it asserted its own premise and could never have noticed drift. The Reviewer produced the state in a rolled-back transaction and renamed a sealed franchise through the manager door (`Unsealed By Manager | retired`). Rule 14(b)/D267 is about a guard an outer condition IN THE SAME FUNCTION has excluded; a guard kept out by remote verbs is a different species and IS provable — so `rename_own_team_internal` step **(3b)** now refuses `retired` by name with the commissioner arm's F354-naming message shape, and 076 **F10/F11/F12** prove it on exactly the Reviewer's fixture (a `retired` team seated by a real user). **The general rule, corrected: "structurally unreachable" means excluded by THIS function's own earlier gate; anything else is an invariant somebody else maintains, and the guard goes in.** Break probe: the guard removed ⇒ F11 *"no exception thrown"*, F12 *"have: Unsealed By Manager"*, 90/92 otherwise green; restored, `diff` empty. **AND THE GUARD READS THE LOCKED ROW (R1036/R1037, the second fix round, 2026-09-15 — by Chris's ruling, see the findings block): the R1029 guard was placed at the old step (3b), evaluated on step (1)'s UNLOCKED select BEFORE the `FOR UPDATE` re-read, so a retire committed while the rename waited on the league lock was invisible to it — the manager door renamed a franchise sealed 4.5 s earlier (`Raced Past The Seal | retired`). The commissioner arm was never exposed (its guard at step 6 already read its locked re-read at step 5). Now the manager arm locks league → team, re-reads, and THEN evaluates auth (step 4) and the retired guard (step 5) against the locked state — the commissioner arm's shape; 076 F13/F14 pin both orders as `prosrc` positions. The general rule, sharpened once more: a guard that reads a row is only as good as the read — a gate evaluated before the lock decides on a row that may already be history.** **(7) A REFUSAL'S MESSAGE IS PART OF THE PROOF, AND THE PATTERN MUST RED ON THE STRING IT REPLACED.** I1 pins the FROZEN wording, the F354 honesty AND the successor it offers; break probe 2 regressed the message to R1020's *"un-retire the franchise first"* route-to-nowhere and I1 reded alone while I2 stayed green. That is the two-sided attribution R1026 had to add to 127 one round late. **(8) NAME UNIQUENESS IS REPORTED, NEVER REFUSED.** Measured: no UNIQUE index and no CHECK on `teams.name` anywhere in 001-128, and `add_placeholder_seat` will happily mint a second *"Team 3"*. Inventing a refusal inside a verb whose whole purpose is to REMOVE a restriction would be new product, so both doors return `name_collides_with[]` (case-insensitive, other franchises in the league) and the caller decides. **(9) NO STATUS GATE, STATED SO THE ABSENCE IS NOT READ AS AN OVERSIGHT.** A rename is meaningful in every league status — `setup` is exactly where Chris's *"the commissioner names every team"* lives — and nothing about a name touches the lock, the week or the scoring snapshot, so `bypassed` is `[]` **with a `bypassed_why`**: an empty array that does not explain itself is a silence (§4 rule 15). **(10) THE PROPAGATION ANSWER IS A REPORT, NOT A PASS.** `teams.name` is read LIVE at every call site, so nothing needs rewriting; the frozen copies — already-written chat posts and `commissioner_actions.metadata.team_name` — keep the OLD name because a receipt records what was true, and `123:339-410`'s `ENABLE ALWAYS` trigger would refuse an UPDATE of one in any case. `propagation.frozen_receipts_for_this_team` is a MEASURED count scoped to receipts about THIS franchise, and 076 §H proves the frozen half on a second rename. **(11) A pgTAP SUITE RUNS IN ONE TRANSACTION, SO `now()` IS FROZEN — a fixture that takes the `DEFAULT now()` cannot tell "updated_at moved" from "updated_at did not move".** 076 stamps its teams ten days back for exactly that reason, which is what makes **E4** and **G10** real cells rather than two comparisons of `now()` with `now()`. **(12) `commissioner_actions` IS APPEND-ONLY AND THAT CONSTRAINS TEST LAYOUT, not just production.** The first cut tidied a section's receipt away with a `DELETE` and was refused by the immutability trigger — correctly. The gate cells whose one successful call writes a receipt therefore run AFTER every section that asserts a count, rather than before it. **(13) `action_type = 'reassign_team'`** per tasks-M6A §5's contractual table — §12.12's printed vocabulary (`spec:1189-1193`, re-stated at `123:280-286`) has no `rename_team`, and `action_type` is deliberately not a CHECK so that adding one would not be a schema change. The word reads like an owner reassignment, so **F355** carries the rendering rule to L.E1.11/L.E1.13: derive the verb from the `before`/`after` key set, never from the string. **(14) THE DROP SEAM IS WRITTEN DOWN IN TWO PLACES AND IS EXACT.** If Chris wants only the commissioner's half: delete §4 of migration 128 (`rename_own_team_internal` + `rename_own_team` + their REVOKEs); delete pgTAP 076 §F (F1-F12), take A6's expected count 5 → 3, drop the two `rename_own_team%` names from A7/A8/A11/A12, delete A10, A14 **and J6** (the anon probe of the manager door — omitted by the first cut, R1030; executing the seam as first written left the suite red on `42883`), and `plan(92)` → `plan(77)`; REGENERATE `database.ts` (which drops exactly two entries — `supabase gen types` emits every public-schema function regardless of grants, measured again here on three triple-REVOKEd internals) and re-append the 42-export alias block; and delete this decision's `rename_own_team` sentences. Nothing else moves. **Executed on a scratch copy in the fix round (the manager functions DROPped inside the test's own rolled-back transaction): 77/77, nothing dangling; J1's description mentions the manager door in prose only.**
- **D360 — THE SETTINGS OVERRIDE'S BUILD MECHANICS: ONE KEY PER CALL, A POLICY TABLE AS DATA, TWO 118 STATEMENTS RE-DECIDED, AND ONE MARKED SEAM (L.E1.8, migration 129 / pgTAP 077).** **(1) NUMBERS.** Heads measured `128_team_rename.sql` / `076_team_rename.sql` ⇒ **129 / 077**; the split seam **132 / 080 was NOT taken** and is released — `reopen_week` is not built, and 077 K6 pins that no `reopen_week%` function exists. **130 / 078** is next free (L.E1.9's, as §7 promised). **(2) 129 REPLACES NOTHING — ZERO D137 HUNKS.** `update_league_settings` (`118:2438`; 061 and 105 are decoys) is byte-untouched; 077 §K pins its gate string (`118:2489-2497`), its re-seed statement (`118:2617-2621`) and its single overload. The verb LIFTS the gate as a property of the NEW verb (§4 rule 13) and carries no status gate of its own beyond `deleted_at IS NULL`. **(3) ONE KEY, READ-MODIFY-WRITE.** Typed columns are written each by name in a `CASE`; blob keys through `settings || jsonb_build_object(key, v)` so every other key is byte-untouched (077 C2). The current value is read from the LOCKED row in the same canonical form (`to_jsonb(v_league) -> key` / `settings -> key`, an absent blob key = `null`). **(4) THE NO-OP IS CANONICAL-JSONB EQUALITY.** Every value passes a per-key gate (`commish_setting_canon_internal` over three small typed helpers) mirroring `leagueSettingsSchema`'s type and range, so `72` and `"72"` canonicalise to the same jsonb and a re-send in a different JSON type is a no-op (077 D1–D3, the three-way cell; break probe 2 reds D4/D7). **(5) THE POLICY TABLE IS DATA:** `commish_setting_policy(key)` (IMMUTABLE, EXECUTE for `authenticated`) returns `{storage, class, refused_why}` — FREE (waiver/trade/lineup knobs, `tiebreakers`, `playoff_reseed`, `faab_budget`, `roster_settings`), RESCORE (`scoring_system_id`), BRACKET (`playoff_teams`, `playoff_weeks_per_round`, `consolation_bracket`, `third_place_game` — refused BY NAME once status is `playoffs`/`complete`, because `118:1075-1077`/`:1338-1340` have seeded the bracket), REFUSED always (`regular_season_weeks`/`playoff_start_week` — the season window under rows 111 generated, Q10-coupled; `team_count`; `schedule_mode`/`median_game`/`second_opponent` — schedule shape; the pinned `format`/`lineup_lock`/`divisions`/`playoff_byes`; `schedule_seed`; the `draft` block), UNKNOWN refused by name. `roster_settings` is allowed post-draft because the §7.3 header says so ("allowed but logged and warned") and the warning is a MEASURED count of un-refit lineup rows (077 H12). **(6) RE-DECISION 1 — THE FAAB RE-SEED FIRES ONLY IN `setup`/`scheduled`**, the precondition 118's own comment names; in-season the budget lands and every balance is byte-unchanged, with the off-budget seat count measured and `commish_edit_faab` (M5, F340) named as the per-team route. Rejected: refusing the key (a reachability defect under standing rule (a)) and adding the delta (invented policy, and a negative balance for an overspent team). **(7) RE-DECISION 2 — THE RE-FREEZE STAYS,** in the same UPDATE as the reference (§7.3.3, never-weaken); NULL stays NULL; 104's `trg_leagues_scoring_rules_valid` + `trg_leagues_scoring_reference_guard` fire and are not bypassed; the attachable scope is 118 step 5's (a template, or the current reference). And it is SAID that the re-freeze rewrites no stored score: `rescore = false` reports `not_requested` and flags an open week `score_stale = snapshot_changed_without_rescore`, because that week is now MIXED. **(8) `rescore` — Q64's recommendation, built as instructed.** A malformed call (22023) on any key but `scoring_system_id`; a P0001 refusal BY NAME with ≥ 1 final week (whole call rolled back — a rescored season or nothing); otherwise one `score_fanout` row per starter per open week stamped `MIN(player_stats.updated_at)` (123's SCORING rule — a `now()` stamp is `not_ready` for ever), starters derived from `slot_map` the way the worker's `startersOf` does (IR keys excluded — 077 G19), the unqueueable NAMED (`stats_unstamped` / `no_stat_row`, G20). **THE SEAM IS ONE MARKED BLOCK** (`-- Q64 SEAM`, step 11b, pinned by G14): a future `reopen_week` replaces the RAISE with a per-week `reopen_week_internal` call and the existing enqueue loop covers the reopened weeks. **(9) 045's CENSUS moved 70 → 71** with §C/§E's mid-state allowlists re-derived UNCHANGED (a mock cannot reach a zero-policy ledger only the override verb writes). **(10) FOR L.E1.11 / L.E1.13:** the route mirrors the per-key gates in Zod in FRONT of the RPC (the SQL is the server-authoritative copy); the settings panel reads `commish_setting_policy` for its refused copy and renders `rescore_not_performed_why` and `score_stale_reason` FIRST among the success branches (§4 rule 15 / R971).
- **D361 — THE SCHEDULE OVERRIDE'S BUILD MECHANICS: A SIBLING THAT LIFTS FOUR TIMING GATES BY NAME AND KEEPS TWO LEGALITY GATES, ONE RECEIPT HUNK THAT MAKES 111's REASON UNCONDITIONAL, AND A BRACKET ROW LEFT REFUSED (L.E1.9, migration 130 / pgTAP 078).** **(1) NUMBERS.** Heads measured `129_commish_change_setting.sql` / `077_commish_change_setting.sql` ⇒ **130 / 078**; the M6A band (125–130 / 073–078) is now spent; 131 / 079 next free (D161 at task time). `grep -ln schedule_edit_matchup supabase/migrations/*.sql` → **111 alone** — the citation held; no decoy. **(2) THE GATES, RE-MEASURED AGAINST STANDING RULE (i).** §2.2's "four state refusals" (`111:881`/`:887`/`:894`/`:904`) do not split cleanly into lifted/kept, so the banner carries a table. LIFTED and named in `bypassed[]` (timing / reachability): `:887` matchup status (`matchup_status_gate:<status>`), `:904` week status (`week_status_gate:<status>`; a MISSING `league_weeks` row is still refused — data integrity, not timing), `:913` the week's own kickoff (`kickoff_lock` — standing rule (g), D335; not in the four, but a `live` week has kicked off by definition so lifting `:904` without it lands nothing), and `:993` a sibling row's status (`sibling_status_gate:<id>:<status>` — `:887`'s rule on the row the new team vacates). KEPT by name (legality): `:894` and `:999` (a scored / overridden cell — §22.2; the message names `commish_edit_score` / `commish_set_result` as the owner), `:867` (`in_season` — standing rule (a)'s "meaningful state"), the bye row, the foreign/retired team, the parking-collision check, and 111's in-body re-validation (every team once; E40). **`:881` (a bracket row) is KEPT though listed among the four — F360:** lifting it lands nothing because the kept every-team-once re-validation counts every non-retired team per (week, round_type) and a bracket seats a subset (the edit refuses one gate later with the wrong message), and `playoff_bracket_sync_internal` (118:1075-1077) re-seeds bracket rows at each round advance; under (i) a hand-edited bracket is not a repair. D366 was the head → **D367**; F371 was the head → **F372**; no R-number minted; the one open PR (#180, docs) carries none of them. **(2) THE SOURCE WAS OURS, NOT SUPABASE'S.** The default ACL that re-grants TRUNCATE to every new table is the per-schema `postgres` entry that **migration 037** wrote (`ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE postgres IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON TABLES`, D18→D23). Measured local AND hosted (hosted by a read-only catalog query — nothing written): **every `public` table is owned by `postgres`**, every TRUNCATE grant's grantor is `postgres`, and `pg_default_acl` holds two per-schema `r` entries — `postgres` and `supabase_admin`, both `anon=arwdDxtm`. 133 revokes `D` from the `postgres` entry (after: `anon=arwdxtm/postgres`; `service_role=arwdDxtm/postgres` untouched). It is inert for this repo (no table owned by `supabase_admin`, no migration runs as it), but a table created by a path that runs as `supabase_admin` would still be born with the grant. **(4) THE STANDING RULE, RESTATED PRECISELY (amends D350's TRUNCATE clause).** A table created **by a migration** (i.e. by `postgres`, in `public`) **no longer needs** a per-table `REVOKE TRUNCATE` — it is born without the grant (081 **B2**, probed red). - **D340 — AUTOPILOT BUILDS ITS MAP BY CALLING `lineup_fit_internal` (112:439), NEVER BY RE-IMPLEMENTING SEATING.** The matcher can CHOOSE a lineup, not only validate one: fed the whole roster with `wanted = null, fixed = false`, its augmenting-path loop (`112:519-555`, under the banner at `:514-518`) runs a BFS bipartite match in **array order**, and because an augmenting path only re-routes already-matched players (`112:545-553`), no player is ever unmatched once matched. Input order is therefore a strict priority order, and the matchable sets form a transversal matroid — greedy-by-order is **optimal, not approximate**. So autopilot needs no new matcher and no placement policy: "which players start" reduces to one `ORDER BY` (§11 **Q62**). **This is also a free oracle and a trap:** invariant 2 `checkLineupLegality` (`season-invariants.ts:303-337`) calls the same function over the stored map and reds on `unplaced.length > 0` OR `rearranged`, so a map built THROUGH the matcher satisfies it by construction — but the sim's own `chooseStarterSlots` is a greedy FIRST-FIT over slots in order (`season-runner.ts` → `chooseStarterSlots` (docblock :1854-1867, signature :1868-1872 at 7a2a436)), so a first-fit clone in the migration reds the gate on a contested-flex roster. **Already-placed players are seeded `fixed = true, wanted = <their key>` so a carried or manager-set placement is NEVER overridden.**

The storage-level reason they cannot be independent is `117:826-841`. Supplying neither arm is refused by name. **A BYE ROW REFUSES THE RESULT ARM BY NAME:** `matchup_result_internal` returns NULL when `away_team_id IS NULL` and the derive maps a NULL away side to `bye` before consulting `result` at all — setting a result there writes a column nothing reads, a no-op wearing a success's clothes.
- **D342 — `is_overridden` STAYS ROW-SCOPED, AND THE VERB TAKES BOTH SCORES.** §22.2 says *"overridden cells"* but all seven readers are row-scoped (`119:634`/`:654`, `117:834`, `118:1437`/`:2095`, `111:894`/`:999`, and reconcile's exclusion at `reconcile.ts:699`). After this decision it means *"a commissioner CHANGED this lineup row"* — which a force-drop out of a starting slot genuinely is, but a manager's own placement now carries the badge for the week. **The widening is accepted, not denied, and it costs one proof cell**: L.E1.6's PROOF pins what the badge renders after a commissioner roster move, and L.E1.13 re-reads the badge copy against the wider meaning. **The rejected alternative — a distinct column or a second signal — loses on cost with its number stated:** `score-week-worker.ts:940` selects exactly `team_id, slot_map, edited_by_commish`, so a new signal is a migration PLUS a worker change PLUS a new never-weaken surface, to re-express something the row already says.

Naming: `commish_matchup_actions`, `commish_roster_actions`, `commish_team_actions`, `commish_setting_actions`, `commish_schedule_actions`. Since migration 133 a table created by a migration is born WITHOUT the TRUNCATE grant, so the per-table `REVOKE TRUNCATE` is no longer REQUIRED of a new ledger (it stays legal and harmless; the eight existing ones are untouched). **2026-09-09 — Builder (F308 standalone — branch `fix/M4-F308-nomination-broadcast`; NO migration (heads stay 122 / 070), no typegen, no `db reset`, no schema, no RPC, **NO APPLICATION CHANGE**, no spec change — one new E2E helper, one E2E spec, two harness lines and `.gitignore`)**

  **Number note (D161 — measured 2026-09-09 on `main` @ `2c2dc7e` and on the working tree):** `D334` / `F310` / `F311` / `F312` / `Q49` / `R952` → **0 occurrences each in PROGRESS** ⇒ D334 taken here, ledger rows from **F310**, the question is **Q49**, reviewer band from **R952**.   **(1) THE RECORDED REASON F308 HAD NO EVIDENCE IS FALSE, AND THAT MATTERS BECAUSE IT MISDIRECTS THE FIX.** D332(24) and the #278 review say a trace was impossible because `trace: 'retain-on-failure'` "applies only to Playwright's default fixtures" and the spec "builds both clients manually with fresh contexts". **Measured false on playwright 1.62.1:** the `_setupArtifacts` auto-fixture hooks `didCreateBrowserContext` for EVERY context created during a test (`node_modules/playwright/lib/index.js:150` → `_startTraceChunkOnContextCreation`, `:710-717`, which calls `tracing.start(...)` on a context that has none), so a hand-built `browser.newContext()` IS traced. The true statement is STRICTLY STRONGER: **not one of the four gate scripts so much as mentions `test-results`**; the only `artifact` hit anywhere in them is `gate-m3.sh:22`, a comment about draft ORDERING artifacts. The conclusion the citation supported is unchanged and better supported*), so the isolation re-run that immediately followed the failure — the standard next move, and the one the F308 session made — deleted the only copy. **That is F56's own recorded lesson ("copy the trace BEFORE re-running") repeating on a new row**, and the fix is therefore not "start tracing" but "write the evidence where playwright does not own it, and above all to STDOUT", which is what a composed gate's log actually keeps (F135). D332(24) and the F308 cell are corrected in place.

  **(2) THE INSTRUMENTS (`e2e/helpers/evidence.ts`, new; wired into `e2e/auction-live.spec.ts`).** Three, each answering one thing the failure could not say. **(a) `confirmNominationLanded` — the SEPARATOR.** `nominateFirstAvailable` clicked "Nominate at $1" and returned with no server read-back, so *"the commissioner nominated and the manager missed the broadcast"* and *"no nomination was ever issued"* were the same red. It now polls `readAuctionMarket` until `drafts.current_nomination` exists **and resolves the nominated `player_id` to a NAME** (new harness read `readPlayerFullName`) and matches the row that was clicked; a submit that never lands fails BY NAME one step from its cause, and a wrong-player nomination cannot pass as the right one. Every run — the gate's included — now prints `[auction-live] <actor> nomination for <player> live server-side in <n>ms` (measured 207–1,278 ms), so a later broadcast timeout is unambiguous in the log alone. **(b) `SocketLedger` — WHAT EACH BROWSER ACTUALLY RECEIVED.** A per-page record of the realtime frames, with a real supabase-realtime decoder rather than a `JSON.parse`: control frames are a JSON **array** `[join_ref, ref, topic, event, payload]` (so `parsed.event` is `undefined` on every one) and **every user broadcast is a BINARY frame**, kind `4`, `[kind][topicSize][eventSize][metaSize][encoding]` then topic/event/metadata/payload (`@supabase/realtime-js/lib/serializer.js` `_decodeUserBroadcast`) — in the first instrumented run **110 of the commissioner's frames were binary**, i.e. the entire `drafts`/`tick`/`draft_bids` traffic the ledger exists to record. It separates a DEAF CHANNEL (nothing after the join) from a LOST BROADCAST (beats arrive, the `drafts` frame does not) from a CLIENT-SIDE defect (the frame arrived and the page rendered the old state — F304's stomp). **(c) `captureDraftFailureEvidence` — AHEAD OF THE SWEEP.** Called from the describe's **`test.afterEach`**, and on the assertion path from the spec's own `catch` behind a per-test once-flag — ***amended in place at the #280 fix round (R952): the `catch` ALONE was not enough, because a Playwright TEST-LEVEL timeout abandons the body and runs neither `catch` nor `finally`. That was demonstrated red-then-green on this spec; see the fix-round block in §6.*** Either way it runs before `test.afterAll`'s `cleanupSweep` deletes the draft (the `0 rows` that ended F308's session): the authoritative market + bid ledger + live pick count + the nominated player's name, both pages' full rendered body text, both screenshots, and every ledger — to `e2e-evidence/<stamp>/` (gitignored, outside playwright's reach) **and to stdout**, with a line naming the playwright output dir and instructing the reader to copy it before re-running anything.

  **(3) A SECOND MEASURED CORRECTION, and it changes the instrument's shape: on a page behind `routeWebSocket`, `page.on('websocket')` observes the UPSTREAM leg.** The opposite looked true at first — with nothing being dropped, a CDP ledger and a ledger fed from inside the passthrough recorded the SAME 107 frames — and only a probe that DROPPED every frame showed the difference: **all 15 dropped frames still appeared on the CDP ledger.** So the manager carries TWO ledgers, `manager-upstream` (server → harness) and `manager-delivered` (harness → browser), which is also the only pair that can indict or exonerate the harness's own Node hop — the competing explanation F56's cell keeps on the record for this family. Recording happens one statement before each forward and `record` swallows its own errors by construction, so the instrument cannot change what the passthrough delivers.

  **(4) WHAT A LOST FRAME ACTUALLY COSTS — three constructed probes, on the shipped tree, each measured rather than argued** (temporary probe spec, deleted; the shipped spec's md5 `c16e097766cd3281f588fac044595676` before = after every patched run). Drop only the `drafts` frame that CARRIES the nomination, beats still delivered ⇒ the manager rendered it after **4,125 ms**. Drop every `drafts` frame ⇒ **3,100 ms**. Drop EVERY server frame (F74/D325's deaf-channel shape) ⇒ **49,000 ms**. **The conclusion is sharp and it is the reason this row exists: a single lost nomination broadcast is NOT F308** — `heartbeatSignalsGap` catches it on the next 5 s beat (the beat carries the new bid deadline, the room holds the old nomination deadline) and heals in ~4 s, far inside the spec's 20 s. **Only TOTAL broadcast silence outlasts 20 s**, because the live arm of `roomWatchdogWantsRefetch` is gated on `HEARTBEAT_SILENCE_MS` = **45 s**.

  **(5) THE INSTRUMENTS PROVEN ON A DELIBERATELY INDUCED FAILURE — and it reproduces F308's snapshot VERBATIM.** With a temporary three-line patch making the manager deaf from the nomination onward, `auction-live` went red at the nomination line in 20 s and the capture printed: read-back `nomination for Jahmyr Gibbs live server-side in 823ms`; server `nomination.player_id 9221`, `nominatedPlayerName "Jahmyr Gibbs"`, `livePickCount 0`; **`manager-upstream` 2 × `drafts` + 5 × `tick` + 1 × `draft_bids` INCLUDING the frame with `nomination=9221`, `manager-delivered` ONE `drafts` (the pre-nomination one) and then nothing** — i.e. "the server sent it, the browser never got it", stated by the instrument. The manager's captured body: *"Draft live … On the clock · auction live commish … Live Round 1 · Pick 1 … 0:39 Nominating **Waiting on the nominating team to put a player up.**"* — F308's recorded snapshot, string for string, timer in the same range. Patch reverted, md5 restored.

  **(6) REPRODUCED AT 3-IN-8 UNDER THE CONDITIONS IT ACTUALLY APPEARED IN — not in isolation.** Isolation proves nothing here (F308 isolates green; so does this), so the lever was CONTENTION, the D333(1) method: nine CPU busy-loops (load average 17–21 on 16 cores) **plus a loop of `npx tsx scripts/sim.ts draft --type auction --leagues 25 --clock 30 --seed 42`** — the gate's own M3 sim, running CONCURRENTLY with the browsers rather than before them — then `npx playwright test e2e/auction-live.spec.ts --repeat-each=8`. Result: **6 failed / 4 passed (12.1 m)**, and **three of the six are F308 exactly** — `getByText(/Gibbs/)` not visible in 20,000 ms at the nomination-broadcast line. *(The other three are a different, load-induced red at the completion assertion — the 16-lot drive not finishing inside its own budget — and are reported, not folded in.)* Two earlier, weaker attempts are reported too, because they bound the lever: `--repeat-each=6` under CPU load alone went **8 passed** twice (once with a broken load script that started no processes at all — `timeout` does not exist on this Mac — and once with a real 9-way load). **CPU pressure alone does not do it; concurrent DRAFT traffic does.**

  **(7) THE MECHANISM, FROM THE SERVICE'S OWN LOG.** At the failure the capture read: read-back `nomination for Jahmyr Gibbs live server-side in 1278ms`, server holding `player_id 9221` / `Jahmyr Gibbs`, and **all three ledgers carrying `phx_join` / `phx_reply` / `presence_state` / `presence_diff` / `heartbeat` and ZERO `broadcast:drafts`, ZERO `broadcast:tick`, ZERO `broadcast:draft_bids` — on BOTH clients.** Not a lost frame: the whole broadcast plane was dead for that draft while the channels stayed joined. `docker logs supabase_realtime_fieldscout` says why, in its own words: **`UnableToBroadcastChanges: :too_many_requests` — 25,801 of them in the minute 10:19 UTC**, the minute the nomination row was written (`draft_bids.created_at 2026-09-09T10:19:59.200012+00:00`), and 13,747–28,316 per minute across 10:18–10:34. The ceiling is the local tenant's: `_realtime.tenants.max_events_per_second = **100**`. `realtime.send()` traps its own errors (068 ARM 3), the drop happens in the Realtime service AFTER the write, and no client sees an error — **so the room's ONLY signal that anything is wrong is the absence of beats, and it waits 45 s for that.** **The corroboration that ties this to the gate's snapshot:** Presence kept working throughout, because Phoenix presence is channel-level and not `realtime.send()` — which is exactly why F308's own snapshot showed a **live presence list** beside a room that believed no nomination had happened.

  **(8) THE CONTROL, RUN BECAUSE THE ANSWER MATTERS: a clean `npm run test:e2e` trips the limiter ZERO times.** 16 passed (7.8 m), drop count before **1,674,468** and after **1,674,468** — **delta 0**. So the browser suite by itself does not exceed 100 events/s; the pressure in this reproduction came from the 25-league sim running BESIDE it. **THIS IS THE HONEST LIMIT OF THE DIAGNOSIS, stated rather than smoothed over:** the composed gate runs its sims BEFORE its browser stages, not beside them, so **what tripped the plane in the gate's own 2,644 s run is NOT established** — only that it must have been total broadcast silence on the manager, because nothing else outlasts 20 s (item 4), and that Presence survived it (item 7). The instruments now name it on the next occurrence: the three ledgers say deaf-vs-lost-vs-rendered, the read-back says server-vs-client, and the capture survives the sweep and the next run.

  **(9) WHY NO PRODUCTION CODE CHANGED, said plainly.** The cause measured here is a Realtime tenant rate limit dropping `realtime.send()` payloads under load — not M4 code, not this spec, and not something the application can currently observe. The one application-side number in the chain is `HEARTBEAT_SILENCE_MS = 45_000`, and lowering it would be a **tuning change that makes a red go away**, which is the thing this task forbids — it repairs no drop and shortens no cause. It is also arithmetically interesting rather than obviously wrong: its docblock justifies 45 s as "≤ 2 missed printed-cadence beats" against **§9.1's printed 15 s heartbeat**, while the shipped cron beats every **5 s** (068:1265), so the shipped tolerance is nine missed beats. How long a live draft room may render a state it has moved past is a product definition the spec does not make — filed as **§3 Q49** with the measurement and a recommendation, and tracked as **F312**. **Nothing was retried, slept, skipped, reordered, re-timed or added to any flake policy**, and F308 keeps its ledger row and its blocker.

 **(1) Reproduction first, attribution second (F139’s rule).** Both rows isolate green, so isolation proves nothing; the lever was AMPLIFICATION plus instrumentation, never re-running. Temporary instrumentation (reverted; `use-draft.ts` md5 `0ea07bac…` before = after) logged, per browser and per millisecond, every channel open/sweep/subscribe status, every broadcast and tick with the record’s status and deadline, every `refetchDraft()` with its `fetchStatus`/`failureCount`/`visibilityState` and what it resolved to, plus the raw `phx_join`/`phx_leave`/error frames through `page.on('websocket')`. **F297 fell to a 9-way CPU load + `--repeat-each=6`: 1 red of 6, at its recorded line, first attempt.** **F56 did NOT** — 18 consecutive greens under the same load, including 8 on a stack still hot from the gate’s own `sim draft --type auction --leagues 25 --seed 42` (which cleans up after itself: 0 leagues remain, so the gate’s DB state is not the variable) — so it was reproduced by CONSTRUCTION instead, which is the PR #271 method.

If the e2e sweep did the same, a sim run and an e2e run would clobber each other's fixtures mid-flight — both suites hold the service key and both live on the one shared synthetic season. So this lane sweeps **by IDENTITY** (`nfl_games` by the new `E2E_SEASON_GAME_PREFIX` — an `nfl_games.id` IS its identity, 001:92) and **by LEDGER** (a module-level record of the exact `(season, week, player_id)` tuples and the exact weeks THIS process planted; Playwright runs the lane in one worker, `playwright.config.ts:36-37`). Foreign residue is therefore never deleted — it is REFUSED at the door instead (5 below). **PROVEN, not asserted:** a scratch probe planted `simseason-probe-wk1` + a 2099 `player_stats`/`score_fanout` pair + a week-2 `last_game_ends_at`, ran the e2e sweep, and all four survived byte-for-byte while the door check threw naming the game row; the probe then cleaned itself and the door check passed. A resident foreign row silently changes three answers, each measured from the migration text: `schedule_window_internal` takes `min(nfl_games.kickoff_at)` for the league's first week (`111:262-266`) so one past kickoff pushes every Remix into the E41 OVERRIDE branch and freezes week 1; `week_games_state_internal`'s game gate is `(season, week)`-scoped with NO league column (`116:317-358`) so one non-final row blocks `finalize_matchups` for an unrelated league; and `lineup_kickoff_internal`'s week-datum fallback stops applying once ANY row exists for the week (`112:397-425`), byeing out every club without one. The M0 gate's byte-compare against `fixtures/nfl/2026/wk02/synthetic.jsonl.gz` therefore cannot move (`md5 9f983a36…`, file untouched; `test:gate` 24/24), `SCENARIO_LIBRARY_VERSION` stays **2**, and the library's declared games, beats and determinism split are exactly what they were. Had the honest fix required changing any of those, R801 makes it a §3 question; it did not.

  **(4) A PRE-EXISTING FLAKE THE SCALE EXPOSED, FIXED HERE (this corrects D327(15)(d)).** R921 asserted `named === startedScratched` over EVERY started scratched player. §22.2 is INCREMENTAL: a team is rescored only when a delta lands for a player it starts, and a scratched player emits no line and so no delta — so a team whose only bridged starter is scratched is NEVER recomputed, no per-starter report exists for it, and the worker cannot have named anybody on it.   **(8) PROOF CHAIN (all shown, LOCAL stack only — `.env.local` is PRODUCTION and was untouched).** `npm run test` **217 files / 4,062 tests, green, FIRST attempt (114.8 s)** (was 4,015 — **+47** pins); `npm run test:db` **71 files / 5,398 asserts, PASS**; `npm run test:gate` **24 / 24** (the M0 byte-compare among them); `npm run type-check` clean; `npm run lint` clean ("No ESLint warnings or errors"); `npx vitest run src/lib/leagues/sim/` **181 / 181**. `npm run sim:census` **CLEAN 0 × 9 before AND after every run**, and the residue arm shown exiting 1 on a planted filler row.
