- **D327 — L.D6.1 build mechanics: the number note, the phase split and why the M2 golden did not move, the D299 matrix from the CURRENT schema (and the two axes that no longer exist), the SCENARIO BRIDGE and exactly what it costs, the ONE clock and the interleaved timeline, the one instant that is not virtual, one scenario per run (a mechanism, not a preference), the seven invariants and the three that cannot be planted, what the sweep refuses to encode, what "zero worker errors" counts, the reconcile classification, no `--speed` and why, the run id and what a replay reproduces, F199's durable fix demonstrated, the proof chain.**
  **Number note (D161 — measured 2026-09-08 on `main` @ `103bda2`):** `D327` / `F283` → 0 each ⇒ D327 and F283–F285 taken here (no R — no review yet). Migration heads stay **122 / 070** (no schema change ⇒ no `db reset` owed, no checklists §8.1–8.4, no HELD-range extension); no typegen (the hand-written alias block is untouched); spec unchanged. Action-id prefix **ad6** for `season-sweep-db.test.ts` (measured free).
  **(1) THE PHASE SPLIT — one `keepLeagues` flag, and the M2 golden is unmoved.** `runDraftSim` gained `keepLeagues?: boolean`: the start-of-run stale sweep still runs, only the `finally` sweep is deferred to the SEASON runner's own `finally`, so the run is still swept exactly once and a cleanup failure is still an invariant failure. `gate-m2.sh:78` / `gate-m3.sh` pass neither `season` nor `keepLeagues`, so their behaviour is byte-identical. The D299 axes are drawn from a SEPARATE stream (`deriveStream(seed, 'season:matrix')`), never from `rng` — `plan.test.ts`'s stored-literal golden matrix at seed 42 is re-asserted inside the new season describe so a future season edit that leaked into the shared stream fails where the edit was made. Season mode DOES change two draft-plan inputs on its own path and says so in a pin: `rounds = SEASON_ROUNDS (7)` with a roster preset carrying ONE starting slot per scoring position (the M2 preset starts QB/RB/WR only, which would make a bridged TE/K/D-ST line unreachable by construction — a scenario the sim cannot observe is a decorative one), and `humanCount = min(team_count, BOT_POOL_SIZE)` (every human seat is a lineup the sim can set). Those change how many persona draws the shared `rng` makes, so a SEASON plan's sizes differ from a draft-only plan's at the same seed — pinned as a stored literal (`[16, 12, 16, 8]`) rather than left to be discovered.
  **(2) THE MATRIX IS BUILT FROM THE CURRENT SCHEMA, and two of D299's axes are RETIREMENTS, not gaps.** "strict/lax locks" cannot be `lineup_lock`: Q34(A)/migration 114 retired `first_game_of_week` and the enum is single-valued, and Q35/migration 115 retired `player_game_lock` (the strict Zod object refuses the key) — the ONE surviving lock axis is `allow_illegal_lineups`, and `plan.test.ts` PINS both retirements so the matrix regains an arm the day either returns. "divisions 1/2" was cut to 1 by Q30 (d) and the engine ignores the value, so the matrix does not draw it. What IS drawn, guaranteed by construction (the `plan.ts:96-112` discipline): both `schedule_mode`s at ≥2 leagues, ≥1 `median_game` at ≥3, ≥1 `second_opponent` at ≥4, ≥1 `allow_illegal_lineups` OFF at ≥5. **[AMENDED 2026-09-08 by the fix round (R918).** As first built, the two MODE-GATED arms were not guaranteed at all: `medianIndex` / `secondIndex` were drawn without forcing that league to `h2h`, and both flags are gated on `scheduleMode === 'h2h'`, so the free-league coin (`rng() < 0.25 → total_points`) could flip the guarantee league and drop the arm. MEASURED over seeds 1-300: at 6 leagues **19** seeds lost median and **21** lost second opponent; at 4 leagues 22 / 24; at 3 leagues 19 lost median — including seed **42**, the very seed the single-seed pin used. With `scripts/sim.ts` defaulting the seed to a wall-clock value, ~6-7 % of unseeded runs certified a thinner matrix than this paragraph claims and exited 0. FIXED: the guarantee indices are FORCED to `h2h` before the coin is tossed (`plan.ts:296-300`, `forcedH2h`), and `plan.test.ts` now asserts the guarantee over seeds **1..200** at 2/3/4/6/25 leagues plus the four failing seeds by name, rather than sampling one. Re-measured after the fix: **0 of 300** seeds lose any guaranteed arm at its threshold.]** Two couplings the schema refuses to break are respected rather than rediscovered: `total_points` ⇒ `playoff_teams = 0` (v2.16.25 / Q39 (C); 118 and `validateLeagueSettings` both refuse the pair) and `playoff_start_week = regular_season_weeks + 1` (Q10). A points race also carries no median/second game — the mode already scores every team against the field (§11.7).
  **(3) THE SCENARIO BRIDGE — the decision, and what it costs.** §23.6's world is EIGHTEEN players (`syn-g{1,2,3}-{qb,rb,wr,te,k,def}`) in three games, and none of those ids exists in `players`; the sim seeds NO players (`runner.ts:56-58`, the R286 lesson) and `ingestWeek` counts an unknown id into `unknownPlayer` and writes nothing — so as built, no drafted starter could ever receive a line. **Taken: a BIJECTIVE RENAMING** onto 18 real player ids, chosen per (game, position) from the players whose `players.team` is one of that game's two clubs, best ADP first, ties by id. It works with no change to the slate because the library's three games already carry REAL NFL abbreviations — DAL@PHI, BUF@KC, SEA@SF — so `players.team` still joins `nfl_games.home_team/away_team` for every bridged player and 112/115's lock datum is untouched. **PRESERVED, and pinned:** `makeScenario`'s DEFAULT output (the M0 gate byte-compares `happy_path` at 2026 wk2 against `fixtures/nfl/2026/wk02/synthetic.jsonl.gz`, so a transform that moved it would force a `SCENARIO_LIBRARY_VERSION` bump — this transform is downstream and additive), and the library's documented determinism SPLIT: the renaming is a pure function of the environment's `players` rows and NOT of the scenario id, so two scenarios at one seed still emit identical lines for the same bridged player, which is exactly what the `provider_outage` back-fill proof rests on (`scenario.ts:15-18`; `ingest-week-db.test.ts:435`). **THE COST, said plainly rather than buried:** a bridged player's numbers are `finalLine(seed, <real id>)`, so the slot's VALUES differ from the fixture's for the corresponding synthetic slot, and a run only reproduces against the same `players` table — which is why the run PRINTS its whole 18-line bridge map, so a replay in a different pool is visible line by line instead of silently different. **THE COVERAGE COST, also said:** eighteen players is the library's law, not an artefact of the bridge, so a sim league holds at most 18 scorable players however many teams it seats and every other starter is a lawful `no_stat_row`; the run MEASURES and prints `bridged N rostered / N started` and the `no_stat_row` count rather than implying more. Options not taken: seeding the 18 ids as real `players` rows (breaks `runner.ts:56-58` outright and adds a `players`-row teardown to F199's blast radius), and planting `player_stats` directly (forfeits `source='synthetic'`, the gate's own zero-real-data instrument).
  **(4) ONE CLOCK, AND THE TIMELINE INTERLEAVES WEEKS.** A single step-driven `VirtualClock` (speed 0) carries the whole run and reaches three places at once. Virtual time is monotonic, so the run is ONE sorted timeline across every driven week — which is also how a real season behaves: week W's correction window (start + 8d 6h) closes AFTER week W+1 has opened (start + 7d), and the driver interleaves them rather than pretending weeks are disjoint. Per week the structural instants are open (`starts_at + 1 min`), close (one minute after the last in-week game ends — the poll that first sees every in-week game final is what stamps `nfl_weeks.last_game_ends_at` via `weekBounds`, so the advance a minute later has its datum) and finalize (`correction_window_ends_at + 1 min`); between them the scenario's OWN declared instants are walked (announcements, the ~90-min inactives publication, kickoffs, mid-game, final, charted SLA/post, three polls inside an outage window plus one after it, corrections, revisions). At every instant: `ingestWeek` → `runScoreWeekBatch({leagueIds})` → `lineup_lock_tick`; advance runs TWICE at each structural instant (the recorded idempotence proof — `dev-drive-inseason-week.ts:273-277`). A POSTPONED game contributes only its announcement: by 116's rule it has LEFT the week, so there is no in-week instant to poll for it. The re-anchor is a pure SHIFT that preserves every offset from the week's start, and it is EXACT by arithmetic rather than luck — `synthetic-season.ts` reuses the 2026 opener's shape, so shifting the library's window end lands it on the target week's stored `correction_window_ends_at` to the millisecond; `assertAnchorConsistent` re-checks that against the row it read and THROWS rather than run a week whose window it has moved. Anchored `nfl_games.id`s are week-unique (`simseason-2099-wNN-AWY@HOM`) because the PK is the id and a re-used one would move week N's row out of week N — out of a week already final.
  **(5) THE ONE INSTANT THAT IS NOT VIRTUAL.** `set_lineup` and `roster_add_drop` accept NO caller clock — their DEFINER wrappers pass transaction `now()` (112:1233, 113:912; D307(3)). A lineup the sim sets is therefore set at WALL time, which on 2099 lies before every kickoff, so nothing is ever locked at submit: **this harness cannot observe a lineup-edit LOCK REFUSAL**, stated rather than worked around. Locks are exercised where they live — `lineup_lock_tick` at an injected `p_now` (E42's evaluation-time read), and `flex_move`'s assertion captures `nfl_games.kickoff_at` either side of the announcement. Week 1's lineups go through the REAL door under each manager's own JWT (D100); a PLACEHOLDER seat has no manager, so its lineup goes through the COMMISSIONER arm of the same RPC with a reason (D290/R738's interim audit posture, which posts the system message). **A measured bug worth recording:** inferring the manager from `teams.owner_id` is WRONG — a placeholder seat is owned by the commissioner (the D96 capacity remedy), so `owner_id` finds a client that is nonetheless not that team's manager and 112:684 refuses for want of a reason; 34 of a 6-league run's lineups were refused exactly that way until the read moved to `league_members`. Later weeks are NOT re-submitted: they come from `lineup_carry_internal` at the advance (D293), which is the path a real league takes and therefore the one worth driving. The submitted map is a greedy first fit by eligibility and is NOT a TS mirror of the matcher (D289/D33) — the SERVER's `lineup_fit_internal` decides the canonical placement and the sim keeps what came back, which is what invariant 2 then re-checks against the same oracle.
  **(6) ONE SCENARIO PER RUN — a mechanism, not a preference.** `nfl_games` has no league column and locks read it by `(season, week, nfl_team)` (`pool_game_lock_any_internal` / `lineup_kickoff_internal`; 115:225-344, 112:380-384), so planting `flex_move`'s moved kickoff for one league moves it for EVERY league whose roster touches that club: a hundred leagues on one synthetic season cannot each carry a different scenario's slate. L.D6.3 runs the library as nine stages; mixing scenarios inside one run would require partitioning club abbreviations across league cohorts — a design decision to be recorded, not assumed. Related and worth saying: **pg_cron is INERT here**, and 2099 is what makes it so — 116:1337-1349 schedules all three jobs UNSCOPED at wall-clock `now()` on every stack including local, and season 2099's instants are all in the wall-clock future, so the unscoped cron finds nothing due for a sim league. That is also why every job call still passes `p_league_id` and why the run must not leave leagues behind.
  **(7) THE SEVEN INVARIANTS, AND THE THREE PLANTS THE CHAIN REFUSES.** exclusivity · lineup legality (through `lineup_fit_internal` as service role) · standings ≡ recompute (`rebuild_team_week_results`, `changed=false` AND the two md5 digests equal) · pool/roster mirror · PF once per week · zero final-cell rewrites · zero unhandled worker errors. Each is a pure function over an audit snapshot, each failure names league AND week, each is falsifiable alone (31 unit pins) and PLANTED IN THE DATABASE (12 stack cells) against 001–122. **Three plants the chain REFUSES outright, and each refusal is recorded as defence in depth rather than worked around:** roster exclusivity (`UNIQUE(league_id, player_id)`, 072:147 — refused even to the service role, so the live check can never redden and the CONSTRAINT is the proof under D267, with the checker's falsifiability in the unit pin); a NULL `scoring_rules_snapshot` on an `in_season` league (`trg_leagues_snapshot_guard` / D43); a CORRUPT one (`trg_leagues_scoring_rules_valid`, which fires ALWAYS and validates the §7.3.3.1 shape in-database); and `team_lineups.slot_map` cannot be made non-object (`team_lineups_slot_map_is_object`). All four refusals are ASSERTED in the suite. What IS plantable, and is: a started player on nobody's roster and one player started by two teams (`slot_map` is unconstrained JSONB); an RB in the QB slot key (the oracle returns a non-empty `unplaced`); a perturbed `team_week_results.points`; a pool state flipped to `free_agent`; a direct UPDATE of a FINAL matchup; and a starter with no `players` row, which is a genuine `LeagueWeekFailure` quarantined per-league (D292) and carries invariant 1's other arm with it.
  **(8) ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING, because invariant 3's probe WRITES.** 117:855 re-runs `week_results_write_internal` unconditionally and 117:858-866 UPDATEs `league_weeks.median_score` every time, so `changed:false` means the resulting ROWS are byte-identical, NOT that nothing was written. The collector therefore takes invariant 6's final-cell snapshot BEFORE calling the rebuild — a sweep that ordered them the other way would trip its own invariant. That is not theory: the stack suite's own final-cell revert was incomplete until an extra audit re-derived the reverted matchup into `team_week_results` (measured 2026-09-08 as an ordering red in a full-suite run), and the comment there says so.
  **(9) WHAT THE SWEEP REFUSES TO ENCODE (R801).** Q38 (PA is explicitly PROVISIONAL — PF-once only; never Σ PF ≡ Σ PA, which would ratify unruled law), Q42 (a starter with no line — the worker's REPORT is asserted, never the arithmetic consequence of either reading; the count is printed), Q37 (a held week is CLASSIFIED with its lawful explanation and never counted as a failure), Q40 (nothing asserts against `team_lineups.locked_at`, which is a RECORD, not the lock). **F273's DEFAULT-0 hole is NAMED, not closed and not papered over:** R890 asks this sweep to assert "an unscored regular row is NULL until its first batch", and on the current chain that assertion RED-FAILS by construction (109:162-163's `DEFAULT 0` + 110's column-less INSERT). L.D6.1 is a gate task, not a schema task, so the sweep NEVER reads a `0` as "unscored" — invariant 5 sums `team_week_results.points`, the worker's own output, precisely because a `0` in the matchups columns cannot be distinguished from a DEFAULT. Hardening that confusion into a gate condition would be worse than leaving the hole visible; F273's closer is amended to a standalone schema PR.
  **(10) WHAT "ZERO UNHANDLED WORKER ERRORS" COUNTS.** The worker's `problems[]` is deliberately loud and NAMES lawful states: `drain scored nothing: <reason>` (R875 calls `queue_empty` / `all_leased` / `all_deferred` informational), a `week_final` skip (which is D295(b) WORKING), a `week_not_open` hold, and "no team starts a mapped player this week (all bench/unstarted)" — §22.2's incremental rule stated out loud. In a sim that polls at every declared instant most drains legitimately have nothing to do, and counting those would make invariant 7 fire on the pipeline behaving correctly. §23.2's "job failures: 0" is about FAILURES, so invariant 7 counts exactly: `outcome === 'failed'` with its error, `ack_missed.lease_lost + gone > 0` (the one window a stale write can land in — R869/R873/F263(f)), the three job payloads' `failures[]` (F244/R798: those arrays ARE truthful even where the payload's counters are not), and any other `problems[]` line. Everything filtered is COUNTED BY REASON and printed as WORKER NOTES.
  **(11) RECONCILE IS EVIDENCE; THREE FINDINGS ARE INVARIANTS.** `drift` + `twr_mirror_drift` → invariant 3, `pool_mirror_broken` → invariant 4. Every other ALERT is surfaced into `problems[]` (loud, RED) EXCEPT four that are CLASSIFIED with a named lawful reason and counted: `starter_final_game_no_line` (the §23.6 world has 18 players and three games, so every other starter on a scenario club has a final game and no line — Q42), `no_game_rows` for a week the run never drove (`--weeks` bounds the slate), `stuck_queue` for a player NO run league rosters (D313(2)'s scope seam: a scoped drain leaves the row for the unscoped production one), and `game_not_final_late` for a game the scenario declared postponed (E43). No migration (heads stay 122 / 070), no typegen, no `db reset` (no schema change), no RPC, no `src/lib/leagues/**` production line; spec unchanged. **(1) "Serialize the realtime + auction suites" was never a fix:** `vitest.config.ts` gives the `stack` project `fileParallelism: false` (L.B7.1's F52 design) and `npm run test:stack` runs that project alone — every one of the five sightings ran one file at a time on the runner; the race was inside the cell. `.github/workflows/db.yml`'s "Database-backed tests" step is unchanged in what it runs. **(2) `draft-realtime-db.test.ts` — the member-side heartbeat (F74 → F264).** MECHANISM, read from the installed code and then reproduced: realtime-js 2.101.1's `removeChannel()` awaits its own `channel.unsubscribe()` — which, on an already-closed channel, still pushes a second `phx_leave` frame (`@supabase/phoenix` 0.4.0 `Channel.leave` → `Push.send` → `Socket.push` sends whenever the socket is open) — tears the channel down, and if `channels.length === 0` calls `disconnect()` WITHOUT awaiting it (`RealtimeClient.js:221-229`). Phoenix's `disconnect` → `teardown` → `waitForBufferDone(conn)` checks `conn.bufferedAmount`; with the leave frame not yet flushed it defers `close()` by 150/300/450/600 ms (`phoenix.cjs.js:1568-1602`), during which the socket is still `open`. The suite's next channel — test (b)'s member probe, created within ms of test (a)'s `finally` — therefore subscribes on a socket already sentenced: the join is acked (`SUBSCRIBED`), then the deferred `close()` lands, `onConnClose` → `triggerChanError` → the channel goes `errored`, and nothing rejoins (`Channel` rejoins only `if (this.socket.isConnected())`; `closeWasClean` suppresses the socket's reconnect). Six direct ticks and ~9 cron beats then broadcast into a channel no socket carries: `expected undefined to be truthy` after ~50.8 s, the four CI reds verbatim (#263 run 34011211671 att. 1 at 50,777 ms; #267 run 34177879274 att. 2 at 50,858 ms). Locally the suite stays green because the close handshake completes in ~1 ms and vitest's inter-test hop is longer, so the next channel finds `closed` and opens a fresh socket — the runner's slower flush/handshake is the whole difference. **REPRODUCED 2026-09-08** (a scratch copy of the suite, deleted after; the runner's condition simulated by pinning `conn.bufferedAmount` non-zero at the release sites): OLD harness → `[probe] member probe status: SUBSCRIBED socket: open` → `socket 3s later: closed channel state: errored` → **the CI assertion verbatim at 51,120 ms** (2 of 3 forced runs; the third heard one beat before the close — which is exactly the slow-runner sensitivity); NEW harness under the SAME condition → `released, state: closed` at both sites, `socket 3s later: open channel state: joined`, **3/3 green in 9.4 s**. FIX (test file only): `releaseChannel(client, channel)` = `unsubscribe` → `teardown()` → **`await client.realtime.disconnect()`** → assert `connectionState() === 'closed'` (loud otherwise), used at the readiness gate and test (a)'s `finally` — after it the next `subscribe()` provably opens a fresh socket (phoenix `connect()` with `conn === null`). Test (b)'s fire-then-poll stays as the honest wait on a LIVE socket; no budget moved. F74 said "awaiting `removeChannel` does not close the race" — true, because `removeChannel` never awaits the `disconnect()` it starts; awaiting the DISCONNECT does. The sweep F74 asked for: `removeChannel` appears in exactly three stack suites — this one (fixed), `auction-realtime-db` (a dedicated gate client, `await removeChannel` + `disconnect()` before any test channel — safe), `inseason-realtime-db` (one socket per cell, R847(iii) — safe). **(3) `auction-api-db.test.ts:569` — the launcher's bid (R795's cell).** NOT a race, and the F113 freeze could not have touched it: the asserted `body.draft.current_nomination.high_bidder_team_id` is read INSIDE `draft_place_bid`'s own transaction, under the drafts row lock, so no concurrent actor (cron or otherwise) can change the high bidder between the launcher's write and the response — the only writer that can is 091's `draft_mock_cpu_respond_internal`, called from the same `draft_place_bid_internal`. Its candidate value is `draft_mock_cpu_bid_value(draft, seq, team, pass, …)` with ±15 % noise seeded per (draft uuid, seq, team, **pass = live bid count**): the nomination's ladder ends at price X where every CPU's pass-k value folds, and the launcher's `X+3` makes pass k+1 re-draw every CPU's value afresh — any CPU whose new value reaches X+4 answers in the same RPC and holds the high bid in the response. **SIMULATED through the real IMMUTABLE functions on the local stack** (P4 = ADP rank 4, $200 / 16 slots / 8 seats, need 1.0, 3,000 fresh draft uuids): ladder end X mean 51.5 (42–53), max 22 rungs; **149 / 3,000 = 4.97 % answered `X+3` in-RPC** — the per-run failure probability of the old cell, independent of load (18/18 green in isolation is a 40 % event at that rate, not evidence of a race). - **D323 — L.D5.2 build mechanics: the number note, the box read (why a new GET, the ONE implementation, what a starter is), the badge as a stored status, the Q42/E61 rendering, the three §16.5.3 variants, the degraded banner's poll, the room (one channel, one invalidation list), the week resolution, the browser pass (with the DEFAULT-0 observation), what was deliberately not built, the proof chain.** **Number note (D161 — measured 2026-09-08 on `main` @ `671157e`):** `D323` / `F272` / `F273` / `F274` / `F275` / `R887` → 0 each ⇒ D323, F272–F275 taken here (no R — no review yet). No migration (heads stay 122 / 070), no typegen (`database.ts` untouched), no `db reset` (no schema touched), no spec change — the §15.3 route list does not print the box GET and §16.2's `matchup-view` row does not name it; recorded HERE, not folded (the L.D5.3 precedent for `POST …/schedule/matchup`); the reviewer may ask for a §15.3/§16.2 annotation. **(1) The box read, and why it is a new GET.** §11.4 says "the matchup view refetches box-score lines on `scores_updated`" and §16.2 says "Live Mode patterns" — per-starter lines with per-starter points. The schema stores no per-player points (D321(7): "the report carries them; L.D5.2 renders box lines from `player_stats` per §11.4") and the client may compute no score (CLAUDE.md; the F226 posture extended to the UI). So `box-score-service.ts` computes them SERVER-side through the worker's own exported pipeline: `computeTeamWeek(snapshot, teamId, refs, statsByPlayer)` — never `scorePlayerWeek`/`resolveRules`/`deriveTierIndicators` called here (pinned in `inseason-routes.test.ts`: the service must call `computeTeamWeek` and must not call the three) — so the box's per-starter points, its `pending[]` and its `no_stat_row[]` are the worker's verbatim, and the box total is the same function the door stores from. The page still shows the DOOR'S cell as THE number (`matchups.home_score`); the box total is labelled `Box total` and is the same function over the same rows — they differ only while a batch is in flight. `assertSnapshotScorable` runs before any starter (the D292 gate applied to a read). A STARTER is the canonical `slot_map` (§12.13/D293) read exactly as `startersOf` reads it for scoring — never the derived `starters` JSONB (pinned: no `select('starters`) — with slot labels from `roster_settings.starting_slots`; an empty seat is `reason: 'empty'`, an id with no `players` row `unknown_player` (named, never a silent 0). **(2) The Live Mode phase is a stored status.** `starterPhase(nflTeam, games)`: the week's `nfl_games` rows for the player's `players.team` — `live` → Now playing, `final` → Done, `scheduled`/`postponed`/NULL → Up next, no row in a week that HAS rows → Bye (§11.2's own reading), no rows at all → Up next with `game: null` (the F238 posture). No clock anywhere in the file (the `src/lib/leagues/**` fence): the stack cell plants a `scheduled` game with a 2001 kickoff literal and it reads Up next. - **D322 — L.D2.3 build mechanics: the number note, the two persisted surfaces (122), the two minute-crons and why the cadence lives inside the invocation, the plan read from the tables (the window closes on observation), the lease inequality, the reconciliation's classification order (why not every mismatch is drift), what each cron costs when idle, the hosted go-live sequence (F228/F238), what was deliberately not built, the proof chain.** **Number note (D161 — measured 2026-09-07 on `main` @ `a46f45f`):** `D322` → 1 (D321(10)'s "→ 0 each" mention, not a definition) / `F265` / `F266` / `F267` / `R876` → 0 each ⇒ D322, F265–F267 taken here (no R — no review yet); migration head 121 ⇒ **122**, pgTAP head 069 ⇒ **070** (`ls`); HELD `082-121 → 082-122`; typegen `npx supabase gen types typescript --local` with the alias block re-appended — **+27/−1**, the ONE deletion the ack's `Args` line replaced by its 4-argument form (a signature change, said). **(1) `system_flags` (F217).** One row per key, `value` jsonb (is-object CHECK), world-SELECT, no client write policy — the F217 recommendation as written. Keys: `stats_degraded` → `{degraded, consecutive_failures, last_failure_at, last_success_at, last_error, provider}`; `ingest_poll:<season>:<week>` → `{completed_at, provider}`. `ingest-flags.ts` loads the tracker from the count BEFORE a poll (`DegradationTracker` gains an `initialConsecutiveFailures` constructor argument + a `consecutiveFailures` getter — additive) and persists it AFTER; the week's key is written ONLY after `ingestWeek` returned `ok` (both writes landed), `completed_at = report.polledAt` (the poll's injected instant — the stamp every row it wrote carries). `ingestWeek` itself is untouched by this (the harness/sim/gates run it against nothing but the tables it owns); the ROUTE owns the flag. The worker's `lastPollCompletedAt` seam (D321(1)) is bound to `readLastPollCompletedAt` — F263(e)'s first half. **(2) `deferred_until` + the pair re-authored (R872 — F263(e)'s second half).** 121's claim could not evaluate readiness (the F218 predicate needs the last-poll surface the SQL could not read; `week_not_open` is per LEAGUE, which a queue row does not know), so a permanently held row sat at the head of every claim and starved it at ≥ `batchSize`. The closer R872 named: the ack takes the held rows back with `deferred_until = time.now() + deferSeconds` (30 s default; D291 — the deferral reads no clock the worker does not) and the claim skips a row while `deferred_until > p_now` (claimable AT the instant — 070 D4/D5). By-stamp like the delete: a row re-stamped under the lease is released, never deferred (a newer delta is ready — 070 F1). The deferral and the release are ONE statement per row (unleased AND deferred — never leased-and-hidden). Ingestion's enqueue payload gains `deferred_until: null`, so PostgREST's upsert clears the hold on every real delta (070 E2; the worker stack suite's `enqueue` helper mirrors the payload). The ack's return gains `deferred`; `released` keeps 121's meaning (every row handed back) — 069's five return literals moved in place. The empty-claim reason gains `all_deferred` beside `all_leased` (both informational, R875) with the queue's counts on the problem line. **(3) Two minute-ROUTES, the cadence inside — BUILT AND UNSCHEDULED (R884 / Q43, the #268 fix round).** Vercel's finest cron is one minute AND ONLY ON A PAID PLAN: the project is on HOBBY, which refuses `* * * * *` at deploy time — the #268 head with both routes at `* * * * *` FAILED to deploy while CI passed (the Vercel bot: "Hobby accounts are limited to daily cron jobs") — so `vercel.json` carries NO entry for `sync-live` / `score-week` (the daily `reconcile` stays; daily is allowed) and the scheduler is Q43's ruling (Vercel Pro — the recommendation — / an external minute pinger / pg_cron + pg_net). Both routes are scheduler-agnostic: any caller presenting `CRON_SECRET` once a minute is the production cadence, because the cadence lives inside the invocation. §14 asks for 20–30 s polls and 5–10 s drains. Each route runs a bounded loop under its `maxDuration` (60 s): `sync-live` polls at 0 / 20 / 40 s (a round starts only while its start + cadence < the 45 s budget — pinned at the D146 pair 40,001 / 40,000 ms), `score-week` drains every 5 s for 50 s (a FULL claim drains again at once). Overlap between consecutive invocations is by design and is what the lease (121) and the deferral (122) serialize. **(4) The plan is read from the tables (§23.3; F216(b)).** `planLivePoll(games, weeks, now)`: HOT when an in-week game (`scheduled` | `live`; 001's NULL status reads `scheduled`; `postponed` has left the window, E43) has `kickoff_at ≤ now + 15 min` and has NOT been observed `final` — which is R711's rule made structural: the window closes on OBSERVATION, never on the clock, so the poll that sees the last game `final` is the one that stamps `last_game_ends_at` (F238's release writer), and a game the provider never flips (Q37) costs THREE polls a minute — the plan is hot ⇒ rounds at 0 / 20 / 40 s, `resetScheduleMemo()` before each ⇒ three ~2 MB nflverse CSV reads per minute, ≈ 6 MB/min ≈ 8.6 GB/day for the rest of the season (R878's correction of this note's original "one poll a minute") — said in the plan and named by the reconciliation as `game_not_final_late`: a warn while the week's window is ahead, an ALERT once the week is past it and can no longer finalize (R878). SWEEP on the top-of-hour minute of the injected instant (a flex move reaches `nfl_games` within the hour, E42) and on EVERY invocation while the season has zero game rows (F228: the composite provider's nflverse half lands the calendar without a manual run). IDLE otherwise — no provider call. The current calendar week is the greatest `starts_at ≤ now` (112's datum), week 1 before the season. `getCurrentNflWeek()` (Sleeper's `/state/nfl` behind Next's fetch cache — an external call and wall-clock math) is gone from this route; `sync-stats` still uses it (a launch-surface route, not this task's). The nflverse CSV is memoized PER ROUND (`withScheduleMemo` — reset before each round so a status flip is observed): ~2 MB × 3 per hot minute, once per idle hour — said, not hidden (F216's cost question). `score-week`'s `isHot` is the same plan, so an idle season costs one claim RPC per minute. TWO RESIDUALS (R880 / R882, the #268 review): the sweep's target is the CURRENT week only, so a week is not re-polled between the next week's `starts_at` and its own `correction_window_ends_at` (~30 h — 2026 week 1: Wed 09-16 04:00Z to Thu 09-17 10:00Z); an in-window Wed/Thu correction is M6 L.E2's `sync-stat-corrections` (**F270**; Sleeper's Tuesday corrections ARE covered — the week stays current until Wed 04:00Z and the hourly sweep re-polls it); and the composite's `getInactives` is EXPOSED and consumed by NOTHING on the production path (`ingest-week.ts` never calls it) until M5's auto-sub (F211) / L.E2 — "carries nflverse's inactives" means exposed, not landed (**F269(c)**). **(5) The lease inequality (F263(f)/R874).** `SCORE_WEEK_LEASE_SECONDS = 120 ≥ SCORE_WEEK_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS (60) + CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS (30)`; the route exports `maxDuration = SCORE_WEEK_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS` and `route.test.ts` asserts the inequality against the route's OWN export (a Next route module may export only Next's fields, so the pin lives beside it). No migration (heads stay 120 / 068 — the door's `total_points` arm EXISTS in 119, so F259(d)'s CREATE OR REPLACE authorization was not needed), no typegen (`database.ts` untouched), no `db reset` — **as first landed; the #267 fix round (10) ADDS migration 121 / pgTAP 069, typegen +22/−0 and a fresh `db reset` 001–121.** **(1) The module.** `src/lib/leagues/scoring/score-week-worker.ts` — D292's shape: a pure module with injected IO (D12's `IngestIo` pattern): `deps = {time, db, lastPollCompletedAt?}`, `opts = {batchSize?, leagueIds?}`; `time` only stamps the report (`ran_at`) — NO scoring decision reads a clock: the week's `league_weeks.status` is the door datum (§23.3), the readiness predicate compares two stored stamps, and the D3 fence covers the file. `db` is a service-role `SupabaseClient<Database>` — the queue is service-role-only (109) and the door refuses a JWT (119). `leagueIds` is the stack lane's scope seam (D313(2)'s shape): a scoped drain consumes ONLY rows it scored for a scoped league — another suite's rows on the shared stack are never touched; production passes nothing. The pure helpers (`deliveredLine`, `scoreStarter`, `computeTeamWeek`, `startersOf`, `irKeysOf`, `bookOwnerForWeek`, `applicableKeys`, `assertSnapshotScorable`, `normalizePosition`) are exported so L.D2.3's reconciliation recomputes through the SAME functions (one implementation, D33/D57 — never a second dot product). **(2) The queue contract — the race that forced ingestion's one change.** PostgREST cannot express `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (§22.3's in-database claim idiom) and a claim RPC would have been a migration in the worker lane, so the drain is read-then-ack: the worker reads stamped rows, scores, and DELETEs `WHERE (season, week, player_id) AND enqueued_at = <the stamp it read>`. With L.D2.1's `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` enqueue that ack had a lost-delta hole: a poll landing between the worker's stats read and its delete would fold into the still-queued row WITHOUT moving anything, the worker would delete it having scored the OLD line, and nothing would ever re-enqueue it (the next poll's diff reads the stored row as current; §23.2's reconciliation only alerts) — a silently stale score, the CLAUDE.md class. Closed on the ingestion side in this PR (`ingest-week.ts`, the one line + its report): a re-enqueue is `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET enqueued_at` — one row per PK still (D292's dedupe; 057's SQL-level pin unchanged), the stamp moved to the newer poll's instant, so the by-stamp delete MISSES a row re-stamped mid-drain and the next drain scores the newer line; `IngestStatsReport.restamped` tells the re-stamped from the new (`enqueued`). The five orderings of (claim, stats read, ack) × (enqueue, stats write) are walked in the worker's banner; the stack suite injects the race deterministically after the claim read (a `select` interceptor) and shows the ack miss + the next drain's fresh score. ~~Two concurrent drains are safe by idempotence (both score, the door reports `no_change` for the second, the second delete matches 0) — SKIP LOCKED was an efficiency device, not a correctness one; a claim RPC is F263(d) if contention ever shows.~~ **FALSE — R866 (the #267 review; corrected in (10)):** two overlapping drains with a poll between them left a STALE score in `matchups` and an EMPTY queue — the door is last-writer-wins by design (119's `IS DISTINCT FROM` is idempotence for identical re-sends, not ordering), so drain B consuming the re-stamped row while drain A was still in flight let A's old score land last with nothing left to re-enqueue it. SKIP LOCKED was never an efficiency device: the claim RPC with a LEASE (121) is what makes §22.3's sentence true. **(3) The map's two halves.** §22.2/D292 name `league_rosters(player_id)` as the fan-out index; the worker takes the LEAGUE from it and NOT the team: the TEAM is the one whose `team_lineups` row for (season, week) STARTS the player. That one split honours F262(d) for free (120 re-points rosters whole but past-week lineups stay the predecessor's, so a past-week correction lands on the retired franchise's row and the successor is never minted a row — pinned both ways: P's week-1 row moves, S has no week-1 row, `league_standings_projected` folds week 1 once), keeps E34's kept-locked-slot semantics (a dropped-after-kickoff starter still scores for the team that started him while his row stays), and makes "bench" exact (§22.2's incremental rule: a rostered player no lineup starts triggers no recompute — `bench_player_ids` on the report). What it does NOT reach: a player dropped to FA/waivers after his game (no roster row anywhere in the league) — a correction on him does not find the league; §23.2's reconciliation (L.D2.3) recomputes from lineups and alerts — F263(a). `total_points` seeding walks the lineage backward (`bookOwnerForWeek`: while the predecessor's `retired_at_week > week`) so a seated successor is seeded for its own weeks only. **(4) Three starter states, and pending is position-scoped.** L.A1.10's parity fixtures model a position's line as its OWN keys (a QB line never carries `def_points_allowed`; K/D-ST keys are `pending` in a QB's breakdown by design), so "any pending key ⇒ team NULL" would NULL every team under every template forever. The worker scopes both the DELIVERED line and the PENDING set by `POSITION_SCORABLE_KEYS` (the validator's guardrail-3 table — one definition; the D/ST raw sources delivered to D/ST lines only, so a QB's `def_points_allowed = 0` — ingestion writes the whole column surface, D303 — can never one-hot `def_pa_0`); advanced keys apply to every position until the registry says otherwise (F263(b)). SCORED: a line, every applicable key delivered (a stored 0 is a delivered zero). PENDING: a line, an applicable key absent (the charted/tracking two-phase, §23.5) — the team is NULL; on a `total_points` league a pending team after a provisional row exists KEEPS its last value (the door never deletes — F259(d)) and the report names it (`pending_kept_provisional`) — F263 **[R873: the window reports as `lease_lost` OR `gone` — `gone` when the re-claiming drain finished first; the alert is on the SUM.]** (c) carries the withdraw question. NO STAT LINE: 0 and named (`no_stat_row`) — Q42's reading. **(5) The quarantine, measured unreachable for a frozen snapshot.** `assertSnapshotScorable` (resolve + score an empty line for all six positions) runs BEFORE any team is computed; a throw fails the league-week by name (`snapshot_missing` / `snapshot_corrupt: <the calculator's own message naming the key>`), nothing is written for it, the drain continues (the first cut's D292 posture). On this chain the state cannot be reached through the column: 059's guard refuses NULL on an `in_season` league, 104's wall refuses a non-finite coefficient ("Bounds … must be a finite number; got \"corrupt\"") AND the D15 charted placeholder (a `reserved` key fails the scorable allowlist) — three refusals pinned as stack cells — so the stack suite drives the worker's quarantine and E61 paths through a `leagues`-read overlay over the REAL door (the DB rows stay valid). Consequence for E61 on the record: no shipped or fork-able snapshot can pay an undelivered key today (the Q9 lesson, structurally), so the pending path is machinery-proof until a real advanced key is registered scorable. **(6) The report is the loud surface.** No `worker_errors` table exists; `BatchReport` carries per-league-week entries (`outcome` ∈ written · no_change · nothing_writable · skipped · held · failed, the door's report verbatim, the computed teams with per-starter points/pending/no_stat_row) and a flat `problems[]` — every quarantine, every door skip by name, `nothing_writable`, a held week, a re-stamped ack miss, an empty drain's reason (`queue_empty` / `nothing_ready` / `nothing_mapped` / `nothing_in_scope`). The lease serializes in-flight processing PER ROW across drains: ingestion's re-stamp (`ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET enqueued_at` — PostgREST SETs only the payload's columns, so the lease survives; pinned in 069 E1b as the SQL twin and on the stack through PostgREST itself) moves the stamp under A's lease, B's claim SKIPS the row (`all_leased` on B's report — never "queue empty"), A's ack misses by stamp and releases it, and the next drain scores the newer line. Both pinned on the stack (a raw claim that never acks hides its rows until the virtual clock passes 120 s; a thrown drain's rows are re-claimed by the very next drain). **(c) R867 — the stamp verbatim, readiness at microsecond precision.** The old ack normalised `enqueued_at` through `new Date(…).toISOString()` (milliseconds) and `.eq`'d it back: a six-digit stamp (`DEFAULT now()`, any SQL-side enqueue) could NEVER match, so such a row was re-claimed forever and the problem line blamed a re-stamp that never happened. - **D319 — L.D1.9 build mechanics: the numbers, the triggers' shape (per-statement × 3 and why), the door's contract (refuse vs skip, the one write, resolution by pairing, E61), the F42/F9/F224(d)/F248(c) dispositions, the D137 tick replacement, the pool event and the client list, typegen, the 024 edit, the realtime warm-window OBSERVATION (re-measured in the #265 fix round — R847), the proof chain, what was deliberately not built.** (1) **Numbering.** Migration head measured 118 ⇒ **119**, pgTAP head 066 ⇒ **067** — confirmed with `ls` (D161/D166); §7's "~~117~~ → +1" was the reservation. (2) **The triggers.** 070's envelope `{operation, table, schema, record}` and convention (event = the table name — the client's dispatch key). `matchups` is THREE single-event per-STATEMENT triggers (`tr_broadcast_matchups_insert/update/delete`, transition table `changed_rows` on each) sharing `broadcast_matchups_statement()`: PostgreSQL 17.6 refuses `REFERENCING` on a multi-event trigger (measured: "transition tables cannot be specified for triggers with more than one event"), and per-statement is what makes D292's ONE-event claim TRUE rather than assumed — the function groups the transition table BY `league_id` and sends one message per league with `{season, week, count, matchups: [14-key rows]}`; `week` is carried only when the statement touched ONE week (a whole-season INSERT carries null — the client's reducer refetches on a missing week, R773); an EMPTY transition table (an UPDATE matching 0 rows — the door's identical re-send) sends nothing (067 F5e/J4d). INSERT and DELETE ride the same function so a Remix (111: DELETE + INSERT) and a bracket (re)build (118: DELETE + INSERT) reach an open schedule page — the reason F254(a)'s `league_chat` stand-in could retire honestly (a matchups UPDATE-only trigger would have left a Remix dark). `team_week_results` is per-statement INSERT + UPDATE (finalization's one INSERT … ON CONFLICT + one median UPDATE = two events per finalization; the door's provisional rows one; a mixed insert+update batch two — said, 067 J3/J3d/H). `transactions` is row INSERT (append-only). `league_weeks` is row `UPDATE OF status` — 070's leagues discriminator (a `median_score`-only write emits nothing, 067 J1c). Payload functions are 070's form (plain, STABLE, triple-REVOKEd) with exact key literals + named negatives: matchups 14 keys (no `override_action_id` / `league_id` / `created_at` / per-player keys); results 10; transactions 8 (`add_player_id` / `drop_player_id` lifted from 113's normalized payload, the BLOB never forwarded — a planted `faab` and `action_id` do not appear: M5's amounts can never leak through a select that never reads the blob); league_weeks 5 (no `reopened_by_action_id`). (3) **The door.** `score_write_week_batch(p_league_id uuid, p_week int, p_scores jsonb) RETURNS jsonb` — §5's signature verbatim; `p_scores` = `[{team_id, points}]` with `points` a JSON number of scale ≤ 2 or `null`; no `p_now` (a writer verb like 111/113, not a job — the door evaluates no calendar; `updated_at = now()` is the transaction instant). Order: the 42501 JWT refusal (116's shape) → the batch's SHAPE (22023 — array, non-empty, objects, valid `team_id`, no duplicate, `points` present as number|null, scale ≤ 2: a 3-dp value is REFUSED by name so no path lets the DB round a divergent value, F22) → the league row `FOR UPDATE` FIRST (rule 8 lock order; serializes with the jobs, which SKIP LOCKED it) and `in_season|playoffs` (P0001 `league_not_in_season`) → every team this league's (P0002 — a mapping bug is loud) → the week row exists / not `final` / not `upcoming` (P0001 `week_not_scheduled` / `week_final` — D295(b) / `week_not_open` — the week's own status is the datum, §23.3; F241(a): the advance job opens it). **Refuse vs skip, decided:** the WEEK-level conditions refuse the batch; the ROW-level protections SKIP BY NAME (`overridden`, `matchup_final`) and a row-less team is named (`no_matchup_row`) — because a commissioner override on ONE matchup (M6) or an eliminated playoff seat in the worker's map must never freeze live scoring for the whole league-week; the report lists every skip. **The one write:** a single UPDATE statement over the week's writable rows the batch touches, each row once with both cells coalesced (`CASE WHEN has_home … END`), rows whose cells would not change LEFT OUT (`IS DISTINCT FROM`, numeric equality — `100.50` vs `100.5` is no change) — so the statement trigger sees exactly what changed and the re-send is silent; `written` / `writable` / `unchanged` / `skipped` / `reason` (`no_change` | `nothing_writable` | null) on the report — rule 10's loud emptiness. **Resolution by pairing (F257(a′)):** the write statement joins the batch to `matchups` on (league, season, week, `home_team_id` | `away_team_id`) and updates through the id resolved IN THAT STATEMENT — no id crosses a call boundary; 067 G2 deletes and re-inserts the bracket row (new id) between two door calls and the second finds the new row. **E61:** `null` writes NULL (the ONLY pending word, F241(a)); a written score goes back to NULL when the worker says pending, never to 0 (067 F7); a cell whose team is not in the batch is never touched — 109's `DEFAULT 0` on an unscored bracket cell stays what it is (067 G1): the door never writes 0 for "no data", and changing the sentinel's READING ("written = non-NULL") is 118's sync's half (F257(a)), deliberately not replaced here (F258's owner unchanged — no trigger forced it). `status` / `result` are never written (finalize's and the advance job's). **`total_points`:** no matchups — provisional `team_week_results` rows (`is_final` FALSE) through one INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE with `WHERE is_final = FALSE AND points IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.points` (changed rows only; a final row is named `result_final`, never overwritten — a reopened week is M6's); `points: null` writes NO row (`pending_no_row`) because `points NUMERIC(8,2) NOT NULL` cannot hold pending and F241(b) makes the row's ABSENCE that mode's pending word — the E61 representation for total_points is the worker's (F259(d)). (4) **Dispositions.** F42 per table: `league_weeks` (subscribers L.D4.1/L.D5.3) and `transactions` (L.D4.2's feed) gain triggers; `league_members` / `team_managers` / `teams` / `league_invites` / `league_lists` re-waived on D38's rationale, 024's pin shrunk to the five and 067 B5 pins each with its reason. (9) **The realtime warm-window OBSERVATION (F259(c)) — observed, contested, re-measured; NOT a platform property; ~~cause unknown~~ **cause MEASURED at the #265 final re-review (R852): realtime-js's last-channel `removeChannel()` calls `disconnect()` when `channels.length === 0` (`RealtimeClient.js:221-231`), Phoenix then closes the websocket after a ~150 ms `waitForBufferDone` tick (`phoenix.cjs.js:1568-1600`), and `connect()` is a no-op while the socket is disconnecting — so a channel created inside that ~150 ms–1.5 s window joins the DYING connection, reports `SUBSCRIBED`, then is orphaned at the close (`onError` rejoins only `if (this.socket.isConnected())`; a clean close never reconnects). Client-side entirely — hosted behaves identically; the local service is not the cause. The browser room does NOT go deaf: `scheduleReopen` catches the `CHANNEL_ERROR` and heals in ~1.0–1.2 s with one extra refetch (8/8 walks on the real `joinLeagueRoom`) — the cost is a ~1 s "Reconnecting" blip on every intra-league navigation, F261.**.** *(As first recorded, 2026-09-07:)* the wire suite's non-member cell first failed with the member's positive control undelivered; three scratch probes (PR body, not the repo) read it as: on the local Realtime v2.124.4 with realtime-js 2.101.1 in Node a private-channel subscriber receives Broadcast-from-DB only within ~1 s of a join or under continuous traffic (+0 s ok, +1 s / +3 s / +6 s MISS; 15 back-to-back 15/15; 070's `leagues` trigger identical; a new join on the same socket revives it); the suite was shaped to that reading and the member's receipt of the SECOND write was left unasserted. *(R847, the #265 review:)* the reviewer could NOT reproduce it — plain Node, one private channel, 070's `leagues` trigger after idle gaps: `+0.3 s DELIVERED 3ms · +3.5 s DELIVERED 0ms · +13.8 s DELIVERED 1ms · +44.0 s DELIVERED 1ms · +104.2 s DELIVERED 0ms` (5/5), and inside the vitest stack lane at +0.2 / +1 / +3 / +6 / +15 / +30 s idle: zero MISS (11/11 in Node, 6/6 in the lane) — contradicted at every gap the record named. *(The #265 fix round, 2026-09-07 — re-measured in 14 fresh-process scratch runs on the local stack, files not kept:)* both are right about their own shape. (i) The RESTORED assertion (the member receives the second write across a 3 s idle gap — cell 3 in its original shape, a later channel on the one shared manager socket) went RED **3/3** in isolation — deterministic, not a flake. (ii) The determinant is NOT the gap: on that shared socket, channels joined after the gate's channel left delivered **10/11** (gaps 0 / 3 / 6 s, with and without the refused outsider, `leagues` and door alike) and the suite's exact cell-1 → cell-2 → cell-3 sequence re-run in a probe file DELIVERED; each process lost messages on ONE later channel, and once deaf that channel stayed deaf (three writes 1 s apart: 1/3 then +0 of 3 more; one write, 5 s idle, one write: 1/2; five back-to-back on the same kind of channel: 5/5 — continuous traffic never missed). (iii) The loss is PER SOCKET, not the pipeline: a second manager socket's channel on the same topic received all three messages the first socket's channel missed (**3/3 vs 1/3**, `realtime.messages` holds every row, the service logs nothing but the outsider's `Unauthorized` rejoin loop). (iv) A socket's FIRST channel never missed in any run — the reviewer's shape (a gate-less file: 3/3 across 3 s gaps) — and a 12 s idle after the gate did NOT cure a later channel (cell 2 then missed 3/3 at a 200 ms gap), so "time since connect" is out. (v) NOT isolated: what makes one later channel on a socket deaf and its neighbour not (excluded: gap length alone, the outsider, the event name or its trigger, time since the socket connected, the previous channel's idle before it left). **Recorded, not doctrine:** no "drive the write within the window" stack-lane rule; no attribution of `draft-realtime-db`'s R163/F52 flake to this (unknown). **The suite's shape now:** ONE SOCKET PER CELL — each cell signs the member in afresh, so the cell's channel is its socket's first (the only shape that delivered in every probe, and the shape a browser tab starts in; the only harness code added for the artifact — the 12 s warm-up tried in between was removed because it cured nothing) — and the non-member cell asserts the member's receipt of the SECOND write across a deliberate 3 s idle gap, the standing measurement D276 asks for (probe: the second write commented out → red at that wait, file md5 `2e35fb49…` → `6c4c2307…` → restored; 3/3 green in isolation, green in the full run). Whether a BROWSER client can produce a deaf later channel (join → leave → rejoin the topic on one socket — a StrictMode double-mount does exactly that) is L.D6.2's ROUTINE check with that recipe, not a go-live gate (R847's ruling; its premise has moved from "does not reproduce" to "reproduces per socket, ~~cause unknown~~ **cause MEASURED at the #265 final re-review (R852): realtime-js's last-channel `removeChannel()` calls `disconnect()` when `channels.length === 0` (`RealtimeClient.js:221-231`), Phoenix then closes the websocket after a ~150 ms `waitForBufferDone` tick (`phoenix.cjs.js:1568-1600`), and `connect()` is a no-op while the socket is disconnecting — so a channel created inside that ~150 ms–1.5 s window joins the DYING connection, reports `SUBSCRIBED`, then is orphaned at the close (`onError` rejoins only `if (this.socket.isConnected())`; a clean close never reconnects). Client-side entirely — hosted behaves identically; the local service is not the cause. The browser room does NOT go deaf: `scheduleReopen` catches the `CHANNEL_ERROR` and heals in ~1.0–1.2 s with one extra refetch (8/8 walks on the real `joinLeagueRoom`) — the cost is a ~1 s "Reconnecting" blip on every intra-league navigation, F261.**" — said to the reviewer in the fix-round report). (10) **Proof chain** in the §2 row and the PR body; the four probes there with their red counts. (11) **Deliberately not built, each named:** a separately named `scores_updated` synthetic event (the `matchups` UPDATE IS it under the 070 convention — spec v2.16.27 says so in §12.14; the client already dispatched on the table name); a `team_lineups` trigger (4); coalescing finalize's per-row status flips (118's loop: N single-row UPDATEs ⇒ N `matchups` events once per week per league — F259(b)); consolidating a total_points batch's INSERT + UPDATE into one event (≤ 2, steady state 1 — said in (2)); a `p_now` on the door (3); changing 109's `home_score`/`away_score` `DEFAULT 0` (spec §12.8 prints it — a §3 question if anyone wants NULL as the default, not a fold; the door writes NULL only for an explicit pending); replacing 118's sync for F258(a)/(b) (no trigger forced it); the poll's TS retirement (F259(a)); a Route Handler for the door (there is none by design — the worker calls the RPC with the service client, L.D2.2).
- **D318 — L.D1.8 build mechanics: the numbers, the rulings as code (what each became), the standings arm's shape (why a sibling wrapper and ONE implementation), the CHECK that was withdrawn, the sync's contract (one writer, two callers, every no-op named), the read model, the D137 derivations, what was deliberately not built, typegen, the proof chain.** (1) **Numbering.** Migration head measured 117 ⇒ **118**, pgTAP head 065 ⇒ **066** — confirmed with `ls`, not inherited (D161/D166). (2) **The rulings as code.** (A) `playoff_bracket_state_internal`'s verdict: the round's SUM of the two-decimal scores per week (`sum(round(score, 2))`), equal ⇒ the smaller seed number, a bye ⇒ the home side; `decided_by` ∈ points · higher_seed · bye; the stored `result` is neither consulted nor rewritten (066 I6b: the B–F row is `final:tie`). (B) the same sum over `playoff_weeks_per_round` rows of one pairing (066 J1b 200–170, the week-1 loser wins; J1 the equal-sum arm 170–170 ⇒ P by `higher_seed` — the recorded reading, pinned so it reds if ruled otherwise). (C) `create_league` (077's text) and `update_league_settings` (105's text) each gain ONE hunk after their Q10 backstops — `p_playoff_teams > 0 AND COALESCE(p_settings ->> 'schedule_mode', 'h2h') = 'total_points'` ⇒ P0001 whose message names `playoff_teams` and no other marker (the leagues-service field mappers are first-match; both lists gain the marker; `settings-round-trip-db` pins the text and its disjointness); `validateLeagueSettings` refuses the pair (the route path never reaches the RPC); the panel disables the select under total-points and `scheduleModePatch` carries `playoff_teams: 0` with the mode switch (`settings-panel-ops`); the round-trip fixture moves to `playoff_teams: 0` (its total_points is the non-default worth keeping). The engine reads the MODE: `playoff_bracket_state_internal` returns `kind = points_race` for any `total_points` row whatever `playoff_teams` stores (066 K1). (D) the sync's no-bracket arm: every regular-season week `final` (a held earlier week — a named finalize skip — still waits; "the last week final" alone would crown on an incomplete table) ⇒ `league_standings_internal(…, FALSE)` rank 1 ⇒ `UPDATE leagues SET status = 'complete', champion_team_id WHERE status = 'in_season'`, ROW_COUNT asserted (066 H5/H5b: W 3-1/300 over the PF leader X 2-2/400; H6: the total_points K). (E) the trigger is `league_weeks.status` — 116's (b) flips `live → correction_window` ON `nfl_weeks.last_game_ends_at`, so "rolled" = every week of the prior stage `correction_window`/`final` and the sync needs no clock of its own; both jobs call it every claim (idempotent; a bracket problem is a nested-guarded `bracket_failures` entry + WARNING, retried next run, never a block on the week machine); the provisional build reads the PROJECTED standings, the final rebuild the final ones (066 G4/G4b then H3/H3b: the correction moved seed 6 from G to D and the round was rewritten `live` in the open week). (3) **The standings arm — a sibling wrapper over ONE implementation, not a new parameter.** 065 A3/A6 pin `league_standings(uuid)`'s one-argument signature and its EXECUTE shape, so `p_projected` could not be a parameter without editing a merged suite; 117's body became `league_standings_internal(uuid, boolean)` (PLAIN, REVOKEd; the chain byte-for-byte; `rows_` = `final_` — 117's scan — ∪ the projected arm) with two thin DEFINER wrappers carrying 117's member check: `league_standings(uuid)` (FALSE — payload identical plus `projected: false` / `weeks_projected: 0`) and `league_standings_projected(uuid)` (TRUE). The projected arm: an OPEN regular-season week (`live` / `correction_window`) holding no final row, derived through the SAME helper finalization writes from — `week_results_derive_internal(…, TRUE)`: a NULL `result` read from the scores via `matchup_result_internal` (E38), a NULL score read as 0.00 SO FAR (a projection is not a finalization — E61's pending word is finalize's; 066 E4d/E4e), total_points from the worker's rows (066 E5), the median re-derived per week through `week_median_internal` (066 E6 ≡ H8: P5's projected W-L-T with the median equals what finalization wrote); an `upcoming` week never counts (066 E2b); a reopened week (final rows present) reads its final rows. `week_results_write_internal` (117's text) now INSERTs from the derive helper (FALSE) and reads the median helper — two asserted hunks; 064/065 ran unchanged and green against the replaced bodies BEFORE 066 was written (the behaviour-preservation proof came first, the D314(2) precedent). (4) **The CHECK that was withdrawn.** A `leagues_total_points_no_bracket` CHECK (the 115 shape) was authored as the structural twin of the (C) refusals; run 1 of `test:db` redded pgTAP 058 (L8 — `update leagues set settings = total_points` on a playoff_teams-6 row, the engine's mode-arm golden) and 059 (LT, the same pair). The ruling's letter is "refused at SETTINGS time" — the four sites — and the engine reads the mode, so the CHECK bought nothing the K1 pin does not, at the price of re-cutting two merged fixtures; withdrawn, the stored-pair behaviour pinned instead. (5) **The sync's contract.** ONE writer (`playoff_bracket_sync_internal`), two callers (the rollover and the close), the league row re-taken `FOR UPDATE` (free — the jobs hold it; rule 8). Forward only: `not_in_play` for a `complete` league (066 J6c); the flips are `UPDATE … WHERE status = <from>` with ROW_COUNT 1. Round by round: a playoff row with NO seed is not the engine's (`bracket_foreign_rows`, named, nothing written — the 064/065 fixture shape; 066 G2b–G2e, then the retry builds G4); a round whose prior stage has not rolled ⇒ `waiting_round` / `waiting_regular_season` (with the open weeks); a DECIDED round (any `final` / overridden / result-bearing row) is history — never compared, never rewritten, its survivors feed the next (066 I7–I7d: a corrupted regular season after round 1 is final changes nothing and does not block round 2); **[amended 2026-09-07, R839] a ROLLED round (every week `correction_window` / `final`) or a SCORED one (any row with a WRITTEN score — non-NULL and not 109's `DEFAULT 0`, which is what an unscored bracket row holds) is history TOO — "played": the games happened, the scores are on the rows; a prior verdict that moves after that (the F238/Q37 family — a held finalization on the last regular week outliving round 1's kickoff; the reviewer's probe wiped a played E–G row to 0/0 and re-paired round 2 from 0–0 verdicts) is REFUSED BY NAME — `rebuild_refused_round_played` (round, `stored`, `desired`, `rolled`, `scored_rows`) + WARNING, nothing deleted, later rounds not revisited (the loop returns — the cascade stops); the refusal lifts when a commissioner rewrites the round with seeds (M6 §10 — a row written with seeds is the engine's) OR when the played round FINALIZES on its own close (117's loop skips the held week by name and finalizes later due weeks — then the round is decided, above, and its survivors feed the next; 066 L6–L7d). The score-written arm is in the definition because "rolled" alone is too late: round 1's games are Sunday, its rollover Tuesday — a correction landing Monday would still find the round "open" and wipe played rows. The ruled rebuild ((E): the correction close, Thursday 06:00 ET, before any playoff kickoff) meets neither arm. Residual: a round whose every score is exactly 0.00 reads as unplayed until it rolls (109's default) — F257(a).** an open round equal to the prior stage's verdict ⇒ `round_in_progress` (its source named); different ⇒ DELETE + INSERT (066 I4/I4b/I4c — the reseed divergence exercised THROUGH the rewrite path, both directions); empty ⇒ INSERT — `scheduled` into an `upcoming` week, `live` into an open one (116's (a) flips the former at open — 066 G5), seeds frozen, the expected row count asserted; **[amended 2026-09-07, R840] before ANY provisional build or rebuild (the prior stage rolled, not final) the sync asks the prior stage's non-final weeks finalization's ONE pending question — `week_results_pending_internal` (D137: h2h — a NULL score on any matchup; total_points — a seated team without a result row) — and any pending ⇒ `bracket_waiting` (round, `pending: [{week, reason, pending}]`), nothing written, NO status flip, retried next run (066 G3i–G3m: a NULL score at the rollover ⇒ no build, `in_season`; scored ⇒ built; L4/L4b the same gate behind a BUILT round on the close job). "Provisional" therefore means every score of the prior stage WRITTEN and none yet final — Q39 (E)'s "built from provisional scores" reconciled: provisional ≠ absent; §23.2's letter ("no league state is ever advanced on partial data") governs the WRITE and the flip; the projected READ keeps its 0.00-so-far (E4d) as a view, never a write. A FINAL prior stage passed the same question when it finalized — the gate is skipped for it.** the champion only when the last round is FINAL (066 J2c/J4b: never provisional). Every write says `action` (built · rebuilt · complete) with `source` (provisional · final), `rollover_at`, the pairing text and what it `replaced`; every no-op says `reason`. The jobs' `nothing_due` / `nothing_finalized` now count a bracket action as something happening (066 G4e/J5c). **[amended 2026-09-07, R841] Both jobs' payloads carry `bracket_blocked` (a `bracket_foreign_rows` or `rebuild_refused_round_played` return — a human must act) and `bracket_waiting` (a `bracket_waiting` return — retried hourly), each + WARNING (066 G2f, G3k, H7b, L4b, L6, L7b); the calendar `waiting_regular_season` / `waiting_round` states (the prior stage not yet rolled — every in-season league, every hour) stay OUT of the payload deliberately: they carry no signal and would be a league-count-sized array every run. The refusal's own WARNING is raised in the sync (a direct call warns too); the jobs warn on foreign rows and waiting.** (6) **The read model** (`playoff_bracket_state_internal` → `league_playoff_bracket`): per round its weeks (status, `rollover_at`, `corrections_close_at`), games with seeds / per-week rows / totals / `winner_team_id` / `decided_by` / `final`, `survivors` (seed + LINE), `foreign_rows`, `expected_games`, `source` (= the prior stage final NOW — a minutes-level lag between the close and finalize's :05 run is the honest reading, F256(a)); `next_round`, `entrants_next`, `bracket_champion_team_id` (derived) beside `champion_team_id` (stored — 066 J7 equal). While `in_season`: `projected_round_1` from the projected table + `projection_basis` (weeks final / projected / seeded) + `rollover_week` / `rollover_at` / `corrections_close_at` — ONE absolute instant per league, a `timestamptz` (066 F1d); NULL until ingestion records the last game's end (F238's posture — never inferred). A no-bracket league: `kind` points_race / no_playoffs + the champion. (7) **D137 derivations** — `derive_118.py` (PR body; `verify` mode asserts 118 carries each body byte-for-byte): six functions from md5-asserted file text (116 `3728ee39…`, 117 `6198b881…`, 077 `9560e204…`, 105 `23f7b3e4…`) with exact-match hunks each asserted to hit once — the write helper (2), the standings (8 — signature, DECLARE, the member check out, `v_median_on`, the `rows_` split, the counts, the payload keys, the reason), the advance (3 — DECLARE, the guarded sync after the F238 block, the payload + reason), finalize (3 — DECLARE, the guarded sync after the weeks loop INSIDE the F244 subtransaction, the payload + reason; F244's locals + merge byte-identical — 066 A10), create (1), update (1). (8) **Deliberately not built, each named:** consolation + third-place (F212 — the round types are admitted by the seed CHECK, nothing writes them); the per-week mode for a total_points December bracket (Q39 (C)'s return path — F255); the "current week" boundary at the rollover (offered, not built — Q39); the bracket VIEW (L.D5.5); a system chat post at the champion (unspecced — the hero reads the column); commissioner bracket edits (M6 — a row written with seeds is the engine's); team names in the bracket payload (the UI joins `teams`); a `matchups` broadcast (L.D1.9, D296). (9) **Typegen:** `supabase gen types --local` on the fresh 001–118 chain, alias block re-appended: **+58 / −0** (the two columns + the FK relationship; nine `Functions` entries — the two member reads and seven REVOKEd helpers PostgREST exposes by signature, EXECUTE gates them). (4) **Schedule: the grid is the ladder's, the edit affordance is the client-visible half of 111's gate, and E41 is the server's on both doors.** `scheduleGrid` walks `league_weeks` in order, pairs each week's `matchups` (byes as a null away side; `secondary` rows badged "second game"; `✸ commissioner-adjusted` on `is_overridden`; scores dash when `scheduled` and say `pending` when live-but-unscored — E61), classifies regular vs playoff POSITIONALLY in league-week terms (`weekKind`, Q29) and says why a week has no rows: playoff → "bracket arrives with the playoffs engine" (Q39/L.D1.8, pending by name), `total_points` → §16.5.3's copy. `matchupEditable` shows Edit to a commissioner only on an `upcoming` week's `scheduled`, unscored, un-overridden regular/secondary pairing with two teams — the checks a client can see; the week's own kickoff (R730) and the reason law are the server's, and the refusal renders VERBATIM (`role="alert"`) and marks the field. - **D316 — L.D5.1 build mechanics: the lock is READ not computed, the current week from the ladder, why `@dnd-kit/core` and not either existing drag stack, the two ledger dispositions, the verification environment, and what was deliberately not built.** (1) **The per-player 🔒 comes from the FETCHED evaluation and from nothing stored on the lineup row.** `lockedPlayerIds` (`lineup-editor-ops.ts`) reads `use-rosters`'s `game_lock` only — the pool VIEW migration 116's `lineup_lock_tick` refreshes every minute from 115's `pool_game_lock_any_internal` at the tick instant, normalised by L.D4.1 (D315(5)): `unlocked` / `locked_until` / `locked_release_unrecorded` (F241(d)'s `'infinity'`, rendered as "locked — the week's last game has not ended" from the STATE). `team_lineups.locked_at` renders as "Locks from …" (R779) and `starters[].kickoff_at` as the row's kickoff datum — the DoD probe (derive the lock from those two) reds the render pin on a fixture whose record says 2001 while the view says unlocked. **Measured live (the browser pass):** with the pool row cleared by hand the UI let the kicked-off RB be placed, the server refused with its own sentence (the kickoff and slot named), the draft stayed unsaved, and the cron tick re-locked the view within the minute — the UI shows the server's answer, never a guess (§11.2/D293). **[Qualified in the fix round — R822:** the tick refreshes the VIEW; the page sees it AT THE NEXT FETCH, and before the round nothing fetched — the re-lock the browser pass reports was a DB observation carried to the screen by a reload. Now (10): a refusal re-reads the roster + the row, and the current week polls the rosters route every 60 s until L.D1.9 broadcasts the pool — F252.**]** The view is applied to the CURRENT week only (a future week has nothing kicked off; a past/`correction_window`/`final` week is closed whole) — one known edge is F251(b). (2) **The current week is 112's arm read through `league_weeks.status`**, because `lineup_current_week_internal` is deliberately not granted (D315(3)/F248(b)) and §23.3 forbids wall-clock arithmetic: `league_week_advance` (116) flips a week out of `upcoming` at its `starts_at`, so the greatest non-`upcoming` week is current and, when nothing has started, the first week is (112's COALESCE arm — exactly what the 2099 fixture needs). No `Date.now`/`new Date()` anywhere in the three new files; the one `Date.parse` + `Intl` formats STORED instants (viewer-local, league zone on hover — §16.4). (3) **Drag: `@dnd-kit/core` draggable/droppable, and why neither existing stack was reused.** This is a SLOT model — a player drops INTO a keyed seat and displaces its occupant — and both in-repo drag stacks are LIST models: `my-queue.tsx` is `@dnd-kit/sortable` (items transform out of the way) and `lists/v2/use-list-drag.tsx` is the drop-gap list model (a gap opens at an index; it has no notion of a seat). Reusing either would have carried list semantics into a grid that has none — the LV.7 failure in the other direction. What IS reused: dnd-kit itself (no new dependency), `use-list-drag`'s sensor pair (mouse after 6px, touch after a 220ms press so a finger scroll stays a scroll), and the app's primitives (Card/Badge/Button/Segment/Skeleton/PositionBadge — no new shared component, no variant added). Every drag has a tap twin (select a player, tap a seat) so keyboard/assistive users get the same moves without a second mechanism; a swap re-seats the displaced occupant into the mover's old seat when he fits it, else benches him (E16's augmenting path is the server's — the client keeps every move legible). (4) **F249(a) — the page is the gate, by decision.** `useLineup` stays a member-RLS read with no assertion of its own; `team-page.tsx` mounts nothing below `useLeague`'s 403/404, so the hook cannot mount for a non-member (the `leagues` SELECT policy is member/owner-only, 052:126). Chosen over a per-query `is_league_member` RPC because that is an extra round trip on a path only a member reaches (D315(12)'s reasoning) and `use-lineup.ts` carries the never-optimistic pins the round must not disturb; the hook's docblock now says the surface gates. A future consumer mounting `useLineup` outside a league page inherits the hazard and the row's one-line cure. (5) **F250(a) — one 404 copy at the UI.** `problemCopy` renders `INSEASON_LEAGUE_GONE_MESSAGE` for ANY 404 the page meets, whatever the body said (`useLeague` throws a plain Error; the family's `LeagueActionError` carries a status) — pinned. The SQL-side nit (map standings' P0002 to the family message in `standings-service.ts`) stays F250(a)'s for L.D5.3, which is the first surface to call standings. (6) **The lock countdown is a NAMED placeholder (Q40/F251), not an invention.** The spec names a "lock countdown" (§16.5.1, tasks-M4) but never its referent under the one lock; the record R779 mandates renders, the placeholder carries `data-lock-countdown="placeholder-q40"`, and the ruling is one pure function away. (7) **States (§16.5.4) are real renders, pinned:** `team-page.render.test.ts` renders the actual components through `renderToStaticMarkup` with the React Query cache pre-seeded (the SE.9 rig; `useAuth` mocked at the module edge because it reaches Next's app router), error/degraded built by setting query state directly — with `retryOnMount: false`, because v5's optimistic result reports an errored data-less query that WOULD retry on mount as `pending`, which is not the state a mounted component sees after its fetch failed (measured: the first cut rendered the skeleton for every error cell). Elevation is pinned for the two feature files (the `ui/` pin stops at `ui/`): exactly one resting `shadow-hard-*` and it is inside `<DragOverlay>`. The new URL is declared in `route-groups.test.ts`'s `APP_URLS_ADDED_SINCE_GOLDEN` (its census caught the undeclared route on the first full run — the pin working as designed). (8) **Verification environment:** every browser step on `.claude/launch.json`'s `dev-local` (port 3123, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321`), confirmed by the network log (`127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1/team_lineups…`), the fixture created by `scripts/dev-seed-inseason-league.ts` (refuses a non-local URL; 2099 synthetic season — F215; `dev-ld51-*` ids for F199's census; `lineup_lock_tick` run once for the league so the pool view is populated before the page opens) and TORN DOWN after the pass (`--teardown`; its players carry a null ADP the stack suites' lowest-ADP cells could pick — F199) — re-creatable in one command, recorded in the script header and F251. Hosted was never touched.
