- **D315 — L.D4.1 build mechanics: the layering, the membership gate and its posture, why `week` is required, the placement guard, the two normalisers, which events each surface listens to, the non-optimistic reading of §15.6, and what was deliberately not built.** (1) **Layering is the D68/D71 house pattern, extended not forked:** four thin Route Handlers (auth + param plumbing; pinned by `inseason-routes.test.ts`, which now covers the family's eight routes), four services over an INJECTED client (`lineup-service.ts` · `rosters-service.ts` · `matchups-service.ts` · `standings-service.ts`), the shared `inseason-errors.ts` mapper and `inseason-ids.ts` normaliser composed onto rather than re-typed, and ONE new shared helper `inseason-reads.ts` (the membership gate + the PostgREST-cap assertion). Nothing in `app/` names an RPC, a table or a rule (pinned, incl. `.rpc(`). (2) **The membership gate precedes every direct read, and it is the database's own predicate.** `league_rosters` / `matchups` / `team_week_results` / `league_player_pool` / `league_weeks` / `team_lineups` are member-SELECT, so a non-member's read through the user's client returns ZERO rows — and a route that served that as `{ teams: [] }` would make an empty league and a forbidden league the same JSON (CLAUDE.md; rule 10). So `readRosters` / `readMatchups` call `is_league_member(p_league_id)` (052 — the very function the policies call, PUBLIC-executable, SECURITY DEFINER, `false` for no-such-league and not-a-member alike) BEFORE the first `.from(`, and answer ONE no-leak 403 (`INSEASON_READ_FORBIDDEN_MESSAGE`). `league_standings` (117) carries the same check in-body and raises 42501, which the family mapper answers as the same 403 — so the three reads answer one status with one shape for one caller. **Posture note, recorded not smoothed:** the activity feed (D310(5b)) answers a non-member an EMPTY feed under the D114(5) league-read posture; this task's three reads answer 403, the RPC family's shape (112/113/117's single 42501). Both are no-leak; F248(d) names the divergence so a reviewer can rule ONE posture in a line. **[R807, #261 fix round: RULED by the reviewer as house convention (not a Chris call) — refuse-by-name is the family's posture. `readActivity` now calls `assertLeagueMember` before its first `.from(`, the two L.D4.2 cells flipped to `{ 403, INSEASON_READ_FORBIDDEN_MESSAGE }`, F248(d) closed; the route docblock and the service header say so. The leak analysis stands either way — league existence is discoverable through world-readable `teams`.]** (3) **`week` is REQUIRED on the matchups GET.** §15.3 prints `?week=` and the route reads it literally; a default view's "current week" is the surface's call over `useSchedule`'s ladder (L.D5.2/L.D5.4), because §23.3 forbids inferring it from wall-clock math and the one server definition (`lineup_current_week_internal`, 112) is deliberately not granted to clients — exposing it is a product-shaped choice this task did not make (F248(b)). A week off the league's calendar is a 404 BY NAME quoting the ladder's bounds, never an empty week; an empty `matchups` array under a real `league_weeks` row is a legal state (`total_points` generates none; a playoff week has none until L.D1.8) and the payload carries `schedule_mode` so the UI can say why. (4) **The F65(b) guard covers the PLACEMENT, not only the ids.** 112's replay is keyed on `(league_id, action_id)` alone — not team, week or map — so a reused id for a different lineup returns the FIRST document with no error. The guard compares `team_id`, `week`, `action_id` AND the placement: `placementMatches(submitted, canonical, moved)` accepts a submitted `(key → player)` held verbatim by the canonical map OR named in `moved[]` as that player moving FROM that key, and requires both maps to place exactly the same players. That is what lets an E16 re-seat of ONE submit pass (its own `moved[]` accounts for it — pinned live: the TE placed at `wr:2` is re-seated and the replay of the same submit is byte-identical) while a reuse for a different arrangement, a different week or a swapped player is a 409 with its own copy. R768 applies to the PATH team id as well as the body's `action_id` (both are compared against Postgres's rendering); pinned live with uppercase fixtures for both. (5) **F241(d) without a clock.** `gameLockView` turns §12.19's three shapes into a discriminated view — NULL → `unlocked`, an instant → `locked_until` (carried verbatim; the UI compares with its own time — `src/lib/leagues/**` reads none, D3), the literal `'infinity'` → `locked_release_unrecorded` — and THROWS on anything else (a 500 by name, never a silently-unlocked row). Pinned pure and over the wire with a planted `'infinity'` row (the raw column really arrives as the string `"infinity"`, and `new Date("infinity")` really is Invalid Date — both asserted so the hazard is measured, not assumed). Per §12.19/§13.1 the view is display state, never the E32 decider (113 evaluates kickoffs itself). (6) **F247(b) at the service, and the hole the first cut had.** `normalizeStandingsRow` coerces `points_for` / `points_against` / `win_pct` and asserts each FINITE, refusing the document by name otherwise. The first cut used `Number(x)` — and `Number(null) === 0`, so a NULL figure would have rendered as a plausible `0.00`, the CLAUDE.md shape exactly; the unit test written to pin the refusal caught it before the stack suite ran, and the coercion now accepts a JSON number or a non-empty numeric string and NOTHING else. **[R811, #261 fix round: "numeric string" is now DECIMAL-ONLY — `DECIMAL_FIGURE = /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, the one shape a `numeric` can arrive as. The first cut's `trim() !== ''` + `Number()` refused `''`/`'  '` only by the trim and read `'0x10'`/`'1e3'`/`' 5 '` as 16/1000/5; the boundary is pinned both ways (ten refused literals, five accepted).]** The wire difference R804 measured is pinned over RAW BYTES in the stack suite (R601): a direct PostgREST fetch shows `"points_for": 71.50` beside `"points_for": 0` in one document. The SQL-side uniform scale stays F247(b)'s for whoever next opens 117. (7) **Which events each surface listens to — three pure predicates in the R773 shape, and a reducer.** `MATCHUPS_INVALIDATING_EVENTS` = `matchups` (the coalesced `scores_updated`, D296) + `team_week_results` + `league_weeks`; the matchups hook narrows further BY WEEK through `matchupsEventEffect` (a known event naming this week → refetch; naming another week → inert; carrying no week → refetch, conservatively; unknown → inert — the M2 forward-compat pattern, pinned with strangers incl. a case variant). `STANDINGS_INVALIDATING_EVENTS` = `team_week_results` + `league_weeks` and deliberately NOT `matchups`: 117 reads only final rows (§11.5 v2.16.23), the live projection is L.D5.3's over provisional cells, and refetching a SECURITY DEFINER scan for every member on every tick is the waste D310(4) refused for the feed — pinned as a negative. `ROSTERS_INVALIDATING_EVENTS` = `league_rosters` (072's trigger, LIVE TODAY — its first subscriber, which is why the name joins the closed set now; the ops test's exact-list pin updated to seven) + `transactions` (a DROP is a DELETE on `league_rosters`, which 072 does not broadcast — without the move's own event a dropped player would stay rendered until a rejoin). The wiring is EXECUTABLE in node: the hooks' own handler builders (`matchupsHandlers`, `invalidatingHandlers(pred, invalidate)`) are joined through the real `joinLeagueRoom` with the client mocked and a synthetic event is driven through the ONE channel — the DoD's cell, which the probe reds. Every consumer refetches on every confirmed (re)join and first on a drop (§9.3), and never patches a column-selected payload. (8) **Never optimistic — the reading of §15.6.** §15.6 lists "lineup set" among the optimistic updates; the breakdown (tasks-M4 §6 L.D4.1 item 2) says `use-lineup` is never optimistic for lock-adjacent state, and §11.2/D293 make every lineup submit lock-adjacent: each refusal is about state the client cannot evaluate (the per-player kickoff read at transaction `now()`, the bipartite fit, the IR stint, `allow_illegal_lineups`), and even the SUCCESS is not the submitted map — 112 may re-seat it. So the hook invalidates and re-reads on success, and the mutation's `data` carries the canonical document (`slot_map`, `starters[].flags`, `rearranged`/`moved[]`, `no_changes`, `locked_at` as "locks at" — R779) for immediate render. No spec erratum is owed: §15.6's list is indicative (D310(10)) and the breakdown's narrower rule is Chris-approved. **[R816, #261 fix round: taken anyway — the sentence stood as LAW as printed, so §15.6 now strikes "lineup set" with a one-line annotation naming §11.2/D293/D315(8); spec v2.16.24, a PATCH.] [R815: the hook's "reused on retry" over-claimed — `useMutation` sets no `retry` (mutations default to 0; the provider's `retry: 1` is under `queries`) and `submit`/`submitAsync` mint per call, so NO code path re-sends an id on its own; the docblock now says a caller re-invoking `mutate` with the same variables replays, and that automatic replay is deliberately not set so a refusal surfaces rather than being re-sent behind the manager's back. Harmless either way — a re-tap is a content-idempotent `no_changes` set.]** (9) **What was deliberately NOT built, each with its reason:** no `GET …/lineup` route (§15.3 prints none — `use-lineup` reads `team_lineups` under 112's member SELECT, D92); no current-week inference (item 3; F248(b)); no `team_lineups` subscription (the table has no trigger — F224(d), L.D1.9's decision; F248(c) says how to add it); no Route Handler harness (F233(f) — the four new routes' ANON arm is source-pinned the same way, and the row's owner is now whoever builds the harness); no wire-level delivery proof for the three refetch-on-event hooks (the `matchups`/`team_week_results`/`league_weeks` triggers are L.D1.9's, behind B9 — the pins are synthetic through the real room; **F248(a)**); no cache patching from any event (D296's payloads are column-selected). (10) **Suite mechanics.** Action-id prefixes **afa** (lineup-api-db) and **afb** (inseason-reads-api-db) — the D108(14) registry, swept 2026-09-05 (af0–af9 taken). Calendar per F215/F226: the leagues live on the 2099 synthetic season; the lineup suite's two game rows are its own (2001-09-09 past / 2099-09-13 future — neither can rot around transaction `now()`); the reads suite places NO game rows and its one instant literal is a 2099 `locked_until`. `Date.parse` in `rosters-service.ts` is the D310(7)-legal parse of a database value; the one raw `fetch` is in the stack SUITE (a wire measurement), never in a service. The lineup suite's first cut asserted `locked_at` NULL when no starter had kicked off — wrong: 112 records the earliest kickoff among the STARTERS (the "locks at" instant, still ahead), and the cell now pins that reading, which is R779's point. (11) **Numbers:** D315 · F248 · the R-band for this PR's review starts at **R807** (per the orchestrator's disjoint bands; the halt branch `halt/M4-L.D1.8-playoffs-Q39` carries Q39/B9 and took no numbers). **(12) The #261 fix round (R807–R816), and what each one changed.** **R807 — the activity feed's 200-empty for a non-member, aligned to the family's 403.** F248(d) had named the divergence for a reviewer to rule in a line; the reviewer ruled it (house convention: §11.5 v2.16.23's "refused by name, never handed an empty table", the RPC family's one 42501, CLAUDE.md's "assert the reason for emptiness"), and the line is `const refused = await assertLeagueMember(supabase, leagueId); if (refused) return refused` after the query parse in `readActivity` — the `readMatchups` order, so a malformed filter is still a 400 before any RPC. **2026-09-05 — Builder (L.D1.7, standings + the derived-results rebuild — migration 117 + pgTAP 065; branch `feat/M4-L.D1.7-standings-rebuild`; takes **D314**; discharges **F244**; files **F245** + **F246**; spec **v2.16.23**)**

- **D314 — L.D1.7 build mechanics: the numbers, WHY the results math was factored out of 116 (and how — D137 by derivation, again), the rebuild's contract (final weeks only; refusals by name; never a write to `matchups`), the standings' contract (PA once; regular season only; the stored order is the chain; H2H meetings; the seed; DEFINER for a read), the E64 fixture rows, the single-scan measurement, what was NOT touched, typegen, the proof chain.** (1) **Numbering.** Migration head measured 116 ⇒ **117**, pgTAP head 064 ⇒ **065** (D311(1)/D312(1) — confirmed with `ls`, not inherited). (2) **The factoring, and why.** **[R802, added at merge: one under-described change — 116 ran the matchup shape guards BEFORE the flip loop; 117 runs them inside `week_results_write_internal`, AFTER the flips. Invisible in effect because the per-league subtransaction rolls the flips back (measured: L4's four matchups stayed `live`/`result` NULL and weeks 3–4 `correction_window` after a rolled-back run), but it is a reorder and the "every other byte 116's" sentence did not say so.]** The task's own equivalence — `standings ≡ rebuild-from-scratch` — is a claim that the rebuild produces the rows finalization produced; two copies of the math (116's inline block + a rebuild's) could only ever be PINNED equal, and would drift on the first fix to either. So the (b)/(c)/(d) block of 116's `finalize_matchups` — the pending checks, the shape guards, the `team_week_results` INSERT, the total_points UPDATE, the exact median — became three plain helpers (`matchup_result_internal` IMMUTABLE — the E38 rule; `week_results_pending_internal` — NULL or the named shape; `week_results_write_internal` — RETURNS (results, teams, median)) and `finalize_matchups` was CREATE OR REPLACE'd against **116's FILE TEXT** (md5 `3728ee39c2fb305baa974357150a9668`, the PR #258 fix-round text — the CLAUDE.md rule; 116 NOT edited, its banner historical). `derive_117.py` (PR body) extracts the function verbatim and applies SIX exact-match substitutions each asserted to hit once — two DECLARE hunks, the per-league prelude, the results block (pending helper → the flip loop VERBATIM with its derivation lifted → write helper), and the two F244 hunks — then asserts the INSERT / the median arrays / every retired variable survive nowhere and the three helper calls, the override branch and the F244 merge appear exactly once. The write helper reads `matchups.result` AS WRITTEN (finalization's flip has just written it; the rebuild's drift check guarantees it) — so its INSERT is 116's INSERT text with the arguments bound, and the h2h `CASE` never recomputes from scores (probe 2 makes it, and 064 E7 reds beside 065's cells: one implementation). 064's 140 ran unchanged against the replaced body BEFORE 065 was written — the behaviour-preservation proof came first. (3) **F244 taken here, not left for L.D6.1:** the replacement was already being authored against 116's text, so the fix is two hunks in the same derivation (locals `v_lg_finalized` / `v_lg_report` reset before the subtransaction, discarded in the handler, merged after it) and 065 C1–C1d pin it with a league whose week 4 carries a shape defect — its week 3 rolls back, the report says so, and the database agrees. (4) **The rebuild's contract, each choice named.** **[R801, added at merge: the Points Against definition this build introduced — primary opponent's points, once per week — is a NEW rule (116 computed no PA), folded where the spec was silent; it stands PROVISIONALLY under §3 Q38 (three sub-questions: second-opponent PA; PA ≡ 0 in total_points making E64's hop vacuous; win_pct reorderable).]** FINAL weeks only (`week_not_final` otherwise): results for an open week are not results (§11.5, §23.2), the write door owns every non-final week and refuses final ones (D292/D295(b)) — the two verbs partition weeks by status and never overlap; "the correction path's rebuild arm" (D297) is the §23.4 post-window correction, which by definition touches a final week. The pending shapes RAISE by name (finalize SKIPS by name — the same helper, two postures: a job continues its scan, a single-week verb fails its caller's transaction, which is what an M6 apply path needs). `result_drift`: a non-overridden final matchup whose stored `result` is not its scores' E38 result is REFUSED, not repaired — the rebuild never writes `matchups` (rule 9: a final matchup is never recomputed here; §12.18: the source of truth is read) — so a score correction must write `result` with the score; **F245** hands L.E2 that duty (one line in its apply verb, or a call to `matchup_result_internal`). An overridden row is exempt from the drift check by definition — disagreeing with its scores IS the override (065 E7d/E7e: 'tie' under an override rebuilds as 'tie'). `league_weeks.median_score` is rewritten (D313(7)(d)'s rounded store), `status` / `finalized_at` never. Authority: triple REVOKE + the in-body JWT refusal — the rebuild is not a user verb (the service role, the harness, M6's audited verbs in-body); widening it is M6's decision. Lock order: `leagues` FOR UPDATE, then `league_weeks` (rule 8). Idempotent by digest, `already_consistent` said out loud (rule 10). **The standings' contract.** PA = Σ the PRIMARY opponent's `points` that week — the spec pinned PF-once (§11.7) and was silent on PA; the mirror reading keeps Σ PF ≡ Σ PA over a league and is the reading under which "more PA = harder schedule" (§7.3.7) compares like with like; folded into §7.3.7 as v2.16.23 (the fold-back rule — a resolved ambiguity goes into the LAW). A missing opponent row is counted (`pa_gaps`), never a silent 0. Regular season only (`week < first + regular_season_weeks`): §7.3.7 says the chain seeds "at end of regular season" and playoff results never reorder a regular-season table on any platform; the median rule in 116 draws the same line. Combined record (§11.7's own sentence); Win % exact as (2W + T)/2G — equal rationals compute to equal NUMERICs at these magnitudes (all operands weight 0, one division scale), and the display rounds to 4 while the sort key does not. The stored `tiebreakers` array IS the chain, `win_pct` wherever it sits — §7.3.7 prints it as entry (1) of a "fully reorderable" array and the Zod catalog accepts any order; the catalog's remainder is appended so a trimmed array ("candidates to trim later") still ends in a total order, and the completion is named (`chain_appended`). **2026-09-03 — Builder (L.D4.2, in-season API + hooks part 2 — transactions / schedule Remix / activity; branch `feat/M4-L.D4.2-transactions-schedule-activity`; takes **D310**; discharges **F227(f)**; files **F233**; NO migration, no typegen, no schema, no spec change)**

- **D310 — L.D4.2 build mechanics: the layering, the family's SQLSTATE split and why it differs from members/draft, §9.3's second channel, the activity feed's scoping decisions, and what was deliberately not built.** (1) **Layering is the D68/D71 house pattern, extended not forked:** four Route Handlers that do auth + param plumbing only (pinned by `inseason-routes.test.ts`, the `scoring-routes.test.ts` shape), three services over an INJECTED client (`transactions-service.ts` · `schedule-service.ts` · `activity-service.ts`), and ONE shared SQLSTATE mapper `inseason-errors.ts` that L.D4.1 composes onto rather than re-typing. Nothing in `app/` names an RPC, a table or a rule (pinned). (2) **The family maps `P0001 → 409`, and the difference from members/draft (`→ 400`) is deliberate and recorded rather than smoothed over.** Two ledger rows written by two different Builders — **F224(e)** (L.D1.4's lineup-route contract) and **F227(f)** (L.D1.5's transactions contract) — print the same mapping, so it is a family contract, not a slip; both cite "the members-api precedent", which maps P0001 → 400 (`members-service.ts:56`, `draft-service.ts:124`), and the tension is named here so a reviewer can rule it either way with one line changed. The substantive argument for 409: every P0001 that 111/112/113 raise is a refusal ABOUT LEAGUE STATE — this player is on another roster, his game kicked off, the roster is full, the week is live, the league is not `in_season` — none of which is a defect in a perfectly well-formed request that simply lost a race; 22023 (a genuinely malformed argument) keeps 400, which is what makes the split carry information. The MESSAGE is passed through verbatim on every raised arm either way (F227(f)'s clause; `client-fetch.ts:userFacingMessage` strips the raiser's prefix and the §-citation at the one surfacing layer). (3) **§9.3's SECOND `.channel(` in `src/`, opened deliberately and reviewed with this PR.** The budget pin in `single-room-tab.test.ts` said a second hit "is a §9.3 budget event that needs its own review, whoever adds it" — this is that event. §9.3's own budget line names the league channel as one of the three a client may hold ("one socket per client, ≤ 3 channels (current league, current draft, notifications)"), so this is the spec's shape, not an extension of it; the draft spine's topic is `draft:<id>` and structurally cannot carry `league:<id>` events. The pin was rewritten as ONE CHANNEL PER TOPIC and now names both spines. The rule that did NOT move: a consumer never opens its own channel — `use-league-channel.ts` registers every `LEAGUE_CHANNEL_EVENTS` member once and dispatches to the caller's handler map (D109(1)), so L.D4.1's matchups/standings hooks add handlers, never a channel (**F233(a)**). Handlers live in refs so the effect depends only on `leagueId`; the D109(9) stale-registry sweep, the pre-join `setAuth`, `private: true`, refetch-on-every-confirmed-join, refetch-before-resubscribe and the capped backoff are all carried from the draft spine. (4) **Freshness is refetch-on-event, not cache patching (D298), and the decision of WHICH events is pure and pinned.** D296's payloads are column-selected DB-side, so an event cannot reconstruct a feed row; `activityEventInvalidates` admits `transactions` (117/L.D1.9) and `league_chat` (070 — LIVE TODAY: a non-draft context broadcasts to `league:<league_id>`, so a Remix confirmed in one browser already reaches another member's open feed) and refuses everything else, so a `matchups` score tick every few seconds never re-fetches a paged list. The four unshipped D296 events are registered NOW on purpose: the listener costs nothing and the feed starts moving the moment 117 lands, with no edit here. (5) **The activity feed's two scoping decisions, both no-leak.** (a) System posts are filtered to `context = 'league'` — the literal every league-room D97 post carries (111:749, 111:1124, 112:1141). Taking "every system post of this league" instead would publish one member's SOLO MOCK practice to the whole league, because a mock draft's posts carry the launcher's `league_id` with a `draft:<id>` context; the draft room and the recap render their own posts. Non-system chat is never in the feed (chat is its own surface). (b) A non-member reads NOTHING and gets an empty feed rather than a 404 — the established posture for league reads (D114(5)); a transport error is a 500, never an empty list (rule 10). (6) **Paging is measured, not inferred (CLAUDE.md's 1000-row rule).** `limit` ≤ 100 with an over-fetch of `limit + 1` PER SOURCE, so the union's top `limit` is provably the true top `limit` and `has_more` is a measurement; the ceiling plus the over-fetch cannot reach PostgREST's cap, which is asserted in the suite rather than assumed. A NULL or unparseable `created_at` sorts LAST, never as the newest event. (7) **`Date.parse` inside `src/leagues/**` is legal and checked:** the M0 fence bans `Date.now`, argless `new Date()`, bare `Date(...)`, `Date['now']`, `globalThis.Date` and constructor aliases — not a pure parse of a value the database wrote. Lexicographic string compare was rejected as only accidentally correct while every row carries the same UTC offset. All entropy (both `action_id`s and the Remix seed) is minted in the HOOKS, outside the fence (the D112(3)/D114(5) precedent); the seed goes through the catalog's own `mintScheduleSeed`, so the wire value is always inside §11.7's space. (8) **The F65(b) identity guard, applied at BOTH verbs.** 113's replay is kind- and team-scoped (R732) but not ARGUMENT-scoped, and 111's is kind-scoped but not SEED-scoped: reusing your own `action_id` for a different move — or a different seed — returns the FIRST result with no error, and answering 200 would report something the caller never did. Both results carry what the check needs (`team_id`/`add_player_id`/`drop_player_id`; `schedule_seed`), so it costs no extra query. Both are pinned live, with the negative control (the second player really was not added; the board really is still the first seed). (9) **What was deliberately NOT built, each with its reason:** no `GET …/schedule` route (§15.3 prints none — `use-schedule` reads `matchups` + `league_weeks` under the member SELECT policies, D92); no `transactions` READ hook separate from the feed (one read of that table in the app, not two that can disagree); no commissioner-action ENRICHMENT (`commissioner_actions` does not exist — the task text says M6); no `schedule_edit_matchup` route (the drag arm is L.D5.3's UI task, not in this task's four); no live-realtime DELIVERY test (the `draft-realtime-db` harness budgets ~224s of retry for the boot-window race and R163 already records what parallel load does to it — the wiring is source-pinned here and L.D6.2's E2E is the end-to-end proof; **F233(c)**). (10) **§15.6's hook list was CHECKED, not missed:** it names 15 hooks and has never been amended for the ~35 that landed since (`use-draft-bids`, `use-draft-controls`, `use-mock-drafts`, `use-scoring-templates` are all absent), so it is indicative and no erratum is owed — the spec needed no change for this task at all. (11) Action-id prefixes **af7** (transactions-api-db) and **af8** (schedule-api-db) — the D108(14) registry, swept 2026-09-03 (af0–af6 taken). **(12) The #255 fix round (R768–R775), and what each one changed.** **R768 — the one real defect: a COMMITTED move reported to the caller as a failure.** The F65(b) guards at both verbs compare client strings byte-for-byte against uuids POSTGRES wrote, and Postgres renders `uuid` lowercase while `z.uuid()` is case-INSENSITIVE — so an UPPERCASE `team_id`/`action_id` (a body the route's own schema accepts) reached the RPC, the add/drop COMMITTED (roster row + transactions row), and the guard then answered **409 'That didn't go through'** with the `action_id` spent, so the retry the copy asks for could not work either. CLAUDE.md's "never let 'nothing happened' mean 'it worked'" run in reverse, by the very guard that exists to prevent it. Fixed at the SCHEMA, once, in a new shared `inseason-ids.ts` (`normalizedUuid = z.uuid().transform(v => v.toLowerCase())`) applied to `team_id`/`action_id` on add/drop and `action_id` on the Remix confirm — so the RPC and the guard both see the form the database returns. The guards keep every tooth: a reused id naming a different move, or a different seed, is still 409, pinned uppercase in both stack suites. **R769 — the `league:<id>` spine was per-hook-instance, and its D109(9) stale-registry sweep evicted OTHER LIVE INSTANCES OF ITSELF.** Latent (one caller today) and guaranteed the moment L.D4.1 followed F233(a): the supabase browser client is a singleton so `getChannels()` is shared, realtime-js returns the existing channel for a held topic, and B's mount removed A's channel → A saw CLOSED → `onDrop` (an invalidate) + reopen in 1s → A's sweep removed B's → forever, two invalidations per cycle, with `attempt` reset to 0 on every SUBSCRIBED so the backoff never grew out of it. The spine is now a **module-level refcounted room per topic** (`leagueRooms` / `joinLeagueRoom` / release), fanning ONE channel out to N handler maps — which is what the file's docblock had claimed all along, so the code was made true rather than the claim weakened. Still exactly one `.channel(` in the file, so both budget pins hold unchanged. A late joiner gets `onJoin` on attach when the room is already live (its cache may predate the room), and the room closes only on the LAST release. **R770 — the activity cursor was `created_at` alone against a `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` order**, so every item sharing a page-boundary instant was served on NO page, silently, forever. No M4 writer produces such a tie; §13.2/§14's waiver processor (N claims resolved atomically) and M6's `commissioner_move` (a transactions row + a system post in one txn) both will. The cursor is now composite — `before` + `before_id`, applied as PostgREST `or(created_at.lt."T",and(created_at.eq."T",id.lt."ID"))` on BOTH source queries, with `next_before_id` beside `next_before` and a lone `before_id` refused by name rather than paging as if no cursor were sent. `activity-service.test.ts`'s header had already CLAIMED this coverage (its tie test proved determinism, not cursor survival) — the claim is now true. **R773 — three guards that could not fail** (`isLeagueChannelEvent(event)` on a value drawn from `LEAGUE_CHANNEL_EVENTS`; `activityEventInvalidates('transactions'|'league_chat')` inside handlers that only existed for those two events). Taken the second way D272(20) allows: the feed's handler map is now DERIVED — `LEAGUE_CHANNEL_EVENTS.filter(activityEventInvalidates)` — so the predicate SELECTS the events rather than decorating them, and `isLeagueChannelEvent` was deleted as dead (the unknown-event-inert property holds by construction: only known events are bound, and dispatch is an optional call). **R771/R772/R774/R775 were record corrections**, each fixed at its site: a docblock pointing at `schedule-routes.test.ts`, which does not exist; F227(f)/F224(e) citing "the members-api precedent" for a P0001 → 409 mapping that precedent does not carry (the CODE is right — 409 governs the in-season family per the #255 ruling — the CITATION was false); F233(c) implying nothing about realtime delivery was provable when the `league_chat` arm was; and F233(f), the new row routing the source-pinned ANON arm to a future Route Handler harness (the reviewer verified the DB defence in depth: anon reads 0 rows on all four tables, no anon EXECUTE on the three RPCs).

- **D309 — L.D1.5 build mechanics: the number note, the verb's shape (and why the idempotency key is a STAMP, not a third ledger), E32 as built (which weeks, which datum, which edges), the lineup-lock question decided from the text (E34), the `free_agency` reading, fa_hold's inclusive boundary, caps by payload key, the CHECK, fixture discipline, the proof chain, and what was deliberately not done.** **Number note (D161 — measured 2026-09-02 on `origin/main` @ `a5ee6bd` and `origin/docs/DR2-draft-room-v2`, the only other open branch):** `D309` / `F227` / `R753` → **0** on both ⇒ D309 and F227 taken here (no R taken — no review yet; no Q filed — nothing halted); chain heads at task time: `ls supabase/migrations/ | tail -1` → `112_lineups.sql`, `ls supabase/tests/ | tail -1` → `060_lineups.sql` ⇒ **113 / 061**, the tasks-M4 §7 reservations CONFIRMED; spec header 2.16.16 ⇒ **2.16.17** (a PATCH: §13.1 / §12.9 / §12.19 annotations the build measured — no ruling touched). D137 provenance: NO function is replaced — 112's `lineup_kickoff_internal` (the per-player kickoff for a player's NFL team) and `lineup_current_week_internal`, 111's `schedule_window_internal`, 052's `is_league_member` are CALLED by name. **(1) The shape — one verb, one seam, two lock helpers, one stamp.** `roster_add_drop` (DEFINER, `search_path=''`, REVOKE FROM PUBLIC/anon) reads transaction `now()` and calls `roster_add_drop_internal(…, p_at)` (plain, triple-REVOKEd — the D307(3)/D308 seam 061 drives at kickoff±1s and close±1s); `pool_game_lock_internal` (E32 for one week) and `pool_game_lock_any_internal` (every week that could still bind). **Why the idempotency key is a column on `transactions` (`action_id` + a partial UNIQUE on `(league_id, action_id)`) and not a third ledger table:** D307(2)'s argument for `schedule_actions`/`lineup_actions` was that those verbs' domain rows are deleted/overwritten by later actions, erasing a stamp; a `transactions` row is APPEND-ONLY (§12.9 — M6 may flip `status`, the row never goes away), so the stamp survives every later action, exactly the 099 `draft_budget_adjustments` shape; `payload` IS the returned document, replayed byte-identically (061 D2 text equality + a four-table digest unchanged); a refused call writes nothing so the retry re-evaluates; replay is kind-scoped (a `trade` row with the same id refuses by name — R732) and team-scoped (another team's id refuses). One more ledger for M6's fold (F223(a)/F224(f)) avoided. **(2) E32 as built.** The lock is evaluated PER PLAYER from `nfl_games.kickoff_at` at the instant, over the set of NFL weeks `w ≤ current` whose `correction_window_ends_at > at` (or is NULL) — the current week AND the previous one when its Thursday-06:00 window is still open (a week's window closes inside the NEXT week; 061's calendar closes week 2's window before the fixture instant so the no-game-rows fallback of an earlier week cannot bind — the first cut's calendar had it open and locked everyone, which is how the two-window shape was found; the two-window claim was UNMEASURED in the first cut (R754) and is now pinned in 061 §F5/E7: NE played in week 2 and is a week-3 bye, week 2's window at close−1s refuses BOTH the add and the drop naming week 2, AT the close and at +1s both live and the result reports the current week's bye datum). Per week: 112's `lineup_kickoff_internal` (bye = game rows but none for the team → never locked; NO game rows → the week datum for EVERYONE, the R740 posture, arm named `nfl_weeks.starts_at` — which on the REAL calendar is a full-season FREEZE of add/drop until game rows exist: the reviewer measured hourly over 2026 from week 1's start with 0 `nfl_games` → free 0 of 2,709 hours, and 270 of 2,709 with only `first_kickoff_at` seeded; local stack and production carry 0 games for 2026 — the dated dependency on L.D2.1/L.D3.1 is F228 (R755)) and the week's `nfl_weeks.correction_window_ends_at` (D294's letter; a NULL window after a kickoff refuses BY NAME — never an unbounded lock read as free, 061 E6). Locked iff `kickoff ≤ at < window_end`: closed AT the kickoff (the E41 convention), OPEN at the close ("until the week clears" is strictly before) — 061 E1/E2 (add) and F1/F2 (drop) pin −1s/AT/+1s at BOTH edges; the two sides are independent clauses and the DoD probe removes the drop clause alone. **Probe figures, corrected 2026-09-03 (R761 — the number written here was the FIRST CUT's and three rounds stale):** the CURRENT figures are **10 drop-side cells red (49/50/52/57/67/75/76/84/86/87) and the file ABORTS at cell 88 — 87 of 160 ran** (the accepted drop's state breaks a later fixture), every add-lock cell green. The trail: 7 of 130 (first cut) → 8 of 139 (review round) → 10 of 150 (Q32/Q33 application) → 10 of 160 (this fix round). `league_player_pool.locked_until` and the `locked_in_game` state are NEVER read (pinned by prosrc) — 114's `lineup_lock_tick` maintains them for the pool VIEW (D291); an add evaluates the games table whatever the stored state says. **(3) The lineup-lock question — RULED BY CHRIS 2026-09-03 (Q32 + its amendment, §3, verbatim there) and APPLIED: the lock is PLAYER-LEVEL.** A player locks at his own kickoff (E32's window) and then cannot move in ANY direction — not bench→lineup, not lineup→bench, not into another slot, not dropped; a player whose game has not started moves and drops freely regardless of what else is locked ("if its mid day sunday and all the users starters are locked … a player on their Bench that doesn't play until Monday night … can be dropped"). 113 as landed: the drop is refused iff the player's OWN game has kicked off (both settings' letter); - **D308 — L.D1.4 build mechanics: the number note, the six-function shape and why a second ledger table, the F18 swap and the legacy-row disposition, the fit as built (and the measurement that shaped its golden), the lock law's datum chain, the current-week read, the IR contract and the designation bridge, `allow_illegal_lineups` as built, the commissioner arm, idempotency, and what was deliberately not done.** **Number note (D161 — measured 2026-09-02 on `origin/main` @ `4fd3f8a` and `origin/docs/DR2-draft-room-v2`, the only other open branch):** `D308` / `F224` / `R736` → **0** on both (the one `Q32` hit on main is D306's own number-note text, not a filed question) ⇒ D308 and F224 taken here (no R taken — no review yet; no Q filed — nothing halted); chain heads at task time: `ls supabase/migrations/ | tail -1` → `111_schedule_remix.sql`, `ls supabase/tests/ | tail -1` → `059_schedule_remix.sql` ⇒ **112 / 060**, the tasks-M4 §7 reservations CONFIRMED; spec header 2.16.15 ⇒ **2.16.16** (a PATCH: §11.2/§12.13 annotations the build measured — no ruling touched). D137 provenance: NO function is replaced — `schedule_window_internal` (111) and `is_league_member`/`is_league_commish` (052) are CALLED by name; 001's two `team_lineups` policies are DROPPED by name (the swap). **(1) The shape — one verb, one seam, four helpers, one ledger.** `set_lineup` (DEFINER, `search_path=''`, REVOKE FROM PUBLIC/anon) reads transaction `now()` and calls `set_lineup_internal(…, p_at)` — plain, triple-REVOKEd, the postgres-only seam pgTAP drives at kickoff±1s (rule 10 / D307(3): a client-facing verb never takes a caller-supplied instant — a manager could pick the free window). Helpers, all plain + `search_path=''` + REVOKEd: `lineup_fit_internal` (the pure E16 matcher), `lineup_kickoff_internal` (the per-player datum), `lineup_current_week_internal`, `lineup_designation_internal`; plus `team_league_id`, a DEFINER policy predicate deliberately WITHOUT a REVOKE (the 052:27–29 documented deviation — it is evaluated as the calling role by the RLS policy). **Why a second ledger TABLE (`lineup_actions`) rather than a stamp:** a lineup's domain row is OVERWRITTEN by every later set, so an action_id stamped on `team_lineups` would be erased by the next edit and a stale retry of an EARLIER submit would re-execute over the newer lineup (exactly D307(2)'s argument for `schedule_actions`); the ledger row survives every later action, the replay is byte-identical (060 pins text equality + digest unchanged), RLS on with ZERO policies (060 walks manager/commish/anon: SELECT 0 while postgres sees N, INSERT 42501, UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING 0). Not an audit; M6 folds it with `schedule_actions` (F224(f)). **(2) The F18 swap (C12), and the legacy rows.** DROP `"Lineups follow team visibility"` (001:853–854, USING (true)) and `"Users can manage own team lineups"` (001:856–861, keyed on `teams.owner_id`); CREATE one SELECT `is_league_member(team_league_id(team_id))`; NO write policy for any role. 060 pins both directions (the 052/019 pattern): a member with NO teams row reads every lineup in the league; the C12 ghost (owns a teams row in the league, not a member) reads NOTHING and his INSERT raises 42501 — both of which 001 GRANTED; the manager who owns T2 reads but gets UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING 0 and INSERT 42501; the commissioner's direct UPDATE touches 0. **Legacy rows:** MEASURED on the local stack 2026-09-02 — `team_lineups` holds **0** rows (0 on standalone teams, 0 on league teams; `teams` holds 0). Production was NOT queried from this session (the Builder cannot) and may hold pre-league rows on standalone teams (`teams.league_id IS NULL`). Disposition: **EXPLICITLY ORPHANED**, not owner-readable — after 112 no policy reaches such a row (060 pins the standalone owner reading 0 of his own legacy row while postgres sees 1). Safe under either population because NO application code reads or writes `team_lineups` (`grep -rn team_lineups src e2e scripts` → only `src/types/database.ts`; 053's banner: no app code writes teams), so an orphaned row is one no product surface could show before either; if the standalone teams feature returns it gets its own policy then (F224(g)). **(3) The fit as built — and the measurement that shaped the E1 golden.** `lineup_fit_internal(slots, players)` is a BFS augmenting-path matcher over ≤ ~12 slot instances × ≤ ~11 starters. The submitted `slot_map` KEYS are the manager's placement: every per-slot-valid placement is SEEDED verbatim (fixed/locked players first) and kept unless an augmenting path needs to move it; a per-slot-invalid placement is re-seated along an augmenting path if ANY legal arrangement exists and the canonical map is returned (`rearranged: true`, `moved[]` named); a player with no augmenting path is refused BY NAME with the slot he wanted and what it accepts (E16's "names the unfillable slot"). Locked players are FIXED vertices: no path may traverse a slot a locked player owns (060 §D pins the fixed shape unplaced beside its unlocked twin re-seated). Greedy first-eligible (no augmentation) fails the two-flex trap — the DoD probe. **Measured while pinning the RPC golden:** the first cut of E1 left SUPERFLEX empty, and the matcher placed the mis-keyed RB1 THERE (the shortest augmenting path is a free eligible slot, no displacement) — correct, but not the trap; the shipped E1 fixture fills SUPERFLEX (TE2) so the only route is the displacement (WR1 → W/T, RB1 → W/R/T), and the stored map is pinned as a literal. Positions are normalized DEF → DST (the 086 shape); `players.position` is single-valued, so the spec's per-player multi-position eligibility array is not consulted (none exists — F224(h)). **(4) The lock law's datum chain (§11.2/§7.3.6/E42/§23.3; rule 9).** Every instant is read from `nfl_games.kickoff_at` at evaluation time; `locked_at` is the RECORD of the earliest instant any slot of the lineup locks (the week datum under `first_game_of_week`, the earliest started player's kickoff under `per_player_kickoff`), never the decider — 060 E6 moves KC's kickoff to now+1h and the "locked" slot re-opens with `locked_at` still saying otherwise, then to exactly now() and it locks again (E42 both ways; AT the kickoff is locked — closed on the kickoff side, the E41 convention). `per_player_kickoff`: (a) every stored starter whose game has kicked off must sit at the same key (replace / move / bench all refuse naming slot, player, instant and datum arm); (b) a played player never enters a slot he was not stored at; every unlocked slot of the same lineup stays editable (pinned by editing wr:0 beside the locked qb:0). The per-player datum `lineup_kickoff_internal(season, week, nfl_team, at)`: min kickoff of the team's game(s) that week (`players.team` ↔ `nfl_games.home_team/away_team`, both the Sleeper vocabulary L.D2.1 writes); a week WITH game rows but none for the team = BYE (no lock, flagged `bye`); a week with NO game rows at all falls back to `schedule_window_internal`'s chain (`nfl_weeks.first_kickoff_at` → `starts_at`) for EVERY player — the conservative direction (D307(3): the window only narrows) — 060 §H pins week 4 locked for every slot once `first_kickoff_at` passes, the arm NAMED in the refusal. `players.bye_week` is NOT read (§23.3: kickoff-driven). `first_game_of_week`: after the week datum ANY change refuses; an identical submit under lock is `no_changes`, never a refusal (pinned). **(5) The current week, the IR contract, the designation bridge.** `lineup_current_week_internal(league, at)` = the league's greatest `league_weeks.week` whose `nfl_weeks.starts_at` ≤ at, clamped to the first week before the season — a read of the calendar TABLE at the §23.3 boundaries 114's `league_week_advance` will flip `league_weeks.status` on, not wall-clock arithmetic; `league_weeks.status` is NOT read for tenure because it has no writer on this chain (R730's lesson) — F224(a) hands 114 the choice of switching the read or keeping it (they derive from the same rows). IR spots are ROSTER-level state, so an IR move is judged against the current week whatever `p_week` the submit names, and the submitted map is the WHOLE picture: IR spots ride `slot_map` as `"<ir_key>:0"` and an absent IR key is a REMOVAL (the contract L.D4.1/L.D5.1 inherit — F224(e)). Placement requires the designation NOW; a spot change is a placement on the new spot (restricted tenure re-checked); Restricted sets `ir_lock_until_week = current + min_weeks` and removal refuses while `current < lock` (060: placed week 3 with min 4 ⇒ 7; refused at 3 and at **6**, ACCEPTED at **7** — the calendar moved inside the txn with the weeks' `first_kickoff_at` arm kept ahead so tenure, not lock timing, is what those cells measure); an IR'd player who turns Active is KEPT and flagged `ir_ineligible`; IR + starter in one map refuses ("exactly one slot"); an IR move on a played player refuses on lock timing. **The designation bridge, measured:** `players.status` on the stack carries the FEED's spellings (Active 720, Questionable 85, IR 71, Inactive 10, PUP 7, Sus 1, DNR 1, NA 1 — `sleeper.ts:202` collapses `injury_status` into it, C56) while the catalog's `IR_DESIGNATIONS` are OUT/IR/Doubtful/PUP/NFI/Suspended (§7.3.2); `lineup_designation_internal` maps case-insensitively with `Sus` → Suspended and everything else (Active, Questionable, Inactive, NA, DNR) → no designation. Pinned (`Out` → OUT accepted on an OUT/IR spot; Questionable refused by name; `Sus` → Suspended). F224(b) asks the sync layer to normalize at ingestion so the bridge becomes the identity. **(6) `allow_illegal_lineups` as built (§7.3.6).** Flags per starter: `bye`, `out` (designation in the non-playing set OUT/IR/PUP/NFI/Suspended — Doubtful/Questionable PLAY as far as the lock is concerned), `empty` (an empty instance is allowed under BOTH settings — the setting governs byes/OUT, not vacancies; an empty slot scores 0 like everywhere in the industry); `ir_ineligible` on IR entries; `illegal` = any bye/out/ir_ineligible. TRUE: accepted, flags stored on `starters[].flags` and returned. FALSE: a bye/OUT player in an UNLOCKED starting slot blocks the submit BY NAME (a locked slot's bye/OUT player is not the manager's to change — flagged only); pinned both ways on L2 with the benched twin succeeding. **(7) The commissioner arm.** D293's "(or commissioner)" is built: a commissioner may set ANY team's lineup under the SAME lock law (no past-lock, no past-week edit), and the row records `edited_by_commish = TRUE` (the manager's own set FALSE — both pinned); tasks-M4 §12's audited past-lock/retroactive override is M6's and does not exist here (F224(c)). **(8) Idempotency, loud emptiness, `slot_key`.** `p_action_id` REQUIRED (22023); replay returns the stored jsonb byte-identically and writes nothing; an identical canonical map with no IR move is `no_changes: true` BY NAME (returned, ledgered, `set_at` and the roster digest unchanged — pinned). The lineup row is created on first touch (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then FOR UPDATE, FOUND asserted); every UPDATE's row count is asserted; a week off the calendar, a PAST week (current is 3, week 2 refuses naming the M6 override), a closed week (`correction_window`/`final`), a league not in season, a team of another league, a retired team, an empty roster, an unknown slot key (naming every slot the roster has), an unrostered player, a duplicated player, a non-object map, a non-string value — every one refused by name (060 §G/§H). `league_rosters.slot_key` (072's "M4 manages"): when `p_week` is the current week, starters take their instance key and the rest `bn` (counts asserted against the roster); IR keys are written on placement and `bn` on removal whatever the week; a future-week submit leaves the starters' `slot_key` alone (pinned by digest). - **D307 — L.D1.3 build mechanics: the number note, the five-function shape and why a ledger table, E41 at transaction time (not injected), the seam a post-kickoff Remix leaves, the R728 disposition, the permutation that was measured before it was trusted, and what was deliberately not done.** **Number note (D161 — measured 2026-09-02 on `origin/main` @ `ae61e72` and `origin/docs/DR2-draft-room-v2`, the only other open branch):** `D307` / `F223` / `R730` → **0** on both ⇒ D307 and F223 taken here (no R taken — no review yet; no Q filed — nothing halted); chain heads at task time: `ls supabase/migrations/ | tail -1` → `110_schedule_engine.sql`, `ls supabase/tests/ | tail -1` → `058_schedule_engine.sql` ⇒ **111 / 059**, the tasks-M4 §7 reservations CONFIRMED; spec header 2.16.14 ⇒ **2.16.15** (a PATCH: two §11.7 Remix annotations the build measured — the per-week reading of "all `scheduled` matchups" and E41's datum chain — no ruling touched). D137 provenance: NO function is replaced — 110's `schedule_build_internal` is CALLED by name, never copied (rule 11). **(1) The shape — one plan, three doors.** `schedule_remix_plan_internal(league, seed, at)` is the single place a proposed schedule is computed: the league's seated franchises (110's own team source, same-league by construction), its EFFECTIVE `regular_season_weeks`, the first week (= `min(league_weeks.week)`, so a mid-season league regenerates NFL weeks 10..15, not 1..6), the pure builder with the candidate seed over the WHOLE regular season, then a per-WEEK classification — regenerable iff the `league_weeks` row is `upcoming`, the week's OWN first kickoff is still ahead at call time (R730 — the same datum as E41's, per week), and every row is `scheduled`, un-overridden and unscored (R733). Preview returns the plan; confirm writes from the SAME plan (a client-supplied schedule is never read — D289's "confirm regenerates from the previewed seed in-body"). The diff is one row per (week, game type, team) whose opponent or side changed, with a human line in two shapes ("now plays X instead of Y" / "now hosts|visits X (was away|home)"), `change_count`, and an EXPLICIT `no_changes` for an identical seed (rule 10 — never an empty array read as success). **Why per week, whole:** the spec's "replaces all `scheduled` matchups" cannot be read per ROW without breaking §11.7's own uniqueness invariants — a week with one `final` row and three `scheduled` ones cannot take three generated rows without double-booking the final row's two teams — so a week holding ANY non-`scheduled` row is frozen whole, named in `weeks_frozen[].reason` (`week_live` / `week_final` / `week_correction_window` / `week_kicked_off` / `matchup_not_scheduled` / `matchup_overridden_or_scored`); the never-weaken direction (freeze more, never less). Folded into the spec as v2.16.15 (the fold-back rule). **(2) Why the idempotency ledger is a TABLE (`schedule_actions`), not a stamp on the rows written.** The M3 precedents stamp the action_id on the domain row (099 `draft_budget_adjustments`, 098 `drafts.config`, 077 `leagues.creation_action_id`). A Remix's domain rows are the matchups it writes — and the NEXT Remix deletes every one of them, so a stale retry of the earlier action_id would find no stamp and RE-EXECUTE (regenerating over the later schedule and posting twice); an edit's two stamped rows are erased by any later edit of the same rows the same way. A ledger row survives every later action, so the replay is exact: the stored `result` jsonb is returned byte-identically (059 pins text equality, the post count, the ledger count and a five-table digest unchanged — and that the replay WINS even when the retry carries a different seed: the action_id identifies the SUBMIT, 099/E2). It is an idempotency key, NOT an audit (099/C39's own words): no reason column, no before/after, no actor-facing surface, RLS on with ZERO policies (the 109 `score_fanout` shape — 059 walks commish/manager/anon: SELECT sees 0 while postgres sees 10, INSERT 42501, UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING 0). `commissioner_actions` stays M6's; M6 folds the ledger in (F223(a)). The reason lives in exactly one place until then — the D97 system post's text — which is F40's shipped posture, unchanged. **(3) E41 is evaluated at TRANSACTION time (`now()`), deliberately NOT at an injected instant — and how the boundary is still pinned one unit either side.** D291's `p_now` is the front door of the JOB RPCs (cron-driven, never client-callable). `schedule_remix_confirm` / `schedule_edit_matchup` are CLIENT-FACING commissioner controls: a caller-supplied instant would let a commissioner pick the free window and skip the reason (110 kept `draft_start(uuid)` injection-free for the same reason). So the verbs read `now()`, and 059 applies D146's one-unit rule to the DATUM instead of the clock: inside a transaction `now()` is frozen, so `nfl_games.kickoff_at = now() ± 1s` IS kickoff−1s / kickoff+1s exactly, and `= now()` is AT the kickoff (closed — "until" is strictly before). The datum itself: the league's FIRST week's earliest `nfl_games.kickoff_at` (E41/E42 — a moved kickoff moves the window), falling back to the ruled Mid-season entry chain when the week has no game rows (`nfl_weeks.first_kickoff_at`, then `starts_at` — Wednesday 00:00 ET, EARLIER than the letter): with no game rows the window can only be NARROWER than the truth. Every arm pinned directly on `schedule_window_internal` with −1s/+1s twins; the nfl_games arm also through the RPCs (no-reason confirm free at −1s, refused by name at +1s and AT, blank reason refused, a reason succeeds); and a MID-SEASON league (L2, first week 10) previews FREE while NFL week 1 has already kicked off — league Week 1 is ITS first week (Q29/D288). The sim/e2e drive the window the same way (move `nfl_games.kickoff_at` on the synthetic season — F223(f)). **(4) The seam a post-kickoff Remix leaves, said so nobody reads §11.7's Generation invariants as promises across it.** Frozen weeks keep their rows (pinned BYTE-IDENTICAL over `m::text` — id, scores, updated_at, everything — R601) and the regenerable weeks take the builder's rows for THOSE week numbers from the new seed (pinned ≡ the builder restricted to those weeks — the season stays ONE generation with weeks carved out, never re-numbered). Within every regenerated week the per-week invariants hold (each team once per game type cross-side, E40 — pinned over every week after the carve-out). ACROSS the seam the season-wide balance (repeat spacing/spread, home/away alternation within a pairing) is NOT re-established: a team may meet the same opponent in a frozen week 3 and a regenerated week 4. That is exactly E41's "affecting only `scheduled` future weeks" — the past stands, the future is a new draw. **(5) R728, dispositioned.** The builder folds `seed mod 2^31−1` with 0 → 1, so THREE catalog seeds share LCG state 1 — 0, 1 and 2^31−1 — not the one collision 110:550–553 and D306(1) named; 110 is merged and its comment is left as printed (111's banner and this entry carry the correction). 059 §B pins `build(2147483647) = build(1)` and `build(0) = build(1)` beside `build(2147483646) ≠ build(1)`. DECIDED: the accepted seed space stays the catalog's [0, 2^31−1] (`SCHEDULE_SEED_MAX`), NOT capped at 2^31−2 — the alias is behaviourally harmless (every stored seed still reproduces ITS schedule, which is all §11.7 asks; two of 2^31 seeds happen to reproduce another's) and a cap would move `mintScheduleSeed` + its `0x7fffffff` pin for no product effect. Both verbs refuse outside the space by name (22023) with the one-unit twins pinned (−1 / 0, 2^31−1 / 2^31). **(6) The permutation — a design claim measured FALSE before it shipped (D276).** A pairing change is never a single-row write: every team plays exactly once per week per game type, so the new teams' vacated slots must take the displaced teams (home-slot displaced → the new home team's slot, away → the new away team's; a side flip displaces nobody; two new teams from one sibling swap the pairings; two from two siblings touch three rows). The first draft wrote single-row UPDATEs and CLAIMED the per-side unique indexes could never see a duplicate mid-way; the smoke run refused it on `uniq_matchup_away_per_week` — a same-side swap (T3 away in both rows) collides in EITHER order. The shipped shape PARKS the sibling rows on a game type asserted EMPTY for that week (`third_place`; a row already there refuses by name — pinned, with the no-sibling side flip as the one-unit sibling), writes the edited row, then returns each sibling to its game type with its displaced team seated — every intermediate state legal to both indexes, one transaction. Two new teams from the SAME sibling merge into one entry (the second draft's parking count assertion caught the duplicate — also a real refusal, also fixed). After the writes, IN-BODY: every seated franchise exactly once across home ∪ away for that (week, game type) — R703's cross-side shape — and E40 (no pair in both game types that week); the unique indexes stay the race backstop. 059 walks all four arms, pins zero rows left on the parking type, and every refusal by name (foreign team — F222(a)'s L.D1.3 half — retired team, self, bye, no-op, live row, live sibling, non-upcoming week, playoff row, E40, parking type in use). **(7) 045's census, 62 → 63.** `schedule_actions` joins the sorted literal (before `score_fanout` — `sch` < `sco`); §C's/§E's mid-state allowlists are re-derived UNCHANGED (the ledger is written only by the two DEFINER verbs, both `in_season`-only and commish-only — unreachable from a mock; the delta cells passed in the same run). **(8) Proof chain (F135: every run recorded).** Fresh `db reset` 001–111 clean; `test:db` **60 files / 4,163 asserts, PASS** (059 = **132**; +132 over 4,031); `npm run test` ****167 files / 3,150 tests, all green (first attempt, stack up)****; `test:gate` **24/24**; type-check + lint clean; typegen **+82 / −0** (the table, the five functions, `ScheduleAction` alias; the seam byte-identical). One cycle of n−1 rounds is a 1-factorization of K_n, so plain cycling gives balanced repeats (spread ≤ 1) with every repeat exactly n−1 weeks later — that is ≥ 7 for every v1 size, so the spec's "≥ 3" holds with room, and 058 pins the MEASURED minimum (7/9/11/13) rather than the construction. Home/away: a pair's base side is (round, position) parity — stable per pair because a pair meets at exactly one (round, position) — and flips on every later meeting of that pair in that game type (a jsonb counter). `second_opponent` = round (r + offset) of the same factorization with offset drawn 1..n−2, so the secondary round shares no edge with the primary round: E40 by construction, pinned by measurement (and the break probe skews exactly that offset). Input-order independence is designed in (the ids are sorted before the seed acts) and pinned. The seed folds mod 2^31−1 with a 0 → 1 map (R727 — was mod 2^31−2, which aliased 0 ≡ 2147483646 and 1 ≡ 2147483647): the one unavoidable collision of a 2^31 seed space onto 2^31−2 states is seed 0 ≡ seed 1, said out loud and pinned beside seed 0 ≠ seed 2147483646. **2026-09-02 — Builder (L.D3.1, the nflverse data adapter — the F11 parallel data PR; branch `feat/M4-L.D3.1-nflverse-adapter`; **TS only — no migration, no schema, no typegen**; takes **D304**; **FLIPS F11 ✅**; amends **F216** + **F211**; files **F219**)**

- **D304 — L.D3.1 build mechanics: the number note, composition-not-fork (why `ingestWeek` is untouched), the two published files and what each honestly supplies, the Eastern→UTC seam, the status/team/season vocabularies, the inactives measurement (C56's site), the CLI + the one real back-fill and why it was restored, the proofs + probes as run, and the residuals.** **Number note (D161 — D, F, R, Q checked together 2026-09-02 across `main` @ `2c0e016`, the open halt branch `halt/M4-L.D1.2-schedule-engine-Q30` (#248 — Q30/Q31, B7, F215 taken there) and `docs/DR2-draft-room-v2` (#180)):** D head **D303**, F head **F218**, R head **R715** on main ⇒ this task takes **D304** + **F219** (`grep -c` each → 0 on all three); no R number is taken (the reviewer's band starts at R716). No migration, no pgTAP, no typegen — `git diff -- src/types/database.ts` empty; chain heads untouched (109 / 057); D137 n/a. Worked in the main tree on its own branch — no other builder was live (the schema lane is halted on #248). **(1) Composition, not a fork.** `NflverseProvider` (`src/lib/leagues/stats/nflverse/nflverse-provider.ts`, +`csv.ts`, +`eastern-time.ts`) implements the §23.1 `StatsProvider` interface unchanged, and the back-fill is `ingestWeek(provider, time, io)` exactly as L.D2.1 shipped it — `ingestWeek` is byte-identical on this branch, its contract needed no addition, and `nfl_games` keeps ONE writer (D303(3)). The stack suite composes the two the way production will. **(2) The files, pinned by path** (`NFLVERSE_URLS`; plain `fetch` of nflverse-data GitHub release assets, no HTML, no third-party API — the standing rule): `schedules/games.csv` (all seasons, one 2 MB file; 2026 = 272 REG rows, every `gametime` published, measured) and `weekly_rosters/roster_weekly_<season>.csv` (per (team, week, player) with roster `status` AND a `sleeper_id` column). Every column the adapter reads is required BY NAME (`requireColumns`) and every row is a Zod parse — a renamed column or a ragged row refuses before a single game is interpreted (pinned both ways). `injuries_<season>.csv` exists for 2025 but NOT for 2026 (404 at fetch time) and is not consumed: it is the Friday report (`Out/Doubtful/Questionable`), not inactives, and Q1 keeps Sleeper as the designation source. **(3) The Eastern→UTC seam (§23.3's load-bearing conversion).** `gametime` is a US/Eastern wall clock with no offset. `easternToUtc(gameday, gametime)` takes the offset from the platform's IANA data through `Intl` (`America/New_York`) — never a hard-coded −4/−5 and never the process zone — with a one-step re-check across the shift, so the fall-back of 2026-11-01 02:00 (INSIDE NFL week 8: Thu Oct 29 20:15 EDT → `2026-10-30T00:15Z`, Sun Nov 1 13:00 EST → `18:00Z`) resolves from zone rules; the ambiguous 01:xx hour (never a kickoff) resolves to its first occurrence. Ten literals pin it (the September opener, the week-8 Thu/Sun/SNF/MNF quartet, the week-9 09:30 ET Madrid game, a January week-18 slot, and the D146 pair 01:59 EDT / 03:00 EST), plus the raw offset read (240 on Oct 31, 300 on Nov 2). **(4) Status honesty.** nflverse can say only "a result is posted" — the adapter emits exactly `{scheduled, final}` (pinned over both fixture seasons), never `live` or `postponed`; a postponed/moved game arrives as a changed `gameday`/`gametime`/`week` and becomes a moved `nfl_games` row through `ingestWeek`'s diff (E42's mechanism is evaluation-time reads of that row). Live status comes from the composite's base tier (see (8)). **Regular season only** (`game_type = 'REG'`, like the sleeper tier's `/schedule/nfl/regular/`): postseason rows are counted and dropped — `nfl_games.game_type` defaults to `'regular'` and `ingestWeek` never writes it, so writing week 19–22 rows would have mislabelled them; D303's "once L.D3.1's feed carries 19–22" is therefore "it deliberately does not" (R707's skip stays dormant, still pinned by L.D2.1). **(5) Team vocabulary.** The house codes are `nfl-teams.ts`'s (Sleeper's schedule uses them too — measured on the 2025-wk2 fixture, `LAR`); nflverse's 2026 rows differ in exactly one code, `LA` → `LAR` (`NFLVERSE_TEAM_TO_HOUSE`, measured against all 32); any code outside the house set REFUSES (a relocation must be mapped deliberately, never written as a stray string). The nflverse `game_id` (`2026_01_NE_SEA`) is the `nfl_games.id` — stable, published, self-describing (F219 records that the table has no `source` column). **(6) Inactives — C56's site.** Measured on `roster_weekly_2025.csv` (46,849 rows): `status = 'INA'` appears for 3,593 rows, 5–6 per team per played week (KC 6 / ARI 5 in week 1, beside 48 `ACT`), ZERO for teams on bye, present weeks 1–18 — that is the game-day inactive list, published after the fact. 876 of those rows lack `sleeper_id` (OL/DL/LB — positions Sleeper does not track); the adapter drops and COUNTS them. `getInactives(season, week)` groups INA rows onto the week's game per team (`ProviderInactives` is per game) and sorts ids for determinism; `publishedAt` = the injected `time.now()` — D16's accepted limitation (a back-fill loses arrival timing), stated on the type, not hidden. A team with INA rows but no game that week is counted and named (never seen in 2025); a week with finals but zero INA rows is named as a feed that has not caught up. The 2026 file at land time carries pre-season week-1 rows only (`ACT/CUT/RES/W04/RET/EXE`, no `INA`), so the CLI's inactives pass for 2026 week 1 reports "no game of the week is final yet (nothing to declare)" — the fixture is the 2025 KC+ARI week for shape. Nothing writes inactives anywhere (no table exists; M5's consumer reads the feed — F211 amended). The adapter never touches `players.status`. **(7) What it does NOT supply, loudly.** `getWeekStats`/`getInjuries` return `[]` with the reason on the adapter's call log (`provider.reports` / `lastReport` — a provider method has no report channel of its own), and `ingestWeek` then names the empty section in its own report (`provider returned zero stat rows…`, `score_fanout: no scoring delta…` — both pinned over the stack). `capabilities` is the empty set: no §23.5 tier is claimed. A season the file lacks THROWS (`zero rows for season 2024 … refusing an empty schedule`), never an empty success. **(8) The composite.** `withNflverseCalendar(base, nflverse)` — name `<base>+nflverse`, capabilities the base's — returns nflverse's schedule with the base tier's status merged per game matched on `week:away@home` (rank scheduled < live < final < postponed; `postponed` is a positive claim a T+1 `scheduled` must not undo), base-only games counted (`lastScheduleReport`), `getGameStates` from the merged set, `getWeekStats`/`getInjuries` delegated to the base, `getInactives` to nflverse — pinned with a fake base incl. the LAR match on both sides. This is what L.D2.3 binds (F216 amended). **(9) The CLI and the one real run.** `npm run sync:nflverse -- <season> [week]` (`scripts/sync-nflverse.ts`; sync territory, service client, `.env.local` unless overridden) runs ONE `ingestWeek` poll with the standalone adapter — the schedule read is season-wide, so one run back-fills every game and every calendar week's bounds — then lists the week's inactives read-only. - **D300 — Ingestion writes everything the jobs read; the delta queue only ever sees real changes.** L.D2.1 extends the ingestion path (the `sync-live` seam): `getSchedule` upserts `nfl_games` (idempotent, diff-aware) and maintains `nfl_weeks.first_kickoff_at`/`last_game_ends_at` (F9's columns — live-updated at last); `getWeekStats` upserts `player_stats` incl. the NEW `advanced` JSONB (C59) with **injected time on `updated_at`** (the D12 replay-determinism seam, already refactored in M0); unchanged rows are skipped and only real deltas enqueue to `score_fanout` (§23.2). Provider outage → after 3 failed polls the `stats_degraded` flag raises (a small flag surface the UI banner reads; never wrong numbers, E45). **F13 dispositioned here (its row names the M4 Architect): non-`'sleeper'` `source` values are CORRECT** — fixture/synthetic ingestion writes `source: provider.name` so a row's provenance is always honest; the gate's zero-real-data claim is asserted BY that column (`source = 'synthetic'` for every gate-written row), which turns F13's worry into the gate's own instrument.

L.D6.4 is the real-replay gate: **calendar-blocked on the first recorded 2026 week (F10's ops window)**; cent-exactness proven against **hand-computed fixtures** (≥ 2 leagues × all teams × the full week, computed by hand on paper into stored literals — the D62 discipline — plus per-position spot checks), lock instants asserted against recorded kickoffs, Remix walked with its D290 posture. **The flexed-game clause (C55): asserted on the first recorded week that CONTAINS a kickoff move** — recorded reality decides which week that is; if the chosen replay week lacks one, the lock-move assertion runs additionally against the earliest recorded week that has one (E42's mechanism is evaluation-time reads, which a recorded move exercises exactly).
- **D298 — Where F167's freshness question lands for in-season surfaces.** In-season member views (matchups, standings, activity, lineup lock state) get their freshness from the **`league:<id>` broadcast + refetch-on-event** — the one mechanism F167's own row names as prompt and event-driven — so the SE-era "an open view learns nothing" limitation does not propagate into the season surfaces. **This does NOT close F167**: the scoring-DOCUMENT editor/member-view mechanism (a pre-draft surface) remains the row's open decision, Chris's/SE's, untouched here. Recorded so the next reader knows M4 chose the broadcast lane deliberately, not by accident.
- **D297 — Standings are a computed read over `team_week_results`; the results table is derived and rebuildable.** `league_standings(league_id)` orders by the league's stored `tiebreakers` chain (§7.3.7): Win% → PF → H2H (clean two-team ties only — 3+ groups SKIP it, E63; `total_points` leagues skip it entirely, E64) → PA (higher wins, deliberate) → division record → seeded deterministic coin flip. `matchups` stays the pairing/score/override source of truth; `rebuild_team_week_results(league_id, week)` re-derives a week from `matchups` + lineups for corrections/overrides (§12.18's precedence note) and is the write door's rebuild path. Points For counts **once per week** regardless of median/second games (§11.7); E38 two-decimal ties are real ties; E39 exact-median = tie.
- **D296 — In-season realtime: one compact event per league per batch; F42 dispositioned per table.** New Broadcast-from-DB triggers on `league:<league_id>`: `matchups` (UPDATE — the coalesced `scores_updated` carrier), `team_week_results` (finalization), `transactions` (INSERT — the activity feed's subscriber arrives in M4), `league_weeks` (status flips — the "week is final" moment). Payloads column-selected, nothing blind (never scores-by-player, never claim data). Of F42's six: `league_weeks` + (via `transactions`' feed) the activity surface gain their subscribers here; **`league_members`/`team_managers`/`teams`/`league_invites`/`league_lists` still have NO M4 subscriber and are re-waived per table again** (pgTAP 024's pin updates to the shrunken set with the same message discipline). **F9 (nfl_weeks trigger): decided NO trigger** — locks are server-evaluated and clients read week state through `league_weeks` (which now broadcasts); `nfl_weeks` stays reference data with zero subscribers, pinned trigger-less with its reason. Clients refetch box-score lines on `scores_updated` (§11.4); **no Postgres Changes anywhere** (§9 doctrine).
- **D295 — The correction-window split (C54, decided).** M4 owns the SEMANTICS: (a) a post-final-game delta arriving **inside** the week's correction window flows through the same fan-out and recomputes non-final matchups (they display `final (pending corrections)` — `league_weeks.status = 'correction_window'`); (b) `finalize_matchups` runs only after `correction_window_ends_at` AND all games final (§23.2 — no league state advances on partial data), flips `league_weeks → final`, and from then on the write door **refuses** auto-recompute for that week — a post-window delta lands in `player_stats` but changes NO league cell (the §23.4 "not auto-applied" half, proven by the `correction_post_window` scenario). M6's L.E2 adds the DETECTION artifacts (`stat_correction_events`, the corrections view, the flagged commissioner-apply path). Two-phase/charted semantics ride the same rails: a rules key with no delivered stat is **pending, never 0** (E61 — the worker carries delivered-key bookkeeping so `charted_late` renders pending and `charted_revision` recomputes in-window).
- **D294 — Pool discipline (L.D5): derived truth + lazy rows, one serialization point.** A player with no `league_player_pool` row is `free_agent` if unowned (§12.19); rows are created on first transition. `rostered` rows mirror `league_rosters` and the mirror is ASSERTED, not trusted — the reconciliation job (L.D2.3) checks it nightly, and the sim sweep checks it after every scenario. `roster_add_drop` is SECURITY DEFINER, locks the **league row** first (the house lock-order law: `leagues` before anything), then validates: exclusivity (072's unique — a friendly refusal, never a raw 23505), roster capacity, **E32 game-day locks** (`player_game_lock` on ⇒ add AND drop refuse from that player's kickoff until the week's `correction_window_ends_at`, evaluated per D291), waiver state (an `on_waivers` player with `waivers_until` in the future refuses; a lapsed `waivers_until` is FCFS-addable per `free_agency` — state evaluated at read, no sweeper needed in M4), acquisition caps (`acquisitions_per_week`/`per_season` counted from `transactions`), `fa_hold_hours` (an early drop of a held FA add returns the player to FA, not waivers), and dropped players enter `on_waivers` with `waivers_until = now + waiver_period_hours` (`none_fcfs` ⇒ straight to FA). Every executed move writes a `transactions` row (`type='add_drop'`) in the same txn. **Claim PROCESSING, FAAB, bench_lock (E33), priority orders — all M5**; the pool's state vocabulary ships complete so M5 adds writers, not columns.
- **D293 — Lineup law.** `slot_map` (`"<slot_key>:<index>" → player_id`, §12.13) is the canonical lineup representation everywhere; `starters`/`bench` JSONB stay as derived render state written in the same txn. `set_lineup` validates in-body: membership/ownership (or commissioner), every started player rostered by the team, **bipartite slot-fit** (E16 — each player fills exactly one slot; augmenting-path over ≤ ~10 starters, implemented in the RPC), per-slot eligibility from `roster_settings.starting_slots[].eligible`, lock state per `lineup_lock` (locked slots read-only — a change touching a locked slot refuses with the player and kickoff named; unlocked slots of the same lineup remain editable), `allow_illegal_lineups` semantics (TRUE: byes/OUT start and score 0, flagged; FALSE: blocked at submit). **IR enforcement lands here** (the columns already exist on `league_rosters`, 072): placement requires an eligible designation; Restricted sets `ir_lock_until_week = ir_placed_week + min_weeks` and early removal refuses (commissioner override is M6's). **Auto-carry is materialized by `league_week_advance` at week open**: the new week's row is written from last week's legal lineup (invalid/bye players kept and flagged, never silently dropped) so lock/scoring/UI all read explicit rows — no lazy "which week does this row mean" inference.
- **D292 — `score-league-week` is a TS worker, because the calculator is TS and one-implementation is LAW (D33/D57); its writes go through ONE SQL door.** The worker is a pure module (`src/lib/leagues/scoring/score-week-worker.ts`-shaped) with injected `TimeProvider`, provider-fed stats rows, and a service client; it drains `score_fanout` in batches, maps player deltas → affected (league, team) via the new `league_rosters(player_id)` index ∩ in-season leagues, recomputes affected teams **through the real pipeline — `resolveRules(snapshot, position)` with `deriveTierIndicators` composed BEFORE `scorePlayerWeek` (discharging F23 at the production call site, with the composition PINNED)** — and stores **JS-rounded** (`roundHalfUp`) totals so no path lets the DB round a divergent value (discharging **F22**). Writes land through one SECURITY DEFINER RPC (`score_write_week_batch`) that revalidates in-body: league in `in_season|playoffs`, week not `final`, **never a `final` matchup, never an overridden cell** (§22.2's rule), one coalesced write + one broadcast per league per batch. **Queue vehicle: a plain `score_fanout` table drained with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`** — pgmq does not exist on this stack (survey §6) and §22.3's claim pattern is already the house pattern; §22.2's "pgmq" is a vehicle erratum folded when built (C51, the D87 precedent). **Corrupt-snapshot posture (the F23 decision, made): quarantine the LEAGUE, never the batch** — a snapshot that makes `scorePlayerWeek` throw marks that league's week scoring-blocked (a loud worker-error row + skip), other leagues' batches proceed, and nothing writes a partial or zero score for the broken league (CLAUDE.md's "never let nothing-happened mean it-worked": absence of a score with a named reason, never a plausible 0.00).
- **D291 — Time discipline for in-season machinery: in-database jobs take `p_now`, TS takes TimeProvider.** Every M4 job RPC (`lineup_lock_tick`, `league_week_advance`, `finalize_matchups`) is an in-database RPC on pg_cron (the D87/draft-tick precedent — no Edge Function) whose signature is `(p_now timestamptz DEFAULT now())`: production cron passes nothing; the harness/sim passes the virtual instant, generalizing the `rewindDeadline` pattern into the front door instead of a column hack. The alternative — discard overrides, revert to base — makes the visible numbers jump on flip. > **(3) F173 — WHAT ACTUALLY BOUNDS THE STALENESS: NOTHING. Measured against the INSTALLED `@tanstack/query-core` 5.96.1** with a virtual clock (`Date.now` patched) and the browser branch forced via the library's own `environmentManager.setIsServer(() => false)`, using the production options (`staleTime: 10 * 60 * 1000`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, no `refetchInterval`, no `gcTime`):
>
> | probe | result |
> |---|---|
> | mounted, 60 virtual minutes, nothing focuses/reconnects/polls | **fetches 1 → 1** |
> | closed 4 min, reopened (data 4 min old) | **fetches 1 → 1**, entry still present |
> | 15 × 4-minute close/reopen cycles | **5 fetches**, on cycles 0, 3, 6, 9, 12 |
> | closed past `gcTime` (entry evicted), reopened | **fetches 1 → 2** |
>
> **Read at source rather than inferred:** `queryObserver.js` gates `refetchOnMount`, `refetchOnReconnect` and `refetchOnWindowFocus` **alike** through `shouldFetchOn → isStale → query.isStaleByTime(staleTime)`; `shouldFetchOnMount` short-circuits to an unconditional load **only while `query.state.data === undefined`**, i.e. only once the entry is gone; and `#updateStaleTimeout` calls `this.updateResult()` — it re-renders, it never fetches. So **a room closed and reopened inside 5 minutes over data younger than 10 minutes does NOT refetch**, and *"a later mount refetches regardless"* is withdrawn at all four sites (`use-league.ts`, `use-draft-pool.ts`, spec **E81** → **v2.16.8**, and D275(2) itself). So is *"Ten minutes overstated the closed case"* — it did not; the closed case has no bound either. **The `removable.js` quotation was mis-transcribed too** and is fixed to the real line: `newGcTime ?? (environmentManager.isServer() ? Infinity : 5 * 60 * 1e3)`.
>
> **The nuance is kept rather than traded for a cleaner sentence:** repeated close/reopen cycles **do** eventually refresh once the data crosses `staleTime`. The correct claim is therefore **"no timer guarantees a bound"** — never *"nothing ever refreshes"*, which would be the next wrong correction. **The gate's own figure for this was `~6` fetches over 15 cycles; re-measured here it is `5`.** It is stated as measured rather than inherited precisely because inheriting a number is what produced this whole round.
