> **(11) THE REVIEW ROUND (R666–R679, fix-then-merge on this same branch; verdict MERGE-WITH-FOLLOWUPS, no BLOCKER, no MAJOR — five lenses, 18 claims tested, 16 survived, 2 killed). ONE UNIFYING SHAPE, and it is the next rung of this lane's ladder.** Prior rungs: *vacuity sits on permissive branches* → *pin whether a guard RUNS, not only what it does* → *where layers share an observable, an outcome assertion cannot localize.* **This rung: when a defect class is closed by CONSTRUCTION, the construction gets pinned and its EDGES do not — and the docblock then states the construction's guarantee as an ABSOLUTE.** I closed §0(C) structurally (one shared key factory, options exported away from the hook, strict schemas, a marker table) and pinned every interior — every mapper arm, every factory body, the save's determinant. **A construction only guarantees anything at its seams, and every SHOULD-FIX in this round was a seam.** The sharpest form: **a claim of structural impossibility is itself an untested assertion, and it is the one assertion the suite never checks.** *"Cannot drift"*, *"by construction"*, *"no live fixture can construct it"*, *"any future writer owes"* — four load-bearing sentences doing a test's work, and **three were measurably false while the code they described was correct.** The standing rule this leaves for SE.7 onward, alongside D272(20): **a sentence containing "cannot", "never", or "by construction" needs either a killing cell or a hedge — and when a class is closed by construction, the pin goes on the EDGE, not the construction.**

> **(1) THE ONE THAT MATTERS — 052 §K1 WAS A FALSE NEGATIVE ON THE ONE THING IT EXISTS TO CATCH.** §K1 and §K2 matched raw `pg_proc.prosrc`, which is body text INCLUDING comments. Measured against the shipped file with the transactional mutation harness (`BEGIN;` + mutant DDL + the test file, whose own `rollback;` reverts the DDL — F145's discipline; the DB is never written, re-verified after every probe by reading the deployed body back):
>
> | mutation of wall 3 | before this PR | after |
> |---|---|---|
> | *(control — no mutation)* | 93 / **0** | 93 / **0** |
> | lock deleted, no comment | 93 / **2** (A22 + K1) | 93 / **2** (A22 + K1) |
> | lock deleted **+ one prose line** `-- The reference is resolved WHERE s.id = NEW.scoring_system_id FOR SHARE (105 §5 / F147).` | 93 / **1 — A22 ALONE, K1 GREEN** | 93 / **2** (A22 + K1) |
> | lock intact + a lock-ORDER comment naming `NEW.scoring_system_id FOR UPDATE` | 93 / **2 — A22 + K2 RED** (false positive) | 93 / **1** (A22 alone) |
>
> **Why the middle row is the dangerous one and not merely wrong:** §A22 is a golden on the trigger bodies' md5s, so it moves on **every** comment edit and is hand-cleared by a human — twice in SE.5 alone. A22 firing ALONE is therefore indistinguishable from ordinary churn, and the single cell that would have said *"the lock is gone"* said nothing. That is the exact hand-clearing window K1's own description says it exists to cover.
>
> **The fix is `regexp_replace(p.prosrc, '--[^\n]*', '', 'g')` on both cells** — line comments deleted, their newlines kept, so the multi-line anchors still span the statement (and an interleaved comment can no longer break a match either). It is **lossless ON THIS CORPUS — and that is a bounded claim, not a property of the technique (R662).** A `--` inside a STRING LITERAL is invisible to a line-based strip, so the strip can eat real code, and the direction it fails in is **masking on a BAN cell**: measured, a mutant carrying a genuinely banned lock and **no comment anywhere** — `RAISE NOTICE 'resolve -- step'; PERFORM 1 FROM public.scoring_systems s2 WHERE s2.id = NEW.scoring_system_id FOR UPDATE;` on one line — is **93 / 2 pre-fix (K2 correctly RED) and 93 / 1 post-fix (K2 GREEN)**. **It is unreachable today, and that is the claim that is defensible:** a SQL-aware lexer (single-quoted, dollar-quoted, quoted-identifier and nestable `/* */` aware) run over **all 124 `public` function bodies read from `pg_proc`** and over **all 245 dollar-quoted bodies in the 98 `supabase/migrations/*.sql` files** finds **zero** `--` inside any literal and **zero** `/* */` blocks, and the naive strip is **byte-identical to the lexer's output for all 369 bodies**. So: no permit cell can be defeated by this (a strip that removes real code makes a permit FAIL, not pass), and no ban cell can be masked by it **unless a body first grows a `--` inside a literal on the same line as the banned construct** — which nothing in the repo does. Every real mutation that red a cell before still reds it after.

> **(1) F147 — THE LOCK GOT WEAKER, AND THAT IS THE STRONGER ANSWER.** 104 shipped `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` and said in its own body that the STRENGTH was SE.5's to choose once a write pattern existed to measure it against. Measured, with `scoring_update_rules` in place:
> **(a) equally protective.** The seam — T1 makes an UNREFERENCED flat row invalid (wall 1 passes: outside the profile), T2 repoints a live league at it — run in BOTH orderings with the F21 double-pay PAIR as the invalid document (each key ALONE is legal, so the probe measures the defect and not the names): `FOR SHARE` refused both, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` refused both, and **a no-lock control BREACHED both**. That control is what makes the other two rows evidence rather than decoration; without it "refused" is equally consistent with a race that never happened. The protective DIRECTION survives the weakening: a racing rules-UPDATE blocks for the holder's full duration (2017.9 ms under `FOR SHARE`, 1973.7 ms under `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`).
> **(b) the contention is on the hottest path in the product.** Wall 3's highest-frequency writer is `create_league`, whose INSERT arm locks the referenced row — and there are exactly **six** template rows, so every league creation in the app contends on one of six. **The axis is CONCURRENCY**: for each level W, W concurrent workers each issue 20 `create_league` calls against the same template row; the figure is mean ms/call, elapsed taken inside the database. Two reps per arm — `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` at W = 1/2/4/6/8/10 → **0.60 / 0.93 / 1.50 / 1.95 / 2.46 / 2.96 ms** (rep 2: 0.85/1.02/1.55/1.91/2.41/2.94); `FOR SHARE` → **0.85 / 0.70 / 0.66 / 0.74 / 0.82 / 0.81** (rep 2: 0.55/0.65/0.66/0.68/0.69/0.76). **`FOR NO KEY UPDATE` rises monotonically; `FOR SHARE` is flat.** That, not any single ratio, is the claim: each additional concurrent creator adds one full call to every other creator's wait, so the gap grows without bound in W (2.6× at W=6, 3.7× at W=10).
> **[RELABELLED 2026-08-26, review R647 — the correction this row exists to carry, because this block is the standing justification for weakening a security wall.** The first form printed `20/37/53/70/88/104 ms` beside `19/19/19/19/19/19` as though both were six comparable per-worker figures at a fixed W=6. They were the sorted **drain cascade** at one level — within a level the strong lock's per-worker elapsed is `[11 23 33 44 54 64]` at W=6 while `FOR SHARE` is `[13 13 13 14 14 14]` — and printing them side by side invited exactly the reading two reviewers gave them. Its headline "~5.5× at 6-way" was `104/19`: the last element of a cascade over a flat value, not a like-for-like ratio. **Nothing about the decision changes; the evidence for it is now stated on the axis it actually varies.** And the early 8-way run "discarded as `docker exec` startup noise" — justified in outcome, sloppy in process, because a discarded measurement needs a stated exclusion rule **or** a re-measurement and it had neither — now has the second: the sweep reaches **W=8 and W=10 and the sign holds in both reps**.]**
> **(c) the multixact trade, measured rather than named.** `FOR SHARE` is a SHARED lock, so concurrent holders go through a multixact. That it really happens is not assumed: `pg_get_multixact_members(s.xmax::text::xid)` → **`1454180/sh, 1454182/sh`**. Its COST is inside the **flat ~0.7 ms `FOR SHARE`** row of the W = 1..10 sweep in (b) above — it does not show up at this shape — **[repointed 2026-08-26, D274/R-item 3: this read "inside that 19 ms", and R647 had already retracted the 19 ms figure one bullet earlier without sweeping its own back-references, leaving a withdrawn number carrying the claim]** — and the risk it carries (member-space pressure) needs long-lived overlapping sharers, while every wall-3 writer in this repo is a short RPC transaction that releases at commit. **If a long-running league-write transaction is ever introduced, this is the thing to re-measure.**

>
> > **In a defence-in-depth design where every layer raises the same error family, an assertion on the OUTCOME cannot localize.** SE.4b round 1: vacuity sits on permissive branches. Round 2 (D272(20)): the suite pins what the guards *do*, not what determines *whether* they run. **SE.5: the suite pins THAT the system refused, not WHICH layer refused — and six cells had an observable alphabet coarser than the distinction their own text claimed to make.**
>
> The count, because the shape is only visible in aggregate: **R638** — the alphabet was `left(sqlerrm, 44)` and the discriminator lives at character **66**, so three `scoring_update_rules` refusals were one byte-identical string and two guards had zero mutation coverage. **R646** — the alphabet was `(SQLSTATE, HINT)` and two arms of the *same function* emit the same pair (delete the no-PA-keys guard and `'{}' <@ anything` is TRUE for both families, so the *ambiguity* arm raises with the identical hint). **R641** — same alphabet, and the RPC's own `PERFORM` and wall 1 behind it emit the same SQLSTATE, HINT **and MESSAGE**, because they call the same validator. **R640** — the alphabet was "outsider reads 0 rows", and three independent tables' RLS all produce 0. **R639** — no assertion at all on the permissive arm, so the alphabet was empty. **And §D2, which this task had already found and fixed in its own probe sweep, was the same thing.**
>
> **Why it is systematic rather than sloppy, which is the part worth carrying:** the architecture that makes SE.5 safe is exactly the architecture that makes it untestable by outcome. Front-door RPC, wall 1, wall 3, RLS and CHECK constraints deliberately converge on the same P0001 families with the same messages — that convergence is a **feature** (one user-facing error however you arrive at it, which is why TS↔SQL guardrail parity is pinned byte-for-byte) and the suite inherited it without inheriting a way to see through it. **Any future task adding a guard behind an existing wall reproduces this defect unless the helper discriminates by construction.**
>
> **The fix was three lines and it was already in the file.** `pg_temp.attach` read `pg_exception_context` and reported a `raised_in:` token; it was applied to one helper of three. Swept to all of them (plus a shared uuid-stripping message widener, because 36 identical characters were eating the whole 44-char budget), every previously-vacuous cell now kills its mutant: **D4 · D5 · C15 · E3b · D7+D10 · B5**, control 71 ok / 0 red. Two of those cells are new (**C15** for R639, **E3b** for R640) and both were written the hard way: R640's *obvious* fixture — "give the outsider membership in a different live league" — is measured **non-killing** (053 already had it, as u5), so the working cell instead makes `leagues` and `league_members` temporarily world-readable so that §12.25's own identity clause is the only thing left standing.
>
> **(12) PATTERN 2, which the reviewers named and this task's banner had missed as a CATEGORY.** *105 is the first migration to put a user-owned, user-writable, user-DELETABLE `scoring_systems` row in front of a live league.* Three findings fall out of that one fact: user-**owned** → it enters an `owner_id` namespace two shipped readers treat as a one-row-per-user store (**F156**); user-**writable** → the §7.3 lifecycle window stops being structural and becomes an RPC-level check (**R645**); user-**deletable** → the FK's NO-ACTION RI check becomes reachable, closing a lock cycle (**R644**). §4's banner *did* re-derive the confinement's consequences and got two of five — the lesson is not carelessness but that **"this row is now client-writable" has a CHECKLIST attached** (who else reads this namespace? what invariants were enforced by unreachability? what RI edges become reachable?) and it was enumerated from memory. The checklist is now written into 105 §4 so the next task does not have to remember it.
>
> **(13) TWO THINGS THE REVIEW DECLINED TO LET ME FIX, AND BOTH REFUSALS ARE CORRECT.** R644's FK direction gets **prose only** — an `ON DELETE RESTRICT`-shaped guard is new surface on a security wall against a statement the FK already refuses 100% of the time (CLAUDE.md's "personal problems"). R648's banner claim that the refusal "names `normalizeScoringDoc`" is **trimmed, not made true** — 103's two `v_msg` literals are byte-identical mirrors of `validate-rules-doc.ts`, and `scoring-parity-db.test.ts` compares only `REJECT|hint|path` under a family regex that would still match an appended function name, so editing them would split TS↔SQL message parity **unpinned**. Trimming a banner is free; editing a mirrored literal is not.
>
> **(14) A22 MOVED TWICE IN ONE PR, AND THE SECOND MOVE IS THE PIN BEHAVING CORRECTLY.** `7a5a0273…` → `a1c16d02…` (the lock change) → `fe392869…` (R644/R647 correcting two claims *inside* wall 3's body). The second is a **comment-only** edit — and a golden on `prosrc` cannot distinguish a comment from code and should not try, because the migration-073 failure it exists to catch is exactly an edit that looks harmless. Both re-derivations followed the same discipline: apply the FILE body in a rolled-back transaction and hash the result, after first proving the deployed body carries a marker only that version has; and re-measure the other three literals in the same breath to make "the diff is wall 3's prosrc alone" a measurement.

> **(1) WALL 1 IS `SECURITY DEFINER` BECAUSE `leagues` HAS RLS — and the argument is a measurement, not a preference.** D175(2) writes the reference arm as a SYSTEM fact: `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM leagues WHERE scoring_system_id = NEW.id AND deleted_at IS NULL)`, with **no membership join** (unlike §12.25's member SELECT policy, which has one). `leagues` carries exactly one policy and it is a SELECT policy — `select polname, polcmd from pg_policy where polrelid='public.leagues'::regclass` → **one row, `polcmd = 'r'`, `is_league_member(id) OR owner_id = auth.uid()`** (001's `"League owners can manage" FOR ALL` is gone; 052 replaced the read policy). That is not a hypothetical writer: it is a commissioner who forked and then left, and it is exactly the writer the arm exists to stop. The house precedent for a DEFINER guard trigger already exists (018/025/026/028), and the newer strict form is used: `search_path = ''` with every reference schema-qualified. **§4.1's third requirement — in-body authorization — is DISCHARGED rather than waived, and the discharge is pinned:** a `RETURNS TRIGGER` function has no callable surface at all (`select public.scoring_systems_rules_guard()` → **`0A000`**, *"trigger functions can only be called as triggers"* — measured, and asserted in pgTAP 052 §A8/§A9), so there is no subject to authorize. **Wall 2 is deliberately NOT DEFINER** (059's shape): it reads no table, so it borrows nothing — and being INVOKER it calls the validator **as the writing role**, which is what makes 103's REVOKE stopping at PUBLIC/anon load-bearing. `service_role` is `rolbypassrls = t, rolsuper = f` and, with only a SELECT policy on `leagues`, is the one client role that can write a league row at all; pgTAP 052 §F8 pins that its refusal is **`P0001` with the field path, not `42501`**, so a REVOKE from service_role reds rather than silently degrades the contract SE.5/SE.6 consume.

> **(11) THE SHAPE, and it is the reason the fix is one thing rather than four.** Every vacuity this lane has found — the fifth (§B4), the sixth (the DEFINER decision), and now R621/R622/R623 — sits on a **permissive** branch: a short-circuit or a skip. Permissive branches are invisible to a suite built from refusal assertions, because a refusal assertion cannot notice a write that was let through *deliberately*. **R615 (the breach) and R621/R622 (the decorations) were literally the same three lines.** A wall whose refusals are heavily pinned and whose skips are unpinned is precisely a wall that lets one write through — and it did. **STANDING RULE, adopted here and recorded so the next schema task inherits it: every skip/short-circuit clause gets a `lives_ok` fixture that reds when the clause is deleted, and the DoD break-probe list must enumerate EVERY DISJUNCT of every predicate — not only the ones a fixture happens to reach.** The first cut's probe list covered arms (a) and (c) and the entry arm; the one arm it omitted (b) was the one with no coverage at all.

F142's "one door" was six.** Measured: (1) repoint · (2) `leagues` INSERT already carrying `scoring_system_id` · (3) soft-delete → legally rewrite → **un-delete** (no un-delete function exists anywhere in 001–104) · (4) detach → rewrite → re-attach · (5) the same **mid-draft** · (6) the R615 promotion. **D169 assigns the remedy to `update_league_settings`, and that RPC is in the path of exactly ONE of them** — five are raw-table writes no function fronts, which is this repo's migration-073 lesson in reverse. > **(20) THE GENERALISATION, AND IT SUBSUMES (11).** Round 1's lesson was *"vacuity sits on permissive branches"*. That was the special case, learned locally and not generalised. The general rule: **the suite pins what the guards DO and not what determines WHETHER they run.** Every surviving test finding in round 2 lives on a guard's **perimeter**, not in its body — the trigger's event mask (R627), its enablement mode (R631), an early `RETURN NEW` (R628), the OLD-side predicate (R629), and one level down at runtime, the cross-table premise (R626). Each decides whether the validator is ever reached; each is invisible to a suite whose assertions are refusals. Meanwhile the refusal itself was pinned two and three times over, in two suites, across two interfaces. **A guard's entry conditions — event mask, enablement, skip clauses, and cross-table premises — are part of the guard and need pins and locks of their own.** It is not a coincidence that four of the five perimeter findings are on wall 3: it is the surface that arrived after the pinning discipline had already been applied to the other two.

> **(21) R635 — THE MIGRATION'S OWN CENTRAL ARGUMENT WAS TOO STRONG, AND MEASURING IT NARROWED IT.** 104 said a guard on the column *"needs no author to remember it"*. A body edit to 059's function that assigned `NEW.scoring_rules_snapshot` overwrites the value **after** wall 2 validated it: the invalid document commits, the trigger **catalog is byte-identical**, and all 53 pgTAP files stay green. It needs DDL, so it is not a security hole — but it is the same migration-073 exposure one function over, which is the exposure D168(2) chose this form to avoid. **Fix: §A22 pins the BEFORE ROW trigger SET on both tables by name in fire order AND by each trigger function's `prosrc` md5**, and the claim is narrowed to its true proviso. Both halves measured: probe 21a (a new later-sorting trigger) reds A22 + E5f2 + F3; **probe 21b (a body edit, byte-identical catalog) reds A22 + F3** — F3 being the freeze-verbatim assertion, i.e. the harm itself becoming visible.

> **(22) R626 — THE TOCTOU SEAM, FIXED WITH A LOCK AND MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Wall 1's arm (c) reads `public.leagues` and wall 3 reads `public.scoring_systems`; each held the row in front of it and neither held still the PREMISE it read from the other's table. Reproduced here as a two-session race on the shipped chain: session A opens a transaction and writes the F21 document to an unreferenced row (legal — outside the profile); session B repoints a league at it. **Without the lock: B reports `UPDATE 1`, `COMMIT`, and the check reads `live_league_referencing_invalid_doc = 1`. With `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`: B blocks, re-reads after A commits, and is REFUSED with the guardrail-2 message; the check reads 0.** `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` is the weakest lock that conflicts with the racing rules-UPDATE and does **not** conflict with the FK's own `FOR KEY SHARE`, so ordinary league writes are not serialised behind scoring edits. It creates a two-direction lock pattern and therefore a **deadlock surface** — named rather than hidden; a deadlock is a clean `40P01` rollback, which is what this seam is being traded up TO. **`UNREPRESENTABLE` and "for every role, every path" are now scoped to sequential** in the banner: the sentence was broader than the code, which is the thing this lane does not do.

A same-transaction `NOWAIT` probe never conflicts with its own locks. So §K pins the clause in the deployed body (probe 20 reds K1 + A22), and the behavioural proof lives where a measurement that cannot live in the suite belongs — item (22) and the PR.

  **(1) THE POSITION-SCOPE MAP IS ENGINE LAW, AND THAT IS THE ONE PLACEMENT CALL THIS TASK HAD TO MAKE.** Guardrail 3 needs a position → legal-keys mapping, and **no registry field carries one**: `StatKeyDef` has `tier`, `storage` and `scoring_surface`, never a position (`grep -n "export interface StatKeyDef" -A 14 src/lib/leagues/stats/stat-keys.ts`). §7.3.3.1's section catalog is the only source, so it is transcribed — into **`POSITION_SCORABLE_KEYS` in `src/lib/leagues/scoring/validate-rules-doc.ts`**, beside the validator that enforces it, because *which keys are legal under which position* is validation law (SE.4 mirrors this exact map in SQL; SE.4b's trigger enforces it on every write), while D167's editor-owned catalog is **rendering** — sections, labels, ordering, D173's `gated` flag. The transcription is **not trusted**: the suite proves the six sets are pairwise disjoint (offense/K/DST — the four offense positions share ONE set by identity, pinned with `toBe`) and that their **union ≡ the registry's scorable set** (48, set equality), so a drift on either side reds. **F136 is filed for the seam:** SE.7 composes this map, never re-transcribes the catalog — two copies would let the editor offer a key the validator refuses.
  **(2) THE FORMAT-1 ARM IS VALIDATED TOO, and that is a reading, not an oversight.** §7.3.3.1's guardrail bullet heads its list with *"what a format-2 doc structurally cannot express"*, but (a) guardrail 2 spells out its own format-1 arm, (b) **D175's wall validates format-1 rows** (`is_template = TRUE`, and any live-league-referenced row — so every template row and every flat league doc passes through `scoring_rules_validate`), and (c) F21's raw-source ban would be hollow if a flat map could still pay `def_points_allowed` beside the buckets derived from it. So a flat document is checked against the three families that have a subject there — allowlist, tier exclusivity (format-1 arm), bounds — and position scope / normal form have none. **Measured, not assumed: all six shipped templates pass** (`it.each` over `SCORING_TEMPLATES`), which is the acceptance floor SE.4's pgTAP re-proves from the seeded rows. One consequence worth carrying to SE.4: for a flat document the violation **path is the key itself**, not `base.<key>` — a flat map has no `base` member and SE.6's route surfaces these paths as fields.
  **(3) THE READING THE SPEC LEFT AMBIGUOUS — guardrail 2's format-1 "⊆ exactly one named platform family" (Builder-carriable, no halt; the D174 / D267(4) precedent).** Read literally as *"a subset of exactly one of the two sets"*, a document naming only the **four shared key names** (`def_pa_0`, `def_pa_1_6`, `def_pa_7_13`, `def_pa_28_34`) would be REFUSED for being a subset of both — though it cannot double-pay anything, because within one family the tiers are non-overlapping by construction. The controlling clause is the guardrail's own stated purpose two sentences earlier — *mixing* families is what must be inexpressible — and the *"the families sharing 4 key names"* parenthetical is the spec telling the implementer that a key can belong to both. **The check is therefore "some published family contains every `def_pa_*` key this document names."** Why no halt: the spec is *ambiguous*, not wrong or self-contradicting, and **no document that exists distinguishes the readings — measured**: each of the six templates matches exactly one family (pinned), and the F21 literal is refused under both. The divergent case is pinned by its own test (with the "at most one of the four is ever hot, PA 0–60" premise measured beside it), so a Chris ruling the other way is a one-line change plus one pin.
  **(4) THE VALIDATOR NEVER THROWS, AND THE FAMILY ORDER IS WHY IT CAN'T.** Its input is a JSONB blob from a route body or a column, so *"this is nonsense"* is an ordinary answer. But two functions it composes DO throw — `tierKeysFromCuts` asserts its cut-list precondition (D267(5)) and `normalizeScoringDoc` refuses a non-object override — so §7.3.3.1(c)'s residuals are evaluated **before** guardrail 2 generates any key set (a table that failed residuals is skipped, never generated), and the shape family gates guardrail 4. Pinned from both sides: `tierKeysFromCuts(DEF_PA_PREFIX, [0, 7, 7])` **throws**, and the same list inside a document is **answered**; a 14-input hostile corpus (`null`, `42`, arrays, `{format: 2}` with no `tier_cuts`, `JSON.parse('{"__proto__": …}')`) never throws and every one of them comes back with a named reason. **Probe G is the falsification** — deleting the residual gate makes guardrail 2 generate from an unvalidated list ⇒ **6 RED**, including that pin.
  **(5) GUARDRAIL 4 COMPOSES `normalizeScoringDoc` — the diff is the report, not a second strip (D268(5)/R582's fix is what makes this safe).** **[CORRECTED 2026-08-25 by the review round — the closing property of this item was FALSE AS FIRST WRITTEN, and the correction is R588's whole shape.** It read *"every document the validator accepts is a **fixed point** of `normalizeScoringDoc`"*, measured over a curated nine-document list. Adding **one** document to that list — `{...espnFork(), def_points_allowed: 5}` — gives **1 failed / 68 passed**, failing on the `toEqual`, not the `expectAccepted`: the stray member was accepted *and* was not a fixed point. The property is true again only because R588's member-set check now refuses the counterexample; it is re-pinned WITH that document (`R588 … > D269(5) RESTATED CORRECTLY`), which is the form it should have had. **The generalisable half: a property measured over a hand-picked list is an example set wearing a property's clothes — the list is chosen by the same intuition that wrote the code, so it inherits the code's blind spot.**]** "Is this document in normal form?" *is* "does normalising change it?", so the strip keeps ONE definition and this module only reports where the two differ. Two consequences: an override object the normal form strips entirely is reported **per key** (all of its keys are no-ops by definition, since `normalizeScoringDoc` keeps a key unless it exists in `base` and matches) — `positions.WR` is not something a commissioner can act on; and the `__proto__` shape R582 fixed is what lets guardrail 3 **refuse** an illegal `positions.__proto__` instead of watching it laundered away, pinned as the two halves in one test. The template path calls it with `defaultsForTeamCount(12)`; **the deferred league path calls the SAME function with `mergeSettings(leagueRow)` and changes nothing else.** The claim is not left as prose: `mock-launch-ops.test.ts` builds a league-shaped settings object sharing no edited value with the defaults, runs it through the same function, and asserts the WIRE schema accepts the result — so the deferred feature's payload is exercised before the feature exists. **Probe A** (the payload rebuilt from a fixed source — the rule-12 defect made real) reddens 3 of 20 including that pin.
3. **THE WHOLE DRAFT BLOCK TRAVELS, NOT A SUBSET, AND THE REASON IS THE ENGINE'S.** 095's league arm snapshots `COALESCE(v_league.settings->'draft', '{}')` into `config` entire. Sending a curated subset would make a standalone mock's `config` a DIFFERENT shape from a league mock's, and every engine reader would then have to know which arm minted the row. Sending the block whole keeps them indifferent — which is also the thing that makes the deferred feature a source swap rather than a second config vocabulary.
4. **DEFAULTS ARE CALLED, NOT RESTATED, SO D229(3) IS STRUCTURAL.** There is no numeric literal for any clock anywhere in the new code: `initialMockLaunchDraft()` returns `defaultsForTeamCount(MOCK_DEFAULT_TEAM_COUNT)`, so "no mock-specific default of any kind" is enforced by there being nowhere for one to live. **Verified against `league-settings.ts` rather than copied from the task text** — `pick_timer_seconds.default(90)`, `auction_nomination_seconds.default(30)`, `auction_bid_seconds.default(20)`, `auction_anti_snipe_seconds.default(10)`, `roster_settings.default(structuredClone(DEFAULT_ROSTER_SETTINGS))` — and pinned as stored literals, plus a whole-object equality so a default cannot hide in an unasserted field. **Probe B** (a mock-specific 10-second bid clock, the withdrawn Q23 value) reddens 2 of 20.
5. **THE TEMPLATE IS THE LAUNCHER'S PICK AND STARTS NULL — the create wizard's posture, adopted rather than invented.** `toCreateInput` returns null until a template is chosen and the wizard's button disables; the same here. **Nothing in this task decides WHICH of the six is a good default**, because that is a product call and D229 does not make it. If Chris wants one preselected it is a one-line change to `initialMockLaunchDraft`.
6. **`scoring_system_id` RIDES THE DRAFT BLOCK, so it lands at `drafts.config->>'scoring_system_id'` with no RPC signature change** — exactly what §4.1 item 11 predicted. It sits beside MP.2's `config->'roster'` for the same reason: the draft row describes its own settings. **It is not read yet and that is filed, not hidden — F117.**
7. **NO SERVER-SIDE EXISTENCE CHECK ON THE TEMPLATE ID, AND RULE 10 IS WHY.** A forged id resolves to no template row and the launcher's own board renders "—" (§16.5.4's "never wrong numbers"). The party harmed is the forger, in their own practice. **Shape** IS checked (`z.uuid()` at the route) because a non-uuid would be stored and read back by a column-typed client. Adding a lookup would be a protection with no party to protect.
8. **THE ROUTE IS NEW, NOT THE LEAGUE ROUTE WIDENED.** `POST /api/mocks` answers *"practice"*; `POST /api/leagues/[id]/mock-drafts` answers *"practice THIS league's draft"* and its whole authorization story is membership. Two questions, two endpoints — MP.5's own instruction for the GET half, applied to the POST. It reads NO feature flag (§4 rule 13): the flag gates the surfaces that call it. It sends neither `p_league_id` nor `p_human_team_id`, because 095 made the arms mutually exclusive **by refusal** and a smuggled league id is a 22023 rather than a silent precedence guess (the wire schema refuses one too, pinned).
9. **`draftConfigSchema` IS NOW EXPORTED, ADDITIVELY, AND THAT IS THE ALTERNATIVE TO A SECOND CATALOG.** MP.4 item 5 says validate with the existing schema. The route parses the payload with `rosterSettingsSchema` + `draftConfigSchema.extend({ scoring_system_id })` — the same two `leagueSettingsSchema` composes — so a §7.3.8 range can never mean one thing on the league surfaces and another on this one. It is **not** the authority: `create_mock_draft` is EXECUTE-able by `authenticated`, so 095's in-body guard is the floor and this is the pre-flight above it.
10. **CONTROLS ARE THE SHIPPED ONES AND THE LIST IS SHORT ON PURPOSE:** `settings-form-controls` (`FieldRow`/`ToggleRow`/`ChoiceSelect`/`InlineIssue`/`numOptions`/`clampInt`), `RosterSlotBuilder`, `ScoringTemplatePicker`. The picker brings its own §16.5.4 loading / error-with-retry / empty states, so the template step's states are the shipped ones rather than a second implementation. A second settings editor is the LV.7 failure pattern and there is none here.
11. **VALIDATION MESSAGES ARE `validateLeagueSettings`'s OWN, FILTERED TO WHAT IS ON SCREEN.** The dialog edits `team_count`, the roster and the draft block; every other field is an untouched creation default and cannot be wrong. Surfacing (say) a `trade_veto_votes` violation inside a practice-draft dialog would be a message about a control that is not there, so `mockLaunchIssues` filters to the three editable prefixes — and a test pins that a real §7.3.5 violation stays silent.

(b) `one-voice.test.ts`'s anti-snipe row gains `mock-launch-dialog.tsx` in `alsoNamedBy` — the same disposition `commish-draft-panel.tsx` already has, and for a stronger reason: this is the control that SETS the value before a draft exists, so there is no live state for it to be a second telling of.

Driving it is how **F116** was found: the raiser's `create_mock_draft: ` prefix reaches the user. Pre-existing and shared with the league launcher, so it is filed rather than fixed here.

Removing the test rows returned 44/3051 PASS. **A fixture must not state its premise about a whole table (D235), and this is that rule's second sighting.**

- **D240 — MP.4 review fix cycle (PR #193, same branch; R505 BLOCKER + R506–R512). The blocker is the one that matters, and it is the lesson MP.4's own D239(10) got wrong about itself.**

1. **R505 [BLOCKER] — THE DRAFT-BLOCK EDITOR WAS FORKED, AND THE PR CLAIMED IT WAS COMPOSED.** The Reviewer measured it: `comm -12` against `settings-panel.tsx`'s `DraftGroup` found **66 identical lines of ~110** after normalizing element ids — same six controls, same order, four byte-identical hint strings, a **fourth** copy of the clamp bounds (50/1000 · 10/120 · 10/60 · 0/15), and a pick-clock label map that **had already diverged at birth** (`No clock` vs `No clock (untimed)`). D239(10) said *"no second settings editor … there is none here"*, which is a **§4 rule 9 violation on top of the fork**: a claim about the post-change world inferred from the intent of the change (*"I imported the shared primitives, therefore I composed"*) rather than observed. **Reusing the shared PRIMITIVES is not composing the FIELDS**, and that distinction is the whole of LV.7.
2. **FIXED BY EXTRACTION, NOT BY RE-WORDING.** `src/components/leagues/draft-config-fields.tsx` now holds `PickClockField`, `SnakeReversalField` and `AuctionConfigFields`, with the pure half in `draft-config-fields-ops.ts` (the `-ops.ts` convention — and required, because a `.test.ts` cannot import a `.tsx` under the unit project). **BOTH surfaces compose them**: the settings panel with `idPrefix="set"`, the launch dialog with `idPrefix="mock"`. What did NOT move is what is league-shaped — the `GroupCard` shell, `DraftOrderEditor` and the draft-order mode (they need a `leagueId` and a franchise list), and the draft-type control (the two surfaces present it as a select and as three cards).

4. **THE FOURTH COPY OF THE BOUNDS IS NOW ONE, AND IT IS PINNED TO THE CONTRACT.** `DRAFT_FIELD_BOUNDS` is a single named table, and `draft-config-fields.test.ts` drives `draftConfigSchema` **edge by edge** for every entry — accepts `min` and `max`, refuses `min-1` and `max+1` — plus a completeness assertion so a new bounded knob with an input and no entry reddens. Options are now **derived from `PICK_TIMER_SECONDS`** (`pickTimerOptions()`), so no surface can quietly drop one, and the label map is the panel's — the birth-divergence is gone with it. **No trim is kept, so there is nothing left to record as a decision.**

The true and narrower claim is **"no mock-specific DEFAULT exists"** — `initialMockLaunchDraft()` returns `defaultsForTeamCount(...)`, so there is no expression in the ops module that could produce one. **Offered values are not defaults**, and the first wording conflated them. Corrected in the module docblock and here. *(R505's extraction removed most of the literals anyway, which is a consequence and not the argument.)*
7. **R508 — `MOCK_DEFAULT_TEAM_COUNT` WAS A THIRD 12 CALLING ITSELF THE SAME ONE.** `league-settings`' `DEFAULT_TEAM_COUNT` is module-private and the wizard exports its own `DEFAULT_WIZARD_TEAM_COUNT`, so the docblock's *"never a second 12"* was false. It now reads `LEAGUE_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.team_count` — `leagueSettingsSchema.parse({})`, the §7.3.1 "D" column itself — and is not a literal at all; the team-count options derive from the exported `V1_TEAM_COUNTS` instead of a third copy of `[8,10,12,14,16]`. **The wizard's duplicate is left alone** (not this task's file), but nothing new joins it.

Auction violations now render through `AuctionConfigFields`' own `issues`, roster ones through `RosterSlotBuilder`'s existing inline render, and the `draft.auction_budget` inline issue **moved into the shared component**, so the panel and the dialog show it identically and beside the field. The disabled-reason status line moved **above** the footer rule (under it, it read as a footnote to the stepper). What stays at the bottom is the SERVER's refusal, which belongs to the submit and to no step.

**2026-08-24 — Builder (MP.3, a mock with no league: launch, bots, storage, cleanup; branch `feat/MP-MP.3-standalone-mock`; migration **095**, pgTAP **043**, spec erratum **v2.16.2**)**

- **D238 — MP.3 review fix cycle (PR #192, same branch; R498–R504, all seven taken). The two that matter are a guard that bounded half its input and a pin that did not exist.**

1. **R498 — THE GUARD BOUNDED THE KNOBS AND LEFT THE ROSTER OPEN, ON THE SAME CLIENT-REACHABLE ARM, AND ITS OWN COMMENT SAID WHY THAT WAS WRONG.** The comment's rationale — *"every one of these knobs can WEDGE the engine"* — applied verbatim to `roster_settings`, which the first cut did not touch. The reviewer's probes as `authenticated`: **`bench 5000` launched a 5,010-round draft**, `starting_slots[{count: 999}]` launched, `bench -3` launched, `disconnect_grace_seconds 999999` was stored verbatim. **The roster is a SOLVENCY INPUT, not decoration** — `draft_team_budget` reads `drafts.total_rounds` as the auction's per-team capacity, and `total_rounds` is derived from exactly these numbers — so an unbounded roster was an unbounded budget model. `draft_settings_range_guard` now takes `(p_draft, p_roster)` and adds four bounds mirrored from the same catalog: `disconnect_grace_seconds` 0–120 (`league-settings.ts:262`), `bench` 0–20 (`:153`), per-slot `count` 0–10 (`:108`), starting-lineup **sum 1–20** (`:480-485`). **The transferable half is the shape of the miss: a validator that is complete over the fields you were thinking about is not a validator.** It is the same species as D236(1)'s *"a check that covers the shape you thought about cannot fail on the shape you did not"*, one layer out.
2. **TWO SECOND-ORDER BUGS FELL OUT OF BUILDING R498, and both were caught by writing the D146 pins first.** **(a) A single `max((slot->>'count')::int)` bound looked like it checked the per-slot count and did not:** a `-1` slot passes whenever some other slot is larger, so the negative half was never tested. Split into `min()` for the floor and `max()` for the ceiling. **(b) The sum check must be UNCONDITIONAL.** Written as `IF p_roster ? 'starting_slots'` it is evadable by **omitting the key** — which is R498's own species one level down — and `draft_rounds_from_roster` already reads an absent array as 0, so the guard now reads it the same way. Both are pinned (043 §D: the `-1`-with-a-larger-sibling case, and the bare `{"bench": 5}` object).
3. **AND THE BOUND MADE ANOTHER LINE UNREACHABLE, WHICH IS DISCLOSED RATHER THAN PINNED.** With the sum floored at 1, `total_rounds < 1` cannot happen on the standalone arm, so `create_mock_draft`'s standalone no-draftable-rounds RAISE is now a backstop behind another guard. **Kept** (a guard that holds only while a second guard holds is one edit from being wrong) and **deliberately not pinned** — a pin on a line that cannot execute is a pin that can never go red. Stated in the guard's header and in 043 §D. **The same disclosure applies to the §8.6.8 solvency refusal on that arm:** with the roster bounded the largest legal roster is 20 + 20 = 40 draftable spots and the smallest legal budget is $50, so at the $1 reserve solvency holds for every object the guard admits — **v2.13.3's redundancy finding arriving on a second path.** What IS pinned is the positive: `draft_auction_solvent` ANSWERS for a standalone mock and `draft_team_budget` returns `open_slots = 2` for its seat, which is banner item 4's real claim.
4. **R499 — §F AND §G CLAIMED THE R383 COMPOSITE AND 043 CONTAINED NO COMPOSITE AT ALL.** §G compared five `count(*)`s — **the exact instrument R383 exists because it cannot see an in-place UPDATE** — so a regression that flipped `leagues.status` and back, or merely bumped `updated_at`, passed it; and §F's header promised a league-attached bracket with no assertion behind it, while `mp3_before` captured two counts nothing read. §G is rebuilt on the 041:719-736 idiom (`string_agg(to_jsonb(l)::text)` over every `leagues` row **plus** every league-scoped count, **plus** every league franchise ROW entire — a count cannot tell a deleted franchise from a renamed one). §B gains the league-attached bracket §F's header promised, and §F's header is corrected to claim only what §F measures. **Probed:** a bare `update leagues set updated_at = now() + interval '1 second'` mid-lifecycle turns the new §G composite **RED (1 of 97, test 92)** — and would have passed every one of the five counts it replaces. **This is the lane's recurring species and the entry says so plainly: a claimed pin that does not exist is worse than no pin, because the claim is what stops the next session writing the real one.**
5. **R500 — "each bound is pinned one step either side (D146)" was true of two of five knobs.** `pick_timer_seconds`, `auction_budget` and `auction_nomination_seconds` had no boundary pin at all, so widening any of them reddened nothing. 043 §D is now a **full sweep over all nine bounds** — one step outside each end **and** the boundary value itself — and it drives `draft_settings_range_guard` **DIRECTLY** rather than through `create_mock_draft`. **That choice is the point, not a shortcut:** it measures at the layer the claim is about (tasks-DR §4 rule 9), and it is cheap enough to be exhaustive because it mints no seats and trips no §22.5 cap — a sweep driven through the RPC would have burned the 5-per-hour limit inside one section. **Three end-to-end refusals through the RPC stay**, because without them the whole sweep could pass against a function nothing calls.
6. **R503 — the `pick_timer_seconds` whitelist was thirteen literals hand-copied from `PICK_TIMER_SECONDS` with nothing tying them.** `src/lib/leagues/settings/draft-settings-guard.test.ts` (9 tests) pins the SQL against the TS catalog by reading the migration's own text — the `elevation-rule.test.ts` / `lists-v2-flag.test.ts` source-pin idiom — covering the whitelist (exact, in order), all five numeric ranges **including their message text**, the roster bounds, the unconditional-sum property, and the two-argument shape. **Probed: dropping `45` from the SQL list turns it RED**, restored md5-identical. A message that disagrees with the bound it enforces is its own bug, which is why the message is part of the assertion.
7. **R504 — the redundant conjunct is now ALARMED, and the alarm had to be structural.** The three child policies carry `league_id IS NULL` even though the helper carries it too, so removing either copy alone changes no query's answer — **a behavioural pin on them is impossible in principle**, and unalarmed defence-in-depth is indistinguishable from nobody checking. 043 §B asserts the conjunct's presence in each policy's `qual`. **Probed: dropping it from `draft_picks`' policy reddens test 23 with no runtime behaviour change at all** — which is exactly the class of edit that would otherwise land unnoticed.
8. **R501 — "the policy is TO public" says why the GRANT is needed, not why the ANSWER is safe.** `team_is_mock_seat` is DEFINER, reads RLS-hidden `drafts` rows, and returns one bit about a `teams` row. The argument, now written: **that bit is already public through a row the caller can read anyway** — `teams` is world-readable by design (§17) and a mock seat is exactly a `teams` row with `league_id IS NULL`, `list_id NULL` and a `CPU n` name. It reveals nothing about the draft (not its id, owner, type, status, or existence) and is only ASKABLE about a team id the caller already holds. The one thing it adds is a reachability signal — *"this row is spoken for"* — which is the property the guard exists to have, and which the caller would otherwise learn from a 23503 FK error.
9. **R502 — the seat protection outlives its party, and that is the right lifetime.** The banner justified the guard by the pre-first-pick wedge (a LIVE-draft argument) while the helper scopes to every mock. **Because the recap holds the seats:** `draft_picks.team_id` is `NO ACTION`, so a seat with picks is undeletable regardless — narrowing to `status <> 'complete'` would not GRANT the delete, only downgrade this policy's clean *0 rows* into a raw 23503 the user cannot act on — and a completed mock's seat with **zero** picks (an all-CPU board where one seat never picked) is precisely the row whose deletion corrupts the report's seat map. **The right lifetime for a protection is the lifetime of the thing it protects**, and that is the mock, which ends when the launcher deletes it or the 72h expiry does — both of which sweep the seats themselves.

- **D237 — The standalone mock as BUILT: what D234 priced, the three things nobody had priced, and the one item in F109 that turned out to be unreachable.**

*Every figure below was measured against the deployed local schema (chain at 094 = `main` @ `f7c0aa6`) or read out of the migration FILE text — never `pg_get_functiondef` for authoring (CLAUDE.md's superseded-body rule). Each claim names its command (tasks-DR §4 rule 9).*

3. **F109(a) WAS AN UNDERCOUNT, IN ITS OWN ERROR SPECIES.** F109 named SIX `draft_tick` sites — the ones inside its `AND d.is_mock` scans. **A standalone mock needs TEN.** The four nobody had counted, each read off the deployed body with its line number: **ARM 2's body re-check (body 375)** — the claim above it carries NO leagues predicate, so a standalone mock IS claimed and then silently skipped, and its pick clock never expires; **ARM 2.6(a)/(b), the auction clocks (body 810/834)** — scanned by `draft_type = 'auction'`, not by `is_mock`, so a standalone auction was claimed and skipped the same way (no nomination timeout, no bid close); and **ARM 3, the §9.1 heartbeat (body 961)** — every live draft, mocks included since 071, so without it the room's clock drifts with no beat to correct it. **The cause is R484's own species one turn later: the inventory was built by asking "which arms are ABOUT mocks", and three of the four missing arms reach a mock without mentioning one.** Twelve sites are amended; the remaining two (ARM 1.5/1.6's supervision auto-pause, body 186/198) are **behaviourally inert** — that arm is gated on a `league_members` join which is empty with no league — and are amended for uniformity and SAID to be inert, so the next reader does not re-derive it. - **D236 — A mock's roster shape is a SNAPSHOT; a real draft's stays LIVE; and the second half is a decision, not an omission.**

1. **What was wrong, restated at the level that explains why it survived three milestones.** D95's *"a mock never re-hydrates"* was implemented as *"copy `leagues.settings->'draft'` into `drafts.config`"* — and `roster_settings` is a **separate COLUMN**, so the copy never contained it. 2. **The fix is a deletion, not a guard.** `draft_mock_cpu_need`'s `JOIN public.leagues` is **gone** (every caller is a mock arm — `089:2322`, superseded by `091:516`), and `draft_autopick_resolve`'s `SELECT l.* INTO v_league` moved **inside** its `is_mock = FALSE` arm. **No league fallback is written on the mock path**, deliberately: a fallback would re-open exactly the re-hydration D95 forbids and would leave the read MP.2 exists to remove. Legacy rows are handled by a **backfill** instead (094 §2), which is what makes the no-fallback position affordable.
3. **The storage key is `config->'roster'`, holding the WHOLE roster object rather than just `starting_slots`.** Two readers need the slots today; the whole object costs nothing, makes the draft row self-describing beside the `total_rounds` already derived from it, and gives MP.4's settings OBJECT (§4 rule 12) a place to land that is a **new source, not a rewrite**. The §7.3.8 draft block is flat scalars, so the key cannot collide.
4. **REAL DRAFTS KEEP THE LIVE READ, AND THIS IS THE DECISION THE TASK WAS ASKED TO STATE.** §7.3.3's scoring-snapshot doctrine and D95 both point at snapshot-at-start as the house position — but a real draft's settings edits go through **§8.7/D141's pause-first commissioner controls**, which is a different argument with a different blast radius (a live twelve-human draft, mid-flight, whose commissioner is entitled to change the board). **MP.2 had no mandate to settle it and did not.** It is folded into the LAW as spec **v2.16.1** rather than left in a PR body, so the next lane inherits the decision instead of re-deciding it silently, and **042 §D pins it** by showing the same mid-flight edit MOVING a real draft's autopick while the mock's stands still. No `config->'roster'` is written for a real draft either — an unread stored field is a claim nobody checks (042 §A pins the negative).
5. **THE COLLAPSE IS NOW A MEASUREMENT, NOT A PARAGRAPH (probe 2).** §1.2 predicted that a league-less mock would leave `v_slots`/`v_total` NULL and collapse every bot's need term. Probed in a rolled-back transaction (`league_id` NOT NULL and its FK dropped, a standalone mock inserted, the shipped body installed under a probe name): the pre-094 body returns **0.5 for a starter and 0.5 for a bench player** — not an error, not a stall, **every position priced identically** — while the 094 body returns **1.0 / 0.5**. **2026-08-24 — Builder (F110 closure, the fixture-pool fix; branch `fix/F110-fixture-adp-scale`; TEST FILES ONLY — zero migrations, zero function bodies, zero app code)**

- **D235 — A pgTAP fixture may never state its premise about the WHOLE `players` table. Two premises were doing exactly that, and they are two different bugs, not one.**

1. **The band (9 of the 10 failures) — the R286 lesson, applied where F60's sweep had not reached.** `022`, `025` and `026` seeded fixture players on an INTEGER ADP scale (`022` RB `1…17` / WR `31…40` / QB `51…57` / K `151…153` / DST `161…162`; `025` QB `1…20`, RB `101…112`; `026` QB `1…20`, RB `101…120`) and never cleared `players`. A seeded dev pool holds **1,075 rows / 530 with an ADP**, and its **global minimum is 1.8** (RB) — measured, not assumed — so the two scales **interleave** and `draft_autopick_resolve`'s source-4 walk drafted real players. **Fix: every fixture value divided by 1000**, landing the whole band in `(0, 1)`. This is the band `035` has carried and documented since M3 (`035:19–23`) and the exact repair F60 made to `draft-realtime-db.test.ts`; these three files are F60's un-swept remainder.
2. **Why divide rather than re-number, and why it is green in BOTH worlds.** A single positive divisor preserves the order among fixtures **exactly** — every within-file discriminator survives untouched, including `025`'s load-bearing "the 20 best ADPs are ALL QBs" and `026`'s `lr-p003` pin. `draft_autopick_resolve` reads adp **only as an ordering key** (`ORDER BY pl.adp NULLS LAST, pl.id` at `086:692` and `086:742`; the `row_number()` at `086:692` is consumed as an ordinal by `ORDER BY c.src, c.ord` and compared against no threshold), so scale itself carries no meaning and only *relative position* can change. Every fixture moves **strictly below** the real pool's minimum, so the only orderings that can change are the ones where a real player previously preceded a fixture — precisely the failures. **On an EMPTY pool there are no real players, so the fixture-only order is bit-for-bit what it was**: the suites are green after a fresh reset and on a seeded machine alike, and **this was established by reasoning from the fix, not by running a destructive `db reset`** (`players.adp` is unconstrained `numeric`, so the fractions store at full precision — checked).
3. **The 10th failure is a DIFFERENT species and no ADP band could have fixed it — `022`'s FLOOR world (test 38).** Its premise was *"a forced TE need with **ZERO TEs in the pool**"*, which is a claim about the whole table; a seeded pool holds **231 TEs (94 with an ADP, min 22.1)**, one of them fits the need, greedy step h is never reached and the pin went red. **Fix: `022`'s LD roster_settings slot changes from `{"key":"te","eligible":["TE"]}` to `{"key":"floor","eligible":["NOPOS"]}`** — a token no player pool can carry. `draft_autopick_resolve` builds `v_need` straight from that array and tests it with a plain `v_row.pos = ANY(v_need)` (`086:631`/`086:706`): **no slot vocabulary is validated, no other branch keys off `'TE'`**, and `TE` was never load-bearing here — so step h is reached by the identical path, now **true by construction** instead of true by luck. Nothing else in `022` referenced that slot (checked: `starting_slots` appears twice, `"te"` once).
4. **Neither fix loosens anything, and both were probed (§4.3, D146).** The test count is **2923 before and after** — no assertion was dropped, renamed away or widened; the only assertion text that changed is test 38's *description*, from "a forced TE need with ZERO TEs in the pool" to "a forced need NO player in the pool can fill", which is what it now literally does. **Probe A (the semantic change):** plant one player at `position 'NOPOS', adp 0.999` — far WORSE than `tk-rb01`'s `0.001` — and test 38 goes **RED with `have: tk-probe-nopos`**, proving the need gate is live and step h is reached *only* because nothing fits; if the gate were dead the floor pin would have been satisfied anyway and the test would have proved nothing. **Probe B (the band):** restore `025`'s integer scale and tests **48 and 81 go RED again** (`have: 3` / `want: 8`). Both reverted, full suite re-run green.
5. **The standing rule this leaves.** *A fixture that asserts on an ADP-resolved pick must win by VALUE (a fractional band below the real minimum), and a fixture whose premise is an ABSENCE must make that absence true within its own fixture — never by betting on what the shared `players` table happens to contain.* The second half is new; F60/R286 only ever covered the first, which is why the sweep criterion R315 corrected still missed test 38.
6. **`F94` was checked while in the file and deliberately NOT touched (its own row owns it).** `src/lib/leagues/api/draft-board-autopick-db.test.ts` **does not carry F110's exposure** — it is already immune by the R286 redesign, seeding its fixtures at `adp: NULL` ("the one placement no walk can reach", `:83`), so a seeded pool can never steal a fixture from it. **Its exposure is the exact inverse and it is F94's:** `:424` asserts the ADP-resolved pick is **NOT** a fixture and `:436` asserts `picked?.adp` is **not null**, both of which require a **non-empty** real pool with ADPs — they fail on the empty pool a fresh reset leaves. Reported, not fixed.
