- **D234 — The storage shape is DECIDED: a standalone mock lives in the SAME tables, with `league_id` nullable and the ownership arm scoped by `league_id IS NULL`. Mock-owned tables are REFUSED, and D233(3)'s guardrail is the finding, stated plainly.**

*Every figure below was measured against the **deployed local schema** (`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` tops at **093** = repo HEAD `8fc5852`), never by grepping the migration tree — that method difference is how D228's 4× error happened, and it is how two of the figures this entry corrects went wrong too. Each claim names its command (tasks-DR §4 rule 9).*

1. **THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION AS D233(1) STATES IT: no. The engine cannot operate on mock-owned storage without duplicating the auction rules, and it is not close.** `SELECT count(*), sum(array_length(string_to_array(prosrc,E'\n'),1)) FROM pg_proc … WHERE proname ~ '^(draft|create_mock|delete_mock|mock_draft)'` → **58 live functions / 6,310 lines**. *(§1.3's "6,252" is the same measurement by a newline count: 6,310 − 58 = 6,252. No discrepancy — recorded so the next session does not re-derive it as a conflict.)* Of those, **37 functions / 5,901 lines** name one of the six draft tables, across **206 individual table-naming lines**, spread over **17 migration files** (`grep -lE '^CREATE (OR REPLACE )?FUNCTION +(public\.)?(draft_|create_mock|delete_mock|mock_draft)' supabase/migrations/*.sql | wc -l`). **The auction subset alone is 25 functions / 3,604 lines** (`proname ~ '(bid|nominat|auction|solven|budget)' OR prosrc ~ 'public\.draft_bids'` — `draft_tick` 1015, `draft_nominate` 295, `draft_force_pick` 280, `draft_award_nomination_internal` 232, `draft_undo` 204, `draft_place_bid` 178 …). **Dynamic SQL is absent: exactly one function in the family contains `EXECUTE`, and it is `draft_actor_name`** — re-confirmed, not recalled.
2. **And the price of (b) is LARGER than D233(3) priced it, in three places nobody had measured.** **(i) The FK fan-in.** `drafts` has **five** FK children (`pg_constraint … confrelid='public.drafts'::regclass`): `draft_picks`, `draft_queues`, `draft_liveness`, `draft_bids`, **and `draft_dnd_marks`** — the sixth table §1.3 never enumerated. Mock-owned storage duplicates the whole family, not four tables. **(ii) The realtime layer.** Five broadcast triggers fire on the draft path (`tr_broadcast_drafts`, `_draft_picks`, `_draft_bids`, `_draft_bids_void`, `tr_broadcast_league_chat`); each needs a twin. **(iii) The app layer, which §1.3 never measured at all.** `grep -rn "from('<t>')" src --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` → **148 call sites across 24 TypeScript files** (`drafts` 81 · `draft_picks` 33 · `draft_bids` 19 · `league_chat` 8 · `draft_queues` 7 · `draft_liveness` 0). Mock-owned tables mean a table-selecting or a parallel service layer on top of the two copies of the auction rules. **(iv) The suites.** **19 of 42 pgTAP files** name one of the six (836 `drafts` mentions, 284 `draft_bids`, 259 `draft_picks`, 117 `league_chat`, 65 `draft_queues`, 56 `draft_liveness`), and every one asserts against a body that names what it touches — D233(3)'s second argument, now with the count.
3. **Rewriting to table-agnostic dynamic SQL is refused for the reason D233(3) names, and the measurement makes it concrete: 23 of the 58 functions are `SECURITY DEFINER`** (`prosecdef`), every one of them built on `search_path=''` (tasks-M* §4.1). Turning 206 literal table references into `EXECUTE format(...)` is 206 opportunities to reintroduce the search-path hazard that discipline exists to close. **Refused.**
4. **THE SAME-TABLES PATH, RE-PRICED — and TWO of D233(4)'s three figures are wrong, in D228's own error species.**
   - **`NOT NULL` drops: FOUR, confirmed exactly.** `information_schema.columns WHERE column_name='league_id'` → 11 rows: `teams` already nullable, **10 `NOT NULL`**, of which **four are on the draft path** — `drafts`, `draft_picks`, `draft_bids`, `league_chat`. The other six are league-only tables a mock never touches. **D233(4) is right on this one.**
   - **In-body auth sites: EIGHT executable on a mock's path, not eleven — and SEVEN bodies actually change.** §1.3's `length/replace` count returns 13, but **four of those 13 are COMMENT lines**, not calls (`draft_make_pick`, `draft_nominate`, `draft_touch`, `set_team_autodraft` each carry an `-- … is_league_member(NULL) is FALSE` note). Filtering `trim(line) !~ '^--'` gives **9 executable sites across 9 functions**, one per function: `create_mock_draft` · `delete_mock_draft` · `draft_make_pick` · `draft_nominate` · `draft_pause` · `draft_place_bid` · `draft_resume` · `draft_touch` · `set_team_autodraft`. **`set_team_autodraft` is a league verb and out of scope → eight on a mock's path**; **`create_mock_draft` is superseded by MP.3's new standalone launch RPC → seven bodies amended.** **This is exactly D228(3)'s failure repeated one level down: a counting method that cannot tell live code from dead text.** D228 counted superseded bodies; §1.3 counted comments. **The rule the two together establish: count what EXECUTES, not what MATCHES.**
   - **RLS: FOUR SELECT arms required, not five — and the fifth is optional for a reason worth writing down.** `pg_policies` shows **14 policies in `public` naming `is_league_member`** (§1.3's figure — correct once you notice it excludes `realtime`), of which **five sit on four draft-path tables**: SELECT on `drafts`/`draft_picks`/`draft_bids`/`league_chat`, plus **`league_chat`'s INSERT**. **The INSERT arm is not required — but NOT for the reason this entry first gave, and the correction is this session's own rule failing on itself (R485).** The original reason was *"every engine write bypasses RLS"*, resting on `postgres` being `rolbypassrls`. **That establishes a bypass for `SECURITY DEFINER` bodies only, and 35 of the 58 engine functions are `SECURITY INVOKER`** (`prosecdef` → **35 `f` / 23 `t`**) — `draft_queue_replace` is an **invoker, client-callable engine writer** (`has_function_privilege('authenticated', …, 'EXECUTE')` → true) which runs as the caller, and `authenticated` is **not** `rolbypassrls`. **A blanket claim measured on the wrong population — exactly the species tasks-DR §4 rule 9 exists for.** The conclusion survives on the narrower ground that actually holds, re-measured: **every client-reachable `league_chat` writer is `SECURITY DEFINER`** — all thirteen engine-family chat writers except `draft_pause_internal` are definer and granted to `authenticated`, and **`draft_pause_internal` is granted to neither `authenticated` nor `anon`**, being reached only from `draft_pause` and `draft_tick` — and `relforcerowsecurity` is **false** on all seven tables — measured. The INSERT arm is needed only if a human types into a mock room, and D226(2) says there is nobody to type to. **So: four SELECT arms, and a fifth that MP.3 may decline with a reason.**
   - **`draft_queues`, `draft_liveness` and `draft_dnd_marks` cost ZERO** — none carries `league_id`; `draft_liveness` has RLS on with **zero policies** (deny-all to clients, RPC-only); **`draft_queues`' two policies ALREADY carry the exact predicate this decision recommends** — `d.is_mock AND d.config->'mock'->>'launched_by' = auth.uid()::text` — shipped, in production, in `pg_policies` today. **The ownership predicate is not new work and not a new idiom:** `launched_by` appears in **11 live functions** (`create_mock_draft` 6 · `draft_tick` 5 · `draft_make_pick`/`draft_nominate`/`draft_place_bid` 3 each · `draft_autopick_resolve`/`mock_draft_expire` 2 each · `delete_mock_draft`/`draft_pause`/`draft_queue_replace`/`draft_resume` 1 each). **MS.2's gate is reused verbatim, per the lane constraint — nothing is reinvented.**
   - **Indexes and constraints: ZERO work.** **Eight** unique indexes name `league_id` schema-wide (`pg_indexes WHERE indexdef ~ 'UNIQUE' AND indexdef ~ 'league_id'`), but **exactly one is on the draft path** — `drafts.one_active_real_draft_per_league`, already filtered `WHERE is_mock = false`. The other seven are on `league_lists`, `league_members`, `league_rosters` and `league_weeks`, which a mock never touches. *(R487 — the sentence as first written said "the only unique index on `league_id`", which is false schema-wide.)*
5. **THREE ITEMS THE SAME-TABLES PRICE WAS MISSING — and the first one, added at review (R484), is the most severe thing in this entry.**
   - **THE `leagues`-EXISTENCE GUARD CLASS: UNDER THIS SHAPE THE ENGINE NEVER CLAIMS A STANDALONE MOCK AT ALL, AND IT FAILS SILENTLY.** This session's "breaks on a NULL `league_id`" sweep stopped at `is_league_member` and missed a **third, larger class** — the `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.leagues l WHERE l.id = … AND l.deleted_at IS NULL)` soft-delete guards. Re-swept with `LATERAL regexp_matches(prosrc,'([^\n]*public\.leagues\M[^\n]*)','g')`, comment lines filtered: **`draft_tick` 14 · `draft_start_internal` 3 · `create_mock_draft` / `draft_autopick_resolve` / `draft_create_internal` / `draft_reset` / `draft_set_order` 2 each · `draft_complete_internal` / `draft_end` / `draft_make_pick` / `draft_mock_cpu_need` / `draft_nominate` / `draft_place_bid` 1 each.** **SIX of `draft_tick`'s sit INSIDE its `AND d.is_mock` scans** — body lines **268/291** (ARM 1.6), **531/559** (ARM 2.5), **680/722** (ARM 2.6(c)), each an `AND EXISTS (… l.id = d.league_id AND l.deleted_at IS NULL)` on the scan that decides which mock to advance. **Probed live in a rolled-back transaction over three `live` rows: `tick_leagues_guard` is `t` for the REAL draft, `t` for the MOCK-in-league, and `f` for the MOCK-standalone.** **So the tick never picks a standalone mock up — no CPU picks, no nominations, no bids — and it says nothing.** That is strictly worse than the `league_chat` failure below, which this entry credited itself with catching: **that one raises 23502 loudly; this one produces a mock that runs and never bids.** **And the same class is loud in the other direction:** `draft_make_pick`, `draft_nominate` and `draft_place_bid` each carry a **second, uncounted** `IF NOT EXISTS (… leagues …) RAISE … USING ERRCODE = 'P0002'` **immediately after** the `is_league_member` site item 4 counted, and `draft_end` / `draft_reset` carry the `PERFORM … FOR UPDATE; IF NOT FOUND` variant — probed the same way, **`raises_P0002` is `f` / `f` / `t`**, so the human's own pick, nomination and bid would all 404 on their own practice. **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PRICE: item 4's "seven bodies amended" is WRONG. It is seven bodies PLUS the leagues-existence guard class**, which touches `draft_tick` (six mock-scan arms), `draft_make_pick`, `draft_nominate`, `draft_place_bid`, `draft_end` and `draft_reset`. **It does not change the DECISION** — these are predicate edits inside bodies that stay where they are, and mock-owned tables would inherit every one of the same guards — **but MP.3 is materially larger than item 4 implied, and that must not be discovered during the build.** **OWNERSHIP: MP.3, not MP.2.** MP.2's charter is the two live **settings readers** (`roster_settings->'starting_slots'`); these are **candidate-set and existence predicates**, a different class in different bodies, and they belong beside the `NOT NULL` drops in the same migration. **Filed as F109(a).**
   - **`league_chat`'s `NOT NULL` drop is LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic.** `draft_pause_internal` and `draft_resume` each `INSERT INTO public.league_chat (league_id, …) VALUES (v_draft.league_id, …)` **with no `is_mock` guard** — **fourteen** functions in the schema `INSERT INTO public.league_chat`; thirteen are in the engine family and the fourteenth is `set_team_autodraft`, **excluded as a league verb (R489)**. Of the thirteen, **twelve mention `is_mock` at all** (`draft_pause_internal` does not) — and **these two execute the chat INSERT on a mock's path with `v_draft.league_id` unguarded**, both on a standalone mock's path (`draft_pause_internal` is called by `draft_pause` **and `draft_tick`**). With `league_id` NULL and the column still `NOT NULL`, **pausing or resuming a standalone mock raises 23502 and the practice is stuck.** This is §1.2's finding on the storage axis rather than the settings axis, and it is **MP.3's** to close — either by the drop or by an `is_mock` guard, its call. **Not fixed here (MP.1 changes nothing).**
   - **THE REALTIME POLICIES, WHICH NO PRICING HAD COUNTED UNDER EITHER SHAPE.** `realtime.messages` carries **two policies on `draft:%` topics** — `members read draft topics` (SELECT) and `members track presence on draft topics` (INSERT) — and **both gate on `is_league_member(d.league_id)` via a subquery on `drafts`.** Without an arm, **the launcher cannot subscribe to their own mock's channel and the room is dead**, and the room is realtime-driven (tasks-M2 §4 rule 5). **The cost is identical under either shape, so it does not move the decision** — but it must be in MP.3's work list. **And the chat pane's READ is league-keyed too (R490), which this entry's D226(2) appeal covered only for the SEND:** `useDraftChat` (`src/hooks/use-draft-chat.ts:44–50`) is `enabled: Boolean(leagueId && draftId)` and filters `.eq('league_id', leagueId!)`, so with no league **the query never runs, and a standalone launcher cannot read the engine's own SYSTEM posts** — the pause/resume/clock notices the room depends on. "Nobody to chat with" does not mean "nothing to read". **Added to F109(c), and MP.6 is the alternative owner if the room's data hooks land there first.** **The good news is measured:** the four draft broadcast trigger functions (`broadcast_draft_update`, `broadcast_draft_pick_change`, `broadcast_draft_bid_insert`, `broadcast_draft_bid_void`) **do not reference `league_id` at all** — only `broadcast_league_chat_insert` and `broadcast_league_roster_change` do — so the topic and payload layers are **already league-free** and only the two read policies need the arm. **Filed as F109.**
6. **D233(5) ANSWERED, and the answer is stronger than "no weakening" — it is "provably identical".** The recommended predicate is
   `is_league_member(league_id) OR (league_id IS NULL AND is_mock AND config->'mock'->>'launched_by' = auth.uid()::text)`.
   **The truth table is one line:** for any row where `league_id IS NOT NULL`, the second disjunct's **first conjunct is FALSE by construction**, so the whole predicate **reduces to the shipped one, term for term**. There is no real-league row for which the new arm can contribute a TRUE. Separately measured: **`is_league_member(NULL)` returns FALSE, not NULL** — it is a `SELECT EXISTS(…)`, which is never NULL — so **a nullable `league_id` fails CLOSED**. There is no NULL-permissiveness hole to defend against; the column's nullability, on its own, grants nobody anything.
7. **AND IT WAS PROBED, INCLUDING THE DELIBERATE BREAK (§4.3 falsifiability floor).** One rolled-back transaction, three users — `u1` league member and standalone launcher, `u2` outsider, **`u3` an EX-member who launched a league-attached mock and then left the league** — over three `drafts` rows (a REAL draft, a MOCK-in-league, a MOCK-standalone inserted after an in-txn `DROP NOT NULL`), read as `authenticated` under each user's JWT:
   - **A · shipped policy:** u1 → `REAL, MOCK-in-league` · u2 → `(nothing)` · u3 → `(nothing)`.
   - **B · the recommended arm:** u1 → `REAL, MOCK-in-league, MOCK-standalone` · u2 → `(nothing)` · **u3 → `(nothing)`. Every league-owning row is visible to exactly the same people as in A.**
   - **C · THE DELIBERATE BREAK — the identical arm with the `league_id IS NULL` conjunct removed:** **u3 → `MOCK-in-league`.** An ex-member keeps read on a league-attached mock after leaving the league — **strictly more permissive on a row that HAS a league**, which is precisely what D233(5) forbids. **Shown RED, then reverted** (the whole probe is inside `ROLLBACK`; afterwards `pg_policies` shows the shipped `is_league_member(league_id)` qual restored, `drafts.league_id` back to `is_nullable = NO`, and zero probe users left in `auth.users` — all three verified).
   **So the `league_id IS NULL` conjunct is load-bearing, not defensive decoration**, and MP.3 must not "simplify" it away. Probe script: `docs/specs/` carries no fixture; the exact SQL is reproduced in the PR body.
8. **What this decision does NOT do, stated so MP.3 does not over-read it.** It does not touch a real league or an `is_mock = FALSE` draft (§4 rule 11): the four `NOT NULL` drops are **widenings**, which no existing row can violate, and the four RLS arms are **provably inert** on every league-owning row (item 6). It does not choose the launch RPC's signature, the bot-seat shape (D227) or the settings source (D229) — those are MP.3/MP.4. It does not fix the two live `JOIN leagues` readers; **`draft_mock_cpu_need` (`089:394`) and `draft_autopick_resolve` are MP.2's**, and the sequencing is now a hard prerequisite rather than a preference: **under this shape a NULL `league_id` makes that JOIN match nothing and every bot's need term collapse (§1.2), and no storage decision can defend against it — MP.2 must land before MP.3.**
9. **The spec fold this decision OWES, and it is not MP.1's to make.** Spec **§12.4/§12.5/§12.6-adjacent** print `CREATE POLICY … USING (is_league_member(league_id))` for `drafts` (`spec:912`), `draft_picks` (`:938`) and `draft_bids` (`:990`), and §12's DDL prints `league_id` as `NOT NULL`. **v2.16 §8.8 already rules the standalone mock into v1** (`spec:570`), so §12's listings are stale rather than contradictory — but they are LAW as printed, and **the task that changes a policy owes the erratum, not the task that recommends it.** **Filed as F109 with MP.3 named.** *(No halt: D233 explicitly charters MP.1 to price the change to those arms, and the breakdown — merged LAW — already prices "five RLS policy arms on four tables" as in-scope. Recommending a change the lane document sanctions is not improvising around the spec.)*
10. **Recorded because it cost this session an hour and will cost the next one the same: `npm run test:db` is RED on a seeded dev machine, and it is an ENVIRONMENT artifact, not a regression.** 10 failures across `022_draft_tick_autopick` (6), `025_mock_draft_mode` (2), `026_draft_completion_rosters` (2) — every one in the autopick/roster family. **Cause, measured rather than guessed:** those suites seed fixture players on an integer ADP scale (025:213–217 — `mk-qb01…20` at ADP `1…20`, `mk-rb01…12` at `101…112`) and **never clear `players`**; this machine's `players` holds **1,075 rows, 530 with ADP**, topping out at **Jahmyr Gibbs 1.8, Bijan Robinson 2.7, Ja'Marr Chase 3.2** — which **interleave with the fixture scale**, so autopick drafts real players and the fixture assertions fail. **It is F94's mirror image**: F94 says the pool is EMPTY after a reset; here the seeds ran afterwards and the pool is FULL. **Drift was ruled out before concluding this**, per CLAUDE.md's reconciliation rule: `pg_get_functiondef(draft_autopick_resolve)` diffed **byte-identical** against its chain HEAD (`086_auction_tick_completion.sql:552`), and the migration table tops at 093. **No destructive `db reset` was run to "fix" it** — that would have cost Chris his dev login and data for a red this session did not cause. **Filed as F110.**

---

**2026-08-21 — Architect (the MP mock-practice breakdown; transcribed verbatim from `tasks-MP-mock-practice.md` §3.12 at merge, per the tasks-M3 / tasks-AP / tasks-MS precedent. Chris's rulings sit at §3 of that document; the spec fold is **v2.16**. **These decisions are the SECOND cut.** Chris read the first and asked why a mock needed any of it (*"I doubt they are doing any of this inivisible league blah blah blah security container stuff"*), and the lane was rewritten rather than patched: **a mock is standalone, its settings come from the base scoring templates, and the inherited league threat model does not apply.** **D228 is kept as its own WITHDRAWAL** — with the figures it rested on corrected — because a withdrawn decision that leaves no trace is how a rejected design gets re-proposed as a fresh idea.)**

- **D225 — Lane charter, numbering, and what the rewrite changed**

1. **MP is a lane, not a set of MS tasks.** MS's charter is *authority inside the room* — who may drive a mock once it exists. MP's is *what a mock is, how you get to one, and what you take away.* Under the new shape they barely touch at all (§7).
2. **Task ids are `MP.1`–`MP.11`.** No `L.C`, `AP.`, `DR2.`, `SE.` or `MS.` id is reused, retired or renumbered.
3. **Numbers taken: D225–D233, F102–F106, Q24, E78–E80, spec v2.16.** **D228 is occupied by its own withdrawal and F105 is retired with it** — neither number is recycled, because a withdrawn decision that leaves no trace is how a rejected design gets re-proposed as a fresh idea.
4. **This PR folds the spec, and it has to.** §8.8's *"v1 scope: league-attached only"* is LAW and is what ruling 3.1 contradicts; §8.8's 45-minute acceptance bar is LAW and is what ruling 3.11 de-targets. Leaving either would oblige the first Builder to halt.
5. **This lane does NOT touch `ACTIVE-BUILD.md`** — **F102**, the F98 precedent, with a named actor: PR #180 rewrites that block and the loop-order list.
6. **The rewrite deleted more than it added.** Withdrawn: the practice container (D228), the invented *"Scout Scoring"* preset, the 10-second mock bid clock, the mock-report/league-recap route split, and F105. **Kept: everything that serves a user** — the Home entry, the room's own route, the report, the profile list, the More… entry, the flag, and the leagues-off pin.


- **D226 — Two corrections, and the second is the transferable one**

1. §2.1 and §2.2 are the entry, in full, and they govern the lane. **A task that reads as "make league attachment nicer" has misread 2.1; a task that adds a protective mechanism without naming the party it protects against has misread 2.2.**
2. **The threat model was inherited, not derived.** RLS-by-membership, §8.8 isolation, commissioner authority and audit immutability all exist because a real draft has **twelve humans with money at stake**. **A mock has one human and eleven bots.** No adversary, nothing to protect.
3. **What genuinely survives, and it is two things:** a user must not be able to break their own practice irrecoverably (**§1.4/R473**), and one user's practice is not another's to read or drive — **one ownership predicate, not a membership graph.**
4. **The failure mode, generalised:** *when a feature moves out of the context it was born in, its inherited constraints are the first thing to re-derive, not the last.* The first cut re-derived the premise and left the threat model untouched, and so produced a careful design for a problem that had stopped existing. **This is D231(3a)'s species one level up.**
5. **Recorded rather than tidied away.** The container design is kept as **D228, withdrawn**, with its corrected figures, so the reasoning is legible and the design is not re-proposed as new.


- **D227 — Bot opponents: the constraint that survives, and the one protection that is real**

1. **`draft_picks.team_id` is `NOT NULL` FK `teams`** (`065:160`; same on `draft_bids` `083:120` and `draft_queues` `065:193`), so **every seat needs a `teams` row** — league or no league. This is the *only* part of the old seat problem that survives.
2. **A bot seat is a `teams` row with `league_id IS NULL`, `owner_id` = the launcher, `list_id NULL`**, minted in the launch transaction and deleted with the mock. `teams.league_id` is already nullable (`001:499`) and standalone teams already have their own RLS (`053:69–71`). **`add_placeholder_seat` is out of the picture entirely** — there is no league to seat.
3. **The exposure is real and is NOT an adversary problem (R473, live-probed in a rolled-back transaction).** `teams` carries *"Teams are viewable by everyone"* (`001:844`) and *"Users can manage own standalone teams"* (`053:69–71`); as `authenticated` the owner got **`UPDATE 1`** and **`DELETE 1`**. `draft_picks.team_id`'s FK is **`NO ACTION`**, so deleting a bot's seat before its first pick **wedges the mock at that seat's turn with no in-product recovery.**
4. **Disposition: narrow the policy for DELETE; accept UPDATE; accept world-readability explicitly.** Renaming your own bot is cosmetic and self-inflicted; **deleting one mid-draft breaks the practice in a way the product cannot fix**, and that is the line the policy should express. World-readability is accepted and stated rather than hidden — a bot seat carries a label and nothing else (§17). **This is D226(3)'s "a user must not break their own practice", not a security control.**
5. **Naming gets one rule, not a system.** `CPU 1 … CPU N`. No avatars, no personas, no generated team names. Chris ruled no explanatory copy for the mock surface (MS D221(1)) and the same restraint applies.
6. **Deletion order is a Builder trap.** `draft_picks` cascades from `drafts`; `teams` has **no** cascade from `drafts`. Delete the draft **first**, the seats **second**, in one transaction, or the FK refuses.


- **D228 — **WITHDRAWN** — the practice container, why it was proposed, its corrected figures, and why it became moot**

**Kept in the record rather than deleted. A withdrawn decision that leaves no trace is how a rejected design gets re-proposed as a fresh idea.**

1. **What it proposed.** A hidden per-user `leagues` row backing every league-less mock, so that league-shaped RLS, league-shaped FKs and §8.8 isolation could all be satisfied without touching the engine. It carried an exclusion predicate on every league-enumerating surface (F105), a `'manager'`-not-`'commissioner'` member role (R479), and a route requirement so its id never reached the address bar (R470).
2. **Why it was proposed, and this was sound reasoning from an unexamined premise:** the alternative looked enormous. D228(2) priced "make the league optional" at *"4 `NOT NULL` drops, 13 RLS policies, **50 in-body `is_league_member` sites across 18 migration files**"* and concluded *"that is a milestone, not a lane."*
3. **THE FIGURE WAS WRONG, AND BY ROUGHLY 4×.** It counted every occurrence in the migration **tree**, superseded bodies included. Measured against the deployed schema (§1.3): **13 calls across 9 live functions — 11 sites across 8 functions on a mock's path**; **five RLS policy rows on four draft-path tables**; **four `NOT NULL` drops**. **That is a task.** The correction is recorded here because the next person to price this path deserves the real number, and because *a decision resting on a measurement is only as good as the measurement*.
4. **Why it is withdrawn, and it is NOT because of the figure.** Chris's ruling removed the requirement the container existed to serve. **There is no §8.8 isolation obligation for a mock that has no league**, no membership graph to satisfy, and no threat model to inherit (D226). **The container was a careful answer to a question that stopped being asked.**
5. **F105 is retired with it** — its whole content was the container's enumeration obligation. The number is not recycled.
6. **What the storage shape actually is, is `MP.1`'s to determine by measurement** (D233). This entry does not pre-empt it; it only stops the container being the answer.


- **D229 — Settings come from the base templates, and the shape that keeps league inheritance a FILL rather than a rewrite**

1. **The six base scoring templates already ship** — ESPN Standard / Full PPR, Sleeper Standard / Full PPR, Yahoo Standard / Half PPR (`SELECT name FROM scoring_systems WHERE is_template` → 6 rows; migration 058, spec §7.3.3 / App B). **Ruling 3.10 maps onto shipped rows and needs no new scoring content.**
2. **The invented *"Scout Scoring"* preset is WITHDRAWN.** `grep -rn "Scout Scoring" docs/ src/` → no matches; Chris used the phrase describing how a **public league** product would dictate rules, and **public leagues are not this lane.**
3. **The draft settings come from the schema's own defaults, which Chris has now ruled directly and which are already the shipped values** (§1.9): **nomination 30s · bid 20s · anti-snipe 10s · pick timer 90s**, `DEFAULT_ROSTER_SETTINGS` for the roster (`league-settings.ts:164`). **No mock-specific default of any kind** — *"Use the same default."* **Zero lines change for the numbers.**
4. **THE DEFAULTS ARE A SUGGESTION AND THE USER CHANGES THEM AT LAUNCH.** *"just let the user make the clocks what they want … the defaults are merely a suggestion."* So the launch surface is a real settings form, not a fixed preset — which is also what makes the deferred feature cheap.
5. **THE DEFERRAL CONSTRAINT, AND IT IS A DESIGN RULE ON MP.4 (§4 rule 12).** **Do not build the settings path such that values can only come from a template.** The launch RPC takes a **settings object**; where it comes from is the caller's business. **League inheritance must later be "fill this object from a league instead of from a template" — a new source, not a rewrite.** A Builder who hard-codes template lookup inside the launch RPC has broken this rule.


- **D230 — The report: one flat table, two column sets**

1. **Chris asked for a table:** *"a table of every player from the draft and their cost and what team they went to."* Today the auction has a **list** (`AuctionFinalBoard`, `draft-recap.tsx:411–467`) and snake has a **grid**; neither is a table and **snake has no flat cut at all**.
2. **TWO COLUMN SETS, NOT ONE TABLE WITH BLANKS.** Auction: *player · position · team · **price** · **nomination #***, with per-team spend. Snake/linear: *player · position · team · **round** · **pick #***. A single five-column table prints an empty `price` on every snake row and an empty `round` on every auction row — **an empty column claims the value exists and is unknown, which is false in both directions.** `recapBuysInOrder`'s docblock already makes this argument about the board; this is the same argument one layer out.
3. **Compose, do not re-solve.** `recapBuysInOrder` (`draft-recap-ops.ts:157–159`) is the auction row set; `recapTeamSpend` (`:130–152`) the totals; the snake sibling is one new pure derivation **in the same ops file**. **A second recap component tree is the LV.7 failure pattern.**
4. **The route split of the first cut is WITHDRAWN as a task.** With league-attached mocks deferred, there is no ongoing stream of mock recaps at the league level to split off. **The league recap keeps real drafts and is otherwise untouched**, and the one residual — **legacy mock recaps that already exist under `?draft=<mock_id>`** — is a single item inside MP.8, not a lane task.
5. **Chris's *"it emails you the draft results"* (ruling 3.9) is an OBSERVATION about the incumbents, not a request, and email is NOT in this lane.** Recorded so the omission is deliberate: the report has a permanent home and a list, which is the durable version of the same value. If Chris wants the email, it is a small follow-up on top of a report that already exists.


- **D231 — The lane's own release gate, and the route layer**

1. **`NEXT_PUBLIC_FLAG_MOCK_DRAFTS` → `featureFlags.mockDrafts`, never `featureFlags.leagues`.** Chris: *"Mocks do not need to be connected to League work."* Precisely the case `feature-flags.ts:27–31`'s doctrine exists for.
2. **THIS IS A RELEASE STATEMENT, NOT A CODE-ISOLATION ONE.** A mock still runs on the **shared draft engine** — `drafts`, `draft_tick`, the room, the same RPC family, the same suites — **and that sharing is correct and stays** (it is also, per §1.3, what makes the lane affordable at all). What must not exist is a **dependency**: no MP task is blocked on a league task, and **turning the leagues flag off must not turn practice off**.
3. **The pin is the assertion that keeps it true.** With `leagues` **off** and `mockDrafts` **on**: the Home entry renders and launches, **the room loads**, the More… tab renders, `/app/mocks` lists, a report opens. MP.11 owns the end-to-end; MP.7 and MP.9 carry their halves.
3a. **AND THE ROOM HALF IS REFUSED BY A SHIPPED, PINNED ROUTE GUARD UNTIL `MP.6` LANDS (R470).** `(room)/leagues/layout.tsx:18` hard-redirects every `/app/leagues` URL when the leagues flag is off — *"even by direct URL"*, per its own docblock — and the mock room is one of those URLs (§1.7). **`featureFlags.mockDrafts` cannot reach past it**, because the gate is a different flag on a different layout. **This was missed in the first cut and the failure mode is the one worth keeping:** *a release-independence claim is a claim about ROUTES as well as components, and the route layer had a guard the component layer could not see.* **§2.2 is this same failure one level up**, which is why both are recorded.
4. **The flag gates UI SURFACES ONLY, never a `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC.** A `NEXT_PUBLIC_` flag is client-inlined; gating server authority on one is a client-side gate on a server-authoritative surface, which §12 forbids.
5. **Under the new shape there is NO surface with a legitimate leagues dependency.** The first cut carved out the League Home CTA; that CTA now belongs to the **deferred** feature and stays exactly as it is (§6). **Every MP surface works with leagues off, with no exception to state.**


- **D232 — Q23, the fidelity question and the mock bid clock are GONE, not answered**

1. **Q23 asked whether a 10-second mock bid clock overrides a league that chose its own. Under the new shape the question has no subject:** there is no league to inherit from and **no mock-specific default to override with** — Chris ruled *"Use the same default."* **Q23 LAPSES.** It is recorded as lapsed rather than resolved, because "we answered it" would misdescribe what happened: **the design changed underneath it.**
2. **§8.8's fidelity sentence — *"A mock is slow when the league's clocks are slow, and that is correct"* — stays, and is DORMANT while inheritance is deferred.** It is a statement about a league-attached mock; there are none for now. **Not amended, not weakened, not deleted** — it is exactly the sentence the deferred feature will need on the day it returns.
3. **AP.4 has nothing left in it.** Its ruled half already ships (§1.9: bid 20 ✅ · nomination 30 ✅ · anti-snipe 10 ✅ · ranges and floor ✅ — zero lines change), and its unruled half was the override, which no longer exists. **B5 clears.**
4. **AP.4's record is NOT edited by this PR** — the disposition is escalated (the reviewer's R472) and a lane document must not close another lane's task by assertion. **F106** files the obligation with a named actor.
5. **F85 IS DE-TARGETED, and this is Chris's ruling, not an Architect's read.** *"My point about finishing a mock in 45 minutes was just an example not a target … I think we're good."* **The under-45-minute bar stops being a gate**, the spec's acceptance-criteria sentence is amended to say so, and **no MP or AP task is measured against it.** **F92 survives on its own merits** — the CPU nomination still rides the 5-second sweep, and that is a real pacing cost — but it is now *"a thing worth fixing"*, not *"the other term in a bar we must hit."*


- **D233 — The storage shape is an INVESTIGATION, and what the measurement already establishes**

1. **MP.1 decides it, and it comes first.** The question: **can the draft engine operate on mock-owned storage without duplicating the auction/snake logic?** The answer is a measurement, not a preference, and **the deliverable is a decision with evidence, not code.**
2. **What is already measured, so MP.1 starts from facts rather than a blank page (§1.3).** The engine is **58 live functions / 6,252 lines** of plpgsql; it names its tables **literally** (`drafts` in 37 functions, `draft_picks` 15, `league_chat` 15, `draft_bids` 11, `draft_liveness` 5, `draft_queues` 2); and **dynamic SQL is essentially absent — one function in the family contains `EXECUTE`, and it is `draft_actor_name`.**
3. **So the ruling's own guardrail is the likely finding, and MP.1 must state it plainly if it reaches it: separate mock tables mean either two copies of the auction rules or a rewrite of 6,252 lines into table-agnostic dynamic SQL — and BOTH are worse than either option.** Duplication is worse for the obvious reason. Dynamic SQL is worse for a less obvious one: it would break the `search_path=''` discipline every one of these functions is built on (tasks-M* §4.1), and it would make the pgTAP suites assert against a body that no longer names what it touches.
4. **The same-tables path is now priced honestly and it is task-sized** (§1.3, correcting D228(2)): four `NOT NULL` drops, five RLS policy arms on four tables, eleven in-body auth sites across eight functions. **"You own it" is one predicate** — `config->'mock'->>'launched_by' = auth.uid()::text`, the idiom `draft_pause`/`draft_resume` already ship (`069:404–415`).
5. **MP.1 must nevertheless check the thing that would change the answer:** whether a nullable `league_id` weakens any **real-league** guarantee. A policy that reads *"member of the league OR launcher of this mock"* must be provably no more permissive for a row that HAS a league. **If that cannot be shown, the answer changes and the task says so.**
6. **Do not pick the shape by preference, and do not let this decision be made inside a task that is also building something.** The MS.1 precedent: a task that audits *and* enables will report on its own work.

**2026-08-20 — Architect (the MS mock-sandbox breakdown; transcribed verbatim from `tasks-MS-mock-sandbox.md` §3.5 at merge, per the tasks-M2 D86–D101 / tasks-M3 D126–D143 / tasks-AP D197–D203 precedent).**

- **D216 — Lane charter, numbering, and why MS is its own lane.** **Number note (D161's grep-together rule).** R, D, F, Q **and E** swept together across `main` @ `90178a7` and the one open branch (PR **#180**, `docs/DR2-draft-room-v2`) — the full table is tasks-MS §1.9. `main` tops at **R467 / D215 / F97 / Q18 / E70**; #180 holds **D204–D212 / F87–F91 / Q19–Q21 / E71–E74**. R312 first-filed-keeps, so this session takes **D216–D221**, files **F98–F100**, opens **Q22**, and takes edge cases **E75–E76** and spec version **v2.15**. **The amendment round (Chris's order ruling, same day) adds D222–D223, F101 and E77**, re-derived rather than continued: re-swept at amendment time across `main` (**R467 / D215 / F97 / Q18 / E70**, the `spec-tier-view.md` hexes excluded per D180) and **both** open PRs — #180 (**D204–D212 / F87–F91 / Q19–Q21 / E71–E74**) and this one. Re-sweep at merge. (1) **MS is a new lane with its own prefix, not an append to tasks-M3 §6 or to tasks-AP.** The AP/DR2 precedent exactly: Chris drove a *shipped* surface (Mock Draft Mode), ruled changes to it, and those changes get their own Architect document plus an ACTIVE-BUILD clause, while the milestone's approved breakdown stays what it is. MS's subject — who may drive a mock — is orthogonal to M3's exit criteria, to AP's pacing and to DR2's layout. (2) **The lane is small and it is a permissions change with one product consequence.** Six tasks, three of them without a migration. It is filed as a lane rather than as one big task because **the audit must be a separate deliverable from the change it authorizes** (D218), and because the §8.8 pins are the point rather than an afterthought. (3) **Task ids are `MS.1`–`MS.6`.** No `L.C`, `AP.` or `DR2.` id is reused, retired or renumbered. (4) **This PR folds the spec, and it has to.** §8.8's v2.8.16 erratum (`spec:567`) is LAW and says every §8.7 control refuses mocks. Cutting tasks that contradict LAW would oblige the first Builder to stop and file a spec question — a halt this session would have manufactured. The fold is deliberately narrow (§10 item 1) and takes **v2.15** because #180 already filed v2.14.

- **D217 — What D103 got right, what it missed, and the exact shape of the overturn.** (1) **D103/D110(1) were right about authority and right about the bug.** "A commissioner control on a mock is interference with a member's solo practice" is a correct sentence about a commissioner reaching into *someone else's* rehearsal, and the guard caught a live-proven `leagues` write. Neither of those is being called a mistake. (2) **What it missed is that in a mock the launcher IS the commissioner.** The doctrine was written from the *actor* side (who is reaching in) and never asked what happens when there is only one person in the room. Chris's ruling 1 supplies the missing premise, and the whole lane follows from it. (3) **The overturn is scoped to identity, not to isolation.** What changes: *who* may call a §8.7 control on a mock. What does not change: **§8.8's zero-side-effects rule** (unweakened, and now the explicit gate — D218), **D103(2)'s no-other-driver doctrine** (a commissioner who is not the launcher still gets nothing — MS.2 item 7 pins it), and every real-draft behaviour (§4 rule 13). (4) **The pattern is already in the codebase and it is 069's, not `resolveActingSeat`'s.** `draft_pause`/`draft_resume` solved this exact problem at L.B1.6 — member floor, then commissioner for real drafts, then launcher for mocks. MS.2 extracts that into one helper and applies it. The working draft of this document proposed reusing R420's `resolveActingSeat`; that is a **TypeScript API-layer seat resolver** for the F65 response-integrity check, not a server-authoritative gate, and reusing it would have put authorization in the wrong layer (§1.2). (5) **The gate ORDER is the load-bearing bug, and it is measured.** In all eleven controls `is_league_commish` fires before the mock refusal, so today's friendly P0001 is unreachable for a non-commissioner launcher — the exact person this lane is about. D110(1) recorded the consequence in one clause and nobody had a reason to act on it until now. **The reorder therefore runs at ALL ELEVEN sites, cleared AND excluded** — E75 (LAW added by this same PR) requires an excluded control to refuse *"with a message that names its own reason"*, and measured, `draft_reset` and `draft_end` answer a non-commissioner launcher with `42501 not a commissioner of this draft's league`. A reorder scoped to the cleared set would ship LAW the code cannot honour.

- **D218 — §8.8 is the gate, it is answered by measurement, and `draft_reset` was not the only breach.** (1) **The audit is its own task (MS.1) and produces a list, not a change.** Separating them is the point: a task that audits *and* enables will report on its own work, and the enable step's design will bend toward whatever the audit found convenient. MS.1 ships a cleared list with evidence per row and touches no behaviour. (2) **"Which controls are safe" is a measurement, never a reading.** §1.4 is why: two of the eleven reach a `leagues` write through a helper, so the direct write set is not the answer; and §2.2 is why a `draft_*` sweep is not the answer either — two §8.7 *panel sections* reach league verbs that no draft-function query will surface. (3) **FOUR structural breaches, found by this survey, against the working draft's assumption of one — and the fourth is MIS-TARGETED rather than blocked, which is the worse shape.** `draft_reset` (writes `leagues.status` + `settings`, and broadcasts on `league:<id>`); the **autopick toggle** (`set_team_autodraft`, 072 — keyed on `p_league_id`, mocks explicitly excluded from its lock, writes the real `league_members.is_autodraft`); **seat reassignment** (the league's invite/assignment surface, embedded in the panel); and **`draft_set_order`**, whose mock refusal is real, sits in `prosrc` at `087:2341`, and **never fires** (§1.3). The first is a body that could be narrowed; the next two are breaches *by construction*; **the fourth cannot be fixed at the RPC at all**, because the RPC is never handed the mock. None has a mock-scoped version worth building (§10 item 4). (4) **AN RPC-LEVEL AUDIT CANNOT SEE A MIS-TARGET, AND THAT IS THE FINDING THAT GENERALISES.** At the RPC layer `draft_set_order(mock_id, …)` is genuinely mock-local: the guard fires, the composite comes back clean, and the control would be **CLEARED** — the breach lives one layer up, in a resolver an RPC-level audit never executes. This is why **MS.1 drives every control through its ROUTE, with a mock in the room AND a real draft alive in the same league** (§5 MS.1 item 3): without the second draft a mis-targeted write has nothing to hit and looks clean. §1.3's original heading — *"The API layer needs almost nothing"* — was the premise that hid it, and is corrected in place rather than deleted so the failure mode stays legible. (5) **The exclusion mechanism follows the breach's shape, not a house style.** Three of the four are excluded by an in-body refusal that names its own reason; the fourth is excluded by a **service-layer block plus a UI exclusion**, and neither half alone is one — §12's server-authoritative rule means a hidden menu item is not an exclusion when the endpoint still answers. (6) **Isolation has three dimensions, and a row count is the weakest.** Rows (whole-row composites, because three enabled controls UPDATE `draft_picks` in place), **broadcast topics** (`draft_reset`'s `leagues` write reaches every member's `league:<id>` subscription), and the whole-schema sweep as the net for a table nobody enumerated. §4 rule 10 states the standard; MS.6 builds the one harness that applies it.

- **D219 — The D141 carve-out is the CLOCK, and mocks only.** (1) **The carve-out's width is Chris's ruling 1 read literally.** He named two things: *"make it as fast as possible"* and *"pause it if they need to do something"*. Pause already works. The clock is what pause-first makes expensive — you cannot try a shorter bid clock without pausing, resuming, and losing the beat you were trying to feel. (2) **The other five pause-gate consumers keep pause-first even in a mock, and that is deliberate.** `draft_undo`, `draft_reassign_pick`, `draft_move_player`, `draft_reverse_won_bid` and `draft_cancel_nomination` all edit *draft state the tick is concurrently reading*, and the pause is what takes the tick out of the race — the gate's value there is not only social. Chris's own words endorse the workflow (*"pause it if they need to do something"*). **This is a narrowing, stated as one**: widening it later is one predicate, and MS.1's measurements will say whether it is worth it. (3) **D141 and the ALIGN ruling are two events and must be cited as two.** D141 (PROGRESS §4) was enforced **auction-only**, with the snake divergence recorded and filed as **F57**. **Chris ruled ALIGN on 2026-08-18**, folded as spec §8.7 **v2.12.5** and built as migration **090 / L.C1.8**. A document that says "D141 made all clock edits pause-first on every draft type" has compressed a ruling out of the record. (4) **The implementation shape is fixed by a pin, not by taste.** `commish-auction-ops.test.ts:171` couples the gate's *consumer set* to the UI's `PAUSE_FIRST_RPC_SECTIONS`. So the carve-out changes the gate's **body** (`AND NOT p_draft.is_mock`), never which functions call it — one predicate, one place, and the coupling that keeps the UI mirror honest stays intact. (5) **"The new value governs the next clock" is inherited, not built.** Both `extend_current` arms are refusals and 090 **deleted** the snake extend machinery precisely so a future gate-weakening could not resurrect it (`090:291–303`). MS.3 must not undo that reasoning for mocks — the two false refusal messages get re-worded, the machinery stays gone.

- **D220 — `draft_reset` in a mock: the frame, the constraint, and the recommendation.** (1) **The decision is real, not a formality.** "Stays off" is defensible — *Delete practice & exit* already exists and a fresh mock is one click away. (2) **But delete-and-relaunch is rate-limited and lossy.** §22.5 caps mock creations at **5 per hour** per user (in-body, advisory-locked — D110(6)), so a launcher iterating on settings hits a wall; and a relaunch **re-seeds a `random` order** on the new mock's own id (D110(5)), so "run that same board again" is something relaunch cannot do. (3) **The shape is constrained by a measured fact, and it is not the obvious one.** A mock-safe reset **cannot** write `status = 'scheduled'`: `draft_start_internal` filters `is_mock = FALSE`, so nothing could restart it, and `draft-room.tsx:415` would render the real draft's lobby with a Start button that cannot fire (**F99**). The variant must land the mock **`live` at pick 1**. (4) **Recommendation: build it**, as a mock arm inside the one verb (never a second RPC), taking no `leagues` lock and performing no `leagues` write. **Chris can overturn this when he reviews this PR** — it is recorded here rather than decided in a Builder session because it is a product call about what a practice room is for. (5) **Either way, MS.4 owns the lane's single most important pin:** the whole `leagues` row byte-identical around a mock reset, plus the absence of a `league:<id>` broadcast. That is D110(1)'s original live proof, converted from a memory into a permanent assertion.

- **D221 — Surfacing without teaching: the room already has the seam.** (1) **Chris ruled "no" on explanatory copy and that is a build constraint (§4 rule 14).** No teaching label, no "these are the tools a commissioner has" line, no tutorial, no onboarding hint, no first-run tip. **MS.5's bar is FINDABLE, not EXPLAINED.** Ruling 2's discovery benefit is a *consequence* of the tools existing, not a feature to be built on top of them, and copy added to compensate for placement fails both halves. (2) **Recommendation: the launcher gets `Draft Options` itself, not a grown `Practice options`.** Chris's ruling 2 is that a mock is where someone learns what a commissioner has — the honest way to do that is the **same door with the same name**, not a parallel menu that happens to hold the same items. It also means **one** catalog and **one** panel: a second menu re-solving a solved surface is the LV.7 failure pattern. `Delete practice & exit` joins the destructive group beside Reset, and the single-item practice menu disappears (§10 item 3). (3) **No layout is prejudged, and that is measured rather than assumed.** `commandBarModel` already separates `draftOptions` from `practiceOptions` and already takes `isMockLauncher`; the change is which groups a pure ops function returns. DR2's nine tasks do not restructure the command bar (measured against `tasks-DR2-draft-room-v2.md`). **If a control needs a place the room does not have, that is a DR2 question and MS.5 stops and flags it** (§4 rule 15). (4) **The UI must not offer what the engine forbids** — D110(1)'s rule survives the lane that overturns its conclusion. The launcher's group list is derived from MS.1's cleared list through one predicate, not maintained by hand in two places, and **`autopick` and `seats` never render in a mock**. **`order` DOES render** (D222 — Chris ruled parity) **but only after MS.7 lands**: until the service targets the mock's own draft, that group is a one-click rewrite of the real order (§1.3). *An earlier revision of this item listed `order` as never-render; the parity ruling reversed it and a sequencing constraint replaced the exclusion.* (5) **`draft-command-bar.test.ts:151–153` pins `isCommish`'s source text by regex.** It moves to pin the new predicate; it is not deleted, and the docblock at `:21` that states the D110(1) seam is corrected with it.

- **D222 — PARITY is the lane's governing rule, and it reverses `order`'s remedy.** (1) **The ruling (Chris, 2026-08-20, after this document's first review):** *"so the point is the commish will need to set the draft order no matter, and it can always change last second. so there needs to be a way for the commish to set the order and then if real leagues can a mock league should as well so everyone can simulate their actual draft position or test different ones if they have a choice. for example, in my league last place gets to choose their draft position the next year."* (2) **The principle, stated so the lane can be tested against it: A MOCK GETS WHATEVER A REAL LEAGUE GETS.** Not *"whatever is safe to give it."* **A mock that cannot reproduce the user's actual draft position is not practice — it is a different draft.** §8.8 already said this about the engine (*"Same engine, literally… A mock that behaves differently from draft night is worse than no mock"*); D222 extends it to the commissioner surface, which is exactly what D103 had carved out. (3) **What it reverses, and it was the Architect's call rather than a Builder's slip.** The revision written after R468 excluded `draft_set_order` and put it on MS.5's must-not-render list. **Every piece of the diagnosis stands** — the mis-target, the probe, the never-firing guard. **The remedy answered the wrong question.** *"This control is unsafe"* is a reason to **fix** it, not to withhold it, and withholding it costs the user the one thing the motivating case needs. **Exclusion is now reserved for controls that write the real league BY CONSTRUCTION** (the autopick toggle, seat reassignment) **or whose product value is genuinely served another way** (`draft_reset` — MS.4's open decision, where "delete and relaunch" is a real substitute in a way that "don't set your order" is not). (4) **The fix is service-layer, and it is the shape §1.3 already identified.** `orderRequest` gains a `draft_id`; `patchDraftOrder` honours it; the mock room targets its own draft. **An RPC message change still cannot work** — the RPC is never handed the mock, so nothing it says is ever read. **MS.7** owns it. (5) **The severity note travels with the fix, and it is not about row counts.** A draft order is **negotiated property** — *"two people text messaging agree to swap picks."* Silently reversing one destroys an off-platform agreement **and posts a system line that makes it look deliberate**. That is why MS.7's pin is over the **real draft's stored order and its chat context**, not over a count. (6) **The control Chris named next does not exist, and it is NOT this lane's.** A **swap**: *"oh you like the 7th pick i like the 3rd pick. and then the commish needs to be able to swap them."* Filed as **F101** with the measurement that makes it a real gap. §6 says out-of-scope in as many words so it cannot creep in.

- **D223 — Choosing your slot at launch: the fast path, and why the seat picker cannot do this job.** (1) **The launcher already picks a SEAT, and that is a different question from a SLOT.** `mock-draft-launcher.tsx:138–156` renders a `Select` labelled *"Draft from seat"* (`aria-label="Seat to practice from"`) over `mockSeatOptions` (`mock-launcher-ops.ts:84–91`), defaulting to the launcher's own franchise (`defaultMockSeatId`, `:95–97`); the choice rides `config.mock.human_team_id`. **A seat says which franchise you play. A slot says when you pick.** (2) **And seat choice CANNOT be made to answer it — Chris's own correction is why:** *"there is no real draft order, most drafts will set the order right before."* `create_mock_draft` takes the real draft row's stored order as the candidate and resolves through the one implementation, **seeded by the MOCK's own id so an undrawn league gets a fresh deterministic shuffle per mock** (`089:935–957`, the comment says exactly this). So in the **normal** case — no order drawn yet — every launch reshuffles and the seat you chose lands wherever the shuffle puts it. **Picking a seat to get a slot works only in the minority case where an order already exists, which is backwards from how it will be used.** (3) **The task is therefore: choose your SLOT at launch — 1..N, default random — with the other franchises shuffled around you, written to the MOCK'S OWN order.** The real draft's order is neither read for this nor written by it, and is not required to exist. (4) **The fast path, deliberately — not a full order editor at launch.** `DraftOrderEditor` exists and works, and mounting it in the launch dialog would make someone drag twelve franchises into place to express *"put me third."* **The launch dialog answers one question with one control**; a launcher who wants a specific *full* order has the editor in the room once MS.7 lands. Recorded so the omission is not read as an oversight. (5) **Determinism is not optional and there is exactly one shuffle.** Reuse `draft_resolve_order_internal`'s existing seeding — the mock's own id (`089:935–957`) — rather than adding a second randomizer. Two implementations of "randomize an order" is the failure §4.7 exists to prevent, and a mock's replayability depends on it. **A slot choice is a constraint ON that shuffle, not a replacement for it.**

(2) **The removal is a DATA migration, and skipping that half breaks every league that stored the key** — `league-settings.ts:213` is `z.strictObject` and `mergeSettings` (`:643–663`) parses the stored blob on **every read**, so a leftover `settings.draft.auction_min_bid` is a hard parse failure, not a harmless extra. - **D199 — The uncontestable instant award.** (1) **The predicate is ONE query, never a loop** — a `CROSS JOIN LATERAL draft_team_budget` over active franchises excluding the nominator, the shape `draft_auction_solvent` (`084:386`) and `draft_end` (`087:1004`) already use, inside the held draft-row lock — and **the increment is a NAMED constant `1` compared as `high_bid + increment`**, per §8.6.9, because writing it as `> high_bid` would be a latent bug with no symptom while the increment happens to be $1. (2) **A complete roster needs no clause of its own** — `draft_team_budget` forces `max_bid = 0` at `open_slots <= 0` (`084:348–350`) and `high_bid + 1 ≥ 1 > 0`; an explicit `open_slots >= 1` term is documentation and must not be what correctness rests on. (4) **The 3 seconds is the room's beat, and the wire mechanism is decided so nobody improvises one:** a tick-scheduled 3s cannot be 3s (the ≤5s sweep would land it in 3–8s, differently each time), so the server awards immediately and the uncontestable path performs **two UPDATEs inside the one transaction** — the nomination open with an additive `"uncontested": true` on `current_nomination`, then the award-and-advance. Both fire 088's `drafts` broadcast (`current_nomination` is in D134's payload), so every client sees announcement-then-award in one commit: **no new column, no new event, no new topic.** The additive key is the only spec-shape change (§12.3) and rides the migration banner as an erratum. (5) **Deliberately not done:** no scheduled server action, no `pg_net`, no second cron — and D200 does not need one either.

- **D200 — Reactive CPU bidding: change what PROVOKES a bot, not how often the sweep runs.** (1) A CPU response runs **in the transaction that provoked it** (a human's bid, another CPU's raise, the nomination that opened the market; the award already advances the rotation, so a CPU's turn to nominate can be served in that transaction too). The sweep keeps **expiring clocks when nobody acts** — the only job that genuinely needs a timer — and **`cron.schedule('draft-tick','5 seconds')` at `068:1265` is not touched**, because it sweeps every live draft in the system (§22.3). ARM 2.6(a)/(b)/(c1) stay as the no-actor safety net. (2) ARM 2.6(c2)'s candidate query + raise (`089:2313–2345`) is extracted to `draft_mock_cpu_respond_internal`, verbatim first and extended second, so the think-time path and the reactive path are ONE implementation. (3) **Bounded LOUDLY:** the responder recurses through `draft_place_bid_internal`, so a hard cap of `2 × team_count` raises per provoking transaction with a `RAISE EXCEPTION` — never a silent `EXIT` — because a ladder that long means the value model or the candidate query is wrong and a silent stop would hide it. (4) **Jump-bids are a seeded choice between the jump and the nibble, never above `LEAST(value, max_bid)`**, reusing the D93 24-bit PRNG already inside `draft_mock_cpu_bid_value` (`089:329–360`); a second PRNG is a review finding, and determinism is not optional (the sim, the property test and every golden depend on a mock replaying identically). Both textures are required by the ruling. (5) **The honest arithmetic, stated so the task can be judged:** reactive responses collapse the mock's cost to `nominations × (bid window + ≤ one sweep interval)` ⇒ ≈ **67 min at the shipped 20s clock** (a ~3.5× improvement on F76's 3.5–4 h) and ≈ **42 min at 10s**. **So AP.3 alone does NOT meet Chris's 45-minute bar; AP.3 + AP.4 do** — filed as **F85** rather than discovered at the gate. Both figures are estimates, and §4 rule 10 of tasks-AP requires them to be replaced by a measured wall-clock.
