- **D163 — ROSTER CONSTRUCTION IS NOT ENFORCED FROM THE DRAFT (Chris, ruled in session 2026-08-18; recorded in the L.C1.5 batch-5 fix cycle, R374).** Recorded because **nothing in `docs/specs/` carried it**: §3 Open said "None currently", there was no §4 entry, and `grep` for "roster construction" / "positional legality" across `docs/` returned nothing. **The ruling, in Chris's framing:** *"A user may draft 16 WRs — that is their problem to solve in free agency. The draft never consults positional legality: capacity is a pure count, and positional slots are a weekly lineup concern. It can be a legitimate strategy to draft only RB/WR and pick up a QB, K, DST and TE once the season starts. **But whenever AUTODRAFT is doing the picking or nominating**, it should first attempt to fill the remaining **holes** with the final picks rather than add positional depth — 'this roster's only open slot is a Kicker, so draft a kicker with the final pick.' A user can do whatever they want; autodraft should not leave them without a QB/K/DST."* **(1) THIS CONFIRMS SHIPPED BEHAVIOR — it is recorded with the evidence rather than as a new requirement, and every clause was verified before it was written down.** **Capacity is a pure count**: 084's `draft_team_budget` derives `open_slots = total_rounds − non-undone picks` (084:67) with no positional term anywhere in the family, and the v2.8.11 manual-pick rule ("slot validation at pick time = capacity only") is what the priced Manual Edit paths and `draft_nominate` both enforce (D129(1): "humans may buy a 3rd QB"). **The autodraft half is the forced arm**: the auction inherits the snake resolver unchanged at `086:648` — `v_forced := v_remaining <= v_unfilled` — so while a roster has more picks left than holes the chain adds the best available player, and once picks-remaining equals holes it fills the holes. **(2) D129(2)'s OBLIGATION IS THEREFORE DISCHARGED, AND IT WAS DISCHARGED IN L.C1.4 — NOT LEFT OPEN.** D129(2) closed with "(no rounds in auction; deferral holds until open slots force them — Builder finalizes the documented rule, pins the boundary)". The rule was finalized in the **C32 erratum (spec v2.12.1)** — §8.4's K/D-ST deferral maps to its FORCED-only arm because an auction has no rounds for the "final 3 rounds" escape to refer to — and **the boundary is pinned one unit either side in 035 §G**: "ONE UNIT SHORT of FORCED (remaining 2 vs unfilled 1): the auction seat still declines the kicker and takes an RB" (035:955) and "FORCED (remaining 1 = unfilled 1, a K seat among them): the deferral lifts and the kicker is resolved" (035:964), against a SNAKE control in the identical state (035:945). The parenthetical in D129(2) is marked discharged in place. **(3) THE C33 ERRATUM'S *FIX* STANDS BUT ITS *REASONING* DOES NOT, and the spec is corrected (v2.12.3).** C33 argued that §8.6.7(e) "can select a player the NOMINATOR cannot roster" and that (b) would then award an **illegal** pick. Under this ruling that is not a legality problem at all: capacity is a count, and §8.6.7(c)'s rotation-skip already guarantees the nominator has an open slot, so ANY player is rosterable by them. The system nomination still runs the nominator's own §8.4 chain — **no behavior changes** — but the reason is now **"so an absent manager gets a player their own board would have picked"**, which is a quality-of-outcome argument, not **"so the award is legal"**. A wrong reason attached to a right fix is how the next session justifies the wrong change. **(4) WHAT IS NOT RULED, and is deliberately left alone:** whether the autodraft hole-filling should look further ahead than the forced arm does (e.g. a soft preference for holes before the boundary), and anything about weekly lineup legality, which is M4's. No spec section moves for either.
- **D164 — M3 batch-5 fix-cycle mechanics (L.C1.5, PR #159; R367–R374).** **Number note (R, D and F checked TOGETHER per D161, across every open branch):** `main` @ 4930bd8 is at **R366 / D161 / F67**; the only other open PR is #152 (docs), which claims R≤311 / D≤144 / F≤59 — above nothing. This branch already holds **D162**, so the ruling takes **D163** and these mechanics **D164**, and the two new ledger rows take **F68** and **F69**. **(1) A PRE-WRITE CHECK AND A POST-WRITE CHECK ARE NOT THE SAME CHECK, AND CALLING BOTH "the E28 algebra" IS WHAT HID THE BUG.** R367: the priced Manual Edit paths asked `price <= max_bid` **before** the write. That question is about the world in which the pick has NOT landed. The stuck clock is created **by** the pick landing — the receiving team's `open_slots` and `remaining` both fall, its `max_bid` falls with them, and if it is the live high bidder its own standing bid becomes unaffordable. `draft_auction_solvent` cannot see it either, because a bid holds no money (D131(2)) so no derivation reads it: the team passes `remaining >= open_slots × min_bid` and the award is still refused forever. **Rule this cycle adopts: when a guard's subject is changed by the write it guards, the guard must be re-asked after the write.** The two questions now have two implementations at three call sites and ONE helper behind them. **(2) A SECTION THAT CANNOT FAIL FOR THE CASE IT CLAIMS TO COVER IS THE DEFECT, NOT THE MISSING PIN.** 036 §I is titled "the priced Manual Edit Mode paths" and its fixture (LG) is paused **with no live nomination**, so no priced-path pin could ever run against a high bidder. This is the same shape as R362 (an arm nothing swept) and R329 (a pin that could not detect its own mutation). **Rule: when a section's title names a surface, its fixture must be able to reach every state that surface has** — and "is there a state this fixture cannot be in?" is now a question to ask of a fixture before writing pins against it. §I(b) adds the world (LH) rather than editing LG, so §I's own boundary story stays readable. **(3) TWO MORE COVERAGE SENTENCES OUTRAN THEIR PINS — SEVEN TASKS RUNNING.** R369: the banner said §B swept member/commissioner/outsider/anon × INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (it swept member × 4 and commissioner × 2) and that "§H sweeps all eleven" mocks (§H is the reverse-won-bid section; §M swept four). R371: the banner said §G's decoy was "built through the REAL verbs … renominate the same player at the same amount" when §G's own comments say the renomination is the TICK's and the collision is forged privileged. **In all three the substance held** — the reviewer probed outsider/anon directly, and rebuilt the D162 collision through real verbs only (three rows at seq 1, two tying; pre-D162 lookup returns 2, shipped lookup returns 1). **Disposition: EXTEND THE PINS where the claim is the coverage you would want (R369, both halves), CORRECT THE PROSE where the claim was about provenance (R371).** A banner sentence being accidentally true is not a defence. **(4) A HAND-OFF IN A SESSION-LOG CELL IS NOT A HAND-OFF (R51, again — R372).** `voided_at`'s broadcast/payload treatment was deferred to L.C1.6 in a migration comment and a free-text session-log cell, with no ledger row and no amendment to `tasks-M3-auction.md`'s L.C1.6 banner (a file this PR never touched, written before D162 existed). It is now **F69** plus a read-list line. **(5) A DIVERGENCE YOU CHOOSE TO KEEP MUST BE PINNED AND SAID (R373).** `draft_set_order` refuses a pre-start order edit on an auction and accepts one on snake. **Disposition: PIN, do not align** — aligning would be a behavior change to a shipped verb inside a fix cycle, the auction's message points at a real editor (League settings / `nomination_order_mode`, §7.3.8) so it is a UX asymmetry rather than a hole, and which way it should align is the same standing product question F57 already carries. Pinned at 036 §K (auction half) against 023:1248 (snake half). **(6) "RED ON MAIN TOO" IS ANCHORED TO A COMMIT, AND THE MERGE TARGET IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS (R370).** F56's extension recorded the E2E failure against `main` @ 5a1bf1c; on the merge target 4930bd8 the failure set is **larger and different in kind** — `draft-live.spec.ts:162`'s `getByText('Draft lobby')` reproduces **in isolation on a clean stack** and is **DR.1 test debt**, not F56: DR.1 moved the room out of the app shell, so `PageHeader` writes a store `AppHeader` reads and `AppHeader` is shell chrome (the comment at `draft-lobby.tsx:188` on `main` says so outright). Filed as **F68**, owned by the DR lane, deliberately not fixed here. **(7) RECORDED COUNTS RE-RUN, AGAIN (D161(5) applied without being asked).** 036 grew 150 → 181, so all five original probes were re-run against the enlarged file; every original RED SET reproduced exactly (3 / 2 / 10 / 2 / 1), which is the evidence that the first record was honest. Probe 6 is R367's own: **10 of 181** — and its tenth RED is **§A's new no-drift source pin**, added in this cycle because "one helper so the three cannot drift apart" was otherwise unpinned prose, which is the same species of claim R369/R371 were filed for. The D141 gate helper had such a pin from the start; E28 arm 3 did not, and R367 is what the absence buys.
- **D161 — M3 batch-4 fix-cycle mechanics (L.C1.4, PR #158; R362–R366).** **Number note (R312 first-filed-keeps, the FOURTH time this rule has been needed — and the fourth instance was created by this very entry):** this cycle renumbered R339–R343 → **R362–R366** against the open branches, wrote the rule down, **and then filed its own ledger row as `F66` without applying it** — `F66` was already taken by the held DR.1 PR #157 (the unmatched `/app/*` root-404 row). Corrected to **F67** by the orchestrator at review time. The lesson is narrower and more useful than "check the open branches": **check every counter, not the one that just bit you.** R and D were checked here; F was not, because the collision that prompted the check had been an R collision. Until #157 lands, `git show <open-branch>:docs/specs/PROGRESS-leagues.md` must be grepped for **R, D and F together** before any of the three is assigned.  D157–D158 are #156's, D159 belongs to the OPEN Chris-held DR.1 PR #157, D160 is this PR's original entry — so the fix cycle takes **D161**. The reviewer's own R-numbers collided the same way (R339–R343 against #157's R339–R361) and renumbered to R362–R366. **(1) A SECOND DOOR TO THE SAME WRITER IS STILL THE SAME DEFECT, AND "NO ARM CLAIMS IT" IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A READING.** 086 closed ARM 2's auction door with a probe it ran, then asserted in three places that a live auction mock is claimed by no arm — without running that one. ARM 2.5 claimed it and snake-autopicked it (R362). The general rule this cycle adopts: **a sentence of the form "X is claimed/handled by no Y" must name the observation that establishes it, and the observation must sweep every Y, not the two the task was thinking about.** The pin that makes it stick is not the zero — it is the pin BEFORE the zero asserting the fixture was genuinely claimable, and the pin BESIDE it asserting nothing merely failed (`mock_cpu_failures = '[]'`); a zero with neither is the CLAUDE.md "nothing happened means it worked" trap wearing a test's clothes. **(2) A COMMENT THAT JUSTIFIES A `LIMIT 1` IS A CLAIM, AND D143 ALREADY REFUTED THIS ONE.** "Unique by construction" was written about a triple that a ruled-but-unbuilt verb makes non-unique (`draft_cancel_nomination` does not consume the sequence number). The lookup was correct only by an ordering, and the tiebreak behind that ordering is `gen_random_uuid()`. **Rule: when the discriminator is a column you already have, put it in the WHERE — do not let an ORDER BY carry a correctness argument.** `player_id` is now in the WHERE and 035 §K pins the disambiguation with a decoy the ordering deterministically prefers. **(3) D143'S "OPEN BIDS ARE VOIDED" HAS NO SCHEMA REPRESENTATION, and 086 is its first consumer.** `draft_bids` is append-only with no UPDATE/DELETE policy for anyone (083, D131(2)), so a voided nomination's rows stay and merge under one sequence number for every reader keyed on `nomination_seq` alone. 086's award survives it; the room's bid feed, L.C1.6's broadcast and the recap have not met it yet. Routed into **L.C1.5's read-list in tasks-M3 §6** with the three options and the instruction to record the decision or raise a spec question — not left as a comment for someone to find. **(4) A REFUSED AWARD HAS NO REMEDY UNTIL L.C1.5, and pause is not one.** Driven, not reasoned: pause → resume leaves the nomination standing and the next tick reproduces the identical refusal (D160(8), corrected). **Rule: "Z can be recovered by W" is the same species of claim as (1) — drive W before recording it.** **(5) RECORDED COUNTS MUST BE RE-RUN WHEN THE FILE THEY COUNT CHANGES.** Adding 11 pins made "35 of 105" unreproducible, so all three original probes were re-run (D160(10)); the 1–105 sets reproduced exactly, which is the evidence that the original record was honest. **(6) A PIN THAT READS A WHOLE-TICK ARRAY REPORTS A NEIGHBOUR'S FAILURE AS ITS OWN.** §K's first draft asserted `auction_failures = '[]'` and went red under probes that break other worlds; scoped by `draft_id`, it is deterministic. The existing pins 79/87 read `auction_failures->0` and have the same shape — left alone (no drive-by) and filed as **F67**, with the mechanism named: `now()` is transaction-stable inside a pgTAP file, so every forced `now() - interval '1 second'` deadline ties and ARM 2.6's `ORDER BY current_deadline` breaks the tie arbitrarily.


**2026-08-14/15/16 — Architect (the M3 breakdown, PR #150 — merged 2026-08-16; transcribed verbatim from tasks-M3-auction.md §3 per the tasks-M2 D86–D101 precedent; D139–D143 fold Chris's 2026-08-15/16 auction-UI rulings, spec v2.10/v2.10.1):**
- **D126 — Auction state lives on the drafts row; phase is `current_nomination`'s NULLity.** No new state columns: `current_nomination` NULL ⇒ **nominating** (`on_clock_team_id` = the nominator per `nomination_order` rotation, `current_deadline` = nomination clock); non-NULL ⇒ **bidding** (`current_nomination = { player_id, high_bid, high_bidder_team_id }` per 065:121's printed shape, `current_deadline` = bid clock). `current_pick_number` doubles as the 1-based **nomination sequence** (§12.4's "sequence # (auction)"); `draft_picks.round` is NULL for auction rows; `current_round` tracks the rotation lap (display only). `total_rounds` keeps its D91 meaning (draftable slots = starters + bench) — it is the auction's per-team roster capacity, not a rounds count.
- **D127 — Budgets are always DERIVED, never stored counters.** `remaining_budget(team) = auction_budget + adjustment(team) − Σ price(non-undone picks)`; `open_slots(team) = total_rounds − count(non-undone picks)`; `max_bid(team) = remaining − (open_slots − 1) × min_bid` (§8.6.1). One SQL derivation fn family (§5), used by every validator — a stored counter could drift from truth; a derivation cannot. Commissioner budget edits need storage: **additive column `drafts.budget_adjustments JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`** (team_id → integer delta; spec-absent schema recorded here + erratum, the D102 precedent) — validated per E28 at edit time, room-visible (D134), history via the D97 system chat post until M6's audit rows. *Recorded nuance:* the settings-layer floor (league-settings.ts:541) uses roster_size incl. IR — deliberately conservative vs the engine's D91 open-slots; both stand.
- **D128 — Bid-clock semantics: a fixed window with an anti-snipe floor (the E6-consistent reading).** The bid clock starts at `auction_bid_seconds` when bidding opens (at nomination) and is **not** reset by bids; a bid landing with remaining < `auction_anti_snipe_seconds` resets remaining **to** `auction_anti_snipe_seconds` (§7.3.8's own words: "resets clock **to it**"; Appendix C L.C1: "reset bid clock to auction_anti_snipe_seconds"; E6: 3s left, threshold 10 → clock reads 10s). `auction_anti_snipe_seconds = 0` disables extension (pure fixed window). §8.6.3's looser "each bid resets the bid clock per anti-snipe" is read as "each bid applies the anti-snipe rule". **C34 flags this for Chris's read before build** — pacing is product feel; the alternative (Sleeper-style reset-to-full-per-bid) contradicts E6 as printed and would need a spec change. **RULED 2026-08-15 (Chris, in-session): CONFIRMED** — his own scenario language: 30s total clock; bids above the threshold neither reset nor pause it — the countdown continues uninterrupted (Chris's explicit clarification); a higher bid landing inside the final 10 seconds resets the clock to 10 seconds (his "bid with 3 seconds left → clock resets to 10"), repeatable. D128 as written is the LAW reading; no spec change.
- **D129 — Nomination discipline.** (1) Human nomination validates: nominator's turn, player undrafted, opening bid ≥ `auction_min_bid` AND ≤ nominator's max bid (§8.6.7(a)), **capacity-only fit** (open_slots ≥ 1 — the v2.8.11 manual-pick rule extended: need-fit is a system-path rule, humans may buy a 3rd QB). Rotation-skip (§8.6.7(c)) guarantees the nominator has an open slot, so the §8.6.7(b) nominator-award is always legal. (2) **System nomination (timeout) = the M2 autopick resolution chain run for the on-clock team** (queue → primary board → Big Board → ADP with need-fit; 068's `draft_autopick_resolve`) at an opening bid of `min_bid` ($0 legal when `min_bid = 0` — C38; R305) — this satisfies §8.6.7(e)'s "fits *some* team's open slot" (it fits the nominator's) and makes (b) safe; one implementation, snake and auction (C33 records the reading). K/D-ST deferral maps to the forced-only arm (no rounds in auction; deferral holds until open slots force them — ~~Builder finalizes the documented rule, pins the boundary~~ **DISCHARGED in L.C1.4, migration 086 — marked 2026-08-18 (R374/D163(2)), not left open:** the rule is finalized in the **C32 erratum, spec v2.12.1** (§8.4's deferral maps to its FORCED-only arm because an auction has no rounds), and the boundary is pinned ONE UNIT EITHER SIDE in **035 §G** — 035:955 "ONE UNIT SHORT of FORCED (remaining 2 vs unfilled 1) … declines the kicker" and 035:964 "FORCED (remaining 1 = unfilled 1) … the deferral lifts" — against a snake control in the identical state at 035:945. The forced arm itself is `086:648`, `v_forced := v_remaining <= v_unfilled`). (3) The **D102 grace contract carries to the nomination clock**: autodraft/no-user/FRESH seats system-nominate AT deadline; a STALE seat's nomination is held to deadline + grace, manual nomination allowed during the hold. (4) **No auto-bidding for absent seats** (§8.6.5/OQ 10) — grace applies to nominations only; you cannot be timed *into* a bid.
- **D130 — Award path.** Bid-clock expiry under the draft-row lock: winner = `current_nomination.high_bidder_team_id` (or the nominator at the opening bid when no raises — §8.6.7(b)/E26); write `draft_picks` (pick_number = nomination seq, round NULL, `price`, `made_via`/`is_auto` per actor: system-nominated no-raise awards are `is_auto = TRUE, made_via = 'autopick'`); clear `current_nomination`; advance rotation to the next team with open_slots ≥ 1 (E27 skip); next nomination deadline. **Completion = no team has open slots** → the 072 completion txn extended to write `acquisition_cost = price` (D111(3)); "budgets exhausted" (§8.6.6) is unreachable — solvency guarantees every open slot is affordable at min_bid, pinned as a property.
- **D131 — Auction reversals.** (1) **`draft_reverse_won_bid`** (§8.7's "undo a won bid"): targeted soft-undo of a specific auction pick (`is_undone = TRUE`) — player to pool, budget restored by derivation (free), the team re-enters the rotation if it was complete; live/paused drafts only (post-completion reversal is F44's M6 class). (2) **Undo/cascade (E29):** when a nomination has live bids, `draft_undo` FIRST voids the nomination (clear `current_nomination`; `draft_bids` rows stand as append-only history — "bids returned" costs nothing because **bids never hold budget, only won picks do**), then reverts picks; on_clock rewinds to the target nomination's nominator with a fresh nomination clock. (3) Undo is provably solvency-preserving (remaining' = remaining + price ≥ (open+1) × min_bid whenever price ≥ min_bid — pinned as a property). (4) **E28 extends to the live nomination:** a budget edit that would make the CURRENT high bid insolvent for its bidder is refused (friendly: void the nomination or reverse won bids first) — otherwise the close could award an unaffordable player.
- **D132 — CPU bidders: tick-driven, value-based, same validators (one implementation, two consumers).** Mock auction CPUs nominate via D129(2) (their own resolve chain) at humanized think-time (the D93 PRNG pattern) and **bid** via a seeded value model: dollar value = f(ADP rank, budget scale, roster needs) × (1 + seeded noise), deterministic per (draft_id, nomination_seq, team_id, pass) — a CPU raises only while `high_bid + 1 ≤ min(its value, its max_bid)`, at most one raise per tick pass per nomination (bids land ~5s apart — humanized pacing for free), with the near-buzzer tail falling out of the think-fraction distribution (anti-snipe becomes visible, §8.8). E62 by construction: CPUs pass the same server-side max-bid/solvency validator as humans. The sim's auction personas (L.C4.1) drive the same decision spine through real RPCs (D100).
- **D133 — Client Broadcast STAYS CLOSED (the D109(5) decision, made).** M3 adds no `extension = 'broadcast'` INSERT policy: the "bid-button pulse" IS the authoritative `draft_bids` INSERT broadcast (sub-second, already fan-out-cheap), and v1 auction needs no typing indicators. A member who could client-broadcast could forge a server-shaped bid event to the room — the same spoof D109(5) refused. Recorded as deliberate; revisit only with a named consumer + a forgery-safe event namespace (v1.1 at earliest).
- **D134 — Payload extensions (the §9.2 "columns clients render" rule, extended additively).** `draft_broadcast_payload` += `current_nomination` + `budget_adjustments` (neither is blind: the high bid is the room's centerpiece and §8.7 transparency wants budget edits visible); `draft_pick_broadcast_payload` += `price` (the board renders spend; 070's exclusion note is superseded by an auction that renders it — banner updated in place… NO: the exclusion note's migration is released — the NEW payload fn versions in 088 carry the updated banner, D137). New **`draft_bid_broadcast_payload`** (nomination_seq, player_id, team_id, amount, created_at — never `action_id`) + INSERT trigger on `draft_bids`, event name `'draft_bids'` — the exact name the M2 client's inert-default pin already proves safe (use-draft-ops.test.ts:351). Old clients strip additive keys (non-strict Zod, §2) and ignore the new event: no forced-upgrade window.
- **D135 — Room composition: one shell + an auction center stage; the fixture room dies.** The landed room (`snake-draft-room.tsx`) is renamed to §16.2's canonical **`draft-room.tsx`** (D117(8)'s sanctioned consolidation; git mv, no fork) and branches at the :389 fork point: `auction` renders **`auction-block.tsx`** (nomination stage, bid input + max-bid, per-team budgets rail, nomination/bid clocks, anti-snipe indicator — §16.2's printed component) in place of the snake board's on-clock surfaces; board grid becomes results-by-team with prices. Chat, presence, pool, queue, My Lists, commish panel, recap, lobby compose unchanged. **`auction-draft-room.tsx` is DELETED after harvest** (unmounted since M2, §2) and **`mock-draft.ts` goes away entirely** per its own banner — the repo's standing lint warning (auction-draft-room.tsx:107) retires with it.
- **D136 — No route-layer bid limiter in M3.** §22.1's "≤ 5 bids/s/draft" is a load-model assumption; §22.5's "bids 5/s" route limit is F41's, routed to M7 with the rest of the rate-limit family. The draft-row lock is the serializer (§8.1); M3 proves correctness-under-burst (storm E2E + chaos persona), M7 proves latency/quota at k6 scale. The instant "outbid" loser path must be friendly-P0001, never a 429.
- **D137 — Amendment vehicle: CREATE OR REPLACE in NEW migrations, authored against the chain HEAD.** M2's in-place amendment convention (F12/F51) was an intra-milestone convenience on unreleased files; 065–082 are merged, gate-pinned, and awaiting the F12 prod push. M3 therefore replaces `draft_start`/`draft_make_pick`/`draft_tick`/the 072 completion writer via `CREATE OR REPLACE` in 083+ migrations, each authored against the CURRENT file text of the function's last definition (the CLAUDE.md migration-discipline lesson — read the newest migration that defines the function), with the source migration named in the banner. pgTAP files 020/025 are tests, not migrations — their refusal assertions are edited in place in the same PRs.
- **D138 — Mock auctions: the 071 refusal lifts in the same milestone as the engine, and every M2 mock rule carries.** Launcher-only control surface (D110(1)) — pause/resume/delete by `config.mock.launched_by`, every other §8.7 control (incl. the new auction verbs) refuses mocks; caps + advisory-lock serializer + 72h expiry + E59/E60 unchanged; the zero-side-effect diff pin is re-run with `draft_bids` added to the allowed-tables set; the launcher is the only legal human nominator/bidder (the D103(2) rule extended to bids). Mock CPU auctions are the E62 property surface.
- **D139 — Do-Not-Draft home: `draft_dnd_marks`, per-user per-DRAFT, own-rows client-writable (the `draft_queues` precedent), never broadcast.** Spec §12.24 (v2.10). Per-draft chosen over per-league deliberately: a mock's marks never pollute the real draft's, and the drafts row exists from scheduling so pre-draft prep works; marks survive a `draft_reset` (they are prep, not draft state — the R302 clear list deliberately excludes them). Autopick interaction **RULED (C42/OQ 20, 2026-08-16): DISPLAY-ONLY, PERIOD — the skip arm was offered and explicitly declined** (never re-propose it as an oversight). The engine NEVER reads `draft_dnd_marks`: no RPC, trigger, or worker joins against it; the 068 resolve chain is untouched forever, not "until ruled". The table's whole job is persisting the UI label across sessions/devices — schema stands as printed (§12.24), simplified only in that no engine coupling will ever be added.
- **D140 — "Targets" rename = UI copy + component-label scope ONLY (ruled).** Schema (`draft_queues`), routes, RPCs, hooks, service names all unchanged — renaming shipped internals would churn every M2 pin for zero product value. The sweep covers every user-facing string: the room tab, Queue/Queued buttons (pool + best-available), load-into-queue actions and toasts, aria-labels, empty states, and the autopick explainer copy ("Timeouts draft from the top of your Targets first"). Component FILE names stay (`my-queue.tsx` — §16.2 note records the label); a rename-the-file pass is gratuitous churn, declined.
- **D141 — Pause-first commissioner gating (ruled) is enforced IN-BODY, auction-only; snake keeps its shipped posture.** The gated set is exactly what Chris named: undo (single + cascade), Manual Edit Mode's two paths (reverse-won-bid, priced reassign/move), current-nomination edits, and all timer edits — each refuses on a RUNNING auction with a friendly "pause the draft first" P0001 (UI disables with the same copy; RLS-grade truth lives in the RPC). NOT gated (not named in the ruling): pause/resume itself, budget adjust, nomination-order edit, force-nominate, reset. **Snake divergence recorded honestly** rather than silently changing shipped M2 behavior: snake controls stay live-available as landed; whether snake aligns is a standing product follow-up — **filed as ledger row F57 at merge** (with D126–D143), owner Chris, no M3 lane blocked.
- **D142 — Manual Edit Mode is the UX articulation of two existing engine paths, not a new engine surface.** Enter mode (paused, commish) → click any drafted cell → modal with exactly two choices: "Reset pick" → `draft_reverse_won_bid` (refund by derivation); "Move player to a different team" → `draft_reassign_pick`/`draft_move_player` with the commissioner **re-entering the cost to confirm** (the re-entered amount IS the priced validation input — receiving team checked vs max-bid, E28-class). Replaces the spec's drag articulation for auction (v2.10 §8.7). System posts unchanged (D97).
- **D143 — Edit current nomination = cancel-and-renominate.** New small RPC `draft_cancel_nomination(p_draft_id)` (commish, paused auction, bidding phase): voids the live nomination — `current_nomination` cleared, open bids stand as void history (the D131(2) mechanics minus the cascade), **the sequence number is NOT consumed** — and on resume the same nominator's nomination clock restarts. No "swap the player in place" arm: editing a nomination under live bids re-prices other people's bids; cancel-and-renominate is the only honest shape (v2.10 §8.7 prints it).

**2026-08-05 — Builder (identity ruling — not a milestone task):**
- **D115** Identity-ruling build mechanics (Chris's ruling 2026-08-05; spec v2.9; migration 075). (1) **No schema change, on purpose.** The earlier attempt (PR #96) renamed `profiles.display_name` → `full_name`; three reviewers rejected it, and the deploy-order argument is the one that generalizes: production runs the current schema, so any rename breaks the site in one merge order or the other. Storing nothing needs no DDL — the column is NULLABLE with no default, so the old app reads NULL and falls back to `@username` (the post-ruling render anyway) and the new app never reads it. Dropping the column is a separate, later change once no deployed code references it. (2) **The stored names are cleared, not just stopped.** Accounts created before the ruling already carry OAuth real names, and `profiles` is world-readable, so stopping the write alone would leave the leak alive for exactly the users who hit it. `UPDATE profiles SET display_name = NULL` is DML, idempotent, and invisible to both app versions. (3) **The function body is production's, and the 049/050/051 guards are NOT re-imported.** The replacement is `pg_get_functiondef`'s live output minus the name write. That live body has no `*-ai` namespace rejection, no reserved-placeholder shape check, no R31 fallback: 049/050/051 were never applied to production (its ledger is 001-036, 073, 074), and 073's search_path hotfix was rebuilt from a pre-049 body, so a fresh local reset loses them too. Restoring them is a real bug worth its own PR — smuggling a handle-namespace behaviour change into a privacy fix is how the 051 regression happened in the first place. **Flagged for a follow-up, deliberately not fixed here.** (4) **The other five readers are left alone.** `notify_list_followers` / `create_league` / `seat_league_member_internal` / `get_join_preview` / `draft_actor_name` each read the column through `COALESCE(..., username)`. With it permanently NULL they resolve to the handle with no edit — and `CREATE OR REPLACE`-ing league functions that do not exist in production would plant orphans there. The corollary: `get_join_preview` and `draft_actor_name` render the BARE handle, not `@handle`; PR #96's cosmetic `'@' ||` prefix on those two is dropped along with its migration, and pgTAP 016/023/026 are back to `origin/main`'s strings. (5) **Personas keep their name, under their existing column.** The privacy rationale does not apply to a fictional analyst with no human behind it, and the "(AI)" suffix is a transparency device (spec-ai-expert-personas §4.6). Rendering `@bathew-merry-ai` instead of "Bathew Merry (AI)" would be an unrelated product regression. PR #96's `ai_personas.display_name` → `persona_name` rename is DROPPED: no schema churn in this PR. `expert_profiles.display_name` is likewise left alone — dead legacy, no reader anywhere in the app. (6) **Two-line identities collapse to one.** Surfaces that rendered "name" over "@handle" (account menu, profile header, follower rows, command palette) now render the handle once — keeping both lines would print the same string twice. `PublicListCard` and the explore feed gained an OPTIONAL `name`, set only for personas, rather than forking a second card component. (PR #96's render sweep, kept — reviewers passed it.) (7) **Account settings has no name field at all**, so there is no "private" copy to be wrong about. PR #96 shipped helper text promising privacy the database did not provide; the fix is not better copy, it is having nothing to describe. (9) **Held-lock proof form (§4.6):** the stack vitest asserts `min(pick RTTs) < 50ms` — the client RTT upper-bounds the in-RPC lock window, a systematically held lock inflates EVERY sample, and a one-off load spike cannot flake the suite; timing via `process.hrtime.bigint()` (monotonic, outside the D3/D17 wall-clock ban — harness measurement, not league logic).

**2026-07-19 — Builder (L.A0.3):**
- **D26** Synthetic-tier design points. (1) **PRNG streams are keyed by (seed, playerId) only — never scenario id** (FNV-1a + mulberry32, `synthetic/prng.ts`): same-seed scenarios share stat lines, which is what makes the `provider_outage` back-fill proof an *equality against a same-seed `happy_path` world* instead of a self-referential recomputation. (2) **Skeleton/values split:** the timing/event skeleton (slate, kickoffs, event instants, player pool, inactives) is a fixed function of scenario id; only stat values draw from the seed — asserted by the "different seed → different lines, same skeleton" transcript test. (3) Stat lines are `floor(finalLine × progress)` — in-game deltas monotone by construction, outage recovery is cumulative back-fill for free (§23.2). (4) The synthetic tier supplies **real `kickoffAt` timestamps** (plus `gameDate` derived from them) — it's the tier that *can* (§23.6); flex/postponement reveal their new kickoff only from `announceAt`. Prod re-verified before building, per the task's stop condition: all 40 public tables (the full 001–036 surface — 36 is the count of applied migrations, not of tables; corrected per R2) grant all 8 table privileges (`arwdDxtm`, incl. PG17's MAINTAIN; "7" was a miscount, per R2) to the three API roles, and the default ACLs are exactly as D18 recorded. **ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES chosen over per-table grants** because production *is* a default-ACL model: with per-table grants only, any future migration that omitted a grant (by oversight or on purpose) would silently diverge from prod, which auto-grants regardless; the versioned default ACLs replay to prod's exact model in every environment — fresh local reset, and a future re-provisioned hosted project on the new no-auto-grant default. **[Corrected 2026-07-19 per R1 — the original entry claimed the migration was "pushed to prod itself"; it was not.]** What actually happened: 037 was applied locally only; the local grant/default-ACL state after a fresh reset was verified byte-identical to prod's (grants + `pg_default_acl` comparison). **037 has NOT been pushed to prod** — prod's migration history still ends at 036. It lands with the next normal migration push, where it is an idempotent no-op (prod already holds every grant and default ACL it writes). **Implication for every future leagues migration: no per-object GRANT statements — grants stay uniformly broad and RLS is the only effective gate (spec §12; §8.2's per-table pgTAP proves it). Deliberate narrowing (e.g. an internal service-role-only function) must be an explicit REVOKE in that migration.** *Carve-out (R5, 2026-07-19): "RLS is the only effective gate" holds for tables only — SECURITY DEFINER routines bypass RLS, so every one needs in-body auth (plan §8.3, spec §12.0) plus explicit REVOKE discipline; first instance `038_notify_list_followers_auth.sql`.* pgTAP `001_api_grants.sql` pins the surface (witness-table grants, default-ACL canary table + function, RLS-still-gates behavioral check) so a CLI behavior change fails loudly there. *Process note (R6, 2026-07-19): plan §8.1's staging-clone rehearsal line was skipped for 037 without a recorded waiver — recorded now: no staging clone exists (environments are local + prod only); the fresh local `db reset` replay plus the byte-identical grants/`pg_default_acl` comparison against prod served as the rehearsal evidence. Future schema-bearing migrations (039 `nfl_weeks` onward) must rehearse on a staging clone or record this waiver explicitly per migration.* Side effects: `nfl_weeks` renumbers 037 → 038 (tasks doc §5/§6 updated); typegen deliberately not re-run — grants change no schema shape, and regenerating would clobber the hand-written alias block in `src/types/database.ts`.

**2026-07-21 — Builder (M1 batch-5 findings remediation, R57–R61):**
- **D58** Scoring-module failure semantics for corrupt inputs (the two R58/R59 rulings, both pinned by test). **(1) R58 — an unmappable tier source value is UNREPORTED (family absent → pending), never an all-zero delivered family.** The decision hinged on whether the published bucket tables are real-contiguous (which would justify clamping/flooring a fractional value into a bucket) or integer-gapped: they are **integer-gapped** — ESPN's Scoring-Formats article prints PA `1–6 / 7–13 / 14–17 / …` and YA `100–199 / 200–299 / …` (re-verified value-for-value by the batch-4 review), leaving real-valued gaps between adjacent buckets (13.5, 99.5), so the tables' domain is the integers and there is no defensible bucket to clamp into. Consequence: `familyMaps` requires an INTEGER inside ≥1 bucket; a fractional value is out-of-domain even when it happens to sit inside an interval (14.5 pends the family, same as 13.5 — no partial acceptance of corrupt data), and a negative PA (below `def_pa_0`'s pinned floor) pends. Pinned at the exact review-probed gap values (PA=13.5, YA=99.5, negative PA, plus in-interval-fractional PA=14.5); the one-hot property extended beyond integers (fractional/negative/non-finite sweep) asserting *delivered ⇔ integer-in-a-bucket, and delivered ⇒ exactly one hot per platform set*; a named counter-pin proves the all-zero-family state (and partial-family emission) is unconstructible. **(2) R59 — a corrupt rules coefficient THROWS (TypeError naming every offending key), the loud option:** a non-finite-number coefficient in `scoring_rules_snapshot` is corrupt config, not missing data — marking it pending would misbadge corrupt config as "waiting on stats" (the reviewer's own analysis), and letting it through NaN-poisons a total `NUMERIC(8,2)` will store (Postgres numeric has NaN — live-verified in the review). Validation runs up-front over all rules keys (including keys with no delivered stat — corrupt config is never quietly parked as pending); string-numerics (`"0.5"`) throw too, since silent coercion masks the corruption the L.A1.11 freeze should have caught. Pinned: NaN can never reach the return value — every adversarial coefficient shape either throws TypeError or yields a finite total, plus a finite-total assertion inside the 250-run property. The M4 worker (L.D1) decides catch-and-quarantine vs fail-the-run at the call site (F23's composition row is where that lands); the module's contract is simply *never emit a poisoned or silently-wrong breakdown*. **(3) R61 taken:** the round(full sum)≠Σ(rounded perKey) rule now has a stored-literal discriminating pin (`{a:0.111,b:0.111}×{a:3,b:3} → 0.67`; Σ-of-rounded yields 0.66) beside the statistical property. **(4) R57's spec fold-back is v2.8.4** (§7.3.3 parenthetical + changelog; header Version field corrected 2.8.1 → 2.8.4 in passing — it had been stale since v2.8.2).

Nothing in the stack refuses it — `timerSecondsSchema` is `z.number().int().min(0).max(86_400)` (`draft-service.ts:1034`) and 090's auction arm only rejects negatives — and a three-second bid clock makes an auction unplayable. **The idiom already existed for these exact two fields**: `settings-panel.tsx` clamps `auction_bid_seconds` with `clampInt(e.target.value, 10, 60, …)`. So the payload builder became a pure op, `auctionTimerPayload`, which clamps each box into `AUCTION_TIMER_RANGES` (§7.3.8's literals) and includes a key only when the CLAMPED value differs from what is stored; an empty or unreadable box means *unchanged*, never a guess. **The label and the clamp now read the same literals** — `TimerInput` takes a `range` and renders `` `${min}–${max}s` `` from it — so the two cannot drift apart again, which is the actual defect this finding names. **Route and RPC deliberately unchanged**, and pinned as unchanged: they are the backstop, not the enforcement, and server-authoritative is untouched — the UI simply stops proposing a number its own label calls illegal. (2) **ONE `activeTeams`, AND IT IS THE ENGINE'S PREDICATE (R436).** `draft_end` counts open slots over `teams … WHERE t.league_id = … AND t.status <> 'retired'` (`087:1004-1007` — the reviewer cited `1011-1014`; the clause is at **1007** in the shipped file) while `getLeagueDetail` selects teams with **no status filter** (`leagues-service.ts:517-521`), so the panel's raw `detail.teams` fed the End confirm's "N roster spots stay empty", the budget picker and Manual Edit's cells/move targets. Latent today (nothing writes `'retired'` — only `'orphaned'`/`'active'`; `retire_franchise` is F1/M4) and both sides count orphaned seats, which is why the live run agreed at 18 — but it is a wrong number in a TERMINAL confirm the moment M4 lands. `activeFranchises()` is now the single derivation and feeds all three sites. **`teamsById` stays UNFILTERED on purpose**, pinned as such: a retired franchise's existing picks still need a name to render. Pinned three ways — the filter's own golden (retired dropped, **orphaned kept** — 087 excludes exactly one status), the `WHERE` clause read out of the migration chain, and an arithmetic pin showing the unfiltered count would have promised three more empty spots than `draft_end` posts. (3) **THE PER-SECTION GATE PIN WAS SATISFIABLE BY THE OUTER BUTTON (R437).** D193(2)'s pin asserted `disabled={gate.blocked` *somewhere in each section*, which whichever button carried it satisfied — so the confirms INSIDE the Undo, Manual-Edit and Cancel-nomination dialogs shipped ungated, and `ManualEditDialog` is rendered OUTSIDE the `armed && !gate.blocked` guard that hides the cell grid. A dialog opened while paused therefore stays armed if a co-commissioner resumes, and the click meets the server's pause-first refusal — **F72's exact shape, in a race**. All four confirms now read `gate.blocked` and carry `gate.reason` as their title, and the pin is **per BUTTON**: every `<Button>` in a pause-first section that is not on an explicit exemption list (each entry carrying its reason — Pause/Resume is the gate's OWN verb, and the rest are pure client state: arm the mode, pick a branch, open/close a dialog) must contain `gate.blocked`, with a non-vacuity assertion that each section has at least one such button. The old per-section pins stay, and probe C below is the proof they could not have caught this. (4) **THE DOUBLE-SUBMIT GUARD IS MOUNT-SCOPED, AND THE REAL GAP IS THE ENGINE'S (R438).** The reviewer measured it: `SheetContent` has no `forceMount`, so closing and reopening the panel mid-flight destroys the `useAdjustBudget` observer and re-enables the submit. The reach is genuinely narrow — the reopened form is empty, so team, delta AND reason must all be re-entered — but **the residual is wider than the panel and no client can close it**: `draft_adjust_budget` still takes no `action_id`, so a retry after a lost response double-charges. D193(4)/the session log's *"closed where it bites"* therefore **over-claimed, and is softened here rather than defended**: the guard covers re-render and mid-flight refetch, not unmount. Hosting the mutation outside the sheet was NOT taken — it restructures the panel to buy a narrower version of a hazard the engine has to fix anyway — so the honest disposition is the F-row: **F82**, an engine-side `action_id` on `draft_adjust_budget`, owned by the next migration task in the lane. The limitation is now stated at the guard itself, so the next reader does not inherit the over-claim from a comment. (5) **`clampInt` MOVED, NOT FORKED.** A pure `.ts` ops module cannot import `settings-form-controls.tsx` under the unit lane (esbuild parses the JSX with the wrong loader and the suite fails to transform), and copying four lines is the near-duplicate CLAUDE.md forbids. So the body moved to `src/utils/clamp-int.ts` and `settings-form-controls.tsx` **re-exports it unchanged** — every existing import site (`settings-panel.tsx`'s **thirteen** call sites, and `roster-slot-builder-ops.ts`'s own private same-named helper is untouched) reads exactly as before, and `type-check` + `lint` are the proof. (6) **PROOFS AND PROBES.** `npm run test` **127 files / 2133 green** (+20 in `commish-auction-ops.test.ts`, 57 → 77) · `test:gate` **24/24** · `type-check` clean · **`lint` CLEAN — zero warnings** · production build **`routes-manifest.json` BYTE-IDENTICAL** vs `main` @ `b62a63c` (`NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_AUTH=false`, `rm -rf .next` both sides, main built in a detached worktree; sha256 `0f591746…8013c88` on both — corroborated by `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- src/app/` returning **zero files**) · no SQL in the diff, so `test:db` and typegen are untouched. **LOCAL STACK ONLY and no `db reset`** — a sibling Builder held the same stack for L.C3.3. **Five probes, each shown RED then reverted** (working tree verified clean after each): **A** and **B** re-run at the corrected denominator (3 of 77 · 1 of 77, same named tests — see D193(11)); **C** (R437 — `gate.blocked` removed from all four dialog confirms, i.e. the exact pre-fix state) → **3 of 77**, naming `UndoSection`, `ManualEditDialog` and `CancelNominationSection`, **and the old per-section pins stayed GREEN throughout** — the demonstration that the outer-button pin could not catch this; **D** (R435 — the clamp replaced by a bare `Number.parseInt`) → **6 of 77**, both bounds of all three clocks plus the negative and the clamped-equals-stored cases; **E** (R436 — `activeFranchises` made an identity filter) → **2 of 77**, the filter golden and the count-agreement pin.

| F329 | **pg_net IS FIRE-AND-FORGET, AND NOTHING IN THIS SYSTEM READS ITS RESULT.** 124's `cron_ping_route` returns a request id and nothing waits on it: pg_net does not retry, and the response lands in `net._http_response`, which has **zero readers in this repo**. That table cannot carry a check either — measured: it has **no `url` column at all** (so it cannot say WHICH ping failed; the table that does carry `url`, `net.http_request_queue`, is emptied as the worker processes each row), a connect failure records `status_code = NULL` rather than a non-2xx (so the obvious `>= 400` predicate misses the likeliest failure), and it is **UNLOGGED with `pg_net.ttl = '6 hours'`** (so a daily reader always finds it empty and reports all-clear — the same 'nothing happened means it worked' bug this task exists to end). It is a debugging aid for a live incident, never a mitigation. **WHAT IS ACTUALLY COVERED — AMENDED 2026-09-10 at the fix round, because the first version of this sentence was FALSE for the likeliest failure of this very design.** It said a ping that never lands is caught by its consequence — the queue stops draining and `scoring-stall-check` raises within ten minutes. That holds only for the SCORE-WEEK ping dying ALONE. Both pings share one helper, one pg_net worker, two Vault secrets and one origin, so every failure mode named in this row kills them TOGETHER — and with `sync-live` dead, `ingest-week.ts:752-784` is the only enqueue path, so no new `score_fanout` rows ever arrive: the queue drains to empty and a queue-only check reports `stalled: false` FOREVER while the pipeline is completely dark. Silence reading as health, one level up from the incident this migration exists to end. **THE FIX SHIPPED IN THIS PR:** `scoring_stall_check` grew a SECOND arm, `ingest_stale` — `max(updated_at)` over the `ingest_poll:<season>:<week>` keys (already written per successful poll since 122, no new heartbeat) older than **two hours**, which is one missed hourly sweep (`SWEEP_MINUTE = 0`, `live-poll.ts`). ### Blocker

- **R1 · blocker · PROGRESS-leagues.md:104 (D23) + session log 2026-07-19 — refs: plan §2.3 DoD ("shown, not claimed"); CLAUDE.md Active Builds.** D23 records "The migration is an idempotent no-op pushed to prod itself" (session log: "local grants/default-ACLs verified byte-identical to prod") — but the hosted project's migration history, queried live this session, ends at `20260714171131 / player_usage_table` (= 036). **No 037 entry exists in prod.** Either the push never happened or it bypassed migration tracking; either way the decisions log asserts a prod state production contradicts, on a security-relevant migration. Until resolved, D23's premise (prod carries the versioned grant model) is unverified and the next `db push` will find 037 unapplied. Resolve by actually pushing 037 (recording it in prod's history) or correcting D23/the session log to what was actually done, with the verification evidence.

### Should-fix

**L.A0.5c — grants migration**

- **R2 · should-fix · PROGRESS:104 (D23) + 037_explicit_api_grants.sql:8 + commit 3d813ef — refs: tasks-M0 L.A0.5c stop condition.** The re-verification record miscounts its own surface: "all 36 public tables" — there are **40** (40 `CREATE TABLE`s, zero `DROP TABLE`s, in 001–036; 36 is the count of *applied migrations*) — and "all 7 privileges" contradicts the ACL D23 itself quotes (`arwdDxtm` = 8 bits incl. PG17 MAINTAIN). Compounds R1: the stop-condition verification record is internally inconsistent.
- **R3 · should-fix · 037:36–41 — refs: spec §12 ("RLS on every table"); spec §12.0 (REVOKE EXECUTE on league RPCs); plan §8.1–8.2; D23.** The default-ACL model flips the failure mode fail-closed → fail-open: pre-037, a forgotten grant produced a loud 42501; now a future migration that forgets `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` ships a table on which anon holds full privileges, silently. No automated backstop landed. A one-line pgTAP global assertion in 001_api_grants.sql (e.g. `is_empty($$ select tablename from pg_tables where schemaname='public' and not rowsecurity $$)`) would machine-enforce spec §12; the same fail-open logic will apply to §12.0's per-RPC REVOKEs.
- **R4 · should-fix · supabase/tests/001_api_grants.sql:30 — refs: D23 ("pins the surface"); tasks-M0 L.A0.5c item 3.** The pin has holes: the canary table (`id int primary key`) creates no sequence and there is no `has_sequence_privilege` assertion, so 037's sequence catch-up grant *and* sequence default ACL have zero coverage — deleting 037 lines 29 and 38–39 still passes 10/10. No existing-routine catch-up witness either (e.g. the 004 reorder RPC), and the table/function checks sample SELECT/INSERT/EXECUTE rather than the full privilege set D23 claims to pin.
- **R5 · should-fix · 037:30 + 019_list_update_notifications.sql:18 — refs: spec §12.0; plan §8.3; D23.** D23's doctrine "grants stay uniformly broad and RLS is the only effective gate" is false for routines: SECURITY DEFINER bodies bypass RLS. 037 versions anon EXECUTE on `notify_list_followers(p_list_id, p_actor)` — SECURITY DEFINER, zero `auth.*` checks in the body, caller-supplied `p_actor` — which can insert notifications attributed to arbitrary users. The exposure pre-exists under the legacy model, but the migration now codifies it; the doctrine needs a SECURITY DEFINER carve-out, and future league RPCs need §8.3 in-body auth + explicit REVOKE discipline.
- **R6 · should-fix · 037 (process) — refs: plan §8.1 ("staging-clone rehearsal noted"); plan §2.3.** §8.1's rehearsal line is silently skipped: no note in the migration, D23, the session log, or commit 3d813ef, and no waiver covers it (contrast D10/D23, which waive other checklist lines explicitly).

### Should-fix

- **R22 · should-fix · .eslintrc.json:50 — refs: D3/R15 ("mechanical, not convention"); D26 item 5.** The new `Math.random` guard did not inherit the R15 widening the Date guard got. Empirically probed via ESLint stdin against `src/lib/leagues/**`: `globalThis.Math.random()` and `const M = Math; M.random()` are both **lint-clean** — the exact two escape shapes (globalThis routing, constructor/object aliasing) R15 closed for `Date`. `crypto.getRandomValues(...)` is also unbanned (a common "random" reach). D26 records "two new D3-style lint selectors," but the shipped guard is strictly narrower than the D3 guard it cites. Add `MemberExpression[object.name='globalThis'][property.name='Math']`, Math-aliasing selectors, and (optionally) a crypto.getRandomValues ban.
- **R23 · should-fix · synthetic-stats-provider.test.ts:128 + scenarios.ts:21 — refs: §23.6 ("versioned, deterministic, re-runnable"); D26 (library versioning).** No test pins any concrete PRNG-derived stat value against a stored golden constant. Both determinism tests compare two in-process runs of the same code (`fullWeekTranscript` twice; outage vs happy_path), so an *unintended* behavior change — a draw-order refactor in `finalLine`, a range tweak, a `mulberry32` edit — changes every scenario's "deterministic" world while the entire suite stays green. That defeats the versioning contract the schema declares ("bump `version` on ANY behavior change"): nothing can detect an unversioned behavior change, and any future fixture/simulator run pinned against library v1 silently diverges. One golden test (e.g. the full DEFAULT_SEED stat line for one player per position, as literals) makes version bumps mechanical instead of honor-system.
- **R24 · should-fix · live-stats.test.ts:40 — refs: the falsifiability standard this batch claims throughout; §23.2.** The seam's game-window boundary is the one instant-sensitive edge in this diff with **no** boundary pin: tests run mid-window (18:00Z on game day) and 3 days out, never at `kickoffDay` exactly or `kickoffDay + 36h` exactly (live-stats.ts:163 — both edges inclusive). An off-by-one in either comparison (`>=`→`>`, `<=`→`<`) passes the suite. Two exact-instant cases close it; the window semantics are load-bearing for the finalization pass (`weeksToFinalize` gets `inWindow` from this check).

### Nit

- **R25 · nit · synthetic-stats-provider.ts:249 — refs: D25 ("provider-reported calendar day").** Synthetic derives `gameDate` from the kickoff's **UTC** day, so the SNF game (Sun 8:20pm ET) reports Monday `2026-09-21`, while the sleeper tier reports the ET day (checked-in 2025 fixture: Sunday games carry the Sunday date). Literally D25-compliant but a cross-tier semantic drift in the same field: composed with the seam's UTC-day-start+36h window it shifts a late game's window by a day vs. real data. Harmless on the current slate (earlier games open the window); worth aligning to the ET day before L.A0.6 composes synthetic with the seam.
- **R26 · nit · scenario-beats.test.ts:290 (D26 back-fill proof) — refs: §23.2 (back-fill on recovery).** Answering the brief directly: the outage-vs-happy_path equality is genuinely cross-scenario (it would catch PRNG streams keyed by scenario id, or outage state leaking into values — the two ways this provider *could* regress), but it is **not an independent computation**: both sides run the identical pure `finalLine`/`progress` code on identical inputs, and since the provider is stateless the equality is near-tautological. What §23.2 actually cares about — writer-side cumulative back-fill after a degraded window (upserts catching up in `player_stats`) — is untested anywhere in this batch and lands on L.A0.6. Fine for M0 provider scope; recorded so the gate task doesn't inherit "back-fill is proven" as a premise.
- **R27 · nit · scripts/record-fixtures.ts:90,99 — refs: D27 (identity lives IN the artifact).** The CLI hardcodes `provider: 'sleeper'` in the header and `sleeper.jsonl.gz` in the path instead of reading `provider.name` — re-introducing at write time exactly the guessing D27 exists to prevent. Equal today; a silent lie the day the CLI wraps any other provider.
- **R28 · nit · fixture-format.ts:68 — refs: D27 ("parse-rejected loudly on mismatch").** Loud rejection covers `format`/`version` only; a header missing `provider`/`season`/`week` parses fine and yields `name = 'fixture:undefined'` downstream. A three-field presence check would make the identity guarantee total.
- **R29 · nit · fixture-replay-provider.ts:104 — refs: D6 (failures replay as failures).** Recorded failures replay as a generic `Error` carrying the message only — the recorded `status` (e.g. 429 vs 500) is dropped, so a future consumer branching on status sees a different shape live vs replay. No consumer branches today.
- **R30 · nit · D24/D28 seam composition (live-stats.ts:94 + fixture-replay-provider.ts:58).** D24's "record/replay reproduces today's writes" is true for every column *except* `source`: the writer stamps `provider.name`, and replay's name is `'fixture:sleeper'`, so a replayed ingestion writes `source: 'fixture:sleeper'`. That is D28's intended honest default — but the documented opt-in (`recordedProviderName`) has **no supported mechanism** reaching the writer; L.A0.6 will have to hand-roll a delegating wrapper that overrides `name` to get byte-identical rows. Deliberate-by-design per D28; recorded so the gate builder budgets for it (and so the wrapper, when written, is recognized as the sanctioned deliberate-impersonation path, not a smell).

### Should-fix

- **R37 · should-fix · 052:127 (kept "League owners can manage") + 040 (`scoring_rules_snapshot`, `status`, `settings` columns) — refs: spec §8.1 (server-authoritative), §7.3.3/§7.3.8, §12.1 ("keep"), CLAUDE.md never-weaken (snapshot reads); recommend a §3 spec question.** 001's `FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = owner_id)` policy — which §12.1 explicitly says to keep, and 052 duly kept — now composes with 040's columns into a client-writable league-state surface: **live-proven this session**, an ordinary authenticated user INSERTs a `leagues` row directly, then UPDATEs `scoring_rules_snapshot = '{"forged":true}'` and `status = 'drafting'` in one statement (they cannot seed themselves into `league_members` — the commish bootstrap is closed). Consequences: the templates-only rule's in-body RPC enforcement (the breakdown review's critical fix) is bypassable by direct PostgREST DML; D43's future lifecycle trigger only raises on a NULL snapshot, so forge-snapshot-then-transition sails past it; the owner can also hard-DELETE the league (rule-8 soft-delete bypass), cascading `league_members` — and via `league_id` — `team_managers` rows away (blocked only once league `teams` rows exist, since `teams.league_id` is NO ACTION). Nothing in this batch is wrong against the spec — the spec's own "keep" instruction creates the hole — so per CLAUDE.md this needs a filed spec question (recommendation: replace the owner FOR ALL with owner-manage scoped to safe columns/lifecycle, or guard triggers on `scoring_rules_snapshot`/`status`/`deleted_at`; must be ruled before L.A1.11–L.A1.13 land, where the enforcement-point claims would otherwise be false).

Header states the discharge rule: builders MUST flip a listed obligation in the same PR that builds its task; reviewers audit every batch |
| R48 | **Ledger entry F6, NOT a migration — Builder judgment call as delegated.** Why not DB CHECKs now: **(a)** the mutual-exclusivity CHECK (`NOT (revoked_at AND claimed_at)`) would encode claim semantics L.A1.14 hasn't defined — the review's own probe B shape (claimed_at set AND later revoked_at set) is plausibly *legitimate* for a multi-use invite: some uses claimed, then the commissioner revokes further use; a CHECK baked in now risks a revert migration the day the claim RPC defines this. **(b)** `CHECK (use_count <= max_uses)` alone is safer but settles a clamp-vs-block question that belongs to the RPC (055's own comment says commissioners "may raise" `max_uses` — whether one may ever *lower* it below `use_count` is undefined), and shipping half the backstop invites false confidence. **(c)** Cost: a CHECK-only migration would take 057 and shift the schema lane a third time in one week (057 def_ya → 058, cascading the §7 table + PROGRESS §2 again) for two backstops on a table with **zero writers of any kind** — failing the D53 proportionality test 056's status CHECK passed (that one was free, in-table, at creation). The invariants land as `claim_league_invite`'s in-body duty with pins, tracked as F6 so L.A1.14 can't start without tripping over it |

**Verified sound (for the record):**

- **The §7.3.3 dot-product contract holds under adversarial inputs.** Unknown stat keys ignored (probed: extra keys leave the breakdown deep-equal); undelivered rules keys land in `pending` with no `perKey` entry in every path — a stat delivered AS `null` (out-of-type but JSONB-realistic) resolves pending via the `typeof`/`isFinite` gate, same as absent, which is the honest reading; delivered-zero is the pinned opposite (real `perKey: 0`, no badge). - **F20's structural guarantee survives every input shape tried.** Inbound `def_pa_*`/`def_ya_*` keys are stripped unconditionally and re-emitted only from a delivered source (probed: bogus `def_pa_46_plus: 1` without source → absent; with source → recomputed to 0); families deliver independently (PA=0 without YA → full PA family 0/1, all 9 YA keys absent → exactly the YA rules keys pending — tested and re-probed); non-finite source → family absent → pending. Within `deriveTierIndicators` an indicator-without-source state is unconstructible. *(The guarantee is module-local — the composition obligation is R60(b).)*

D57(2)'s reading is now live-verified, not just asserted. *(The spec-term ambiguity is R57.)*

The platform-set literals in the test are themselves anchored by the both-directions registry cross-check. *(The property's integer-only domain is the gap — R58.)*

### Should-fix

- **R57 · should-fix · calculator.ts:36-49 (`roundHalfUp` doc) + spec §7.3.3 precision rule — "half-up" is ecosystem-ambiguous and the spec never pins which meaning; the implementation's choice is right but lives only in the decisions log; refs: E38 (determinism), D57(2), the §3 fold-back discipline.** The two authorities the rounding question names genuinely diverge at negative half-cent boundaries: strict "round half up" (the Wikipedia/IEEE toward-+∞ convention) gives `−0.005 → −0.00`, while Postgres `NUMERIC(8,2)` assignment — **tested live this session, both numeric-literal and float8 paths** — gives `−0.005 → −0.01` (half away from zero; Java's `RoundingMode.HALF_UP` also means away-from-zero, so the bare term supports both readings). The implementation sides with the DB, which is the only coherent choice under E38's determinism rule (JS result ≡ stored result), and pins it at `−0.005 → −0.01`. But the spec text still says bare "half-up": a future implementer (or the L.D1 writer's author) reading §7.3.3 alone can pick the toward-+∞ reading and diverge from both this module and the column type on negative totals (all-miss K weeks, INT-heavy QB weeks). The divergence window is narrow — with 2-decimal template coefficients × integer stats every sum is exact at 2 decimals, so a negative half-cent boundary needs ≥3-decimal coefficients — but the determinism rule is absolute and the fix is one line. Fold a spec erratum (changelog + §7.3.3 parenthetical): *"half-up = round half away from zero, matching NUMERIC(8,2) assignment; −0.005 → −0.01"* — per the repo's own rule that resolved ambiguities get folded back into the spec, not left in D-rows.
- **R58 · should-fix · derive-stats.ts:83-91 (`emitFamily`) — a delivered source value that lands in no bucket emits an all-zero family: delivered-zero everywhere, nothing hot, nothing pending — the silent-wrong-total class E61/F20 exist to prevent; refs: §23.5, E61, F20, D57(1).** Probed live: `def_points_allowed: 13.5` → all 11 PA keys delivered as 0 (13.5 falls between `def_pa_7_13` and `def_pa_14_20`; both platform sums = 0, violating the one-hot invariant the property test asserts — but that property only scans **integers**, so the state is invisible to it); `def_yards_allowed: 99.5` → same for YA; a (bogus) negative PA → same, since `def_pa_0` pins lo=0. Downstream, every tier rules key scores a delivered 0 with an empty `pending` — for ESPN templates that silently erases the D/ST tier component (up to ±5 points/side) with no badge, which is a *worse* state than the pre-F20 all-pending bug (that one was at least honest). Reachability today is low — `player_stats` sources are INTEGER columns (057), and nothing calls these modules yet — but the helper's input is provider-shaped `Record<string, number>`, not column-shaped, and nothing range-guards it. Cheap close: treat a source value matching **no** bucket as unreported (family absent → pending; for PA that also covers negatives), and extend the one-hot property to assert *delivered ⇒ exactly one hot per platform set* over non-integer samples so the wrong fix (leaving the gap) can't pass.
- **R59 · should-fix · calculator.ts:64-72 — the delivered-stat guard is one-sided: a malformed rules **coefficient** poisons the total to NaN, and NUMERIC(8,2) accepts NaN, so the poisoned total is storable; refs: E61 ("never a silent wrong total"), §7.3.3 snapshot rule, D57(3)'s defensive clause.** Probed live: `{ receptions: "abc" }` (rules values come from `scoring_rules_snapshot` JSONB, which can carry strings) → `contribution = NaN` → `total: NaN` (`roundHalfUp` propagates it), and `INSERT 'NaN'` into a `NUMERIC(8,2)` column **succeeds** (live-tested — Postgres numeric has a NaN value), so nothing downstream is guaranteed to throw. A string-numeric coefficient (`"0.5"`) silently coerces and scores (×4 → 2) — works by accident, masking a corrupt snapshot. The module already defends the *stats* side against exactly this class (non-finite → pending, D57's "never poisoning a total"); the rules side, same trust boundary (a JSONB blob), has no guard. Reachability requires a corrupt snapshot — v1 rules are code-authored templates frozen via the L.A1.11 RPC — but the v1.1 custom editor (F21's scope) makes rules user-shaped, and this module is the last line. Semantics call for the Builder to make **and record**: marking a bad-coefficient key `pending` would misbadge corrupt config as "waiting on data," so the honest options are throw (corrupt snapshot = programming/config error, loud) or a distinct breakdown flag; either way, pin it with a test.
- **R60 · should-fix · PROGRESS §6 — two hand-offs this task created live only in prose; per the §6 header rule (R51: "creating a hand-off without an F-row is itself a review finding") both need rows; refs: R51 precedent, E38, F20/D57(1), D44.** **(a) Rounding vs the real writer (L.D1):** D57(2)'s NUMERIC-matching claim carried no DB evidence at build time (this review supplied it — live temp-table proof, see header), and the actual consistency obligation — the L.D1 writer stores the **JS-rounded** total into `matchups`/`team_week_results` `NUMERIC(8,2)`, with a pin proving no path lets the DB do the rounding on a diverging value (benign only while both round half-away-from-zero; E38's determinism must be *pinned* at the writer, not inherited silently) — belongs to a task that doesn't exist yet in any ledger row. Add F22 → discharged by L.D1 (M4). **(b) The derive→score composition:** F20's guarantee is module-local — `scorePlayerWeek` happily accepts raw stats that never passed `deriveTierIndicators` (tier rules keys then read pending forever), and a worker that skips derive also loses the inbound-indicator stripping (D44's "never stored" laundering guard). The composition appears only in L.A1.10's task-text usage sketch (`scorePlayerWeek(template.rules, derive(stats))`); the production call site is M4's `score-league-week` (§22.2/L.D1), and no F-row keys it. Add F23 → *`score-league-week` composes `deriveTierIndicators` before `scorePlayerWeek`; pinned at the worker* — discharged by L.D1 (M4), with L.A1.10 as the interim proof-of-pattern.

### Nit

- **R61 · nit · calculator.test.ts — no stored-literal golden pin discriminates round(full sum) from Σ(rounded perKey); only the 250-run property carries E38's precision rule; refs: §4.3(a) (golden pins as stored literals), E38, D57(3).** Every literal pin's contributions are exact at ≤2 decimals (QB 11.48+8−2+2+1.2; E38 tie 9.2+6+0.04) — a Σ-of-rounded implementation passes all of them; the single-key `0.335×3 → 1.01` pin rounds identically under both (one entry). The property test does catch the wrong implementation (near-certainly, per the verified-sound note), but §4.3(a)'s point is a falsifiable *literal*: one two-key pin, e.g. rules `{a: 0.111, b: 0.111}` × stats `{a: 3, b: 3}` → full sum 0.666 → `total: 0.67` (a Σ-of-rounded impl yields 0.33+0.33 = **0.66**), pins the rule as a stored literal instead of a statistical consequence.

## Review findings — 2026-07-26 (M1 batch 15)

*Reviewer session (fresh context, red-team brief): diff = PR #60 (`feat/M1-L.A1.15-member-management` — L.A1.15, migration 063 member management + 062 amended in place + pgTAP 017 + `members-service.ts` + 3 routes + the stack suite). **Method: a 101-agent adversarial pass — 7 review lenses plus a completeness critic and a gap round, every surviving candidate put through 3 INDEPENDENT refuters each required to reproduce from its own fixture rather than re-run the reporter's. 29 candidates reached refutation; **19 were REFUTED** and dropped; 10 survived (R90–R99: 5 should-fix, 5 nits). Live probing ran exclusively inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` with residue counts and `git status --short` verified clean after every probe.** VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — no blocker, no spec violation, no data-corruption path reachable on M1's shipped surface. Findings recorded verbatim below; resolution on the SAME branch (fix-then-merge — no new PR). The refutation count is recorded because it is the evidence that the surviving 10 are not noise.*

**What the pass CONFIRMED (recorded so no later session re-litigates it):** the S1 fix on the amended 062 (the seat-targeted claim branch and `assign_manager` genuinely FILL an existing placeholder; the live-proven 23505→`seat_filled` mislabel is gone); mode semantics (takeover closes with `replaced` and reseats with no `league_invites` row touched; vacate sets `orphaned` per §7.2.1(c) and closes `kicked`; leave closes `left`) — two candidates attacking them were refuted 3/3 against §7.2.1(a); the atomic transfer under the league lock (exactly one commissioner survives every path including the failed replay; the co-commissioner coup raises 42501; creator protection fires on the correct target); capacity across all five seat paths including the F28 cross-writer re-run; and the S2 policy drop's blast radius — the loudest counter-thesis (that dropping the DELETE carve-out makes `add_placeholder_seat` a one-way door burning capacity and killing the open-join link) was raised by three lenses in four shapes and **refuted every time**. The whole 062-arity cluster (amend-in-place with a signature change, no `DROP FUNCTION` guard, orphaned overload) was refuted 3/3 on the unreleased-history/F12 precedent.

### Resolution — 2026-07-26 (Builder, same branch `feat/M1-L.A1.15-member-management`, PR #60)

*Nine of ten taken. **R96 is the exception and it is a deliberate HALT, not a deferral:** its fix direction required ruling the recipient question FIRST, and reading §7.2.1:190 against the shipped `leave_league` leaves two defensible readings — a product call, so it is filed as spec question **Q11** with options and a recommendation, ledgered as **F37**, and the leave-path notification content is left unpinned. R96's other half (the takeover/vacate notification rows, whose recipient is the removed user under BOTH readings) landed. Mechanics recorded as **D75**. **063 amended in place** (unreleased — prod history ends at 036, F12; D64(5)/D69/D72/D73 precedent). No signature changed, so no typegen re-run. Per the remediation brief, R98/R99 were treated as the R84/R89 attestation class RECURRING: every factual claim in 063's banner, the 017 header, D74 and the new F-rows was re-verified against the shipped tree, not just the two the review caught.*

### Should-fix

- **R90 · should-fix · `supabase/migrations/063_league_member_management.sql`:935** — `leave_league` and `remove_manager` reassign `teams.owner_id` only on the departing member's own franchise, so every placeholder seat that user created stays owned by a proven non-member on an `ON DELETE CASCADE` FK. *Evidence:* `add_placeholder_seat` stamps `owner_id = v_uid` (063:381-383); the owner_id reassignment in `leave_league` (063:935-939) and `remove_manager` vacate/takeover (063:809-813 / 784-788) is scoped `WHERE id = v_team.id`. Three independent live probes (BEGIN…ROLLBACK, zero residue) reproduced the residual in two shapes — departed creator, and a `vacate`'d co-commissioner. In the second shape `DELETE FROM public.profiles WHERE id = <removed user>` silently destroyed both of their placeholder franchises (team_count 8, seats_counted 4 → 2) and, because `league_members_team_id_fkey` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, left two `league_members` rows with `team_id NULL` — precisely the "invisible to every capacity check" shape ruling S2 / erratum v2.8.8 / D74(3) removed policies to eliminate. 063's own banner (063:151-152, 807-808) names this exact hazard as the reason it moves `owner_id` at all, then dodges it for one franchise. Secondary limb: the departed non-member retains `team_lineups` FOR ALL via 001:856-861 (unscoped `teams.owner_id` key, unlike 053:71-72) — INSERT and UPDATE both succeeded live — contradicting the shipped wording at 017:953/957, F36 and D74(11) ("no write path survives"). That limb sits on the pre-dispositioned C12/F18 surface; the ownership residual and its CASCADE consequence do not. *Fix direction:* in all three arms, add `UPDATE public.teams SET owner_id = <sitting commissioner>, updated_at = now() WHERE league_id = p_league_id AND owner_id = <departing user> AND id <> v_team.id`, and either land it or reword 017 §L / F36 / D74(11) so the prose stops attesting an invariant the code lacks.

A mutant of `assign_manager` with only `AND t.league_id = p_league_id` removed (063:571) raises `P0001 … that franchise already has a manager` on the same fixture, so the assertion still passes; the real function raises `P0001 … not part of this league`. Retargeting at a fresh unoccupied seat makes the mutant succeed outright — writing an L2 `league_members` row pointing at an L1 franchise (count=1 confirmed). `members-api-db.test.ts:283-285` is masked identically (`seatTeamId` is L1's occupied franchise, `successorId` not yet in L2, and members-service.ts:56 flattens every P0001 to 400). `grep -rn "not part of this league" supabase src docs` returns only the migration — no third pin exists. Violates tasks-M1 §4.3:73. *Fix direction:* retarget the cross-league call at a stint-free `add_placeholder_seat` seat with a user seated in neither league **and** switch to `throws_like`/message assertion — both halves are required.
- **R92 · should-fix · `supabase/tests/017_league_member_management.sql`:419** — pgTAP test 48 ("manager already has a team") is non-discriminating; deleting the pre-check it names leaves the open-stint guard raising the same SQLSTATE. *Evidence:* the target `l1_commish_team` carries the creator's open stint (opened by `create_league`, 060:302; probe: `commish_team open stints = 1`) while u4 is already seated — one call satisfies both guards, and `throws_ok(…, 'P0001', null)` pins neither. On an EMPTY seat — the case that isolates the guard — the mutant instead emits `that seat was just claimed by someone else — refresh and try again`, i.e. race-flavored copy advising a refresh that cannot help. - **R93 · should-fix · `supabase/migrations/063_league_member_management.sql`:461** — commissioner authorization is read before the `leagues … FOR UPDATE` and never re-verified, so an actor demoted while blocked on the lock still completes one privileged write. *Evidence:* `add_placeholder_seat` (345→355), `set_member_role` (428→436), `assign_manager` (544→552) and `remove_manager` (659→667) all evaluate `is_league_commish` ahead of the lock; `leave_league` alone inverts it (lock 867-870 before the role read at 876) and says so in its comment (864-866, restated in D74(8)). `set_member_role` re-reads `v_actor_role` under the lock at 461-463 but consumes it only at 473 and 488, never as a gate — a demoted actor reads back `'manager'`, misses 473/480/485, and reaches the UPDATE at 508. Probed both halves: with the pre-lock check forced to pass, a live-`manager` actor successfully promoted an accomplice to `co_commissioner`; and a separate probe confirmed a plpgsql statement re-snapshots after a lock wait (`snapshot BEFORE 4322 / AFTER 4329`, a transaction committing at 4323 while blocked), so the demotion IS visible post-lock and the function writes anyway. Two aggravations: the target may be the actor's own row, letting them repeatably undo their own demotion; and the creator anti-coup guards key on `v_actor_role='co_commissioner'`, so a stale actor reading `'manager'` is strictly *more* powerful than a legitimate co-commissioner. *Fix direction:* after each `FOR UPDATE`, gate on the fresh actor role (`IF v_actor_role IS NULL OR v_actor_role NOT IN ('commissioner','co_commissioner') THEN RAISE … 42501`) at 063:463 and 063:696, move the `is_league_commish` call below the lock in the other two, and pin the ordering in 017 the way `leave_league`'s is.
- **R94 · should-fix · `supabase/migrations/063_league_member_management.sql`:480** — replaying a successful commissioner transfer returns P0001/400 with copy asserting the target is not commissioner, breaking the D63 idempotency contract 063's own banner states for `set_member_role`. *Evidence:* 063:117 says "setting the role a member already holds is an idempotent success (D63)"; D63(5) gives the motive verbatim ("client retries must not error"). The guard at 063:479-482 is unconditional in `p_role` and sits ahead of the idempotent arm at 503-506, so any request whose target already holds commissioner dies there. The three sibling RPCs in the same file all ship the retry-safe arm (588-592, 713-718, 762-763); 017 §I pins the guard only for `p_role='manager'` (the genuine headless-demote), so nothing pins this either way. One correction carried from verification: the finding's claim that the 42501 arm "fires first when the retrier is the creator" is wrong — 473 keys on the *target* being the creator. *Fix direction:* add an idempotent arm before 063:480 returning `{member_id, role:'commissioner', transferred:false}` when `p_role='commissioner'` and the target already holds it, pin it in 017 §I beside the existing `transferred:false` assert, and keep 480's P0001 for the headless-demote it exists for — or narrow the 063:117 banner sentence instead.
