## Review findings — 2026-07-27 (M1 batch 20)

**Findings-remediation Builder session on `feat/M1-L.A2.6-join-page` (PR #66 — fix-then-merge, no new PR). One should-fix (R114) from the PR #66 review: the join-by-code dialog dead-ended on a pasted `/join/…` link — the exact affordance its own copy advertises. Purely input-normalization on the join-by-code entry; the F2 surface, the six-state claim logic and the v2.8.10 erratum are untouched.**

### Should-fix

- **R114 · should-fix · `src/components/leagues/leagues-index.tsx`:65** — the join-by-code dialog breaks on a pasted `/join/…` link, the exact affordance its own copy advertises. *Evidence:* the submit handler does `router.push(\`/join/${encodeURIComponent(trimmed)}\`)`, passing the whole pasted string verbatim as the `[token]` param with no code/token extraction. But the dialog's DialogDescription tells the user to "paste a fieldscout.gg/join/… link" and the label reads "Invite code or link". The real share artifacts ARE full absolute URLs: `buildJoinLink` (invite-panel-ops.ts:264) returns `${origin}/join/${codeOrToken}`; the wizard copy button (league-create-wizard.tsx:996) copies `${window.location.origin}/join/${result.invite_code}`. `encodeURIComponent('https://fieldscout.gg/join/a1b2c3d4e5')` yields the single unresolvable segment `/join/https%3A%2F%2F…`; `get_join_preview` matches only exact token / lower(invite_code) / lower(invite_slug), so a full URL → `{found:false}` → "This link isn't valid" on a VALID invite. Typing a bare code works; pasting a link (an explicitly-offered input) dead-ends. F2 intact, no security issue. *Fix direction:* before pushing, if the input contains `/join/`, take the last non-empty path segment (strip query/hash) and encodeURIComponent only that; otherwise use the trimmed value as-is.

### Resolution — 2026-07-27 (Builder, same branch `feat/M1-L.A2.6-join-page`, PR #66)

| Finding | Resolved by |
|---|---|
| R114 (should-fix) | this commit — extraction lifted into a PURE helper `extractJoinCode` in `invite-panel-ops.ts` (the §7.2 share-link section, directly beside `buildJoinLink` as its exact inverse — NOT buried in the dialog's onClick), and `JoinLeagueDialog.handleSubmit` + the Continue-button `disabled` gate now push/enable on `extractJoinCode(code)` instead of the raw trim. The helper trims, cuts everything from the first `?`/`#`, then takes the last non-empty path segment after a case-insensitive `/join/` marker; a bare code/slug (no `/join/`) passes through trimmed. It keeps the segment's original case (seat tokens are case-sensitive; the RPC lower()s codes/slugs itself) and does NOT URL-encode — the caller still `encodeURIComponent`s the route param. Pinned in `invite-panel-ops.test.ts` §8: a 16-row table (full absolute URL, bare-host, protocol-relative, path-only, trailing slash, `?query`, `#hash`, query+slash, custom-slug link, whitespace-wrapped link, bare-code + bare-slug passthrough, empty + whitespace-only) **including the two REAL share artifacts** — `buildJoinLink('https://fieldscout.gg', CODE)`'s own output and the wizard's `${origin}/join/${invite_code}` shape — plus a case-preservation pin (mixed-case token unchanged) and an empty-code pin (`/join/` with no segment → `''`, so the dialog no-ops rather than pushing a dead segment). **Break probe shown:** helper body forced to `return raw.trim()` (the pre-R114 verbatim passthrough) → **exactly 14 of the table rows fail** (every link form), while the bare-code and empty rows STAY green — proving the table discriminates the fix rather than passing vacuously; reverted, re-proven green. **D39 browser pass (pre-auth, cheap):** against a seeded local league (`invite_code='r114probe1'`, `status='setup'`, 12 seats), navigated the EXACT URLs `router.push` targets before vs. after — `/join/https%3A%2F%2Ffieldscout.gg%2Fjoin%2Fr114probe1` (the OLD verbatim-encoded target) renders "This link isn't valid" (the bug reproduced on a valid invite); `/join/r114probe1` (the extracted bare code the NEW helper produces) renders the real "R114 Probe League · 12 seats open" claimable card. `get_join_preview` confirmed the same split at the RPC (`{found:true,status:ok}` on the bare code vs. `{found:false}` on the full URL). The authed dialog-click on `/app/leagues` could not be walked in this session (a local GoTrue seed-auth limitation — the hand-seeded user's client login didn't complete its post-sign-in redirect under automation; an environment constraint, not R114), so the observable behavior was verified at the pre-auth route it feeds — the dialog's onClick is a three-line wiring of the unit-pinned helper into `router.push`, and the URL it produces (`/join/r114probe1`) is exactly the one shown resolving. All seeded rows CLEANED (0 leagues/users/profiles/identities after teardown). Proofs: `test` 37 files / **684** (stack up; invite-panel-ops 33→**39**) · `test:gate` **24** · `type-check` clean · `lint` pre-existing-only. **D81** |

## Review findings — 2026-08-20 (AP batch 2 — AP.1)

**Reviewer batch (adversarial review of PR #182 — AP.1, `auction_min_bid` retires, `main...feat/AP.1-auction-reserve-toggle`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE, one blocker.**

**Adjudicated FOR the Builder first, so it is not re-litigated — every load-bearing number was RE-DERIVED by the reviewer rather than accepted:** the head set is exactly 12 (084×3 · 087×2 · 089×1 · 090×2 · 091×4); the two sites the breakdown missed (`draft_force_pick` 087:2175, `create_mock_draft` 089:1036) are real; `draft_place_bid`'s 085:646 read is genuinely dead since 089 made its tail delegate; **43 hunks / +131/−81 reproduces exactly** under `diff -u`; the bid increment did not move; all three shipped probes went RED at the stated counts; the data migration is total, loud and idempotent across ten planted edge rows; and `draft_auction_reserve` is denied to `anon`, `authenticated` and PostgREST. The **F94** baseline was confirmed independently — the reviewer reverted all twelve bodies to `main`'s text and reproduced the same nondeterministic failure.

### Blocker

- **R456 · blocker · a real test deleted on a false premise, and the premise written into LAW — TAKEN, fixed here.** v2.13.2's erratum 2 rested §7.3.8's solvency redundancy on `roster_size` *"topping out at 20 starters + 20 bench + 6 IR = 46"*. **The 20-slot cap is not a schema bound** — it is a sibling arm of the same validator, and `rosterSettingsSchema.starting_slots` is a bare `z.array(...)` with no length bound. Reproduced by this Builder before fixing (30 slots × `count` 10, `auction_budget: 50`): `leagueSettingsSchema.parse` → **OK**, `deriveRosterSize` → **307**, `validateLeagueSettings` → `["roster_settings.starting_slots","draft.auction_budget"]`. On the strength of the false premise, `settings-round-trip-db.test.ts`'s §8.6.8 per-field case had been downgraded to a Zod-range check, losing the only API-surface assertion that the solvency message and its field are wired. **Fixed three ways:** (a) the per-field case is restored with an oversized `starting_slots` array against a $50 budget, asserting the field, `307-player roster`, `per-slot reserve` and the sibling arm beside it — the Zod-layer `auction_budget: 49` case is KEPT, as a separate claim about a separate layer; (b) a new unit pin asserts the arm firing on a **Zod-parsed** object, which is the pin that would have caught the premise, plus the reserve-0 half where the solvency arm drops out and its sibling stays; (c) spec **v2.13.3** withdraws erratum 2 and restates the redundancy as being between two arms of ONE validator. **Falsifiability, measured:** with the arm made dead code (`if (false && …)`) the restored test goes RED while the downgraded Zod-layer test stays GREEN — which is exactly the coverage that had been lost. Mechanics at **D214(5)**.

### Should-fix

- **R457 · should-fix · the D90 TS-vs-SQL parity differential covered only the toggle-OFF column — TAKEN, fixed here.** D198(5) and AP.1 item 4 both require both, and the ON column had been resting on two hand-written literals (pgTAP 040 §B's `max_bid 200` and `auction-budget.test.ts`'s `maxBid: 200`) — parallel goldens, not a differential. `auction-api-db.test.ts`'s existing sweep now runs a **second pass over the SAME planted board with the flag flipped**, re-reading the config off the wire, re-querying `draft_team_budget` for every franchise, and asserting (a) TS ≡ SQL again at reserve 0, (b) that the two columns differ by exactly `(open_slots − 1) × $1` on every open roster while E27's complete roster reads 0 in BOTH — the negative control — and (c) the ON-column literals. Board restored afterwards. **Proved discriminating:** with the TS mirror made toggle-blind the new pass goes RED (`expected … to match object { auctionBudget: 200, reserve: +0 }`), which two parallel goldens could not do.
- **R458 · should-fix · F94's root cause is deeper than recorded, and the `test:db` number is order-dependent — TAKEN as a ledger widening, NOT fixed (scope; routed to the dev-environment task).** Re-measured here: `supabase/seed.sql` contains **zero** `insert into players`, so after any `db reset` the pool is EMPTY and the premise both suites rest on — *"behind the ENTIRE real pool"* — is unsatisfiable locally. On the shipped tree after a vitest run, `players` holds **5 rows, all vitest residue** (`vitest-lla-p1/p2`, `vitest-lpd-p1/p2/p3`) and `npm run test:db` fails **pgTAP 022 §38** (`have: vitest-lpd-p3 / want: tk-rb01`) — a file this branch never touches. **Causal, not correlational:** `delete from public.players where id like 'vitest-%'` and re-running `test:db` with nothing else changed gives `All tests successful. Files=41, Tests=2855, Result: PASS`. **F94** widened to name both instances and the empty-pool root cause; the session log now states that `test:db` is green on the reset-first ordering.

### Nit — recorded, deliberately not fixed

- **R459 · nit · `092:3850-3859` — the data migration's `||` merge lets a computed toggle overwrite a pre-existing `auction_zero_dollar_nominations` on the same row.** Unreachable today: the only rows the `UPDATE` touches are those still carrying `auction_min_bid`, and nothing has ever written both keys. Recorded because a future partial-migration would make it reachable, and the merge order (computed wins) is a choice, not an accident.
- **R460 · nit · a NEGATIVE stored `auction_min_bid` maps to the toggle OFF**, which is outside §7.3.8's printed `0 ⇒ ON / ≥ 1 ⇒ OFF` mapping. Schema-unreachable (`min(0)` on the retired field), and the migration's loud arm only rejects NON-INTEGERS, not negatives. Left as-is rather than adding a branch for a value that cannot exist.
- **R461 · nit · `auction-block.tsx:728` and `commish-draft-panel.tsx:1452` — `pick.price ?? reserve` renders `$0` as the fallback when the toggle is ON.** Cosmetic and arguably more honest than the old `$1`; the fallback is defensive in both places (an auction pick always carries a price). Not changed.
- **R462 · nit · `commish-auction-ops.ts:174` keeps a SECOND copy of the §8.6.1 max-bid formula beside `auction-budget.ts:156`.** It is parameterised by `reserve`, so it is **not** a second reserve derivation and D198(1) is intact — but it is where two formulas can drift, it predates this PR, and **AP.2's uncontestable predicate is about to lean on this family**. Filed as **F95** so AP.2 inherits the warning rather than rediscovering it.

*(Mechanics at **D214**. Ledger: **F94** widened, **F95** filed. Spec erratum owed and folded: **v2.13.3**, withdrawing v2.13.2's erratum 2.)*

## Review findings — 2026-08-19 (M3 batch 12 — L.C3.1)

**Reviewer batch (adversarial review of PR #175 — L.C3.1, the auction room, `main...feat/M3-L.C3.1-auction-room` @ `2a164db`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — four should-fixes, four nits. All eight taken same-branch same-day; mechanics at D192.**

**Adjudicated FOR the Builder first, so it is not re-litigated:** every probe reproduced at the published counts; the lint retirement is genuine (zero `eslint-disable` / `@ts-ignore` / config edits in the diff); the one-channel and never-optimistic claims verified; all 12 `nomination_order` columns measured with their three words and no resting shadow; `$500` disables the Bid button with the max-bid copy; the anti-snipe re-arm watched live. D191(2)'s anti-snipe correction was verified sound against **two of the three** attacks — a commissioner clock edit cannot lie (`draft_set_clock`'s auction arm is pause-gated, writes `config` only, never `current_deadline`, and refuses `p_extend_current` at 087:1160-1166) and cancel-and-renominate cannot either (pause writes `current_deadline = NULL` at 069:357, so the client sees a null frame that clears `previousRef`). **The third landed — R428.**

- **R427 · should-fix · `draft-room.tsx` — the SHARED status strip printed a SNAKE board coordinate in the auction room — TAKEN, suppressed at the source, pinned, and MEASURED BOTH WAYS.** `myNextPick` was computed unconditionally in `DraftRoomLive` and passed as `myNextPickLabel`, so `nextPickNumberForTeam`'s pure board walk reached a room with no board — and the `draftType` coercion whose own comment said *"the value is simply unused"* was, in fact, used. §16.4 zone 2 enumerates the strip's contents (LIVE/PAUSED · Round & Pick · draft order · presence · clock) and "your next pick" is not among them; worse, the auction rotation skips filled rosters (§8.6.7(c)/E27) so the walk coincides only in lap 1 and then diverges permanently. **Fixed** by making `myNextPick` null when `isAuction` (suppression, the smaller claim — §16.4's auction callout already gives per-team standing to the team columns), correcting the coercion comment to name its two real consumers, and pinning the posture in `auction-room.test.ts`. **Measured live on the local stack, same tree, same build, both draft types off the clock:** an 8-team AUCTION with the guard temporarily disabled read `On the clock · Team 8 | Live | Round 1 · Pick 3 | **Your next: 2.07**`; with the guard restored, the same room at pick 4 read the same strip with **no hint at all**; and an 8-team SNAKE room at pick 3 still reads `**Your next: 2.08**` — the fix is auction-only.
- **R428 · should-fix · `auction-block-ops.ts` — "same nomination key + later deadline" is NOT unique to an anti-snipe extension; a RESUME produces exactly that shape — TAKEN, closed with a SIZE test, pinned in both directions.** `draft_pause` writes `current_deadline = NULL` + `deadline_remaining_ms` (069:353-357) and `draft_resume` writes `now() + remaining` (069:485-492) — strictly later, by the pause duration, with `current_pick_number` and `current_nomination.player_id` untouched, so `nominationKey` is unchanged. The only guard was that `useAntiSnipe`'s `previousRef` had observed the NULL frame, and the ref survives refetches and reconnects because DR.7 keeps the block mounted. The reviewer's probe against the real module moved a deadline **12 seconds** (`T+18s` → `T+30s`, key unchanged) and got `reArmed: true` — announced on screen as *"Anti-snipe — clock reset to 10s"*. **They are separable by SIZE:** 085's re-arm is `GREATEST(current_deadline, now() + anti)` (085:780-791), so whenever it moves the deadline at all the new remaining is exactly `anti_snipe`, never more, while a resume restores the pre-pause remainder. `antiSnipeView` now additionally requires `deadlineMs − (nowMs + offsetMs) <= seconds * 1000 + ANTI_SNIPE_REARM_SLACK_MS` (1,500ms, sized for §9.3 offset error and no larger — every millisecond of slack is a millisecond of resume-shaped movement that still slips through). Both directions pinned as stored literals: the reviewer's exact numbers → NOT re-armed, plus a generic resume; and the genuine re-arm → re-armed, including D128's after-zero full-window case, a 400ms-late client sample, and the exact 11,500 / 11,501 boundary.
- **R429 · should-fix · `draft-room.tsx:315` — the D94 lobby's `stale` prop was provably always `false`, and it marked a rule-1/rule-2 contradiction — TAKEN, RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF BOTH RULES, NOT ESCALATED.** The reviewer is right on both halves: `absentDraftIsHonest(h)` is `h === 'ok'`, the gate precedes the lobby, and past the dataless `!detail.data` arm `health` can only be `'ok' | 'degraded'` — so the gate fired on exactly `'degraded'`, the one state rule 2 says must keep rendering behind the banner, and the prop it evicted was a constant `false`. **The rules do not genuinely conflict — the REMEDY was over-broad, and the spec settles which remedy applies.** §16.5.4's required-states line is LAW: *"degraded (banner + last-good data, never wrong numbers)"*. So rule 1 keeps its content (an absence claim must be backed by a read, never by a failure) and its remedy now scales with what the surface can DISCLOSE: the D94 lobby mounts the command bar — §16.5.4 v2.12's single banner surface, DR.7(4) — so it renders `degraded` as the spec requires, last-good data behind `STALE_ROOM_COPY`; the bare recap pointer, "no draft yet" and "Draft not found" cards have no banner and §16.5.4 forbids inventing a one-off treatment, so they keep the error-with-retry surface and keep the gate. Implemented by moving the scheduled-lobby branch AHEAD of the gate (never by weakening the gate's condition — R430's inert-gate shape is explicitly forbidden by a new pin), reasoning recorded in `room-health-ops.ts` and `room-health-ops.test.ts`, and the count pin corrected: `absentDraftIsHonest(health)` still 2, `health === 'degraded'` still 3, plus a new position pin that the scheduled branch precedes the gate. **NOT filed to §3:** the stop condition is for a spec that is ambiguous or wrong, and §16.5.4 is neither; D191(3) is this same PR's own build-mechanics entry, and a fix cycle is where an over-broad remedy in it gets corrected.
- **R430 · should-fix · F56's un-staged rule 1 had no owning row, and its stated reason was over-broad — TAKEN, F79 filed, F56's disclosure corrected with a NEW MEASUREMENT that goes further than the finding.** R430's diagnosis is confirmed — `invalidateQueries` bypasses `staleTime`, and the room calls it on `leaguesKeys.detail(leagueId)` from `use-draft.ts:335` (the R271 path), `use-draft.ts:573` and `use-draft-controls.ts:55,236`, while `retryRoom` calls `detail.refetch()` directly. **And there is a fourth site the finding did not name, inside the D94 lobby itself:** `draft-lobby.tsx:136-149` invalidates `leaguesKeys.detail(leagueId)` every `AUTO_START_POLL_MS` (5s) whenever `autoStartPollMs` is non-null — which is any instant within `AUTO_START_WATCH_MS` (2 minutes) **or already past**. Measured on the local stack: a `LC31FIX D94` league (scheduled, no drafts row, instant ~90s out) with `/api/leagues/<id>` blocked at `window.fetch` logged **8 blocked requests in ~20s with no user action and no mutation**. So **D191(4)'s "a mounted lobby cannot be made to refetch from the page" is WITHDRAWN**, and F56's disclosure is corrected rather than merely narrowed. What still could NOT be staged is the *threshold*: both failure shapes (a rejected `fetch` and a resolved 503 `Response`) park at `fetchStatus: 'paused'` / `fetchFailureCount: 1` in this pane — React Query's offline pause, with `document.visibilityState: 'hidden'` throughout (the same limit the reviewer hit for R428) — and a paused fetch then swallows every later invalidate, so the count never reaches `FETCH_FAILURES_FOR_BANNER`. Dispatched `online` / `focus` / `visibilitychange` and set `networkMode: 'always'` on both the client defaults and the query's own options; it did not clear. **F79** carries the staging shape.
- **R431 · nit · F78's inventory was short by one and self-contradictory — TAKEN, corrected and grown.** Counted: `031_draft_queue_replace.sql` asserts `'A player can appear in the queue only once.'` ×1 (:210) and `'You do not manage this queue.'` ×6 (:249, :258, :277, :288, :310, :335) = **seven**, matching the seven line numbers the row already listed and the PR body's "seven times", while the prose said "six". Two members added: `082:85`'s `'A queue can hold at most 500 players.'` (asserted at `031:224`), which is user-reachable through `queueFromList`'s append mode where the composed `finalOrder` can exceed the cap the TS `.max(500)` only guards on `upsertQueue` (`draft-service.ts:698`); and `draft-service.ts:399`'s `` `queue read failed: ${…}` ``, flagged as what it is — a thrown internal message, not a friendly refusal — so one migration retires the lot.
- **R432 · nit · the nominating fill is silently dropped on every freshly-opened nomination — TAKEN as an explicit precedence plus a pin, not as prose alone.** 085/087 set `high_bidder_team_id = on_clock_team_id` at open (087:2205-2212), so the nominator carries both moving marks until someone raises, and `cn`'s tailwind-merge kept the last fill/border pair — the money mark — dropping the accent pair entirely. §16.3's colour-independent status was never at risk (both badges render), but the PR's "the three compose" claim overstated. The stacked conditionals are now an explicit ternary so the precedence lives in the code rather than emerging from the merge, with no change to a single rendered pixel, and `auction-room.test.ts` pins both the ternary and the badges' independence.
- **R433 · nit · the `You` badge was pinned by exact source whitespace — TAKEN.** `'>\n            You\n          </Badge>'` broke on any Prettier reflow. All three word pins are now `/>\s*You\s*<\/Badge>/`-shaped.
- **R434 · nit · F75's discharge was caught only by SOURCE pins — TAKEN, and given a behavioural pin by extracting the seam.** The disclosure was honest (probe C reddened 2 of 24, both source, while both behavioural chat pins passed in both states) but the coverage gap was real: the behavioural pins drove sinks they built themselves and never `use-draft.ts`'s wiring, which is where F75 actually lives, and no node test could reach a handler defined inside a `useEffect` (this repo has no jsdom or testing-library). The handler body is now `applyChatBroadcast` in `use-draft-feed-sink.ts` — same code, same two rules, no QueryClient (the R271 refresh arrives as a callback, so the module keeps its import graph) — and three behavioural pins drive it: a broadcast delivered mid-fetch survives the resolve, R271 fires for a system post BEFORE the push and never for a member message, and a malformed record is dropped before either side runs. Breaking the seam's push reddens 2 of 26.

**Reviewer batch (adversarial review of PR #174 — L.C2.1, the nominate/bid routes + hooks + the budget mirror, `main...feat/M3-L.C2.1-nominate-bid-api` @ `d0e3a9a`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — two should-fixes, three nits. All five taken same-branch same-day; mechanics at D190.**

**Adjudicated FOR the Builder first, so it is not re-litigated:** D189(2)'s argument that the route-layer integrity check is NOT D157(11)'s rejected in-body shape was accepted in full — the RPC's replay semantics are untouched for every caller (034's E2 pins, the wire suite's amount-999 replay, pgTAP, the future sim), and the service never refuses a *replay*, only refuses to *attribute* the returned row to this caller. Rejections (a) raw 23505 and (c) D143 position-inference do not apply to it. The design stands; its DISCRIMINATOR was the defect.

- **R420 · should-fix · `draft-service.ts:572` and `:609-613` — the F65 integrity check discriminated on values EVERY league member can read, so F65's live-proven false success was still reachable through the shipped route while four ledger sites claimed it was refused unconditionally — TAKEN, fixed, pinned RED-first with the reviewer's own probe.** `draft_bids` RLS is `FOR SELECT USING (is_league_member(league_id))` with no column restriction (083:132-133), so any member reads every row's `action_id`, `player_id`, `amount` and `nomination_seq`. The reviewer's live probe: **mgr3 — a non-nominator during BIDDING — POSTed the nominate route with mgr2's `action_id` plus the (player, amount) read straight off `draft_bids`, and got HTTP 200 carrying `bid.team_id` = mgr2's team.** The shipped pin passed only because it happened to pick opening_bid 1 against a $2 raise; it would have stayed green if the check compared amount alone or player alone, and the converse (`nomination_seq` under the same policy) is symmetric. Blast radius was bounded — nothing written, no money moved, the settle-invalidate corrects the transient false "success" — but the CLAIM SITES said more than the code did. **Fix (the reviewer's preferred option, taken over narrowing the claims): IDENTITY is the discriminator.** The returned row's `team_id` is compared to the caller's ACTING SEAT — own `league_members.team_id`, or on a mock `config.mock.human_team_id` — resolved by the same helper the queue writers already use, renamed `resolveActingSeat` and re-documented as mirroring the RPCs' own team resolution (089:1201/1476). The argument comparison is KEPT as the second arm (it catches a caller reusing their OWN id across verbs, where the seat matches by construction). `nominatePlayer`/`placeBid` take `userId`; the routes pass `user.id`, which they already held. **The reviewer's exact probe is now the pin** — the read premise measured as mgr3, the forgery built ONLY from what that read returned, both directions, `not.toContain` on the other manager's team id, nothing written and the high bid AND its holder unchanged.
- **R421 · should-fix · `draft-service.ts:506-507` — the one user-facing string this PR authors was developer jargon and its remedy was false — TAKEN, replaced, pinned.** `ACTION_ID_REUSED_MESSAGE` read *"That action id was already used for a different action — a nomination and a bid never share one. Please try again."* `client-fetch.ts:52` surfaces a string `error` body verbatim as `LeagueActionError.message` and `use-draft-auction.ts:35-36` instructs callers to show it "as-is — never paraphrased", so a manager mid-auction read "action id"; and **"Please try again" was actively false** — an action_id is consumed forever (R125), so retrying that submit returns the same 409 every time. Spec §16.3 requires races to resolve with friendly product copy and tasks-M3 §4 rule 8 puts every bid-path refusal in that class. New copy: **"That didn't go through — we couldn't confirm it as yours. Check the player and the price, then place it again."** — no internal identifier, and a remedy that works (a fresh gesture mints a fresh id; the hooks' settle-invalidate has already refetched the room).
- **R422 · nit · the branch no longer merged cleanly after the sibling L.C2.2 landed as `3f5ddcc` — TAKEN, `main` merged as `d447d93`.** Two conflicts, no semantic overlap: `draft-service.ts`'s docblock (BOTH "L.C2.x adds…" paragraphs kept) and `PROGRESS-leagues.md` (main's ticked L.C2.2 §2 line taken beside this branch's ticked L.C2.1 line; all three session-log rows kept, newest first). Counters re-grepped on the merged tree: `main` was D188 / F76 / R413, this branch's D189 / F77 stand, so this cycle mints D190 / R420–R424 (no new F-row: R423 widens F77 instead).
- **R423 · nit · F77 was scoped too narrowly to cover the class two reviews found in one day — TAKEN, F77 widened in place.** Its Owner cell already read "the next task that touches `makePick` / `mapDraftRpcError`", so ownership needed no re-scoping; the TITLE (`makePick` maps an unknown player's P0002…) and the single named pin (`draft-queue-api-db.test.ts`) did. F77 now names **`mapDraftRpcError`'s P0002 arm** (`draft-service.ts:98-100`) as the defect and enumerates its measured consumers: `makePick` plus the FOUR commissioner routes R412 flagged — `reverse-bid` (087:567-572, a second Reset-pick on an already-reversed pick), `budget` (087:726, a retired franchise), `reassign` (090:652/671/716), `move-player` (090:947/956) — and records that once the arm passes the RPC's message through, **`mapAuctionRpcError` becomes a redundant wrapper to DELETE in the same change**, with the auction verbs' existing P0002 pin staying green as the proof it was redundant. `main`'s D188(8) forward-referenced this row for exactly this widening; the two now agree.
- **R424 · nit · `auction-budget.ts:79-81`'s parity claim was false for malformed knobs — TAKEN, clause fixed with a measurement.** The docblock said `auctionKnobsOf` "Reads the knobs the same way (a non-integer or missing value falls to the default)". Measured on the local stack: `coalesce(('{"a":null}'::jsonb->>'a')::int, 200)` → **200** and `'{}'` likewise, but `coalesce(('{"a":"abc"}'::jsonb->>'a')::int, 200)` → **ERROR 22P02** `invalid input syntax for type integer: "abc"` — COALESCE never sees a value. So on a malformed knob the mirror silently defaults where the SQL raises: more forgiving than the twin it claimed parity with. The clause now states the divergence, why it stays (a panel that throws is worse than one drawn off a default) and why it is unreachable (§7.3.8's typed settings writes), rather than claiming away a difference that exists. ## Review findings — 2026-08-19 (M3 batch 7 — L.C1.6)

**Reviewer batch (adversarial review of PR #171 — L.C1.6, migration 088 + pgTAP 037 + the client half, `main...feat/M3-L.C1.6-auction-realtime`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — one should-fix (a real correctness hole in a claim the PR makes), four nits. All taken same-branch same-day; mechanics at D185; F75 filed; spec → v2.12.7.**

- **R401 · should-fix · the bid feed's "run-pure by construction / the reset's one event empties a held cache" claim (D184(3)) had a hole in exactly the window the join-refetch opens — TAKEN, fix shape (b) buffer-and-replay, pinned RED-first.** Mechanism: `SUBSCRIBED` → `invalidateQueries(feed)` starts a refetch (snapshot at T0); the `'draft_bids'` handler did `getQueryData → reduceBidEvent → setQueryData`; React Query REPLACES the cache with the fetch result on resolve, discarding every interim `setQueryData`. So a bid landing in the window was lost; rows VOIDED in it (cancel/undo/reset) came back as zombies from the pre-void snapshot; after a reset run-1 zombies merged with run-2 INSERTs at seq 1 until the next rejoin; the first fetch dropped events outright. The feed has no gap detector, so nothing repaired it until another confirmed join. D184(3)'s "cannot happen by construction" sentence was false — **withdrawn in place with the mechanism named.** Fix: NEW `use-draft-feed-sink.ts` (`createFeedSink` — FIFO queue, drained only while `fetchStatus === 'idle'`, a `QueryCache` subscription drains on settle; generic over the reducer), `use-draft.ts` pushes every `draft_bids` event through it and disposes it with the channel. Why (b) over (a): the drafts-event detector is blind in the very window (the interim write may still be in the cache when the `drafts` event arrives, and later `drafts` events compare only the current high bid — a lost historical bid or a cancelled nomination's zombies at a shared seq never trip it) and leans on intra-transaction delivery order. Pin: `use-draft-feed-sink.test.ts` (**18**) — mechanism control, window, hold, first-fetch, dedupe, ZOMBIES, CROSS-RUN, FIFO, error-settle, immediate path, no-cache drop, reducer-doubt via a live `QueryObserver`, dispose, spine source pins. **RED against the pre-fix handler shape: 7 of 16**, on the survival assertions; reverted ⇒ green. NOT deferred to L.C3.1 (the reviewer's instruction; the room is about to consume this feed).
- **R402 · nit · `use-draft-bids.ts` hand-rolled offset paging that `page-all.ts` already warns against (short-page stop without a count; order not ending in a UNIQUE column) — TAKEN.** Now `pageAll(...)` with `{ count: 'exact' }` and `.order('id')` as the final key; `DRAFT_BIDS_PAGE` removed; source-pinned (the exact order sequence). Theoretical today (hosted `max_rows` = 1000; live rows unique on (seq, amount) in practice) but the CLAUDE.md "exactly 1000 rows looked like the whole table" class.
- **R403 · nit · tasks-M3 §2:35 still read "non-strict Zod parses" while the PR said the claim was CORRECTED (the correction lived only in `use-draft-ops.ts` + D184(4)) — TAKEN.** The §2 line is amended in place with a dated note naming the real mechanism (plain interfaces + `isDraftsRecord`/`isPickRecord` structural guards; named-field copy is why additive keys never leak).
- **R404 · nit · two precision slips at three sites (088:58, 088:295, spec §12.14 row) — TAKEN, all sites plus the same phrases in this file.** "NO DDL" is false (CREATE FUNCTION/TRIGGER are DDL; `CREATE TRIGGER` takes ShareRowExclusiveLock on `draft_bids`) → "no table/column/index/policy change"; "cancel/end = 1" → "cancel = 1, end = up to 1" (`draft_end` in the nominating phase: 087's helper finds no live nomination, returns 0, emits nothing). 088's per-writer paragraph corrected too; spec → **v2.12.7** (the v2.12.6 cache sentence corrected in the same entry).
- **R405 · nit · pre-existing, NOT this PR — 026's integer fixture ADPs vs restored players (the R387/R395/F60 class).** Already routed: owned by the pending 025/026 fixture-hardening chip. Not fixed here; recorded as already-routed.

## Review findings — 2026-08-18 (M3 batch 6 — L.C1.5, FINAL fix round)

**Nine findings on PR #159: R375-R377 from the stack-owning reviewer's verification pass, R378-R383 from four independent static lenses that read the diff only. VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — one BLOCKER-class, four should-fix, four nits.** Merge target `main` @ 4930bd8; `git merge-tree` clean. **The framing that matters: every pin involved passed. The lenses found what a live verification structurally could not, and three of the six are further doors into the same D160(8) insolvent/stuck-clock state R367 was filed for — R378 being R367's exact species recurring INSIDE R367's own fix. That is four consecutive rounds in which a correction re-introduced its own defect class.**

- **R378 · BLOCKER-class · the E28 arm-3 gate reproduced ONE of the award's TWO refusals, and at a settings-legal `auction_min_bid = 0` the arithmetic that masked the missing one disappears — TAKEN, fixed in the helper.** §3b's header promised "THE COMPARISON IS THE AWARD'S, RE-ASKED AFTER THE WRITE" and implemented it as the single test `v_high_bid <= v_max_bid`. `draft_tick`'s award arm asks **two** things: `open_slots < 1` (E27, `087:3479`) and `price > max_bid` (`087:3484`), and every other consumer pairs them (`draft_force_pick 087:2168-2173`, `draft_nominate 085:478`) because 084:349's `CASE WHEN v_open <= 0 THEN 0` makes a complete roster's `max_bid` a **semantic** zero — at which point `high_bid <= max_bid` is no longer the affordability question. At `min_bid >= 1` the gap is masked (`high_bid >= min_bid >= 1 > 0`, so the money arm raises anyway, with a message about dollars); at **`auction_min_bid = 0`, which is legal** (`league-settings.ts:220` = `min(0)`; 084:210 names the $0 league), both nomination writers open AT min_bid, so an unraised nomination stands at $0 and the gate computed `0 <= 0` and RETURNED. `draft_auction_solvent`'s floor there is `remaining >= 0`. **Driven:** budget $200 / min_bid $0 / total_rounds 2, t2 the standing high bidder at $0 with one pick; `draft_move_player(..., t2, null, 50)` filled its last slot, committed, and every tick then raised E27 into `auction_failures` forever. **Fix:** the gate re-derives `open_slots` alongside `max_bid`, its pass condition is `v_open >= 1 AND v_high_bid <= v_max_bid`, and the capacity case gets **its own sentence** (folding it into the max-bid message prints "$0 max bid" and sends the commissioner after money instead of a roster slot). **The coverage gap was the fixture, not the pin:** new **§I(c)** on a min_bid-$0 world (LM), one unit of `open_slots` either side, plus a min_bid-$1 pin proving the arm is the award's first question rather than a $0 special case. **Probe 7 → 5 of 199 RED**, reverted.
- **R379 · should-fix · `draft_reset` left the previous run's `draft_bids` live at sequence numbers the restart re-issues, so `draft_undo`'s auction on-clock recovery could seat the WRONG franchise — TAKEN, both halves.** `nomination_seq` IS `current_pick_number`; `draft_reset` rewinds it to 1 (`087:2573`) and `draft_start_internal` re-issues from there (`084:692`/`084:697`), while the recovery lookup (`087:1423`) had **no run discriminator at all** — no `voided_at` filter (deliberately: it must read rows the undo just voided) and no time bound. Two runs' nominations therefore collide on one sequence number, and since the seq→nominator map is not positional (§8.6.7(c) skips complete rosters) the earliest row names a DIFFERENT franchise. **Fix (a):** `draft_reset` stamps its run's rows `voided_at` — rows KEPT, §12.5 stays append-only, the same posture as the `draft_picks` soft-undo beside it — and reset is added as situation **(c)** in the D162 enumeration at `087:230-250` (whose lead-in said "exactly two situations" and now says three), in the spec (**v2.12.4**) and in `voided_at`'s writer inventory, which had said "written ONLY by two sites". **Fix (b):** the lookup scopes to `b.created_at >= v_draft.started_at`, the one discriminator available to a reader that must see voided rows, with a LOUD refusal when `started_at` is NULL on a live/paused draft rather than a silently widened window. Pinned both ways in §K, including the unscoped measurement that shows the ambiguity is real. **Probes 8 and 9 → 1 of 199 RED each**, reverted.
- **R380 · should-fix · `draft_reassign_pick`'s exclusivity check was blind to the one player who must not be assigned: the one under nomination — TAKEN.** On an auction the nominated player has **no** `draft_picks` row until the award writes it (`087:3497`), so a sweep of `draft_picks` passes for exactly him; nothing else on the path reads `current_nomination` (the E28 arms are about money; the §3b gate returns silently when the receiving team is not the high bidder). The award's INSERT then hits `uniq_draft_player_live` (065:178), ARM 2.6's `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS` (`087:3581`) swallows it into `auction_failures`, and the nomination never clears — the same stuck clock, reached through the board instead of through the money. `draft_move_player` cannot reach it (it requires a live pick), which is why the guard lives on reassign and only there. Refusal points at `draft_cancel_nomination` — the verb this task shipped. **Probe 10 → 3 of 199 RED**, reverted.
- **R381 · should-fix · the no-drift pin whose entire job is preventing R367 from recurring was satisfied by a COMMENT — TAKEN, and the weakness was measured rather than argued.** `pg_proc.prosrc` is raw body text INCLUDING comments; `draft_adjust_budget` names the arm-3 helper twice (the R367 comment at `087:776` and the `PERFORM` at `087:781`), so deleting the call and keeping the comment left the pin GREEN. **Proof, not assertion: probe 1 was re-run with exactly that mutation and the pre-R381 predicate still evaluated `TRUE`.** All three sibling pins (`036:230/238/244`) now match the CALL FORM as each helper is actually called (`PERFORM public.X(` for the two gates, `:= public.X(` for the void helper, which returns a count) and assert **cardinality** (`count(*) = N`), because `bool_and` over a shrunken set also returns TRUE. Probe 1's red set consequently GREW by exactly pin 13 — **3 of 181 → 4 of 199** — which is the finding, measured.
- **R375 · should-fix · the stated justification for the eleven-verb mock sweep was false — TAKEN (the sweep KEPT, the reason replaced).** The 087 banner and 036 §M both said "025 already pins their mock refusal" is a claim about function bodies that no longer exist. **It is not:** `025_mock_draft_mode.sql:765-782` pins the mock refusal of `draft_set_clock`/`draft_reassign_pick`/`draft_move_player`, `supabase test db` runs 025 against the fully migrated 001-087 chain, and 025 calls them positionally with fewer arguments — resolving to the new arities through the defaults. Those pins exercise the **post-087 bodies**. The true reason for the sweep is CO-LOCATION: three of the seven were DROP+CREATEd here, so 036 pins the eleven in the post-087 world BESIDE 025's rather than instead of them. **Third instance in this PR of a justification outrunning the facts** — v2.12.3 says exactly why that is dangerous.
- **R382 · nit · pin 127's description inverted the causality — TAKEN (description only; the pin and its arithmetic were right).** It said a cross-team move is refused "because the SLOT it consumes is what shrinks the max bid". From 084:349-350 consuming a slot **raises** max_bid by one min_bid: t2 goes 151/2/150 → 149/1/149, where the $2 price costs $2 and the slot rebates $1, net −$1. The section's own setup comment stated it correctly. Reworded to the measured cause — t2 sits at exact equality after the $49 correction, so any net reduction refuses.
- **R383 · nit · the §M zero-side-effect pin said "measured rather than inferred", and for ten of the eleven verbs it was inferred — TAKEN by WIDENING, not by narrowing the claim.** The counter summed `draft_picks` + `draft_bids` for the mock, and on that fixture only `draft_force_pick` could have added a row to either; every other verb writes where the counter did not look — `leagues.status`/`drafts.status` (reset, end), `drafts.config` (set_clock), `drafts.nomination_order` (set_order), `drafts.budget_adjustments` (adjust_budget), `league_chat` (all). Pointedly, pin 194 one line earlier singles out `draft_reset` as the one whose bypass is an outright §8.8 breach *because it writes leagues.status* — the exact column the composite did not read. Now a 025-§F-style capture of the WHOLE drafts row and the WHOLE leagues row (so `updated_at` alone falsifies a smuggled UPDATE) plus pick/bid/chat/liveness counts. **Probe 11 → 2 of 199 RED; the pre-R383 composite re-run under the identical mutation turned 1** — it watched a mock whose league and draft rows had just been rewritten and reported zero side effects.
- **R376 · nit · the one-off `draft-board-autopick-db.test.ts` red filed as ledger row F70 — TAKEN.** The "re-run without an intervening reset" explanation does not hold: that file carries an error-checked throwing `cleanup()` in both `beforeAll` (`:170`) and `afterAll` (`:224-225`, `:302-305`), hardened after this lane burned on it twice (R285, R286, the F53 class). NOT reproduced this cycle; routed with the F56 shape (observed output, "not reproduced", what to capture next time before re-running).
- **R377 · nit · PROGRESS's spec pointer still read "v2.9.1 (LAW)" — TAKEN.** Stale on `main` identically, so not introduced here, but this PR moves the spec to v2.12.4 and shipping without touching it would leave the pointer more wrong than it found it. Now v2.12.4 with the intervening versions listed.

It also raised and then voided an overload hazard: `CREATE OR REPLACE` with trailing DEFAULT args REPLACED the 3-arg function on a stale DB rather than overloading it (`pg_proc` count 2, and 034 pins that count). **R331's record-arm reasoning was tested rather than read and upheld on all three rejections** — narrowing the replay lookup would re-open 23505 (the same argument that declined the `unique_violation` wrapper — the two positions are consistent, and the unqualified lookup is *why* no wrapper is owed); argument-consistency would redden both shipped E2 pins (the bid replay sends amount 999 and asserts 6; the nominate replay sends a different player); and position inference breaks under D143's cancel-and-renominate, false-refusing a legitimate reconnect retry. - **R330 · should-fix · THE HEADLINE — `draft_place_bid` took only an amount, so a bid in flight across a nomination boundary was applied to whatever player was live when it executed — TAKEN, fixed IN THE RPC (optional identity args + both arms pinned + its own probe)** — the insert took `player_id` from `current_nomination` and `nomination_seq` from `current_pick_number`, both read fresh under the lock, so the RPC could not know what the caller was looking at and E2 did not help (a first-time submit carries a fresh action_id). If nobody raises, 086 awards that player at that price; a manager becomes high bidder on a player they never saw. The snake analogue cannot mis-target because `draft_make_pick` carries `player_id`. §5's sketch prints the amount-only signature, but the same paragraph says "Builder finalizes exact fields" — LATITUDE, not a constraint — and no residual was recorded anywhere (085 banner, the D-entry — then `D147`, renumbered to `D157` by R328 in this same cycle — and the PR body, all three silent). **Resolved (orchestrator decision: fix now in the RPC, do not defer to L.C2.1 — the RPC is the server-authoritative boundary, a route guard would leave the sim, the tests and every future caller exposed, and L.C1.4's completion path awards on this data):** `draft_place_bid` now takes `p_nomination_seq INTEGER DEFAULT NULL` and `p_player_id TEXT DEFAULT NULL` and refuses a mismatch with §16.3's "just went off the board" copy family, checked the moment the live nomination is known and BEFORE the franchise/self-raise/raise/max-bid clauses so a stale bid gets the true reason. **Both arguments, because neither subsumes the other:** `player_id` catches the ordinary moved-on case; `nomination_seq` catches the two states where the SAME player is live under a DIFFERENT nomination — D143's cancel-and-renominate (the sequence number is not consumed) and an undone award returning a player to the pool at a later sequence. **All three arms pinned** (034 §F, pins 43/44/45/46): matching accepted, player-mismatch refused, seq-mismatch refused, and omitted-both unchanged — which is every other bid call in the file and in the wire suite. - **R329 · should-fix · the anti-snipe-disabled pin could not detect the mutation it advertised, and the branch's stated rationale was arithmetically FALSE — TAKEN (reworded everywhere + the discriminating pin ADDED + the silent counterpart recorded)** — the reviewer replaced `085:611–616` with an unconditional `GREATEST(current_deadline, now() + make_interval(secs => v_anti_snipe))` and **all 84 pins and all 3 wire cases stayed GREEN**; found independently by two lenses. The reviewer's better rationale is adopted: the zero branch is also what refuses to INVENT a deadline from NULL. And the previously **unpinned, unrecorded** counterpart now has both — pin 62: at anti_snipe 10 a bid landing after the clock read zero receives a FULL FRESH WINDOW (`now() + 10s`). Defensible under D128's letter and consistent with snake's tick-is-the-enforcer posture, but recorded deliberately rather than left as emergent behavior.

## Review findings — 2026-08-18 (DR batch 1)

**Reviewer batch (adversarial review of PR #157 — DR.1, the full-screen draft-room route, `main...feat/DR.1-fullscreen-route`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — one BLOCKER (a real regression on two surfaces), two should-fixes, three nits; ALL SIX TAKEN plus both lane-level recommendations; resolution on the SAME branch per house precedent.** *(The reviewer's own framing, and it is the durable output of this batch: **every claim in the PR that had been MEASURED held up** — the route-manifest diff, the same-cookie middleware differential in both directions, F66 measured on production builds both ways, the D147–D156 verbatim transcription, the shell-provider enumeration surviving an independent 98-file transitive closure. **Every claim that failed was one species: an assertion about the post-change world inferred from the INTENT of the change rather than observed**, written in the *proved* register beside claims that genuinely were proved. Each was one `grep`, one `wc -l`, or one DOM inventory from being caught. That pattern is now **tasks-DR §4.9**, a standing rule for the lane, and **DR.8's item 5 is extended to re-check disclosure PARAGRAPHS, not only F-rows** — three disclosures were wrong here and not one of them was an F-row.)*

- **R340 · BLOCKER · the route-group split REGRESSED a working exit on two surfaces, and every disclosure site asserted the opposite — TAKEN (both components fixed, six sites pinned, measured before and after).** Mechanism: on `main`, `src/app/app/layout.tsx` returned `<AppShell>`, which renders `<AppHeader />` inside `hidden lg:block`; `AppHeader` reads `useHeaderStore`, which `PageHeader` writes. Both components are byte-identical on `main` and this branch — so the lobby's and the launcher's *Back to league* **did render at ≥`lg` on `main` and render nowhere on this branch**. DR.1 did not create the mobile hole (tasks-DR §1 already named it); it widened a below-`lg` defect into an all-widths one, on the two surfaces nobody enumerated. **Reproduced independently before fixing** (dev-local :3123, a purpose-built SCHEDULED league where the dev-auth user is a plain manager, so `isCommish` is false): the lobby inventoried **one link, pointing DEEPER** — `…/draft?practice=1 :: Practice this draft` — and **zero buttons**; the launcher's past-pre-draft arm inventoried **zero links, zero buttons**; its pre-draft arm inventoried **zero links** and four controls that all go further in. The contradicted claim, verbatim (tasks-DR §1, repeated in D159(5) and the PR body): *"the lobby keeps Draft setup / Practice this draft, so no state is a dead end in the meantime"* — but **Draft setup is inside `{isCommish && …}`**, so a plain member never sees it. **Resolved:** `draft-lobby.tsx` gains an in-card *Back to league* **outside** the commissioner gate; `mock-draft-launcher.tsx` gains one at container level, **above the `preDraft` fork**, so both arms and every `MockList` state keep it. Not deferred to DR.2, per the finding. **Re-measured after the fix, same URLs:** lobby → **2 links** (`…/leagues/<id> :: Back to league` + the practice CTA), launcher pre-draft arm → **1 link** (the exit), launcher past-pre-draft arm → **1 link** (the exit) where it had none. New pin file **`src/components/draft/room-exits.test.ts` (5 pins)**, written to survive DR.2: every assertion runs against the source with **`<PageHeader …/>` elements deleted**, so a header can never satisfy them and they stay green when DR.2 removes those calls. **Four probes shown and reverted** — delete the lobby exit → 2/5 RED (both lobby pins); move it back inside `{isCommish && …}` → **exactly 1/5 RED** (the gate pin alone, proving it discriminates placement, not presence); delete the launcher exit → 2/5 RED; move it inside the `preDraft` arm only → **exactly 1/5 RED** (the both-arms pin). The correction is written at all three disclosure sites (tasks-DR §1, D159(5), the room docblock) and **the live room is now named as the one remaining exit-less state**, which is DR.2's Exit Draft to close.
- **R339 · should-fix · the C46 rename note claimed line numbers "still land" when every one was off by +22 — TAKEN (renumbered, and the offset proven wholesale).** The claim: *"the file is still 1013 lines … every `snake-draft-room.tsx:NNN` citation still lands (re-verified)"*. True of the `git mv`; false of the commit, which added a 22-line docblock above every landmark. Verified: `main` 1013 → branch 1035; `:389`→411, `:443`→465, `:450`→472, `:666`→688, `:719`→741, `:768`→790, and §1's `PageHeader` list `:666/:169/:250/:949/:969/:1001` was really 688/191/272/971/991/1023. **Six task banners (DR.2–DR.7) navigate by these numbers.** **Resolved:** after this cycle's own docblock corrections the file is **1052 lines** and the offset is **+39**; **tasks-DR §1 and the DR.2–DR.7 banners are renumbered** with each anchor also named by symbol (§4.9's preference — a symbol survives the next edit), and §3's D-entries / §6's dispositions are deliberately left at their as-authored numbers because §4 here quotes D147–D156 verbatim (both the note and the room docblock say "add 39" for those). The offset is established rather than spot-checked: **`main:snake-draft-room.tsx` line *N* is byte-identical to `draft-room.tsx` line *N+39* for every *N* in 101–1013**, the single exception being the renamed `export function` line — and every renumbered anchor was re-read by content afterwards.
- **R341 · should-fix · `(shell)/not-found.tsx`'s docblock was rewritten FOR accuracy and still opened with a false sentence — TAKEN, and the measurement turned out to be bigger than either side had it.** The sentence: *"Renders inside the app shell, so the nav survives and the user is never stranded."* **Measured on production builds, signed in, both revisions** — and the two halves disagree, which is why the claim survived so long: **server-rendered HTML has NO shell** (`/app/nfl/ZZZ` → 404, branch 17,621 bytes / `main` @ 9c81f7c 17,109 bytes, `pr-rail-strip` ×0, `h-header` ×0, no sidebar links; control `/app/lists` on the same session → 200, 44,187 bytes, `pr-rail-strip` ×1, `h-header` ×2, sidebar "Home" ×2), while **after hydration the shell IS there** (same URL, fresh `navigate`: DOM 34,450 bytes branch / 33,938 `main`, `pr-rail-strip` ×1, two sidebar "Home" links). **Numbering:** R706–R712 as the reviewer filed them; checked against `main`, the open halt branch `halt/M4-L.D1.2-schedule-engine-Q30` (#248) and `docs/DR2-draft-room-v2` (#180) — the only prior "R706" string is D303's own number-note pointer to #248's residue remark, not a filed finding. ### Should-fix

- **R706 · should-fix · `ingest-week.ts` — the stats write preceded the enqueue, so a crash between the two PostgREST calls lost the delta permanently (at-most-once), and the named net did not repair it — TAKEN: order swapped (queue → stats), D303(2) rewritten, the wrong claim withdrawn, F218 filed.** The reviewer was right on both halves: the loss was real (Vercel `maxDuration=120`, ~1,500 rows in 3 batches — the window is not theoretical), and §23.2's reconciliation "alerts, never silent fix" — it would have NAMED a player's unscored final line, not re-enqueued it. Enqueue-first makes the pair at-least-once for free: the stored row stays stale, the next poll re-detects, the PK dedupes. Pinned over the stack with a db whose `player_stats` upsert throws (queue holds 6 at 18:20 / rows still 18:00 / drained / re-poll 6 updated · 6 enqueued / rows land at 18:20); probe (order swapped back) → `expected [] to deeply equal ['syn-g1-def', …]`, reverted. **One thing the finding did not have:** enqueue-first opens the mirror-image window — a drain that reads `player_stats` between the two calls scores the OLD row, and nothing re-enqueues afterwards. Because both stamps are the one injected instant, `updated_at >= enqueued_at` is a readiness predicate the worker can test (pinned equal on a clean poll, older-than after the crash), so L.D2.2 leaves a not-ready row queued — that obligation, and the single-transaction door, are **F218**.
- **R707 · should-fix · `ingest-week.ts` — a schedule game in a week absent from `nfl_weeks` threw the WHOLE poll after the tracker recorded success, so the live week went stale with no `stats_degraded` banner (the E45 failure mode) — TAKEN: the integrity throw is kept ONLY for the week being ingested (and fires before the first write); every other calendar-less week is skipped, counted (`weeks.outsideCalendar`) and named in `reasons`.** Latent today (sleeper carries no kickoffs) and real at L.D3.1 (nflverse `schedules` carry weeks 19–22 with kickoffs; 039 seeds 1–18). Pinned with the D146 pair: week 18 (039's last row) maintained, week 19 (one past it) skipped / 1 counted / the reason literal, the live week's 6 rows landed and enqueued, both games stored; `io.week = 19` refuses with nothing written. Probe (poll-wide throw restored) → the pin dies on `nfl_weeks has no row for 2026 week 2`, reverted. `IngestWeeksReport` gained `outsideCalendar` (touched = updated + unchanged + outsideCalendar); the six existing `weeks` literals carry `outsideCalendar: 0`.

### Nit

- **R708 · nit · `ingest-week-db.test.ts` — fixture hygiene (F199) was prefix-scoped to a shape real data will share — TAKEN.** `nfl_games` is now deleted BY ID (`SYN_GAME_IDS` — the scenario's three plus R707's `syn-`-prefixed 18/19 pair), every `score_fanout` drain and the queue reader are `syn-%`-scoped, `storedGames` reads by id. Harmless today (local `players` empty, sleeper writes no games); after L.D3.1 a local stack with real week-2 rows survives this suite. The (2026, 18) bounds joined the restore set because R707's sibling moves them; `afterAll` still asserts every 2026 week NULL.
- **R709 · nit · `weekBounds` — "kept once set" was only kept while every in-week game stayed `final` — TAKEN AS A RECORD with a pin, not made sticky.** The re-derivation is the intended semantics: a week with a live in-week game is playing, whatever it read a poll ago, so a later non-final game (moved in, or a provider status regression) re-opens it (NULL) and the stamp is re-taken at the next all-final observation. D303(4) now says so; pinned ended → re-opened → re-stamped at the NEW instant, sibling kept. No consumer reads the column yet (measured — the writer, its suites, `database.ts`).
- **R710 · nit · `toStatRow` — `is_live = status !== 'final'` read a postponed-game player as live — TAKEN.** `isOpenStatus` (in-week AND not final) now serves both `is_live` and the week-level `anyGameOpen` fallback — one definition. Pinned with all three statuses: `postponed` → false; `scheduled` and `live` → true.
- **R711 · nit · F216 should carry the game-window rule the stamp depends on — TAKEN as an F216 amendment.** L.D2.3 keeps polling until every in-week game has been OBSERVED `final`; the window's close is the observation, not the schedule clock; pin it with a game that goes final one poll after the scheduled close.
- **R712 · nit · `readWeeks` was the one reader without a cap assertion — TAKEN.** `POSTGREST_ROW_CAP = 1000` (config.toml `max_rows`), `rows.length >= cap` throws. Pinned on an in-memory chainable client (1000 → throws with the literal message; 999 → the poll completes with the three empty-section reasons). Vacuous at 18 rows, uniform under rule 10.

**Three questions the Builder put to review were RULED (house-convention calls, not Chris calls):**

1. **`P0001 → 409` GOVERNS for the in-season family.** Every P0001 that 111/112/113 raise is a *state* conflict on a well-formed request; nothing in `src/` branches on 400-vs-409 (`client-fetch.ts` surfaces the message regardless), so there is no behavioural regression, and the family is self-consistent because L.D4.1 composes the same mapper. **The code is right; the ledger CITATION was wrong — R772.**
2. **The second `.channel(` is spec-sanctioned** — §9.3 reads "one socket per client, ≤ 3 channels (current league, current draft, notifications)" — and the budget pin was amended honestly (it still asserts an exact two-element set over a recursive sweep of every non-test `.ts/.tsx` under `src/`). Doctrine holds throughout. **But the spine was not actually shareable — R769.**
3. **The F65(b) guard's hazard is real and the guard is warranted** — verified in the merged bodies, not on faith (`113:498-515` scopes the replay by `type` + `initiator_team_id` only; `111:622-634` checks `kind` only). **It was wrong for a case it ACCEPTED — R768.**

**Verified clean and NOT regressed by the fix round:** F227(f) clause by clause (the either-not-both field error, the reused-`action_id` count of 1, the three wire-level SQLSTATE tests, the refusal text verbatim with exclusivity NAMING the holding team, `drop.lineups[]` as the exact `[{week,'wr:0'},{week+1,null}]` literal, no `kept_in_locked_lineup` anywhere in the document, `caps.used_week_after` `toBe(2)` on a drop-only move); the loud-emptiness 500s on both reads; the strict-object DoD pin; and `single-room-tab.test.ts`'s channel-budget pin, which still asserts an EXACT two-element set over the recursive sweep — R769 moved no `.channel(` call, so the pin is unchanged and still load-bearing.

### Should-fix

- **R768 · should-fix · `transactions-service.ts:143-150` (and `schedule-service.ts:154`) — a COMMITTED add/drop reported to the caller as a failure. — TAKEN.** The guards compare client-supplied uuid strings byte-for-byte against uuids Postgres wrote; `z.uuid()` is case-insensitive (zod 4.3.6) and Postgres renders `uuid` lowercase, so an UPPERCASE `team_id`/`action_id` — a body the route's own schema accepts — reached the RPC, the move COMMITTED (roster row + transactions row), and the guard answered **409 "That didn't go through"** with the `action_id` consumed, so the retry the copy asks for could not succeed either. CLAUDE.md's "never let 'nothing happened' mean 'it worked'" in reverse, by the guard that exists to prevent it. Both suites used lowercase literals throughout, so nothing caught it. **Fix:** normalised ONCE at the schema in a new shared `src/lib/leagues/api/inseason-ids.ts` (`normalizedUuid = z.uuid().transform(v => v.toLowerCase())`), applied to `team_id` + `action_id` on add/drop and `action_id` on the Remix confirm, so the RPC and the guard both see the form the database returns. The guards keep every tooth — a reused id naming a different move, or a different seed, is still 409, asserted uppercase. Fixtures beside both reuse pins (`transactions-api-db` §6: uppercase replay → 200 + one row; uppercase FRESH move → 200 + committed + stored under the lowercase id; uppercase reuse for a different move → 409 with the other player still rostered. `schedule-api-db` §6: the same three at the confirm). Source pin in `inseason-routes.test.ts` so L.D4.1 inherits the rule with the mapper. **Probe:** reverting both schemas to bare `z.uuid()` reds **6 cells across 3 files**; restored byte-identically (`80f0f4ea…` / `f43e071f…`).
- **R769 · should-fix · `use-league-channel.ts:122-126` — the `league:<id>` spine was per-hook-instance and its D109(9) stale-registry sweep evicted OTHER LIVE INSTANCES OF ITSELF. — TAKEN.** Latent today (one caller) and guaranteed the moment L.D4.1 followed F233(a): `createBrowserClient` is a browser singleton so `getChannels()` is shared, realtime-js returns the EXISTING channel for a held topic, and B's mount removed A's live channel → A saw `CLOSED` → `onDrop` (an invalidate/refetch) + reopen in 1s → A's sweep removed B's → forever, two invalidations per cycle, `attempt` reset to 0 on every SUBSCRIBED so the backoff never grew out of it. The file's own docblock stated the opposite as the design, so **the code was made true rather than the claim weakened**: the spine is now a MODULE-LEVEL refcounted room per topic (`leagueRooms` / `joinLeagueRoom` / release), one channel fanned out to N handler maps, torn down only when the LAST subscriber releases; a late joiner gets `onJoin` on attach if the room is already live, because its cache may predate the room. Still exactly ONE `.channel(` in the file, so `single-room-tab.test.ts`'s budget pin is untouched. **Pinned behaviourally, not at the source** — new `use-league-channel-room.test.ts` (6 cells) mocks the singleton browser client and its channel registry: two consumers → **1 `.channel()` call, 0 removals, neither dropped**, each receiving only its own events; one release keeps the channel live for the other; the last release closes it; a stale release is idempotent; a different league is a different room. **Probe:** making `joinLeagueRoom` create a fresh room per join reds 4 of the 6 (`expected 2 to be 1` channels), restored to md5 `87cbefa2…`. **F233(a) amended to say HOW L.D4.1 joins**, not merely that it must not `.channel(`.
- **R770 · should-fix · `activity-service.ts:169` (with :202/:238) — the paging cursor was `created_at` alone against a `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` order, so every item sharing a page-boundary instant was served on NO page. — TAKEN.** Silent, and permanent for that item. No M4 writer produces such a tie today, but §13.2/§14's waiver processor (N `transactions` rows resolved atomically on one `now()`) and M6's `commissioner_move` (a transactions row + a system post in one transaction) both will. **Fix:** the cursor is composite — `before` + `before_id` on the way in, `next_before` + `next_before_id` on the way out — applied to BOTH source queries as PostgREST `or(created_at.lt."T",and(created_at.eq."T",id.lt."ID"))` (the exact inverse of the sort; values double-quoted because a timestamptz carries `.`, `:` and `+`, all structural in a filter string), with a lone `before_id` refused BY NAME rather than paging as if no cursor were sent. The filter string is an exported pure function so it is pinnable. `activity-service.test.ts`'s header had already CLAIMED this coverage — its tie test proved determinism, not cursor survival — so the header now says what the file actually pins. Fixtures both sides: pure (a same-instant pair split across two pages, with the negative control that the instant alone would have dropped one) and on the WIRE (`transactions-api-db` §7 writes two `league_chat` system posts at one explicit instant; page 1 returns both cursor halves, page 2 serves the tied row, and the instant-only control returns **0 items**). **Probe:** reverting both queries to `.lt('created_at', before)` makes page 2 **EMPTY** (`expected [] to deeply equal [ 'af7…a1' ]`); restored to md5 `339e952d…`.

## Review findings — 2026-09-03 (M4 batch — L.D4.2 FINAL RE-REVIEW, PR #255)

**Reviewer batch (fresh, independent — the second pass on this PR and the last one it gets: `feat/M4-L.D4.2-transactions-schedule-activity` @ `55601a4`, on `main` @ `f74094d`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE on ONE should-fix that was a PR-artefact correction with no code in it (R776, discharged by the orchestrator at merge) plus three nits (R777–R779). R768–R775 were each verified DISCHARGED by re-running the probes, not by reading the diff.** The reviewer re-ran the chain itself: `npm run test` **175 files / 3,286 tests passed** (its first run hit ONE red — `auction-realtime-db`, a file this branch never touches, timing out at 26s under full parallel load and **green 2/2 in 10.33s in isolation**; the second full run was clean, reproducing the Builder's); `test:db` **62 files / 4,498 asserts PASS** (unchanged — no migration); `test:gate` 24/24; type-check + lint clean; task-file counts re-measured per file **33 / 18 / 26 / 6 / 25 / 19 = 127 across 6 files**. All four probes reproduced and reverted byte-identically: **R768** (both schemas back to bare `z.uuid()` → 6 cells red across 3 files, `expected 409 to be 200`; md5 `80f0f4ea…` / `f43e071f…` restored), **R769** (a fresh room per join → 4 of 6 red, `expected 2 to be 1`; `87cbefa2…`), **R770** (both queries back to `.lt('created_at', …)` → page 2 EMPTY; `339e952d…`), and the **DoD** probe (`z.strictObject` → `z.object` → **9 failed / 43 passed (52)**; `f43e071f…`). Authority re-verified live and rolled back: all three RPCs `secdef=true`, `search_path=''`, no anon EXECUTE; as `anon`, `transactions`/`league_chat`/`matchups`/`league_weeks` all read **0**. Diff-wide: `main` untouched, no migration, no typegen (so the hand-written alias block is untouched), no HELD edit, zero `any` in added `src/` lines.

**The three substantive fixes were stress-tested, not accepted:**

- **R768's normalisation has no side effects and the guards keep their teeth.** Nothing echoes the client's string back (both routes return the RPC payload, which Postgres wrote lowercase — asserted at `transactions-api-db.test.ts:627`); the idempotency key is minted by `crypto.randomUUID()` (lowercase by spec) so a retrying client can never send a form that now differs; `activity-service.ts`'s `team_id`/`before_id` are deliberately NOT normalised because Postgres compares them as `uuid`, which is the rule `inseason-ids.ts`'s docblock states. Both negative controls are real: an uppercase id reused for a genuinely different drop is 409 **with P2 still rostered**, and at a different seed is 409 **with `schedule_seed` unmoved**.
- **R769's refcounted room survives the race walk.** StrictMode double-mount cannot orphan a channel — `open()` always suspends at `await supabase.auth.getSession()` before reaching `supabase.channel(...)`, and cleanup sets `disposed` + deletes the map entry first; there is no `await` between the last `if (room.disposed) return` (:161-163) and `room.channel = ch` (:168), so a release can never miss a channel the room then opens. Two leagues → two rooms (pinned :296). Doctrine holds: exactly one code-level `.channel(` (:165, `private: true`), zero `postgres_changes`, event names read out of `070_*.sql:280-292` / `:305-312` and matching `LEAGUE_CHANNEL_EVENTS` with the `{operation,table,schema,record}` envelope. `single-room-tab.test.ts`'s budget pin is **byte-untouched** by the fix round (`git diff 67add74..55601a4 -- …` empty) and still asserts an exact two-element set over a recursive non-test sweep.
- **The late-joiner `onJoin` (`use-league-channel.ts:239`) was RULED: keep it as built.** At mount the room is `'connecting'` when siblings attach, so N consumers of a fresh page cost N `onJoin` calls, one each at SUBSCRIBED — no storm. The extra invalidate fires only for a consumer attaching to an already-live room, whose cache genuinely may predate it, and the feed's consumers share one React Query key so it collapses to a single refetch. A silent attach would be CLAUDE.md's forbidden shape (inferring freshness from an absence) and would break §9.3's "never depend on having received a broadcast". No loop is possible — the join effect depends only on `leagueId`.
- **R770's composite cursor: no injection, `has_more` still measured, ties deterministic across BOTH sources.** Hostile values were run through both cursor schemas and every one was rejected (embedded `",id.gt."`, `,or(id.gt.0)`, a trailing `)`, a quote, a space). Encoding holds — supabase-js appends `or` through `URLSearchParams` so `+` is percent-encoded — and the quoted composite filter was confirmed against the live local PostgREST with a **non-UTC** offset (`…lt."2026-09-01T10:00:00.5+05:30"…` → 200). `has_more` is still the per-source `limit + 1` over-fetch measured AFTER the filter. Cross-source ties are safe: Postgres renders uuids lowercase at fixed dash offsets, so `sortKey`'s JS lexicographic compare agrees with `uuid` byte order, and the single `(T, ID)` pair is applied to both queries so a tied system post and transaction are cut on the same side. The wire fixture uses `TIE_INSTANT = '2098-06-01T12:00:00.5+00:00'` — fraction **and** offset — with an instant-only negative control.

But nothing writes a bracket score until L.D1.9 exists (today every bracket row is `DEFAULT 0` by construction, so the scored arm is inert and the ROLLED arm is what protects); F257(a) routes the closer to the task that decides the cell's pending word (NULL per E61 makes "written" = non-NULL) with L.D6.1's sweep as backstop; the destructive envelope is bounded to rounds whose EVERY score is exactly 0.00 — no non-zero score is ever destroyed (L6b/L6e). (2) **R840's gate cost is immaterial**: one `Index Scan using idx_matchups_league_week` per non-final prior-stage week (EXPLAIN shown), only while the prior stage is rolled-but-not-final (`IF NOT v_prev_final`), skipped entirely once the regular season is FINAL; a two-week round walks both of round r−1's weeks. (3) **The lift is the right posture and needs no ruling**: after round 1 finalizes behind a held week, the bracket permanently carries seeds from the pre-correction verdict with M6's edit as the escape — spec §23.4 already says a late correction is NOT auto-applied and surfaces as a flagged event the commissioner may apply ("keeps late corrections from silently flipping decided playoff games"); said in D318(5) and F257(b). The gap is only that no SIGNAL survives the lift — R846. (4) **R841's deviation is sound**: the calendar `waiting_*` states would fire for every in-season league every hour — no signal; the three non-calendar reasons are collected and WARNING'd on both jobs. (5) R842's K1b–K1e are real (an in-season `total_points` league with the pair stored → `waiting_regular_season` kind `points_race` → `complete` through the no-bracket arm, zero matchup rows); R843's three corrections verified (the bold (B) sentence ends at `over both weeks."`, the reading in the annotation with "(v2.16.26, R843)", §2 order L.D5.3 → L.D5.4 → L.D5.5, Q39 (D) struck in place to WHERE + ROW_COUNT).

**Reviewer batch (fresh, independent — the scoped pass on the fix diff `ae16ca8..ade6107` plus a no-regression sweep; the last pass this PR gets). VERDICT: CLEAN — R847 discharged, and its per-socket artefact EXPLAINED; three nits (R852 taken as record, R853 → F261, R854 → F261), and the loop merged on it.** The decision of the pass was R847's re-ruled gate question, and the reviewer answered it by finding the cause. Two temporary probe suites (deleted; tree clean) with the Phoenix logger attached: **probe 1** — one socket, six shapes × 3: `first` Y Y Y; `room` (the hook's release → open() sweep at 0 ms) MISS ×3; `awaited` (`await removeChannel(A)` → B) MISS ×3; `room-delay` (+1.5 s) Y Y Y; `unsub-only` Y Y Y; `keep-socket` Y Y Y — the discriminator `opens=1` on every deaf run and a `channel: error` ~155 ms after the leave. Mechanism read from the shipped code: `RealtimeClient.removeChannel` calls `disconnect()` when it removes the LAST channel; Phoenix's `teardown` closes the websocket after a `waitForBufferDone` tick (150 ms, up to 1.5 s); `connect()` is a no-op while disconnecting; a channel created in that window joins the DYING connection, gets `SUBSCRIBED`, then `triggerChanError` fires at the close and Phoenix's `onError` rejoins only `if (this.socket.isConnected())` — it is not, and `closeWasClean = true` means no socket reconnect ever. This explains every one of the fix-round Builder's fourteen observations (per socket = the socket is closed; rows in `realtime.messages`; service silent; a FIRST channel always calls `connect()`; continuous traffic delivers inside the window; "gap not the determinant" — the determinant is creation within the close window). **Client-side entirely — hosted behaves identically.** **Probe 2** — the REAL `joinLeagueRoom` with `createBrowserClient` mocked to one signed-in singleton, join → release → rejoin at 0 / 50 / 300 / 1500 ms × 2: **8/8 walks delivered 3/3 after the idle gap** — at 0/50 ms the room goes `live → error (+160 ms) → reconnecting + onDrop → +1 s new websocket → live + onJoin#2`; at 300/1500 ms clean. **The browser room does NOT go deaf** — `scheduleReopen` catches the `CHANNEL_ERROR` realtime-js surfaces and heals in ~1.0–1.2 s with one extra refetch; §9.3's refetch-on-join covers anything fired in the gap. **Ruling: (c)-with-cause — no go-live gate, no escalation.** The suite's second-write assertion is real (withheld the second door call → the cell red, md5 `2e35fb49…` restored, 3/3 × 3); no keep-warm write, no shortened gap.
