**Measured (LOCAL stack only — `.env.local` untouched, nothing hosted):** fresh `npx supabase db reset` 001–122 (`schema_migrations` max = 122) · `RESTORE_SCOPE=draft npm run restore:dev` · `npm run test:db` **71 files / 5,398 asserts, PASS** · `npm run test` **200 files / 3,632 tests, all green, first attempt (104.5 s)** · `npm run test:gate` **24 / 24** · `type-check` clean · `lint` clean · F199 census after the chain AND after the reviewer's probes: fixture players 0 · `vitest-%` leagues 0 · 2099 `nfl_games` 0 · 2099 stamped 0 · 2026 stamped 0 · `score_fanout` 0 · `system_flags` 0 (no dev in-season fixture was resident — 0 leagues after the reset). **The deliberate-break probe re-run by the reviewer:** `classifyCell`'s drift branch → `return null` ⇒ `reconcile.test.ts` + `reconcile-db.test.ts` **5 failed / 14 passed (19)** — the two pure drift pins, THE PROBE, the `total_points` cell, the final-week cell — restored, md5 `b5bcb60123fecb67857e1ade01ca27ff` before = after, `git status` clean. **The CLI against the local stack** (`npm run reconcile -- 2026` with the two env overrides): exit 1, `[ALERT] no_game_rows: 2026 week 1 (starts 2026-09-09T04:00:00+00:00) has ZERO nfl_games rows` at `ran_at 2026-09-08T03:08:39Z`, `reason: no_leagues_in_scope` — F228's gate alerted a week ahead, as the record says. **The Builder's numbers are all reproduced.**

### Must-fix

- **R876 · must-fix · `reconcile.ts:260–273` (`classifyCell`, the `post_window_correction` arm) + the §23.2 v2.16.32 annotation + D322(6) — the one classification that CAN swallow a real drift, and it does so PERMANENTLY and INVISIBLY.** On a `final` week, stored ≠ recomputed is explained away as soon as ANY starter's `player_stats.updated_at` is past `correction_window_ends_at` — and the finding is `info` (`console.log` on the route; not counted by the CLI's exit code). Two facts make this the common case rather than the rare one: (1) §23.4's own sentence — Sleeper applies corrections "up to and including Thursday", i.e. AFTER FieldScout's Thursday 06:00 ET close — so a corrected cell on a final week is the ordinary Friday state, not an edge; (2) `diffStats`'s `metaOnly` arm (`ingest-week.ts:395–430`, `is_live` / `game_id` / `source` moved) rewrites the row with `updated_at = stamp` and NO scoring delta, so a bookkeeping rewrite of a past week (a never-flipped game keeping that week hot, or L.E2's future correction sync) exempts the cell with nothing having moved. Once exempt, the cell is exempt for the rest of the season: a later rebuild bug, a hand edit, a door regression on that cell can never again reach `drift`. **Failing scenario:** week N final; RB1's line gets a Thursday-afternoon correction (post-window, lawful, stored stays); on Saturday `rebuild_team_week_results` (117) or a service-role edit puts the wrong number in T1's cell; every night from then on the job prints `[INFO] post_window_correction … RB1 moved after the correction window closed` and the wrong cell is never named. The classifier cannot subtract the correction (no history exists until M6 L.E2's `stat_correction_events`), which is exactly why the exemption must not be silent. **Fix (no design change):** (a) severity `warn` for `post_window_correction` — visible on the route's `console.warn` line and in `warns`, still not exit-1 — with the delta named in the message (`stored X ≠ recomputed Y, Δ Z`); (b) the arm cannot be made exact today (a `metaOnly` rewrite and a real correction both read as a moved `updated_at`, and the pre-correction line is gone), so RECORD the residual: an F-row (F268) saying that from the first post-window mover a final-week cell is checked no further until L.E2 lands `stat_correction_events`, whose deltas let the classifier recompute "as of finalization"; owner M6 L.E2 (the reconciliation gains the subtraction when the table exists); (c) the §23.2 annotation + D322(6) say "informational — and the cell is not drift-checked thereafter until L.E2" instead of implying the classification is exact. *(In M4 the arm is nearly dormant — nothing re-polls a week after the next week's `starts_at` (R880) — so no production cell is swallowed before L.E2; the fix is small and the record must be truthful before L.E2 makes it live.)*

- **R877 · must-fix · `reconcile.ts:578` (`started` includes `final`) + `:529–539` (`finalGamesByTeam` keyed on `players.team`, the CURRENT NFL team) + `:730–746` (F263(g) emitted per cell, every run) — `starter_final_game_no_line` fires EVERY NIGHT, for EVERY final week of the season, for EVERY started DNP, and it is an `alert` — the exit-1 signal.** Sleeper returns no line for a player who did not play (the synthetic provider's own contract, Q42: "scratched — never plays, never scores"), so every starter left in a lineup while inactive — a manager who did not update on Sunday morning, the most ordinary thing in fantasy — is "in a FINAL game with NO player_stats row" and stays so forever. By week 14 the nightly run carries every such starter from every league from every week since week 1, each an ALERT, and `npm run reconcile` — "the gates' hook", exit 1 on any alert — can never exit 0 for any league that ever started a scratch. That is §24.1's anti-pattern the Builder cited in D322(6), applied to the wrong finding. Second defect in the same check: `players.team` is the player's team TODAY; for a past week a traded player is attributed to his new team's game (a false alert on his old bye week; a missed one on his old team's final game) — the record does not say so. **Fix:** (a) bound the check in time to when it is actionable — the week's `nfl_weeks.correction_window_ends_at` not yet passed, OR passed within the last 24 h (so the Thursday at-window-close run — the finalization check R871 asked for — still sees it once); on older final weeks either skip it or emit `info` with a "seen before" reading; (b) name the current-team caveat in the message and the banner (the honest datum is the week's game the player's team played, which `nfl_games` gives only through `players.team` today; nflverse's `getInactives` — see R882 — is the real DNP-vs-gap discriminator and is unconsumed); (c) pin (a) at the boundary (window end + 24 h − 1 ms fires, + 1 ms does not — D146).

- **R878 · must-fix · `reconcile.ts:38–41` / `:192` (`game_not_final_late: 'warn'`) / `:338–350` — the ONE calendar state that stalls a league for good is classified BELOW the one that does not, and the record under-counts its cost.** A game the provider never flips (Q37's cancelled game; a status regression) keeps `weekBounds` (`ingest-week.ts:308–316`) from ever stamping `last_game_ends_at` (it needs EVERY in-week game final), so under 116 the league week can never leave `live` — `finalize_matchups` only NAMES a `live` week past its window (`116_week_workers.sql:1016–1018` / `:1040–1046` `v_live_past`), it never finalizes it — and under 115 every player who kicked off that week stays locked (F238's loud state). The week never finalizes; standings, the F4 chain and the playoff bracket behind it never advance. The reconciliation reports this as `[WARN] game_not_final_late` — `console.warn`, not counted by `alerts`, exit 0 — while `all_final_unstamped` (a week that merely needs one observing poll or one operator stamp) is an alert. The Builder's own D322(4) says such a game "costs one poll a minute, said in the plan and named by the reconciliation": it costs THREE polls a minute (`planLivePoll` is hot ⇒ rounds at 0/20/40 s, `resetScheduleMemo()` before each ⇒ three ~2 MB nflverse CSV reads per minute, ≈ 8.6 GB/day, for the rest of the season), and "named" is a warning the automation ignores. **Fix:** (a) `game_not_final_late` becomes an `alert` once the game's week is past `correction_window_ends_at` (the week can no longer finalize — §24.1 "job failures: any, with league_id"), stays `warn` before it (a Monday-morning provider lag is not an incident); pin both sides at the window instant (D146); (b) the message says what is stuck (the week's `last_game_ends_at` cannot be written; every league on the week is held at `live`; the operator escape is Q37's `nfl_games` edit — and say that the sync-live plan will keep re-polling and the composite provider will re-write the status back unless the row is moved OUT of the week, E43's kickoff rule); (c) D322(4) corrected: three polls a minute, and the CSV cost per hot minute. *(Q37 stays open with Chris — this is the reconciliation's severity for a state the law already names, not a ruling.)*

### Nit

- **R879 · nit · D322(12d) + `sync-live/route.test.ts:31` — "`LIVE_POLL_BUDGET_MS − POLL_CADENCE_MS = 25 s` is the latest a round may start" is false by 20 s, and the pin does not pin what its name says.** `live-poll.ts:288–291` breaks when `elapsed + POLL_CADENCE_MS >= budgetMs` — `elapsed` measured AFTER the round — then sleeps the cadence; a round therefore STARTS at any instant below the budget (with instant polls 0 / 20 / 40 s; with a 24 s first poll the second round starts at 44 s), leaving `maxDuration − budget = 15 s` for it. The test's name ("the last round starts at budget − cadence = 25 s at the latest") and D322(12d)'s "a poll slower than 35 s would still be cut" are the stale-record class. **Fix:** re-word both to "a round starts strictly inside the budget (< 45 s), so the last round has at least `maxDuration − LIVE_POLL_BUDGET_MS = 15 s`; a poll slower than that is cut by `maxDuration` — idempotent, re-polled next minute (queue-before-stats, R706)", and pin `maxDuration * 1000 − LIVE_POLL_BUDGET_MS ≥ 15_000`.

- **R880 · nit · `live-poll.ts:139–155` (`planLivePoll`'s sweep target is `currentWeek` only) — a week is not polled after the NEXT week's `starts_at`, although its correction window runs 30 h longer, and the record does not say so.** 2026 week 1: `starts_at` of week 2 is 2026-09-16 04:00Z (Wed 00:00 ET); week 1's `correction_window_ends_at` is 2026-09-17 10:00Z (Thu 06:00 ET). Between them nothing polls week 1 (idle; the hourly sweep reads week 2), so an in-window Wednesday/Thursday correction never reaches `player_stats`, the worker never applies it, and the week finalizes without it — the reconciliation cannot see it either (stored = recomputed over the stale line). §14's `sync-stat-corrections` (M6 L.E2) is the job that owns this, and Sleeper's Tuesday corrections ARE covered (week 1 stays current until Wed 04:00Z, the sweep re-polls hourly). **Fix:** say it on D322(4) and F216 (the residual until L.E2); the one-line closer if wanted now: the sweep polls every week whose `correction_window_ends_at > now` beside the current one (one extra `getWeekStats` per hour for ≤ 30 h a week).

- **R881 · nit · `reconcile.ts:234–246` — `stuck_queue` / `in_flight` are emitted once per CELL (every team in every league that starts the queued player), and `stuck_queue` fires even when the cell agrees.** One orphaned `score_fanout` row for a popular RB is N × M alert lines a night. **Fix:** the queue-age finding is a property of `(season, week, player_id)` — emit it once per queue row (season-wide, beside the calendar findings) and let the cell-level arm stay `in_flight` (info) only; keep "fires even when the cell agrees" (it is the honest signal that the worker is not draining) but at the row, not the cell.

- **R882 · nit · F216's D304 amendment and D322(4) say the composite provider carries "nflverse's inactives"; nothing on the production path consumes them.** `StatsProvider.getInactives` is called by no code outside the fixture/recording providers and the M0 fixture session (`grep -rn getInactives src` — `ingest-week.ts` never calls it; the composite forwards it, C56's note says it is "a provider, not a table"). The record reads as if inactives reach the tables. This matters because the official-inactive list is precisely the DNP-vs-provider-gap discriminator R871/F263(g) lack (R877(b)). **Fix:** one sentence on F216/D322(4): "inactives are exposed by the composite and consumed by nothing until M5's auto-sub (F211) / L.E2"; and name it as R877's closer of record.

- **R883 · nit · `score-week/route.ts:38` builds `createTypedAdminClient()` OUTSIDE the `try` (the other two routes build it inside), so a missing `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` surfaces as an unhandled throw rather than the route's own `[score-week] failed:` line — cosmetic, but the three routes should share one shape. Beside it, for the record only: the hourly sweep keys on `getUTCMinutes() === 0` of the injected instant, so a Vercel cron invocation delayed past :00:59 skips that hour's schedule refresh (D322(12b)'s "a missed minute is latency" covers the polls; say the sweep is the same — E42's flex move then lands in ≤ 2 h, not ≤ 1 h).

**Each mechanism re-derived and re-measured, not taken from the PR body:**
- **(a) `draft-realtime-db` / F74.** Read in the installed sources: `@supabase/realtime-js` 2.101.1 `RealtimeClient.removeChannel()` (`dist/main/RealtimeClient.js:221-229`) awaits `channel.unsubscribe()` and then calls `this.disconnect()` **un-awaited** when `channels.length === 0`; `@supabase/phoenix` 0.4.0 `Socket.teardown` → `waitForBufferDone(conn)` defers `conn.close()` by `150 × tries` ms while `conn.bufferedAmount` is non-zero (`phoenix.cjs.js:1568-1602`); `socketAdapter.disconnect()` resolves only inside phoenix's teardown callback (after `waitForSocketClosed`, `conn = null`), so `await client.realtime.disconnect()` + `connectionState() === 'closed'` is a real settle, and `client.channel(topic)` after it opens a fresh socket (`RealtimeClient.js:297-308`; the torn-down channel left the registry via `_onClose → _remove`, `RealtimeChannel.js:91`). **Reproduced independently** with a scratch copy under `src/lib/leagues/api/` (deleted after; `git status` clean), `conn.bufferedAmount` pinned to 1 at the release sites: **`main`'s harness → `[probe] member probe status: SUBSCRIBED socket: open` → `socket 3s later: closed channel state: errored` → `AssertionError: the member-side heartbeat (positive control, direct-tick-driven): expected undefined to be truthy` at 54,223 ms (1 failed | 1 passed)**; **this branch's harness under the same pin → 2/2 green in 12.46 s.** The positive control still asserts a member-side heartbeat DELIVERED over a real socket, fire-then-poll direct-tick-driven, budget untouched. Sweep confirmed: `removeChannel` in exactly three stack suites (`auction-realtime-db`, `draft-realtime-db`, `inseason-realtime-db`).
- **(b) `auction-api-db:569`.** 092's `draft_place_bid_internal` inserts the bid, updates the nomination, runs 091's `draft_mock_cpu_respond_internal` in the same transaction and **re-reads the draft row before returning** (092:2135-2140), so the response's `high_bidder_team_id` can only be changed by the in-RPC responder — the Builder's root cause holds and the F113 freeze indeed cannot touch it. The responder seeds `draft_mock_cpu_bid_value` per (draft, seq, team, **pass = live bid count**), so the human's bid re-draws every CPU's ±15 % value. **Re-simulated through the real 091 functions on the local stack** (3,000 fresh draft uuids, 8 seats, rank 4, $200/16 slots, need 1.0, $185 cap, the ladder run by the responder's own predicate + `draft_mock_cpu_raise_amount`): ladder end X mean 51.5 (45–53), max 24 rungs, **116 / 3,000 = 3.87 % answered X+3; 0 / 3,000 answered at max bid.** Same regime as the record's 4.97 %, not the same digit (R908). **Meaning preserved:** the CPU raise BEFORE the launcher's bid is still driven and asserted (`:520-551` unchanged — rewind, tick, `high_bidder_team_id !== commishTeamId`, `high_bid ≥ 2`), the launcher still bids through the route FOR the human seat, and the assertion is the same `high_bidder_team_id === commishTeamId`; what changed is the amount (pinned `=== MAX_BID` 185 and `> high_bid`), which is the one amount E5 makes unanswerable — the old cell never asserted a counter-raise (it asserted its absence), so nothing it proved was dropped.

The waits poll for the state the LAW says must arrive (nomination live / closed / pick count) with a 10 s bound under the 30 s bid clock, so a clock the engine wrongly armed still reds on timeout (a cron cannot close it inside the wait). `cronClosed` is inferred, not measured (R906), but the sum cannot pass a wrong tally: every close pass contributes ≥ 1, so 8 passes summing to 8 forces every open pass to report 0 and every close pass ≤ 1, and `pickCount() === 8` is asserted beside it; the per-pass `auction_awarded` report itself stays pinned in pgTAP 038 (`:806`, `awarded: 1`).

### PR #276 — L.D6.2 review findings

*(Adversarial review, 2026-09-08 — `feat/M4-L.D6.2-inseason-e2e` @ `dae64ae`. **Five read-only lenses plus one designated measurer that owned the stack and the e2e port and was told to ACTIVELY DEFEAT each spec**, every finding put to an independent refuter; **5 of 14 raised findings survived**. Numbers continue at R936; ledger rows at F297. **VERDICT: FIX-ROUND** — one BLOCKER: a spec that passes against the exact break it claims to prove.)*

**RULING — would each spec pass against a broken application?** `inseason-week` **holds**: an injected `finalize_matchups` that writes nothing *and lies in its report* went RED at the stored `league_weeks.status` (the spec deliberately reads the database, not the job's self-report); a drain that writes nothing while reporting `outcome: 'written'` went RED on the live score; reversed rank order went RED. `inseason-lock` **holds**: suppressing only the add-side E32 raise went RED with `Expected 409, Received 200`, and the refusal sentence is server-authored, not a client constant. **`inseason-remix` does NOT hold — see R936.**

**RULING — the failing `journey.spec.ts` is PROVEN pre-existing.** The measurer checked out `main` @ `ff52bb6` (confirmed the tip, and an ancestor of this branch) and ran that spec alone: **1 failed, identical error, identical line** (waiting for the scoring-template button). The branch touches nothing on the create-league wizard path. **F292 is correct handling of a genuine pre-existing red, and this is the standard the lane should hold: an excusing claim reproduced on a clean checkout of the base commit BEFORE it is accepted.** What is not proven is a SECOND failure the PR body silently omits — see R942.

**RULING — the break probe is HONEST SATISFACTION.** The row asked for the worker to be held between lock and finalize; no pause switch exists in the repo and the builder said so plainly in the spec header, in D330(9) and in the PR body rather than implying one. It is the real thing because (i) the hold is literally true — `driveScoreBatch` is the only writer of a matchup score in the harness, and no pg_cron job scores matchups; (ii) the control is falsifiable and permanent — 48 stat + 48 queue rows planted and asserted written, both sides asserted to read exactly `0`, and `sideScore` throws if the hook is absent so it cannot pass vacuously; (iii) it was measured discriminating in the right direction under the drain-writes-nothing probe.

- **R936 [BLOCKER]** `e2e/inseason-remix.spec.ts:205-218` — **the spec's headline claim is asserted by nothing.** The only datum that could prove the season was rewritten (`pairing(before) !== pairing(after)`) is computed and then consumed ONLY by a `console.log`. Every post-confirm assertion reads the route's own self-report or a row count invariant under a rewrite that persists the original pairings. **MEASURED, not argued:** the measurer replaced `schedule_remix_confirm` with a variant that snapshots the pre-remix pairings, performs the same DELETE, then re-INSERTs the ORIGINALS instead of the proposed plan — both in-body guards pass, the `no_changes` refusal never fires, the system post is still written, the route still returns `matchups_replaced: 56`, and the spec runs **3 passed**, printing its own DoD evidence line as `week-1 pairings changed: false`. **Three separate refuters knocked this finding down and all three refutations are falsified by that experiment** — each reasoned about a different mutation (a dropped seed) than the one actually built. **Fix:** promote the comparison to an assertion, but NOT scoped to week 1 (`no_changes === false` only guarantees SOME regenerable week changed, so a week-1-only diff would flake): after confirm, read the persisted matchups over each of `applied.weeks_regenerated` and assert they equal the preview's `proposed` filtered to `regenerated`. This is the pattern `inseason-week` already uses correctly and `inseason-remix` is missing.
- **R937 [MAJOR]** `e2e/helpers/harness.ts:1155` (type) / `:1165` (guard) — **`jobReport`'s failure guard is dead code.** `failures` is a JSONB **array of objects**, not a number, so `Number(report.failures) > 0` is `0 > 0` (empty) or `NaN > 0` (non-empty) — **always false**. Verified against the HEAD definitions (`119:734/890/909`, `118:1752/1906/1929`, `118:1979/2181/2208`), not the earliest file. It is the only failure check in the e2e lane and the PR body asserts it works. Failing scenario: `lineup_lock_tick` raises inside its per-league exception block; `v_leagues` was already incremented and PL/pgSQL does not roll that back, so the RPC returns `{leagues: 1, failures: [{...}]}` — `lockTickAt`'s `leagues === 0` throw does not fire, `jobReport`'s cannot, and `inseason-week.spec.ts:281` passes. **A lock pass that failed outright is reported to the spec as a success** — "nothing happened means it worked", with a fuse. MAJOR not BLOCKER because the swallowed exception rolls that league's writes back and the other three call sites are caught by their own downstream assertions. **Fix:** `Array.isArray(report.failures) ? … : []` and throw on `length > 0`, mirroring the neighbouring `driveScoreBatch`'s correct `problems.length > 0`; type it `unknown[]`; guard a non-array shape loudly; correct the PR body.
- **R938 [MUST-FIX]** `e2e/inseason-remix.spec.ts:177-203` — **what was APPLIED is never compared to what was PREVIEWED.** `applied.system_post` round-trips four ways (DOM, route body, `league_chat`, feed) but never against `expectedPreview`. Failing scenario: confirm regenerates from a seed other than the one previewed — the user previews plan A and receives plan B's season — and everything stays green, because the week list is identical across seeds in this fixture and the only datum that moves lives inside the post. **R936 and R938 do not subsume each other:** the measurer's patched function still composes the message from the previewed seed, so the post matched while the rows were the originals. **Fix:** assert `applied.system_post === expectedPreview`, and additionally assert the confirm's own echoed seed equals the previewed seed, since two seeds could coincide on the change count.
- **R939 [SHOULD-FIX]** `e2e/helpers/harness.ts:399-431` / `:294-380` — **the door check cannot see the residue this suite itself leaves when a run dies before `afterAll`.** It checks `nfl_games` by prefix and `nfl_weeks.first_kickoff_at` — a column this suite never writes — while the three surfaces the module-level ledger is the sole record of (`player_stats`, `score_fanout`, `nfl_weeks.last_game_ends_at`) are checked by nothing. Failing scenario: Ctrl-C or a CI timeout after the stat rows are planted; the ledger dies with the process; the next run's sweep iterates an empty ledger, deletes nothing, verifies nothing, and reports a reassuring `0 game row(s) + 0 stat tuple(s)` — while `npm run sim:census` immediately reddens three of nine cells. **F199's exact species, and the R923 comment recording the same one-column-filter mistake sits directly above that census cell.** Fix: make the door check query the same surfaces the census counts, scoped so it still cannot clobber the sim's fixtures.
- **R940 [NIT]** `e2e/inseason-remix.spec.ts:226-230` + PR body — the comment claims "an exact-equality assertion, not a substring one"; the code is `toContainText`, and exact equality is impossible for that element (it also renders a badge and a timestamp). A regression that wrapped or prefixed the message would still pass. Reword, or give the message span a hook and use `toHaveText`.
- **R941 [NIT]** `PROGRESS` §2 row and D330(10) — says "**THREE** hooks were added deliberately" and then names **four**; the commit and the PR body both say four and `git show --stat` adds four. **Same class as R933, same file, one session old.** Also `data-discard-lineup` is consumed by nothing repo-wide — say so.
- **R942 [NIT]** PR body proof table — the claimed `npm run test:e2e` split **15 passed / 1 failed did not reproduce**: the measurer got **14 passed / 2 failed**, the extra being `auction-storm.spec.ts:347`, untouched by this PR, which sorts BEFORE the three in-season specs and passes in isolation — a pre-existing flake that under `retries: 0` is a real concurrency bug until proven otherwise. File it as its own row rather than absorbing it. Also the quoted `52.30 → 84.60` scores are fixture-dependent and did not reproduce (measured `46.80 → 69.60`, `45.60 → 68.40`); the assertions are relational so this is harmless, but the numbers are not evidence.

**A meta-finding worth keeping:** the measurer's own "verified clean" list asserted that `jobReport` refuses `failures > 0` — **false, and it is R937**. Having empirically defeated three refuters on the remix spec, it accepted that one BY INSPECTION and did not execute it: the same failure mode it caught everyone else in. *A reviewer's clean list carries less weight on lines it read than on lines it ran.*

### PR #279 — F56 / F297 flake root-cause review findings

*(Adversarial review, 2026-09-08 — `fix/M4-e2e-flakes-F56-F297` @ `e5a5224`. Three read-only lenses plus one designated measurer that owned the stack and the e2e port and was told to make each flake RETURN; every finding put to an independent refuter. **1 of 6 raised findings survived**, and it is the fix's own new failure mode. Numbers continue at R943. **VERDICT: FIX-ROUND**.)*

**RULING — the APPLICATION change is JUSTIFIED; keep it.** All four candidate recovery paths were traced on `main` and every one is closed in the pre-start state: the beat-silence watchdog was gated on a live draft; the lobby poll returns null outside two minutes of a STORED instant; the room query sets no refetch interval; the global client disables focus refetch with a 60 s stale time. The single start broadcast was the only delivery path and its silent loss is documented, not hypothetical. The defect is real for a user independent of the test.

**RULING — are the flakes gone?** **F297: gone by cause.** The original red reproduces deterministically at the point the hold now sits, and the new guard is load-bearing in both directions (a 1 s hold reds the read-back with `Expected > 30000 / Received 993`); every anti-snipe number is captured above the hold; no retry, sleep, widened timeout or reordering. **F56: gone by MECHANISM for lost broadcasts, and the brief case is MEASURED, not inferred** — total loss (deaf-after-subscribe, socket alive) flips live in **5,383 ms**; **broadcasts dropped for only 4 s across the start flip in 5,356 ms**. The fix is time-based ("ask every 5 s while scheduled"), so it does not depend on loss duration; the brief case is strictly easier. Pre-fix baseline reproduced independently at the spec's own locator and timeout with **0** requests in 60 s — "not one request" is exact. **The hole is R943: the backstop is defeated by 1–2 s of lost CONNECTIVITY landing on a beat, permanently and silently. Until that is closed, "the flake cannot return" is true of lost broadcasts and false of lost connectivity.** Also on the record: the probe's frame filter was checked against the installed serializer — a naive `event === 'broadcast'` filter would have dropped nothing and produced a FALSE GREEN; carry that forward for whoever repeats it.

- **R943 [HIGH — MUST-FIX]** `src/hooks/use-draft.ts:205` (`const fetched = query.isSuccess`), `:495` (deps), `:483/:488/:490` (the new interval and the cleanup that kills it AND the channel) — **the new watchdog self-disarms on a transient fetch error and takes the realtime channel with it.** The 5 s `scheduled` beat is the first thing in the pre-start room that issues fetches; a fetch that fails flips `query.isSuccess` false, re-running the channel effect into its `if (!draftId || !fetched) return` guard, whose cleanup clears the interval and removes the channel — **and nothing left alive can ever set `fetched` back**. The backstop destroys itself with its own request. Verified in the installed react-query reducer (the error case sets `status: 'error'` unconditionally; data is retained, `isSuccess` is not), and the one revival that exists — the lobby poll — arms only inside the two-minute window, i.e. **precisely outside the window this arm was added to cover**. MEASURED twice on the frozen tree: two aborted beats, then connectivity fully restored, and the room never gets in (`flipMs = -1`). Post-fix this path is exercised ~720 times an hour per open room, so the PR converts a latent one-shot into a routine one with the same user-visible outcome as the bug it fixes. **Fix (minimal, same file):** hoist the watchdog into its own effect keyed on `draftId` alone so a failed fetch cannot cancel the mechanism whose job is to retry it; or `query.isSuccess || query.data !== undefined`, which additionally stops a background-refetch failure from tearing down a LIVE room's channel. Pin "a failed beat does not disarm the next beat". **Tolerance to state in the record: the fix survives exactly ONE failed request (react-query's single retry absorbs it); two kill it.**
- **R944 [LOW]** `src/components/draft/draft-room.tsx:377` — the scheduled lobby's `stale` prop reads the OUTER league-detail health, not the resolved room health, so when the room's own query is degraded — the state R943 produces — the lobby renders a confident countdown with no degraded signal. Pre-existing, but it is why R943 fails SILENTLY, so it belongs in the same fix round: pass the resolved combined health into the scheduled render.
- **R945 [LOW — record, do not rebuild]** `use-draft.ts:470-483` with `use-draft-ops.ts:494` — the room query has no version guard on its fetch path (F304), so a beat's read that resolves after the start broadcast was applied replaces the flipped row with the pre-flip one. Pre-fix that window opened once at join; post-fix it re-opens every 5 s for the whole pre-start dwell. Measured deterministically: **4,997 ms rendering "Draft scheduled" while the draft was live and the pick clock ran.** NOT a blocker — the bounce is bounded to one watchdog period BY THIS PR, and pre-fix the identical stomp had no repair at all; net wrong-render time is neutral-to-better and what is new is a flicker at the flip. Amend F304 to say the window is now recurring at the watchdog cadence; its real fix stays its own task.
- **R946 [LOW]** the `scheduled` arm's docblock, the PR body and D333(2) claim "the ONE room state with no reconciliation of any kind" — **not true of the sibling pre-start surface**: a `scheduled` league with NO drafts row renders the lobby with a null draft and returns before the room resolves, so there is no draft id, no channel, and the new watchdog cannot arm. That state is reachable (the start RPC is create-if-absent and the start control is ungated), but bounded — the status transition refuses `scheduled` without a stored instant, so the lobby poll rescues it from T-2min, making the exposure (early-start delta − 2 min) and self-healing. **Do not widen this PR:** file it as its own row, and narrow both absolute claims to the with-row lobby, which is what the fix reaches.
- **R947 [record]** two corrections. (a) The PR presents the F297 probe with a negative hold as a reproduction; it PASSED on the measurer's machine because it depends on where the 5 s cron lands — re-describe it as non-deterministic and name the rewind-plus-tick variant as the deterministic one. (b) A reviewer clean-list entry asserting that a failed refetch "is simply re-issued 5 s later" and that a failure "surfaces as the degraded banner" is **wrong on both halves** (R943 and R944 respectively) and must be struck rather than carried.

**RULING — the MERGE-ORDER hazard.** This branch and the unmerged `feat/M4-L.D6.3-synthetic-gate` rewrite **the same physical line** — §6's F56 row — from a common ancestor at `main@89b267f`. A table row is one line, so git will CONFLICT rather than silently pick a side; the hazard is a careless resolution. **The reconciled row must carry all four:** (1) keep L.D6.3's REOPENED narrative in FULL — it alone records that the widened settle is inherited by the m2 and m3 gates, and the competing harness explanation that the manager's socket is routed through the test runner's own hop, which no stack-side probe can see; (2) the STATUS cell is #279's close, re-stamped to 2026-09-08 with the gate half re-closed here after the earlier discharge was defeated by measurement — not L.D6.3's REOPENED; (3) L.D6.3's "still not known" line is SUPERSEDED, and the row keeps #279's forward instruction that a future red at that exact locator is not this row, plus the corollary that reds at OTHER lines in that spec are unrelated and open; (4) it must carry R943's correction — the gate-half close is conditional on the watchdog surviving a failed beat, and until the disarm is fixed the row covers lost broadcasts and NOT lost connectivity. Nothing else in §6 collides (each branch's new rows verified zero-occurrence on the other). **Resolve by hand against those four points; do not take either side wholesale.**

**Verified clean (do not re-litigate):** the F297 fix holds the lot only AFTER every anti-snipe number and both browser observations are captured, and closes it through the sanctioned rewind-plus-tick path; no forbidden mitigation appears anywhere in the diff (no retry, no sleep, no widened timeout, no skip, no reordered assertion, no loosened matcher); the probe's frame filter was validated against the real serializer rather than assumed; three consecutive full green browser suites on an md5-frozen tree corroborate the mechanism change. **Not claimed and not to be claimed:** that spec is not proven flake-free in general — under deliberately heavy load it red at OTHER lines, but those runs were method-contaminated and carry no weight either way.

**Fix round (Builder), 2026-09-08 — R943–R947 ALL taken or filed; the branch's own new failure mode is closed at the cause, and the application change the review approved is unchanged.** Mechanics in **D333(8)**; **F307** filed; **F304** amended; **F56**'s cell gains its (c) closer. Two files of production code, two test files, no SQL, no typegen, heads still 122 / 070.

- **R943 [HIGH] — TAKEN, and REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED (F139's rule, applied to the reviewer's own finding).** On the frozen pre-fix tree the probe aborts the manager's `/rest/v1/drafts` reads and then restores connectivity **fully**: `ABORT#1@+12453ms, ABORT#2@+13460ms` (one beat plus react-query's single `retry`), `RESTORED@+13469ms`, **0 room GETs in the next 20 s, `flipMs=-1`, 0 room GETs after the start click** — the review's measurement reproduced independently. **The tolerance was measured from BOTH sides on that same tree:** ONE aborted request is absorbed (`ABORT#1@+9341ms`, restored, **5** room GETs in the following 20 s, `flipMs=798`), **two kill it** — so pre-fix the backstop survived exactly one failed request, as the review bounded it. A third arm proves the BACKSTOP rather than the interval — two aborted beats and *then* a lost start broadcast, so only the watchdog can get the room in: **RED pre-fix (`flipMs=-1`), GREEN post-fix at `flipMs=4098`, one watchdog period.** **THE FIX CHOSEN, and why:** the gate at `use-draft.ts:205` is widened through a new pure predicate `draftHasBeenFetched` (`isSuccess || hasData`) rather than the watchdog being hoisted into its own `draftId`-keyed effect. Both close the disarm; only widening also stops the CHANNEL being torn down and rebuilt on every transient fetch error — and a rejoin raced against a closing socket is F74/D325's deaf-channel shape, i.e. the very fault this watchdog exists to back up. It is also the honest reading of §9.3: fetch-then-subscribe asks *do we HOLD the row*, not *did the last request succeed*. **PINNED** as the review asked — a failed beat does not disarm the next beat — by 2 predicate pins, 2 effect-lifecycle pins (a driver over the one React semantic this turns on, running the REAL predicate for the shipped arm and the pre-fix `query.isSuccess` expression literally for the other) and 3 source pins holding the file to the shape the driver models. Break probe A: `fetched` put back to `query.isSuccess` → **2 of 67 RED** by name, reverted, md5 restored.
- **R944 [LOW] — TAKEN.** `renderScheduled` now takes `DraftRoomResolved`'s RESOLVED health (`worstHealth(contextHealth, queryHealth(room))`) as a third argument, and the league lobby reads `stale={roomHealth === 'degraded'}`; the mock mount ignores it (a standalone mock is inserted `live`, so it is never `scheduled`). The pre-existing `occurrences(room, "health === 'degraded'") === 3` pin could not have caught this — `roomHealth === 'degraded'` is a different string and the count is unchanged — so it is re-stated honestly as **2 mount-health + 1 room-health = 3 surfaces** and the wiring itself is pinned end to end. Break probe B: the lobby put back on the mount's context health → **2 of 27 RED**, reverted, md5 restored.
- **R945 [LOW] — RECORDED as instructed, and the optional one-line mitigation DECLINED with a reason rather than skipped silently.** F304's row now states that post-#279 its window is recurring at `ROOM_WATCHDOG_MS` and produces the measured **4,997 ms** live→scheduled bounce, with the ruling that this is net neutral-to-better because pre-fix the identical stomp had no repair at all. The mitigation is refused on two grounds: "skip a beat while a refetch is in flight" silences the beat for as long as that fetch stays non-idle, and a fetch parking at `fetchStatus: 'paused'` and swallowing every later invalidate is already MEASURED in this repo (F79, in F56's own cell) — that is R943's failure mode re-entered through another door, in the round that closes it; and it does not close F304's window regardless, because the stomping read is already in flight when the broadcast lands, so skipping the NEXT beat repairs nothing. F304's real fix stays its own task.
- **R946 [LOW] — TAKEN (both claims narrowed) and FILED as F307.** The `scheduled` arm's docblock, `use-draft.ts`'s watchdog comment, D333(2) and the PR body now say "the ONE room state **that mounts the room** and has no reconciliation of any kind", each naming the sibling and its bound. **Checked rather than assumed while narrowing:** the second clause ("or a league with no stored instant at all") SURVIVES once scoped to the with-row lobby, because `draft_create` admits a league in `setup` (`066:483`) and so a `scheduled` drafts row can exist before any instant is stored. **F307** carries the sibling — arm the lobby poll while a no-row `scheduled` lobby is mounted — with the bound that made it LOW: the status transition refuses `scheduled` without a stored instant (`059:311-317`), so the D94 poll rescues it from T−2min and the exposure is (early-start delta − 2 min) and self-healing.
- **R947 [record] — BOTH corrections taken.** (a) D333(4) now describes the negative-hold F297 probe as **NON-deterministic** — it only moves the deadline back, and whether the lot is closed by `:347` still depends on where the live 5 s cron lands (the reviewer's measurer got 3 passed / 20.0 s from it) — and names the **rewind-plus-tick** variant as the deterministic reproduction. Probe (a), the 1 s hold, is unaffected and reds by name in both hands. (b) The clean-list sentence that a failed refetch "is simply re-issued 5 s later" and that a failure "surfaces as the degraded banner" is **STRUCK and carried nowhere** in this record: both halves are false, and each is a finding of this very round (R943 / R944 respectively).
- **The merge-order hazard is UNTOUCHED beyond what R943 required.** F56's cell gains one appended closer, **(c)**, recording that the gate-half close was conditional for one round and that the condition is now met — the backstop covers lost CONNECTIVITY as well as lost broadcasts, measured. Nothing else in the cell moved, so the four points the reconciliation must carry are still followable line for line by whichever of `fix/M4-e2e-flakes-F56-F297` and `feat/M4-L.D6.3-synthetic-gate` merges second.

### PR #278 — L.D6.3 (the synthetic gate) review findings

*(Adversarial review, 2026-09-09 — `feat/M4-L.D6.3-synthetic-gate` @ `bb23b1d`. Four read-only lenses plus one designated measurer that owned the stack and was told to make the gate CERTIFY WHEN IT SHOULD NOT; every finding put to an independent refuter. **3 of 10 raised findings survived** (plus one the measurer proved by execution). Numbers continue at R948. **VERDICT: FIX-ROUND** — two one-line defects, both in the class this gate exists to eliminate.)*

**RULING — can this gate report success while the milestone is broken? YES, in exactly two proven ways; not in the broad ways the review hunted.** Twelve attacks on the evidence stage and the shell were **all correctly refused**: the shell cannot swallow a red (strict mode, 19 bare foreground stages, no pipe/subshell/`|| true`/trap/retry — demonstrated by injecting a failure at an early stage), and the evidence stage is **fail-closed on absence** — a missing report, a short population, a wrong scenario/seed/week span, a false green, any problem, any invariant failure, any failing assertion, a **missing required assertion BY NAME**, non-zero external calls, foreign-source stat rows, zero stat rows, under-covered reconciliation, any refused or unseated lineup, too few schedule modes or templates, a missing gap declaration, non-zero pool rows, or an unclean census each fail by name, and the artifact directory is wiped first so a stale report cannot be reused. Assertions read the **database**, not job self-reports. Two posited regressions are caught fatally at earlier stages. **The two holes are single-predicate omissions, not design failures — and both fixes are one line.**

- **R948 [MUST-FIX]** `src/lib/leagues/sim/season-runner.ts:2386` — **the postponement arm's `finalized_without_game` is EXISTENTIALLY quantified**: `leagues.some(...)`, where all three sibling arms asserting the same property use universal forms (`every`, and `finalized === leagues.length` twice). The finalize job's second guard is **per-league**, so a starter with no line for the postponed game leaves that league's cell pending and the week held forever — only the handful of leagues rostering no postponed-club player finalize. **One league in a hundred finalizing is a PASS**: the stage prints `[PASS] finalized_without_game … 1/100 leagues`, the run stays green, the evidence stage passes, and the gate certifies with the property it exists to prove broken in 99 leagues. Nothing else catches it — a held week is by design never a failure elsewhere (the classifier only labels; the hold lands in a `skipped` array nothing reads; invariant 5 filters non-final rows out of BOTH sides; the evidence stage computes finals for a print line only). **Aggravating: this PR's own commit hardened the three neighbours for exactly this defect class and left this arm byte-identical to `main`.** Not a false red — the real run recorded 100/100. **Fix:** `leagues.every((l) => l.weeksFinal.has(firstWeek))`; if some leagues are legitimately expected to hold, state the threshold and the reason in the expectation string rather than accepting one.
- **R949 [MUST-FIX]** `season-runner.ts:1455` (with `:563-567`, and its absence from `scripts/gate-m4-evidence.ts`) — **run-wide, league-unattributed worker errors are printed and enforced by nothing.** The run's green flag ANDs invariant failures, problems, reason and per-assertion passes — **`workerErrors` is absent from the conjunction**; the invariant reads only the PER-LEAGUE map, and the two batch-level pushes write to the run-wide array and set nothing in it; the evidence stage never mentions the field. **Proven by execution:** injecting a worker error into the builder's own nine reports yields **exit 0** and the banner "all 9 scenarios green, every assertion present". The pushed line sits under a comment reading *"the ONE window a stale write can land in — alert on both sides"*, and that alert reaches scrollback and no assertion. Partial cross-coverage stated honestly: a stale write that PERSISTS surfaces as reconciliation drift; one later overwritten does not, and the broader class of unclassified batch problems is uncovered. **Fix:** one line in the evidence stage's per-report block beside the existing problem checks, and optionally attribute the two batch-level lines to a run pseudo-league so the run's own green goes false at source.
- **R950 [SHOULD-FIX]** `season-invariants.ts:428-431` and `season-runner.ts:2742` — **the pool-mirror withdrawal declares a surviving live half that is equally dead.** Both texts say reconciliation's mirror check "runs over the real population" and "is the only part of this function that can currently fail"; it reads the SAME empty table over the SAME leagues, so both its branches die on emptiness — and the gate itself asserts that table is empty. Delete a real pool INSERT and every report still prints zero rows, the check returns nothing, and the gate hands the reader a machine-checked artifact saying reconciliation's half was still live. The headline withdrawal is correct and genuinely enforced, which is why this is not MUST-FIX — but the false clause sits inside the very string the evidence stage machine-checks, and it restores the "silence reads as coverage" impression the withdrawal exists to destroy. **Fix: text only, two clauses.**
- **R951 [SHOULD-FIX]** `scripts/gate-m4-evidence.ts:224` — `REQUIRED_BY_SCENARIO[scenario] ?? []` makes a missing or mistyped key mean "this scenario requires only the universals", which is the exact shape this file's own docblock forbids (*"a missing name fails the gate by name"*). No wrong outcome today (the nine keys match exactly), but the mechanism was demonstrated. **Fix:** fail by name on a key the map does not carry.

**RULING — the RED was handled correctly, and it is the strongest evidence in this PR that the instrument works.** The gate reached the composed-M3 stage, went further than either prior attempt (that gate's own vitest, auction sim and its own 16-passed browser run all green, with **neither** previously-fixed flake firing), and died at 2,644 s on a **line never recorded before**. The builder filed it, reported the red, and **refused to add it to the flake-policy block** — which is what the block's own terms require, since it states that a red at any other line of those specs is a new finding that fails the gate. Adding it on the day it was found would have retro-justified the failure and converted a defect into an excuse. **The diagnostic gap is honest, not lazy:** automatic tracing applies only to the default fixtures and both clients in that spec are built manually, so no trace of either existed, *(**CORRECTED 2026-09-09 by D334(1) — this half of the sentence is measurably FALSE.** Playwright's `_setupArtifacts` auto-fixture hooks `didCreateBrowserContext` for EVERY context created during a test (`index.js:150` → `_startTraceChunkOnContextCreation`), so a hand-built `browser.newContext()` IS traced: an explicit `tracing.start()` in that spec errors with *"Tracing has been already started"*, and the retained `trace.zip` carries four sub-traces. The trace EXISTED and was **destroyed** — playwright empties `test-results/` at the start of every run and no gate script preserves it, so the isolation re-run made immediately after the failure deleted it, which is F56's own "copy the trace BEFORE re-running" lesson recurring. **RULING — the mechanism is PROVEN for the reproduction at class granularity, with one named residual, and SHAPE-MATCHED for the gate's own red, which the record already says.** What is proven: the nomination committed (read-back printed on every run); the broadcast trigger is unconditional per row, so the send was necessarily invoked; the send traps its own errors, so a failure can neither fail the transaction nor surface to the client; and all three ledgers carried the join, reply, presence and heartbeat traffic with **zero** draft, tick or bid frames — which excludes deaf-after-join (that path re-joins on a backoff, producing repeated joins and no presence), excludes a client-side stomp, and excludes a broken decoder (live frames decoded cleanly with zero undecodables). **RULING — Q49 is a GENUINE product question, correctly filed rather than tuned away, but it is MIS-HEADLINED and must be corrected before it reaches Chris.** The spec prints a heartbeat **cadence**, never a tolerance, and no sentence anywhere bounds how long a room may render a state it has moved past; the reconnecting banner arms off join failure, which a subscribed-but-deaf channel never trips. So the exposure is **undefined by the spec, not defined-and-violated** — the definition of a product question. The constant has exactly one consumer, whose effect is to trigger a refetch of server truth: it writes nothing, gates no autopick, renders no UI, so a shorter tolerance cannot diverge client from server and there is no wrong output to point at. **The substance deserves an answer regardless: on a surface with 30-second pick clocks, this means a manager can watch a full pick clock elapse on a room state that no longer exists, with no banner and no indication anything is wrong.** The mis-headline: the question says the constant derives from a cadence the engine no longer uses, which conflates two different beats — the one it measures is printed at fifteen seconds and shipped at five, while the fifteen-second beat it points at is an outbound liveness beat that is never broadcast and never reaches the measured reference. ### Blockers

TAKEN, on the DRAIN side.** 123 enqueued the symmetric difference of old and new starters; the worker marks a team `affected` only when a queued player is one of its **CURRENT** starters. Bench a kicked-off starter without replacing him and the one queued player starts NOWHERE: `toCompute.size === 0` ⇒ `outcome:'skipped'`, and the row is `mapped` so it goes to `toDelete`, not `toDefer` (`:982-986`, `:1241-1251`). The row is consumed, `team_week_results.points` keeps the benched player for ever, and the verb reports `no_changes:false, score_stale:false, score_enqueued:[the removed player]` — plain success. **The reviewers' remedy (enqueue the UNION instead) was NOT taken, and the rebuttal is measured:** the union only makes the common case likely. On a Thursday-night week 1 — Chris's actual week — the team's other starters have no `player_stats` rows yet, so the union IS the removed player alone and the drain skips identically. **What shipped instead:** `scoreLeagueWeek` reads `team_lineups.edited_by_commish` (one more column on a select it already makes) and forces those teams into `toCompute` (step 5b). The enqueue is what makes the drain VISIT the league-week; the flag is what makes it compute THIS team once there — including the case where a starting slot is left EMPTY and there is no queued starter to find the team by. Cost: one idempotent extra team per drain of an OPEN week (a `final` week returns at step 4, an `upcoming` week is held), and **nothing changes for an ordinary stat-driven drain** — no flag, no force, and a bench player's delta still recomputes nobody. **Pinned on both sides:** pgTAP 071 §H3 measures the premise (the one queued player is a starter of no team this week; the flag is on the row) and `score-week-worker-db.test.ts` R965 drives the whole drain — control (an ordinary delta reaches the team through step 5), then the override, then `affected_team_ids: []`, `commish_edited_team_ids: [T1]`, `outcome: 'written'`, and the matchup cell down by the D/ST's hand-computed 15.00. **Deliberate-break probe:** delete the one `toCompute.add` line ⇒ that cell reds with `expected 'skipped' to be 'written'` — the pre-fix behaviour by name — restored verbatim, green. **The manager's own mid-week edit has the same hole and is NOT fixed here → F328.**

### Should-fix — all eight taken

- **R966 · `123:222` + `:297` — `ON DELETE CASCADE` and an unconditional immutability trigger cannot both be true.** A cascade IS an ordinary DELETE on the child, so the trigger raised and the declared CASCADE could never execute: a league that had ever been audited became undeletable, and ~10 db-integration suites clean up with exactly `service.from('leagues').delete()`. **Fixed with ONE exemption inside the trigger, and its predicate is the FACT rather than a mode flag:** `TG_OP = 'DELETE' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM leagues WHERE id = OLD.league_id)`. During an `ON DELETE CASCADE` the parent row is already gone when the row trigger fires (measured on the local stack: the arm is taken at `pg_trigger_depth() = 2` and the cascade completes, while a DIRECT delete in the same transaction is still refused). `league_id` is NOT NULL with an FK, so a row can only reach the arm because its league is being destroyed — the log dies WITH its league and never one entry at a time. §12.12 is intact: no client can reach it at all (no DELETE policy; RLS shows a client zero rows). Two new pgTAP cells, beside the existing owner-refusal cell that must stay green with them.

- **R967 · `123:297` — TRUNCATE is the same hole one operation over, and it is not covered.** A `FOR EACH ROW` trigger never fires for TRUNCATE, RLS does not apply to TRUNCATE at all, and Supabase's default grants TRUNCATE on a new public table to `anon` and `authenticated`. MEASURED: as `authenticated`, `DELETE FROM commissioner_actions` → `DELETE 0` (RLS, as designed), then `TRUNCATE … CASCADE` → **succeeded**, cascading into `league_weeks`, `matchups`, `transactions` and `team_week_results` through the three FKs 123 adds — with the RLS cells green throughout. **Fixed:** a `BEFORE TRUNCATE … FOR EACH STATEMENT` trigger, `ENABLE ALWAYS`, plus `REVOKE TRUNCATE` on both new tables. Four new pgTAP cells (the trigger's form, the refusal on the CASCADE form — a bare TRUNCATE is refused earlier with 0A000 by the FKs — and the grants on both tables). **The permissive default is SCHEMA-WIDE and is NOT swept here → F327.**

## Review findings — 2026-09-10 (Q43's scheduler — migration 124 + pgTAP 072: the fix round)

**Two adversarial reviewers on the uncommitted working tree: 1 blocker, 4 should-fixes (two of them the SAME defect reported twice), 4 nits. Blocker and all should-fixes TAKEN; three nits taken, one REBUTTED with a citation and a measurement.** The round is about one shape: a check that cannot see its own most likely cause of failure is CLAUDE.md's "never let 'nothing happened' mean 'it worked'" broken one level up. `scoring_stall_check` had it twice — once in how it read a queue row's stamps, once in what it looked at at all.

**Measured after the round (LOCAL stack only — nothing was run against production, no `db push`, no MCP write):** `npx supabase db reset` 001–124 clean · `npm run test:db` **73 files / 5,575 asserts, PASS** (pgTAP 072 went 40 → **59 cells**) · `npx vitest run` **219 files / 4,132 tests, PASS** · `type-check` clean · `lint` **0 warnings, 0 errors**. `cron.job` holds **8** jobs (068/071/116's five + 124's three, all `* * * * *`, `username = postgres`), and re-running 124's DO block leaves **exactly one job per name**.

### Blocker

- **R973 · BLOCKER · `124` `scoring_stall_check` — THE CHECK WENT BLIND EXACTLY WHEN A DRAIN DIES MID-WORK, THE CASE IT EXISTS FOR. TAKEN.** The predicate counted rows *no drain had EVER touched* (`claimed_at IS NULL AND deferred_until IS NULL`), but nothing ever clears either stamp on a row a dead drain left behind: `claimed_at` only by `score_fanout_ack` under its own token or the next claim (122 §4), `deferred_until` only by ingestion's re-stamp (`ingest-week.ts:757-765`), which never comes once the game is over. So ONE touch exempted a row for the rest of its life — while `score_fanout_claim`'s own predicate (122 §3) says it is still owed. The reviewer measured it on the local stack: two rows enqueued at the incident's own 08:50:35Z, one claimed at 08:50:40Z with a lease expired six hours earlier and one released with a `deferred_until` elapsed at 08:51:05Z, gave `{"rows": 0, "stalled": false}` at 14:50Z while the claim would have taken both. The repo's own worker already drew the line correctly (`score-week-worker.ts:757`: deferral is `deferred_until > now`, not `IS NOT NULL`), and the two pgTAP negatives that were supposed to pin this passed VACUOUSLY — E7's lease is 10 s old inside a 120 s lease and E8's `deferred_until` is in the FUTURE, so neither aged stamp was tested in either direction. **THE FIX:** the check now asks *"would `score_fanout_claim` still take this row, and has nothing moved it in ten minutes?"* — one cutoff applied to all three stamps: `enqueued_at < cutoff AND (claimed_at IS NULL OR claimed_at < cutoff) AND (deferred_until IS NULL OR deferred_until < cutoff)`. Ten minutes rather than the 120 s lease on the lease clause, deliberately: it is a STRICT SUBSET of what the claim would take (10 min > 120 s), so the arm can never name a row the claim would refuse, and the same patience is what the DEFERRAL clause needs — a healthy drain re-defers a held row 30 s at a time, so a bare `deferred_until <= p_now` would fire on a legitimately-held row waiting for the next per-minute invocation, and a stall check that fires on healthy queues gets muted. pgTAP 072 gains **§F (F1-F9)**, all aged-stamp cells, plus **F5** which EXECUTES `score_fanout_claim` at the same instant and proves it takes exactly the two rows the check counts. Every pre-existing E cell stayed green.

### Should-fix — all four taken (R974/R975 are one defect, R976 its twin from the second reviewer)

- **R974 · TAKEN, by R973's fix** — the same defect stated from the lease side (`claimed_at IS NULL` vs the claim's `claimed_at IS NULL OR claimed_at < p_now - lease`), with the invoker's own docblock cited: the `finally` release is best-effort and "the lease expiry is the backstop" (`score-week-invoker.ts:1338-1345`), while Vercel hard-kills at `maxDuration = 60` with up to 500 rows leased.
- **R975 + R976 · TAKEN — THE SHARED-FAILURE HOLE: both pings die together, and then the queue is EMPTY rather than backed up.** F329's "WHAT IS ACTUALLY COVERED" claimed a ping that never lands is caught by its consequence. False for the dominant mode: both jobs call the same `cron_ping_route`, through the same pg_net worker, with the same two Vault secrets, at the same origin — one-sided `CRON_SECRET` rotation, a push before `vault.create_secret`, a typo'd origin, a wedged pg_net, Vercel down — and with `sync-live` dead nothing is ever enqueued (`ingest-week.ts:752-784` is the only enqueue path), so the queue drains to empty and the flag reads healthy forever. **THE FIX:** a SECOND arm, `ingest_stale`, on the surface ingestion already writes per successful poll — `max(updated_at)` over `system_flags` keys `LIKE 'ingest_poll:%'`, older than **two hours** (one missed hourly sweep; `SWEEP_MINUTE = 0`). No new heartbeat and no new writer. `updated_at` is read from the COLUMN rather than the value's `completed_at` so a malformed value can never raise inside a cron job — they are the same instant by construction (`persistPollOutcome`), now pinned by name in `ingest-flags-db.test.ts`. A MISSING `ingest_poll` row is deliberately not a stall (never-ingested is not stopped, and a permanent banner on every developer's league is a muted banner); the exemption is narrow because `system_flags` rows are never deleted. pgTAP 072 gains **§G (G1-G9)** and **E14**. F329's claim is narrowed on the record rather than left standing. *(`cron.job_run_details` was measured and rejected as the vehicle: `has_schema_privilege('service_role','cron','USAGE')` is FALSE, so an INVOKER function reading it would error for the one role the D291 door exists for — and pg_cron records `succeeded` the moment pg_net accepts the request, so it cannot see a ping that lands and 401s.)*
- **R977 · TAKEN — THE ROLLOUT ORDER WAS BACKWARDS AND THE GAP WAS A SILENT TOTAL BLACKOUT.** Merging syncs `vercel.json` within minutes and would have deleted both daily entries, while the pg_cron jobs appear only at a manual `db push` and send nothing until two `vault.create_secret` calls: between those moments scoring runs ZERO times a day instead of once, and 124's stall check is not yet in production to report it. **`vercel.json` is therefore NOT TOUCHED by this PR** — all six entries stay. Running both schedulers is safe, verified from the code (the 120 s claim lease ≥ `maxDuration` + 30 s skew under `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` — two concurrent drains claim disjoint sets, `score-week-worker-db.test.ts:1107`; `ingestWeek` enqueues a DIFF, so a redundant poll writes nothing) at a cost of one extra provider read a day. *A correction to the reasoning that was offered for this: `planLivePoll` does NOT consult the last-poll instant — it plans from `nfl_games`/`nfl_weeks` alone (`live-poll.ts:134-188`). The idempotence is the diff's, not a dedupe's.* Q43's tail is rewritten with the four steps in the correct order (Vault secrets FIRST, before the merge), and **F331** carries the removal with its exact three-part confirmation condition.

### Nits — three taken, one rebutted

- **R978 · TAKEN** — pgTAP 072's falsifiability header named the wrong cells for its own load-bearing claims in four places (C0/C1-C4 and "C3/C4 red" where the hazard pins are C6/C7 and the raise cells C9/C11/C12 with C10/C13 proving nothing queued; "D2-D4" where the file has D2-D5; and the §E bullet's E4/E5/E6/E7/E8 where the file's cells are E7/E8/E9/E10/E11). ## Review findings — 2026-09-11 (M6A — L.E1.2, PR #291)

**Reviewer batch (fresh, independent: `feat/M6A-L.E1.2-errata-questions-ledger` @ `c2461eb`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE on ONE should-fix (R982) plus four nits (R983–R986).
